A group of students stopped, read it, and pulled out their phones to take photos.
sentences.cn: 一群学生停下来，读了一遍，掏出手机拍照。

sentences.en: One of them said it was the best idea she had seen all week.
sentences.cn: 其中一个说这是她这周看到最好的主意。

multiple:1.en: Outside the new branch site, the Manager had set up *multiple* small signs pointing to our main store, each one slightly different — some with arrows, one with a map, one with just the words 'we are open.' Tang counted them and said there were seven. The Manager looked pleased. A woman stopped and read every single one.
multiple:1.cnHint: 店长在新店址外摆了____指引牌，一共七块，各不相同。
multiple:1.hook: The woman pulled out a pen and circled something on the sign with the map.
multiple:1.line: 'I put up *multiple* signs so nobody gets lost on opening day.'

sentences.en: Outside the new branch site, the Manager had set up *multiple* small signs pointing to our main store, each one slightly different — some with arrows, one with a map, one with just the words 'we are open.'
Tang counted them and said there were seven.
sentences.cn: 阿糖数了一下，说一共有七个。

sentences.en: The Manager looked pleased.
sentences.cn: 店长看起来很高兴。

sentences.en: A woman stopped and read every single one.
sentences.cn: 一个女人停下来，一个一个地读了所有的标牌。

path:1.en: There was a narrow *path* between our store and the wall next door, just wide enough for one person. The Manager said the new branch would have no such lane — open space only. A small cat appeared from the path every night at two and sat by the door. I had started leaving a saucer of water out for it.
path:1.cnHint: 我们店旁有条窄____，每晚两点都有一只小猫从那里出现。
path:1.hook: Tonight the saucer was empty, but the cat had not come.
path:1.line: 'That *path* is too dark — we need a light there before winter.'

sentences.en: There was a narrow *path* between our store and the wall next door, just wide enough for one person.
The Manager said the new branch would have no such lane — open space only.
sentences.cn: 店长说新店那边不会有这样的小巷——全是开放空间。

sentences.en: A small cat appeared from the path every night at two and sat by the door.
sentences.cn: 每晚两点左右，一只小猫从小巷里出现，坐在门边。

sentences.en: I had started leaving a saucer of water out for it.
sentences.cn: 我开始每晚给它留一碟水。

safe:1.en: The Manager arrived before dawn carrying a small metal box. 'Follow me,' he said, leading me to the back room. He knelt beside a dusty shelf, moved a stack of old receipts, and revealed a heavy *safe* built into the wall. He pressed a code I was not allowed to see. Whatever was inside, he checked it every single night.
safe:1.cnHint: 店长每天深夜都会去后室打开藏在货架后面的____，查看里面的东西。
safe:1.hook: He never told me what the code was — or what was inside.
safe:1.line: 'Every night I check the *safe* before I go home.'

sentences.en: The Manager arrived before dawn carrying a small metal box.
sentences.cn: 店长天亮前到了，手里拿着一个小金属盒。

sentences.en: 'Follow me,' he said, leading me to the back room.
sentences.cn: "跟我来，"他说，领我走向后屋。

sentences.en: He knelt beside a dusty shelf, moved a stack of old receipts, and revealed a heavy *safe* built into the wall.
He pressed a code I was not allowed to see.
sentences.cn: 他按了一个我不被允许看的密码。

sentences.en: Whatever was inside, he checked it every single night.
sentences.cn: 无论里面是什么，他每晚都要检查一遍。

speed:1.en: Just past two in the morning, a bicycle appeared outside the glass door. The rider jumped off before it even stopped. He grabbed a rice ball, tossed coins onto the counter without counting them, and was back on his bike in under thirty seconds. I had never seen such *speed* in a person buying a snack. He left before I could even say thank you.
speed:1.cnHint: 一个骑自行车的人以惊人的____冲进店里买了饭团，转眼就消失了。
speed:1.hook: The coins added up to exactly the right amount — every time.
speed:1.line: 'You have to admire his *speed* — thirty seconds, every night.'

sentences.en: Just past two in the morning, a bicycle appeared outside the glass door.
sentences.cn: 过了凌晨两点，一辆自行车出现在玻璃门外。

sentences.en: The rider jumped off before it even stopped.
sentences.cn: 骑手还没停稳就跳了下来。

sentences.en: He grabbed a rice ball, tossed coins onto the counter without counting them, and was back on his bike in under thirty seconds.
sentences.cn: 他抓起一个饭团，往柜台上扔了几枚硬币，甚至没数，三十秒不到就回到了自行车上。

sentences.en: I had never seen such *speed* in a person buying a snack.
He left before I could even say thank you.
sentences.cn: 他在我连谢谢都没说出来就离开了。

burden:1.en: Tang came in at the end of a double shift, shoulders low, feet dragging. She set a bag of unsold sandwiches on the counter and sighed. 'Taking these home again,' she said. The Manager always asked her to carry back whatever did not sell — a small but daily *burden* she never complained about out loud. Still, her eyes said everything.
burden:1.cnHint: 唐把没卖完的三明治带回家，这是她每天默默承受的一种____。
burden:1.hook: One night the bag was twice as heavy, and she said nothing at all.
burden:1.line: 'Carrying leftover stock home every day is a real *burden*.'

sentences.en: Tang came in at the end of a double shift, shoulders low, feet dragging.
sentences.cn: 阿糖做完双班后进来，肩膀耷拉着，脚步拖沓。

sentences.en: She set a bag of unsold sandwiches on the counter and sighed.
sentences.cn: 她把一袋没卖出去的三明治放在柜台上，叹了口气。

sentences.en: 'Taking these home again,' she said.
sentences.cn: 她说，又要拿回家了。

sentences.en: The Manager always asked her to carry back whatever did not sell — a small but daily *burden* she never complained about out loud.
Still, her eyes said everything.
sentences.cn: 不过，她的眼神什么都说明了。

former:1.en: Two coffee cups sat side by side on the counter — one black, one with milk. Lin pointed at them and smiled. 'The *former* is mine,' he said, picking up the black one. I had mixed them up twice already this week. He never got annoyed, just corrected me gently each time. I wondered why he always ordered both cups at once.
former:1.cnHint: 林指着两杯咖啡，说____是他的那杯，我总是弄混它们。
former:1.hook: The second cup was always left untouched until a woman arrived.
former:1.line: 'The *former* one is mine — I always drink mine black.'

sentences.en: Two coffee cups sat side by side on the counter — one black, one with milk.
sentences.cn: 柜台上并排放着两个咖啡杯——一个黑的，一个加奶的。

sentences.en: Lin pointed at them and smiled.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林指了指它们，笑了。

sentences.en: 'The *former* is mine,' he said, picking up the black one.
I had mixed them up twice already this week.
sentences.cn: 我这周已经混过两次了。

sentences.en: He never got annoyed, just corrected me gently each time.
sentences.cn: 他从来不烦躁，每次都温和地纠正我。

sentences.en: I wondered why he always ordered both cups at once.
sentences.cn: 我想知道他为什么总是一次点两杯。

oppose:1.en: The Manager wanted to rearrange the snack shelves to put cheap items at eye level. Lin, from the store across the street, happened to be inside buying water. He heard the plan and shook his head. 'I tried that last year,' he said. 'Customers *oppose* it every time — they feel cheated.' The Manager looked at him, then at me, then said nothing.
oppose:1.cnHint: 林听说店长要重新摆放货架，便说顾客每次都会____这种做法。
oppose:1.hook: The Manager changed the shelves anyway — and sales dropped that week.
oppose:1.line: 'Customers will *oppose* any change that feels unfair to them.'

sentences.en: The Manager wanted to rearrange the snack shelves to put cheap items at eye level.
sentences.cn: 店长想重新摆放零食架，把便宜的东西放在眼睛平视的位置。

sentences.en: Lin, from the store across the street, happened to be inside buying water.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林碰巧在里面买水。

sentences.en: He heard the plan and shook his head.
sentences.cn: 他听到了这个计划，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'I tried that last year,' he said.
sentences.cn: "我去年试过，"他说。

sentences.en: 'Customers *oppose* it every time — they feel cheated.'
The Manager looked at him, then at me, then said nothing.
sentences.cn: 店长看了看他，又看了看我，什么也没说。

unable:1.en: A woman knocked on the glass at three in the morning, pointing at the top shelf. I climbed the small step stool and stretched as far as I could, but I was *unable* to reach the last box of crackers pushed to the very back. She watched patiently, arms folded. I tried twice. The third time, Tang walked in and reached it in one easy move.
unable:1.cnHint: 一位顾客想要最高架子最里面的饼干，而我____够到它。
unable:1.hook: The woman smiled at Tang in a way that felt like they already knew each other.
unable:1.line: 'I was completely *unable* to reach it without Tang's help.'

sentences.en: A woman knocked on the glass at three in the morning, pointing at the top shelf.
sentences.cn: 一个女人在凌晨三点敲了敲玻璃，指着最上面的架子。

sentences.en: I climbed the small step stool and stretched as far as I could, but I was *unable* to reach the last box of crackers pushed to the very back.
She watched patiently, arms folded.
sentences.cn: 她耐心地看着，胳膊交叉放在胸前。

sentences.en: I tried twice.
sentences.cn: 我试了两次。

sentences.en: The third time, Tang walked in and reached it in one easy move.
sentences.cn: 第三次，阿糖走进来，轻轻松松就够到了。

unusual:1.en: At four in the morning a man walked in wearing a full suit and carrying a small watering can. He bought a bottle of water, carefully poured half of it into the can, then watered the potted plant by our door. He nodded at me politely and left. It was the most *unusual* thing I had seen all week — and the plant did look healthier after that.
unusual:1.cnHint: 一个穿西装的男人在凌晨四点进来，做了一件十分____的事。
unusual:1.hook: He came back the next night with a different plant under his arm.
unusual:1.line: 'That is *unusual* — most people do not bring a watering can here.'

sentences.en: At four in the morning a man walked in wearing a full suit and carrying a small watering can.
sentences.cn: 凌晨四点，一个穿着正装、拿着一个小喷壶的男人走了进来。

sentences.en: He bought a bottle of water, carefully poured half of it into the can, then watered the potted plant by our door.
sentences.cn: 他买了一瓶水，小心地倒了一半进喷壶，然后给我们门边的盆栽浇水。

sentences.en: He nodded at me politely and left.
sentences.cn: 他礼貌地朝我点了点头，离开了。

sentences.en: It was the most *unusual* thing I had seen all week — and the plant did look healthier after that.

apart:1.en: Lin's store and ours stood just a few metres *apart*, facing each other across the narrow street. Most nights we watched each other through our glass windows like two fish in different bowls. Tang said Lin once worked here before the Manager and he had a falling-out. Whether that story was true, I could not say. But Lin always bought his late-night snacks from us.
apart:1.cnHint: 林的店和我们的店只隔几米，而他过去和我们店的关系远不止____这么简单。
apart:1.hook: One night Lin stood at his door for a long time, just looking over.
apart:1.line: 'Our two stores are only a few steps *apart*, but it feels like miles.'

sentences.en: Lin's store and ours stood just a few metres *apart*, facing each other across the narrow street.
Most nights we watched each other through our glass windows like two fish in different bowls.
sentences.cn: 大多数夜晚，我们隔着狭窄的街道透过玻璃窗互相看着，就像两条在不同鱼缸里的鱼。

sentences.en: Tang said Lin once worked here before the Manager and he had a falling-out.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说隔壁咖啡店的林以前在这里工作过，后来和店长闹翻了。

sentences.en: Whether that story was true, I could not say.
sentences.cn: 不过这个故事是不是真的，我说不准。

sentences.en: But Lin always bought his late-night snacks from us.
sentences.cn: 但隔壁咖啡店的林总是从我们这里买夜宵。

character:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new store site, studying the old building's front. 'This place has real *character*,' he said, tracing the worn bricks with one finger. I watched him smile at a crooked window frame the way most people only smile at something they already love.
character:1.cnHint: 店长站在新店选址前，觉得这栋旧楼很有____。
character:1.hook: But someone had left a note on the door that morning.
character:1.line: 'This building has *character* — that is exactly what we need.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new store site, studying the old building's front.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新店的地址外，研究着那栋旧楼的正面。

sentences.en: 'This place has real *character*,' he said, tracing the worn bricks with one finger.
I watched him smile at a crooked window frame the way most people only smile at something they already love.
sentences.cn: 我看着他用一种大多数人只会对已经爱上的东西才会有的方式，对着一扇歪斜的窗框微笑。

clean:1.en: Before the new branch could open, we had to make the old corner shop spotless. I swept the pavement outside while Tang scrubbed the window glass. By noon, the whole front was *clean* and bright, and passing strangers slowed down to look, as if the building had just woken up.
clean:1.cnHint: 开新店前，我们把店面打扫得____，路人忍不住驻足观看。
clean:1.hook: One stranger stopped a little too long.
clean:1.line: 'Finally *clean* — now it actually looks like a real store.'

sentences.en: Before the new branch could open, we had to make the old corner shop spotless.
sentences.cn: 新店开业前，我们得把这家老店铺打扫得干干净净。

sentences.en: I swept the pavement outside while Tang scrubbed the window glass.
sentences.cn: 我在外面扫人行道，阿糖擦着窗玻璃。

sentences.en: By noon, the whole front was *clean* and bright, and passing strangers slowed down to look, as if the building had just woken up.

convey:1.en: The Manager taped a small sign to the new store's front door. He rewrote it three times, unhappy with the words. 'I want to *convey* that everyone is welcome, day or night,' he told me. Tang read the final version and nodded slowly, which, from Tang, meant a lot.
convey:1.cnHint: 店长想用门口的告示____出"随时欢迎"的感觉，反复修改了好几遍。
convey:1.hook: A figure across the street had been reading the sign for ten minutes.
convey:1.line: 'I need to *convey* the right feeling, or the sign is useless.'

sentences.en: The Manager taped a small sign to the new store's front door.
sentences.cn: 店长在新店门口贴了一张小招牌。

sentences.en: He rewrote it three times, unhappy with the words.
sentences.cn: 他改了三遍，还是不满意字里行间的意思。

sentences.en: 'I want to *convey* that everyone is welcome, day or night,' he told me.
Tang read the final version and nodded slowly, which, from Tang, meant a lot.
sentences.cn: 阿糖读完最后的版本慢慢点了点头，这对阿糖来说意义重大。

distraction:1.en: We were painting the outside wall of the new branch when a street performer set up just across the road. Music drifted over, and my brush strokes went crooked. Tang clicked their tongue. 'No *distraction* until the wall is done,' they said firmly, then immediately turned to watch the performer too.
distraction:1.cnHint: 粉刷新店外墙时，对面街头艺人成了最大的____，连唐自己也忍不住回头看。
distraction:1.hook: The performer glanced at our store and smiled at something specific.
distraction:1.line: 'No *distraction* — we finish the wall first, then we can watch.'

sentences.en: We were painting the outside wall of the new branch when a street performer set up just across the road.
sentences.cn: 我们在新店外墙刷漆的时候，一个街头艺人在对面支起了舞台。

sentences.en: Music drifted over, and my brush strokes went crooked.
sentences.cn: 音乐飘过来，我的笔触歪了。

sentences.en: Tang clicked their tongue.
sentences.cn: 阿糖咂了咂舌。

sentences.en: 'No *distraction* until the wall is done,' they said firmly, then immediately turned to watch the performer too.

fight:1.en: Lin showed up outside the new store site just as we were hanging the sign. I expected sharp words, but Lin only looked up at the shopfront in silence. 'You still have *fight* in you,' Lin said to the Manager at last, almost gently. The Manager said nothing, which told me everything.
fight:1.cnHint: 林出现在新店门口，出乎意料地说店长还有____。
fight:1.hook: Then Lin pulled an envelope from their coat pocket.
fight:1.line: 'I will say this — you still have *fight* in you.'

sentences.en: Lin showed up outside the new store site just as we were hanging the sign.
sentences.cn: 我们正挂着招牌的时候，林出现在新店址的外面。

sentences.en: I expected sharp words, but Lin only looked up at the shopfront in silence.
sentences.cn: 我以为会听到尖锐的话语，但林只是沉默地抬头看着店面。

sentences.en: 'You still have *fight* in you,' Lin said to the Manager at last, almost gently.
The Manager said nothing, which told me everything.
sentences.cn: 店长什么都没说，这本身就说明了一切。

finish:1.en: The outside of the new branch looked almost ready. Almost. One corner of the sign hung lower than the other, and a strip of trim paint was still wet. 'The *finish* has to be perfect,' the Manager said quietly, more to himself than to us. Tang and I exchanged a tired look.
finish:1.cnHint: 新店外观接近完工，但店长坚持____要做到完美。
finish:1.hook: At that moment, a cat walked straight through the wet paint.
finish:1.line: 'The *finish* on this sign has to be perfect — redo it.'

sentences.en: The outside of the new branch looked almost ready.
sentences.cn: 新店的外观看起来差不多准备好了。

sentences.en: Almost.
sentences.cn: 差不多。

sentences.en: One corner of the sign hung lower than the other, and a strip of trim paint was still wet.
sentences.cn: 招牌的一个角低了一点，一道油漆边还没干。

sentences.en: 'The *finish* has to be perfect,' the Manager said quietly, more to himself than to us.
Tang and I exchanged a tired look.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我交换了一个疲倦的眼神。

frequently:1.en: I noticed the same elderly woman walk past the new store site *frequently* — once in the morning, once around lunch, once at dusk. She never stopped, just glanced at our progress and moved on. The Manager noticed her too. 'She used to run a shop here,' he said one evening, quietly.
frequently:1.cnHint: 一位老太太____经过新店工地，店长悄悄说出了她的来历。
frequently:1.hook: The next morning, she finally stopped walking.
frequently:1.line: 'She passes by so *frequently* — I think she misses this corner.'

sentences.en: I noticed the same elderly woman walk past the new store site *frequently* — once in the morning, once around lunch, once at dusk.
She never stopped, just glanced at our progress and moved on.
sentences.cn: 她从没停留，只是瞥一眼我们的进度就走开了。

sentences.en: The Manager noticed her too.
sentences.cn: 店长也注意到了她。

sentences.en: 'She used to run a shop here,' he said one evening, quietly.
sentences.cn: "她以前在这儿开过店，"有天晚上他静静地说。

invest:1.en: 'We are not just *investing* money,' the Manager told me as we stood outside the half-finished new branch one night. He gestured at the lit windows of the homes above the street. 'We are investing in this corner, these neighbours.' I looked up at the warm lights and, for the first time, felt proud.
invest:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门口告诉我，我们____的不只是钱，还有这个街角。
invest:1.hook: One of those lit windows quietly went dark.
invest:1.line: 'We are *investing* in this street, not just in a building.'

sentences.en: 'We are not just *investing* money,' the Manager told me as we stood outside the half-finished new branch one night.
He gestured at the lit windows of the homes above the street.
sentences.cn: 他指了指街上那些亮着窗灯的家。

sentences.en: 'We are investing in this corner, these neighbours.'
sentences.cn: 我们投资的不仅是钱。

sentences.en: I looked up at the warm lights and, for the first time, felt proud.
sentences.cn: 我们投资的是这个街角，还有这些邻居。

moment:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, staring at the empty shop front across the street. He had looked at that spot every night for a month. 'This is the *moment*,' he said quietly, almost to himself. A sign in the window read: FOR RENT. His eyes did not blink.
moment:1.cnHint: 店长盯着街对面的空铺子，觉得____终于来了。
moment:1.hook: He pulled out his phone and dialled before I could ask why.
moment:1.line: 'This is the *moment* we have been waiting for, trust me.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, staring at the empty shop front across the street.
sentences.cn: 店长站在人行道上，盯着对街那家空荡荡的店铺。

sentences.en: He had looked at that spot every night for a month.
sentences.cn: 一个月来他每晚都看那个地方。

sentences.en: 'This is the *moment*,' he said quietly, almost to himself.
A sign in the window read: FOR RENT.
sentences.cn: 窗口上写着：出租。

sentences.en: His eyes did not blink.
sentences.cn: 他的眼睛一眨不眨。

nice:1.en: Lin showed the Manager a hand-drawn floor plan on the pavement outside. Every measurement was exact, every shelf position thought out. 'Your numbers are very *nice*,' the Manager said, tracing a line with his finger. Lin smiled but said nothing, folding the paper with slow, careful hands.
nice:1.cnHint: 林把设计图摊在路边给店长看，店长夸它____。
nice:1.hook: I noticed Lin had drawn a second floor plan tucked behind the first.
nice:1.line: 'The spacing has to be *nice* — one centimetre off and the shelves will not fit.'

sentences.en: Lin showed the Manager a hand-drawn floor plan on the pavement outside.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在人行道上给店长看一张手绘的平面图。

sentences.en: Every measurement was exact, every shelf position thought out.
sentences.cn: 每一个尺寸都精确无误，每一个架子的位置都经过深思熟虑。

sentences.en: 'Your numbers are very *nice*,' the Manager said, tracing a line with his finger.
Lin smiled but said nothing, folding the paper with slow, careful hands.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林笑了笑没说话，用缓慢而仔细的动作折起纸张。

peer:1.en: An old woman stopped on the pavement and pressed her face close to the dark glass of the empty shop. She began to *peer* through the window, shading her eyes with both hands. 'Someone is looking at this place,' I told the Manager. He turned slowly and said nothing for a long time.
peer:1.cnHint: 一位老太太在空铺子门口____，想看清里面的样子。
peer:1.hook: She knocked on the glass twice before walking away into the dark.
peer:1.line: 'Why do you *peer* like that — can you not see the light is off?'

sentences.en: An old woman stopped on the pavement and pressed her face close to the dark glass of the empty shop.
sentences.cn: 一位老阿姨在人行道上停下，把脸贴近那家空店铺的黑玻璃窗。

sentences.en: She began to *peer* through the window, shading her eyes with both hands.
'Someone is looking at this place,' I told the Manager.
sentences.cn: "有人在看这个地方，"我告诉店长。

sentences.en: He turned slowly and said nothing for a long time.
sentences.cn: 他慢慢转身，沉默了很久。

pretty:1.en: Tang arranged a small display of key-rings and hair clips outside on a folding table to draw passing shoppers toward the new location. A girl stopped and picked up a shiny clip. 'Every *pretty* sells faster outdoors,' Tang told me, grinning. The Manager watched from a distance and nodded slowly.
pretty:1.cnHint: 唐把小饰品摆在路边桌上，说____在户外卖得更快。
pretty:1.hook: The girl set the clip down, picked up something else, and went pale.
pretty:1.line: 'Put the *pretties* near the front — people always stop for them first.'

sentences.en: Tang arranged a small display of key-rings and hair clips outside on a folding table to draw passing shoppers toward the new location.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在外面的折叠桌上摆了一些钥匙圈和发夹来吸引行人走进新店。

sentences.en: A girl stopped and picked up a shiny clip.
sentences.cn: 一个小女孩停下来，拿起了一个闪闪发光的发夹。

sentences.en: 'Every *pretty* sells faster outdoors,' Tang told me, grinning.
The Manager watched from a distance and nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 店长在远处看着，慢慢点了点头。

recommendation:1.en: A delivery driver parked his bike outside and handed the Manager a folded note. 'From the landlord next block,' the driver said. The Manager read it twice. It turned out to be a *recommendation* for a local builder who had fitted out three other shops on the street. The Manager folded it very carefully.
recommendation:1.cnHint: 快递员送来一封信，里面是关于装修师傅的____。
recommendation:1.hook: The builder's name at the bottom was the same as the old sign above our store.
recommendation:1.line: 'This *recommendation* comes from three shop owners — that is hard to ignore.'

sentences.en: A delivery driver parked his bike outside and handed the Manager a folded note.
sentences.cn: 一位送货员骑摩托车停在外面，递给店长一张折起来的纸条。

sentences.en: 'From the landlord next block,' the driver said.
sentences.cn: "隔壁街区房东的，"送货员说。

sentences.en: The Manager read it twice.
sentences.cn: 店长读了两遍。

sentences.en: It turned out to be a *recommendation* for a local builder who had fitted out three other shops on the street.
The Manager folded it very carefully.
sentences.cn: 店长很小心地折好了纸条。

strange:1.en: I stepped outside to take the rubbish out and noticed a man standing perfectly still under the lamp across the road, staring at our store. Nothing about him looked familiar. It felt *strange* — the street was empty in both directions, yet he stood there as if waiting for a door to open.
strange:1.cnHint: 我出门倒垃圾，看见路灯下有个____的身影一动不动地盯着店里。
strange:1.hook: When I looked again thirty seconds later, he was gone.
strange:1.line: 'Does it not feel *strange* to you that someone stands there every single night?'

sentences.en: I stepped outside to take the rubbish out and noticed a man standing perfectly still under the lamp across the road, staring at our store.
sentences.cn: 我走出门扔垃圾，注意到对面路灯下站着一个男人，纹丝不动地盯着我们的店。

sentences.en: Nothing about him looked familiar.
sentences.cn: 他长得没什么让人印象深刻的地方。

sentences.en: It felt *strange* — the street was empty in both directions, yet he stood there as if waiting for a door to open.

widespread:1.en: Lin spread a printed map on the bonnet of a parked car outside. Red circles marked six streets nearby. 'The demand is *widespread*,' Lin said, tapping each circle. 'One store cannot cover all of this.' The Manager crossed his arms and studied the map. The red circles looked like small fires.
widespread:1.cnHint: 林展开地图，说附近的需求____，一家店根本顾不过来。
widespread:1.hook: The Manager circled one spot in pen and handed it back without a word.
widespread:1.line: 'The demand is *widespread* — look at how far people are walking just to reach us.'

sentences.en: Lin spread a printed map on the bonnet of a parked car outside.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在停在外面的车引擎盖上铺开了一张打印地图。

sentences.en: Red circles marked six streets nearby.
sentences.cn: 红圈圈出了附近的六条街。

sentences.en: 'The demand is *widespread*,' Lin said, tapping each circle.
'One store cannot cover all of this.'
sentences.cn: 一家店铺根本覆盖不了所有这些。

sentences.en: The Manager crossed his arms and studied the map.
sentences.cn: 店长交叉抱臂，研究着地图。

sentences.en: The red circles looked like small fires.
sentences.cn: 那些红圈看起来像小火焰。

wonderful:1.en: Standing outside at dawn, I watched the sky turn from grey to pale gold above the rooftops. Tang came out with two warm cans of milk tea and handed me one. 'Isn't it *wonderful*?' she said, nodding at the street slowly waking up around us. I did not know if she meant the sky or the new plan.
wonderful:1.cnHint: 唐递给我热奶茶，感慨眼前的一切____。
wonderful:1.hook: Then she said quietly, 'I hope the new store feels like this too.'
wonderful:1.line: 'It is *wonderful* what a single street corner can make you feel at five in the morning.'

sentences.en: Standing outside at dawn, I watched the sky turn from grey to pale gold above the rooftops.
sentences.cn: 天亮时我站在外面，看着天空从灰色变成淡金色，映照在屋顶上。

sentences.en: Tang came out with two warm cans of milk tea and handed me one.
sentences.cn: 阿糖拿出两罐热奶茶走了出来，递给我一罐。

sentences.en: 'Isn't it *wonderful*?' she said, nodding at the street slowly waking up around us.
I did not know if she meant the sky or the new plan.
sentences.cn: 我不确定她指的是天空还是新计划。

immediately:1.en: The Manager pointed at the empty shelf outside and said we needed to restock *immediately*. I grabbed a box of snacks and ran out. The street was cold and bright under the lamp. A passing woman stopped, watched me arrange the shelf, and smiled — she came back three minutes later with a friend.
immediately:1.cnHint: 店长叫我____把外面的货架补好，一位路过的女士看了看，转身离开了。
immediately:1.hook: She whispered something to her friend before they both walked inside.
immediately:1.line: 'We need to restock that shelf *immediately* — people can see it from the street.'

sentences.en: The Manager pointed at the empty shelf outside and said we needed to restock *immediately*.
I grabbed a box of snacks and ran out.
sentences.cn: 我抓起一盒零食冲了出去。

sentences.en: The street was cold and bright under the lamp.
sentences.cn: 街道在路灯下冷得发亮。

sentences.en: A passing woman stopped, watched me arrange the shelf, and smiled — she came back three minutes later with a friend.
sentences.cn: 一个经过的女人停了下来，看着我整理货架，然后笑了——三分钟后她带着一个朋友回来了。

afternoon:1.en: The slow *afternoon* shift belonged to Tang, but Tang was late again. I stood outside sweeping the step in the warm light, watching people drift past with shopping bags. A small boy pressed his face against the glass, leaving a perfect round mark. He looked at me with huge eyes, then ran after his mother.
afternoon:1.cnHint: 在一个懒洋洋的____，一个小男孩把脸贴在玻璃上，随后跑开了。
afternoon:1.hook: His mother stopped at the corner and looked back at the store for a long moment.
afternoon:1.line: 'The *afternoon* crowd is quiet — but watch out around four o'clock.'

sentences.en: The slow *afternoon* shift belonged to Tang, but Tang was late again.
I stood outside sweeping the step in the warm light, watching people drift past with shopping bags.
sentences.cn: 我站在外面，在温暖的灯光下扫着台阶，看着人们拎着购物袋飘过。

sentences.en: A small boy pressed his face against the glass, leaving a perfect round mark.
sentences.cn: 一个小男孩把脸贴在玻璃上，留下了一个完美的圆形印记。

sentences.en: He looked at me with huge eyes, then ran after his mother.
sentences.cn: 他用巨大的眼睛看着我，然后跑着追他妈妈去了。

expand:1.en: Lin from the store across the street crossed over and leaned on our wall. 'I hear the Manager wants to *expand*,' Lin said, nodding at the empty lot next door. I said nothing. Lin smiled, glanced at the lot once more, then walked back without another word.
expand:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林过来说，听说我们要____，然后没等回答就走了。
expand:1.hook: I noticed Lin pause at the lot and take a slow, careful look at its size.
expand:1.line: 'So you really plan to *expand* into that empty space next door?'

sentences.en: Lin from the store across the street crossed over and leaned on our wall.
sentences.cn: 对面咖啡店的林走过街道，靠在我们的墙上。

sentences.en: 'I hear the Manager wants to *expand*,' Lin said, nodding at the empty lot next door.
I said nothing.
sentences.cn: 我什么都没说。

sentences.en: Lin smiled, glanced at the lot once more, then walked back without another word.
sentences.cn: 林笑了笑，又看了一眼那块空地，然后不再说话地走了回去。

regardless:1.en: It had rained all morning, but the old man still came at his usual time, *regardless* of the wet street and his thin jacket. He bought his usual two items, counted coins into my palm, and left without hurrying. The rain had stopped by then, as if it too had decided to wait for him to finish.
regardless:1.cnHint: 尽管下着雨，那位老先生____准时来了，买完东西才慢慢离开。
regardless:1.hook: I realised I had never once seen him carry an umbrella.
regardless:1.line: 'I come every day *regardless* — a little rain never stopped me.'

sentences.en: It had rained all morning, but the old man still came at his usual time, *regardless* of the wet street and his thin jacket.
He bought his usual two items, counted coins into my palm, and left without hurrying.
sentences.cn: 他买了他常买的两样东西，把硬币数进我的手心，然后不紧不慢地离开了。

sentences.en: The rain had stopped by then, as if it too had decided to wait for him to finish.
sentences.cn: 雨在那时停了，仿佛它也决定要等他完成似的。

rid:1.en: A young woman dragged a heavy bag to the door and asked if she could leave it outside for a moment. She wanted to *rid* herself of it long enough to carry two cups of hot tea from the stall across the lane. I held the door. She came back, beaming, with one cup held out for me.
rid:1.cnHint: 一位年轻女士想先____手里的重袋子，去对面给我们买热茶。
rid:1.hook: She mentioned her grandmother's stall across the lane — the one that never seemed to close.
rid:1.line: 'I just need to *rid* myself of this bag for one minute — I promise I'll be back.'

sentences.en: A young woman dragged a heavy bag to the door and asked if she could leave it outside for a moment.
sentences.cn: 一个年轻女人拖着一个沉重的袋子来到门口，问能不能先把它放在外面一会儿。

sentences.en: She wanted to *rid* herself of it long enough to carry two cups of hot tea from the stall across the lane.
I held the door.
sentences.cn: 我扶着门。

sentences.en: She came back, beaming, with one cup held out for me.
sentences.cn: 她回来了，满脸笑容，手里拿着一杯热茶递给我。

dog:1.en: A large, fluffy *dog* sat outside the store at two in the morning, very calm, looking at the door. No owner. No collar. It did not bark. I put a small bowl of water near the step and went back inside. Every time I looked out, the dog was still there, watching patiently, as if waiting for someone who had gone in a very long time ago.
dog:1.cnHint: 凌晨两点，一只____独自坐在店门口，安静地盯着门，没有主人。
dog:1.hook: By sunrise the bowl was empty, and the dog was gone.
dog:1.line: 'That *dog* has been sitting outside every night this week — nobody knows whose it is.'

sentences.en: A large, fluffy *dog* sat outside the store at two in the morning, very calm, looking at the door.
No owner.
sentences.cn: 没有主人。

sentences.en: No collar.
sentences.cn: 没有项圈。

sentences.en: It did not bark.
sentences.cn: 它没有叫。

sentences.en: I put a small bowl of water near the step and went back inside.
sentences.cn: 我在台阶边放了一小碗水，然后走了回去。

sentences.en: Every time I looked out, the dog was still there, watching patiently, as if waiting for someone who had gone in a very long time ago.
sentences.cn: 每次我向外看，那条狗还在那里，耐心地看着，仿佛在等一个很久以前进去的人。

busy:1.en: The corner was *busy* even at midnight — people cutting through on their way home, a noodle cart rattling past, someone arguing on a phone. I stood by the open door, watching it all like a slow river. Tang said the Manager had chosen this corner on purpose. It was the kind of street that never really slept.
busy:1.cnHint: 这个街角到了午夜依然____，店长据说是特意选了这里开店。
busy:1.hook: Tang smiled at that and looked away, like there was more to the story.
busy:1.line: 'Stay *busy* and keep the door open — that's what brings people in.'

sentences.en: The corner was *busy* even at midnight — people cutting through on their way home, a noodle cart rattling past, someone arguing on a phone.
I stood by the open door, watching it all like a slow river.
sentences.cn: 我站在敞开的门边，看着这一切就像看一条缓慢流动的河。

sentences.en: Tang said the Manager had chosen this corner on purpose.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说店长是故意选了这个角落的。

sentences.en: It was the kind of street that never really slept.
sentences.cn: 这是那种永远不会真正睡着的街道。

male:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, counting heads. Most of the construction crew were *male*, but one woman in a yellow hard hat kept shouting orders louder than anyone else. I handed out cold water bottles and tried to remember all their names.
male:1.cnHint: 店长在新分店工地外清点人数，一位女工头的嗓门盖过了所有____工人。
male:1.hook: Then the woman in the hard hat turned and called my name.
male:1.line: Every *male* on this crew listens to me, and so will you.

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, counting heads.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新分店的地点外面，数着人头。

sentences.en: Most of the construction crew were *male*, but one woman in a yellow hard hat kept shouting orders louder than anyone else.
I handed out cold water bottles and tried to remember all their names.
sentences.cn: 我递出冷水瓶，试图记住他们所有人的名字。

fish:1.en: A street vendor had parked his cart right in front of the new branch door. The smell of grilled *fish* floated all the way to where I was sweeping the pavement. The Manager frowned, but the growing line of hungry customers told a different story.
fish:1.cnHint: 一位街头摊贩把车停在新分店门口，烤____的香味引来了长长的队伍。
fish:1.hook: The vendor smiled and slipped the Manager a small wrapped package.
fish:1.line: Try the *fish*. One bite and you will forgive me for parking here.

sentences.en: A street vendor had parked his cart right in front of the new branch door.
sentences.cn: 一个街头小贩把他的推车停在了新分店门口。

sentences.en: The smell of grilled *fish* floated all the way to where I was sweeping the pavement.
The Manager frowned, but the growing line of hungry customers told a different story.
sentences.cn: 店长皱了皱眉，但排队的饥饿顾客越来越多讲述了另一个故事。

fashion:1.en: Lin had dressed the new branch window in a very different *fashion* from our usual store. Colourful signs, tiny fairy lights, a little chalkboard menu outside. I stopped on the pavement and stared. It looked less like a convenience store and more like a café from a magazine.
fashion:1.cnHint: 林以一种与平时截然不同的____装饰了新分店的橱窗，让我驻足呆看。
fashion:1.hook: A crowd had already gathered, and Lin had not even opened the door yet.
fashion:1.line: I decorated it in my own *fashion*, so please do not touch anything.

sentences.en: Lin had dressed the new branch window in a very different *fashion* from our usual store.
Colourful signs, tiny fairy lights, a little chalkboard menu outside.
sentences.cn: 五颜六色的招牌、细小的仙女灯，还有外面一块小黑板菜单。

sentences.en: I stopped on the pavement and stared.
sentences.cn: 我在人行道上停住了，呆呆地盯着。

sentences.en: It looked less like a convenience store and more like a café from a magazine.
sentences.cn: 看起来不像便利店，倒像是杂志里的咖啡馆。

weather:1.en: The morning we were supposed to open the new branch, the *weather* turned mean. Rain hammered the street and puddles swallowed the welcome mat. Tang dragged out a big orange umbrella from the back room and stood outside waving at confused customers like a lighthouse.
weather:1.cnHint: 新分店开业那天，____突变，唐撑着橙色大伞站在门外当起了人形灯塔。
weather:1.hook: A black car slowed down beside Tang and did not drive away.
weather:1.line: Bad *weather* will not stop us. I can stand here all morning.

sentences.en: The morning we were supposed to open the new branch, the *weather* turned mean.
Rain hammered the street and puddles swallowed the welcome mat.
sentences.cn: 雨疯狂地敲打着街道，水洼吞没了欢迎垫。

sentences.en: Tang dragged out a big orange umbrella from the back room and stood outside waving at confused customers like a lighthouse.
sentences.cn: 阿糖从后房间拖出一把大橙伞，站在外面像灯塔一样向困惑的顾客挥手。

device:1.en: Tang arrived carrying a small electronic *device* that projected a arrow of blue light onto the pavement, pointing right at the new branch entrance. 'People follow arrows,' Tang said firmly. Within ten minutes a curious crowd had gathered to see what the light was pointing at.
device:1.cnHint: 唐带来一个能把蓝色箭头投影在地面的____，把路人引向新分店入口。
device:1.hook: One man followed the light arrow and walked straight into a lamppost.
device:1.line: This *device* cost me a week of wages. It had better work.

sentences.en: Tang arrived carrying a small electronic *device* that projected a arrow of blue light onto the pavement, pointing right at the new branch entrance.
'People follow arrows,' Tang said firmly.
sentences.cn: "人们会跟随箭头，"阿糖坚定地说。

sentences.en: Within ten minutes a curious crowd had gathered to see what the light was pointing at.
sentences.cn: 十分钟内，一群好奇的人聚集过来，想看这道光在指向什么。

farm:1.en: An old man stopped me on the street and said he used to own a *farm* right where our new branch now stood. He pulled out a faded photo: green fields, a wooden fence, two goats. I looked at the glass-and-steel front of the store and felt oddly guilty.
farm:1.cnHint: 一位老人告诉我，新分店所在的地方曾经是他的____，并拿出了泛黄的老照片。
farm:1.hook: He asked if he could come inside and sit for a while.
farm:1.line: My whole *farm* once stood on this very spot. Strange, is it not?

sentences.en: An old man stopped me on the street and said he used to own a *farm* right where our new branch now stood.
He pulled out a faded photo: green fields, a wooden fence, two goats.
sentences.cn: 他掏出一张褪色的照片：绿色的田地、木栅栏、两只山羊。

sentences.en: I looked at the glass-and-steel front of the store and felt oddly guilty.
sentences.cn: 我看着店铺的玻璃钢结构外墙，心里莫名地感到内疚。

drug:1.en: A nervous young man asked me quietly if we sold any *drug* for headaches. I pointed him to the small medicine shelf near the door. He bought two packs, paid, then hesitated. He looked like he had something else on his mind entirely.
drug:1.cnHint: 一个紧张的年轻男子轻声问我是否有治头痛的____，买完之后却迟迟不肯离开。
drug:1.hook: He finally whispered, 'Is the Manager here tonight?'
drug:1.line: I just need a *drug* for headaches. Nothing serious, I promise.

sentences.en: A nervous young man asked me quietly if we sold any *drug* for headaches.
I pointed him to the small medicine shelf near the door.
sentences.cn: 我指向门边的小医药架。

sentences.en: He bought two packs, paid, then hesitated.
sentences.cn: 他买了两盒，付了钱，然后停顿了。

sentences.en: He looked like he had something else on his mind entirely.
sentences.cn: 他的样子像是心里还装着完全不同的事。

heat:1.en: By noon the *heat* rising from the pavement outside the new branch was fierce. I had been restocking the outdoor fridge for an hour and my shirt was soaked through. Lin walked past holding an iced drink, did not offer me one, and disappeared inside. Typical.
heat:1.cnHint: 正午地面散发出强烈的____，我在户外忙活了一个小时，林却端着冰饮扬长而去。
heat:1.hook: When I finally went inside, the indoor fridge was completely empty.
heat:1.line: The *heat* out there is no joke. Someone should bring you water.

sentences.en: By noon the *heat* rising from the pavement outside the new branch was fierce.
I had been restocking the outdoor fridge for an hour and my shirt was soaked through.
sentences.cn: 我已经重新整理户外冰箱一个小时了，衣服都被汗水浸透了。

sentences.en: Lin walked past holding an iced drink, did not offer me one, and disappeared inside.
sentences.cn: 林拿着一杯冰饮走过，没有递给我一杯，然后消失在店里。

sentences.en: Typical.
sentences.cn: 真典型。

intelligence:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, studying the street with calm, sharp eyes. 'Opening here takes *intelligence*,' he said, watching how people moved, where they paused, which corner caught the most foot traffic. He had chosen this spot himself, and he looked quietly proud of it.
intelligence:1.cnHint: 店长站在新店选址外，用敏锐的眼光观察街道，觉得选址需要____。
intelligence:1.hook: But someone else had been watching this corner far longer.
intelligence:1.line: 'Opening a second store takes real *intelligence*, not just money.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, studying the street with calm, sharp eyes.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新店外，用冷静而锐利的眼睛研究这条街。

sentences.en: 'Opening here takes *intelligence*,' he said, watching how people moved, where they paused, which corner caught the most foot traffic.
He had chosen this spot himself, and he looked quietly proud of it.
sentences.cn: 他自己选择了这个地点，看起来对此感到暗暗骄傲。

uk:1.en: Tang was taping a small poster to the new store window when a tourist stopped and asked for directions. Tang tried hard, mixing words and gestures. The tourist smiled and pointed at his bag, which had a tiny flag on it. 'Ah,' Tang laughed, 'you are from the *UK*!'
uk:1.cnHint: 阿糖在贴海报时，一位来自____的游客停下来问路。
uk:1.hook: The tourist's next question left Tang completely speechless.
uk:1.line: 'I came all the way from the *UK* just to find good street food.'

sentences.en: Tang was taping a small poster to the new store window when a tourist stopped and asked for directions.
sentences.cn: 阿糖正在给新店窗户贴一张小海报，这时一个游客停下来问路。

sentences.en: Tang tried hard, mixing words and gestures.
sentences.cn: 阿糖费力地混用词语和手势解释。

sentences.en: The tourist smiled and pointed at his bag, which had a tiny flag on it.
sentences.cn: 游客笑了，指了指他包上的一面小旗子。

sentences.en: 'Ah,' Tang laughed, 'you are from the *UK*!'

user:1.en: Outside the new branch, a delivery rider stared at his phone with a frown. 'The app says I am the first *user* to pick up here,' he told me, 'but the address just shows a car park.' He looked up slowly at our bright new sign, then back at his phone, then at me.
user:1.cnHint: 一位外卖骑手盯着手机，因为系统显示他是新店地址的第一个____，但地图显示那里是停车场。
user:1.hook: He pressed 'arrived' and rode away before I could say a word.
user:1.line: 'It says I am the only *user* who has ever ordered from this address.'

sentences.en: Outside the new branch, a delivery rider stared at his phone with a frown.
sentences.cn: 在新店外，一个送餐员皱着眉盯着他的手机。

sentences.en: 'The app says I am the first *user* to pick up here,' he told me, 'but the address just shows a car park.'
He looked up slowly at our bright new sign, then back at his phone, then at me.
sentences.cn: 他抬起头，看了看我们明亮的新招牌，又看了看手机，然后看向我。

park:1.en: The new branch faced a small *park*, where old men played chess under the trees each morning. I arrived early to unlock the door and found three of them already peering through the glass, hands behind their backs, breath fogging the window. They had clearly been waiting a while.
park:1.cnHint: 新店正对着一个____，每天早上老人们在那里下棋，今天他们早早就盯着新店的橱窗了。
park:1.hook: One of them pressed a handwritten note against the glass.
park:1.line: 'The *park* crowd will be your best customers, trust me.'

sentences.en: The new branch faced a small *park*, where old men played chess under the trees each morning.
I arrived early to unlock the door and found three of them already peering through the glass, hands behind their backs, breath fogging the window.
sentences.cn: 我早到开门，发现其中三个已经透过玻璃往里看，双手背在身后，呼吸在窗户上起了雾。

sentences.en: They had clearly been waiting a while.
sentences.cn: 他们显然已经等了一会儿。

reward:1.en: Lin arrived at the new branch holding a small paper bag. 'I walked thirty minutes to bring you warm dumplings,' she said, setting the bag on the counter with a grin. 'Consider it a *reward* for surviving your first week.' The smell was wonderful. I suddenly forgot how tired I was.
reward:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林步行三十分钟来到新店，给我带来了热腾腾的饺子，说这是对我____。
reward:1.hook: Then she pulled out a notepad and started quizzing me on branch procedures.
reward:1.line: 'Think of these dumplings as your *reward* for not quitting yet.'

sentences.en: Lin arrived at the new branch holding a small paper bag.
sentences.cn: 林拿着一个小纸袋来到新店。

sentences.en: 'I walked thirty minutes to bring you warm dumplings,' she said, setting the bag on the counter with a grin.
sentences.cn: "我走了三十分钟给你带来热汤饺，"她把纸袋放在柜台上，咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: 'Consider it a *reward* for surviving your first week.'
The smell was wonderful.
sentences.cn: 味道太香了。

sentences.en: I suddenly forgot how tired I was.
sentences.cn: 我突然忘记了有多累。

credit:1.en: A woman in a bright coat stopped me just outside the new branch door. She had collected loyalty stamps from our old store for two years and wanted to know if her *credit* would carry over. She held up a card so full of tiny stamps that it had gone soft at the edges.
credit:1.cnHint: 一位女士拿着盖满印章的积分卡，想知道她在老店积累的____能不能在新店使用。
credit:1.hook: The Manager had never mentioned anything about transferring old stamps.
credit:1.line: 'I have two years of *credit* on this card and I am not starting over.'

sentences.en: A woman in a bright coat stopped me just outside the new branch door.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着亮色外套的女人在新店门口拦住了我。

sentences.en: She had collected loyalty stamps from our old store for two years and wanted to know if her *credit* would carry over.
She held up a card so full of tiny stamps that it had gone soft at the edges.
sentences.cn: 她拿着一张充满小印章的卡，卡的边缘都被磨软了。

progress:1.en: Every afternoon that week, the Manager walked the length of the new block and noted how the fit-out work *progressed*. He kept a small notebook and ticked things off without a word. On Friday he stopped, looked at the nearly finished shopfront, and allowed himself one slow nod of satisfaction.
progress:1.cnHint: 那周每天下午，店长都会沿着街道巡视，默默记录新店装修____的情况。
progress:1.hook: On Saturday morning the notebook was gone from his desk.
progress:1.line: 'Things *progress* faster when nobody stops to celebrate too early.'

sentences.en: Every afternoon that week, the Manager walked the length of the new block and noted how the fit-out work *progressed*.
He kept a small notebook and ticked things off without a word.
sentences.cn: 他在笔记本上记着，什么话都不说就打上了勾。

sentences.en: On Friday he stopped, looked at the nearly finished shopfront, and allowed himself one slow nod of satisfaction.
sentences.cn: 周五，他停下脚步，看着几乎完工的店面，允许自己缓缓点了一下头，满意极了。

snack:1.en: Just before midnight on the new branch's first night, a small girl tugged her grandfather to our window. She pressed her nose to the glass and pointed at a row of rice crackers. 'One *snack*,' the old man told me gently, counting coins into my palm with great care, one by one.
snack:1.cnHint: 新店第一晚接近午夜，一位老爷爷带着小孙女来买____，老人一枚枚地数硬币付钱。
snack:1.hook: The girl left a tiny handprint on the clean glass, perfectly centred.
snack:1.line: 'Just one *snack*, please — she has been good all day.'

sentences.en: Just before midnight on the new branch's first night, a small girl tugged her grandfather to our window.
sentences.cn: 新店开业的第一晚，刚过午夜，一个小女孩拉着她爷爷来到我们的窗边。

sentences.en: She pressed her nose to the glass and pointed at a row of rice crackers.
sentences.cn: 她把鼻子贴在玻璃上，指着一排米饼。

sentences.en: 'One *snack*,' the old man told me gently, counting coins into my palm with great care, one by one.

retire:1.en: Just past midnight, the Manager stepped out the back door and stretched under the streetlamp. 'I used to *retire* at ten sharp,' he said, watching the empty road. 'Now ten o'clock is when the real rush starts.' He smiled at the irony, then noticed a shadow moving near the recycling bins.
retire:1.cnHint: 店长感慨自己以前很早就____，如今午夜才是忙碌的开始。
retire:1.hook: The shadow stopped moving — and seemed to be listening.
retire:1.line: 'I used to *retire* at ten, but the night shift changed everything.'

sentences.en: Just past midnight, the Manager stepped out the back door and stretched under the streetlamp.
sentences.cn: 午夜刚过，店长从后门走出来，在街灯下伸了个懒腰。

sentences.en: 'I used to *retire* at ten sharp,' he said, watching the empty road.
'Now ten o'clock is when the real rush starts.'
sentences.cn: 现在十点才是真正忙碌的开始。

sentences.en: He smiled at the irony, then noticed a shadow moving near the recycling bins.
sentences.cn: 他笑了笑，为这种讽刺，然后注意到回收桶边有个影子在动。

sea:1.en: The Manager unrolled a large map on the pavement outside, weighting the corners with bottles of tea. 'The new branch will go here,' he said, tapping a dot on the coast. Lin stared at the blue printed *sea* beside the dot and quietly wondered who would staff a store that close to the waves.
sea:1.cnHint: 店长在路边展开地图，新分店的位置就在印刷的____旁边。
sea:1.hook: Lin had never learned to swim.
sea:1.line: 'A store by the *sea* sounds nice — until the storms come.'

sentences.en: The Manager unrolled a large map on the pavement outside, weighting the corners with bottles of tea.
sentences.cn: 店长在门外的人行道上铺开了一张大地图，用茶瓶压住四个角。

sentences.en: 'The new branch will go here,' he said, tapping a dot on the coast.
sentences.cn: 他说，新店就要开在这里，边说边点了点地图上海岸边的一个点。

sentences.en: Lin stared at the blue printed *sea* beside the dot and quietly wondered who would staff a store that close to the waves.

town:1.en: Tang carried a stack of flyers to the corner and stopped. The flyers announced a new branch opening in a small *town* thirty kilometres away. A grandmother on a bicycle slowed down, took one flyer, read it carefully, and then asked Tang in a low voice whether the new store would sell the same sticky-rice pudding as this one.
town:1.cnHint: 阿糖在街角发传单，新分店要开在附近的小____里。
town:1.hook: The grandmother already knew the new store's address by heart.
town:1.line: 'The new *town* branch opens Friday — same pudding, I promise.'

sentences.en: Tang carried a stack of flyers to the corner and stopped.
sentences.cn: 阿糖拿着一叠传单来到街角停了下来。

sentences.en: The flyers announced a new branch opening in a small *town* thirty kilometres away.
A grandmother on a bicycle slowed down, took one flyer, read it carefully, and then asked Tang in a low voice whether the new store would sell the same sticky-rice pudding as this one.
sentences.cn: 一位骑自行车的奶奶放慢了速度，拿了一张传单，仔细读了读，然后用低低的嗓音问阿糖，新店会不会像这家一样卖黏米布丁。

gap:1.en: Lin was taping a poster to the lamppost when she noticed a *gap* between two boards on the old fence across the street. Through it she could see someone writing in a notebook at a folding table. The handwriting was neat and fast. She taped the last corner of the poster and told herself it was none of her business.
gap:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林贴海报时，透过旧围栏的____看到了神秘的人影。
gap:1.hook: The notebook had the store's logo on its cover.
gap:1.line: 'There is a *gap* in the fence — and someone is watching us.'

sentences.en: Lin was taping a poster to the lamppost when she noticed a *gap* between two boards on the old fence across the street.
Through it she could see someone writing in a notebook at a folding table.
sentences.cn: 透过缝隙，她看到有人在折叠桌前写笔记本。

sentences.en: The handwriting was neat and fast.
sentences.cn: 笔迹整洁而迅速。

sentences.en: She taped the last corner of the poster and told herself it was none of her business.
sentences.cn: 她贴好海报的最后一角，告诉自己这不关她的事。

generation:1.en: An elderly man paused in front of the store's outdoor bulletin board, reading the announcement of the new branch. 'My father bought rice from a shop on that same street,' he said to no one in particular. 'Every *generation* finds the same corner useful.' He pressed his palm flat against the notice, as if making sure it was real.
generation:1.cnHint: 一位老人读着公告，感慨每一____的人都离不开街角的小店。
generation:1.hook: His hand was shaking very slightly.
generation:1.line: 'Every *generation* in my family has lived near a shop like this.'

sentences.en: An elderly man paused in front of the store's outdoor bulletin board, reading the announcement of the new branch.
sentences.cn: 一位老人停在店外的公告板前，读着新店开业的通知。

sentences.en: 'My father bought rice from a shop on that same street,' he said to no one in particular.
sentences.cn: 他自言自语地说，他父亲曾在那条街同样的地方买过米。

sentences.en: 'Every *generation* finds the same corner useful.'
He pressed his palm flat against the notice, as if making sure it was real.
sentences.cn: 他用手掌按住了这张通知，好像要确保它是真的。

guide:1.en: Tang had agreed to *guide* a reporter from the local paper to the site of the planned new branch. They set off down the predawn street, past shuttered stalls and sleeping cats. Tang kept three steps ahead, explaining distances and bus routes. The reporter wrote nothing down, which Tang found oddly worrying.
guide:1.cnHint: 阿糖答应____一位记者去新分店的选址地点参观。
guide:1.hook: The reporter's pen had been recording the whole time.
guide:1.line: 'I will *guide* you to the site — it is only ten minutes from here.'

sentences.en: Tang had agreed to *guide* a reporter from the local paper to the site of the planned new branch.
They set off down the predawn street, past shuttered stalls and sleeping cats.
sentences.cn: 他们沿着晨曦前的街道出发了，经过紧闭的摊位和睡着的猫。

sentences.en: Tang kept three steps ahead, explaining distances and bus routes.
sentences.cn: 阿糖走在前面三步，讲解距离和公交路线。

sentences.en: The reporter wrote nothing down, which Tang found oddly worrying.
sentences.cn: 记者一个字都没记下来，这让阿糖感到莫名的担忧。

household:1.en: The Manager pinned a hand-drawn floor plan to the outdoor notice board. A woman with a shopping bag stopped to look at it. 'Your store has become a *household* name on this street,' she said warmly. 'Will the new one be just as small and friendly?' The Manager opened his mouth to answer, then paused longer than felt comfortable.
household:1.cnHint: 一位街坊称赞小店已经是这条街的____名字，询问新店是否一样亲切。
household:1.hook: The Manager's pause lasted almost ten full seconds.
household:1.line: 'This shop is a *household* name here — the new one must earn that.'

sentences.en: The Manager pinned a hand-drawn floor plan to the outdoor notice board.
sentences.cn: 店长把一份手绘的平面图钉在了外面的公告板上。

sentences.en: A woman with a shopping bag stopped to look at it.
sentences.cn: 一位拎着购物袋的女人停下来看了看。

sentences.en: 'Your store has become a *household* name on this street,' she said warmly.
'Will the new one be just as small and friendly?'
sentences.cn: 新店会跟这家一样小巧友善吗？

sentences.en: The Manager opened his mouth to answer, then paused longer than felt comfortable.
sentences.cn: 店长张开嘴想回答，然后停顿得比舒服的时间更长。

luxury:1.en: Lin sat on an upturned crate outside, eating a warm bun before her shift. She watched a polished car idle at the traffic light, music drifting from its windows. 'Clean socks every day is my *luxury*,' she told Tang, who had just arrived. Tang looked at the car, then at Lin's worn shoes, and said nothing at all.
luxury:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林看着豪华轿车感慨，对她来说最大的____其实很简单。
luxury:1.hook: Tang had noticed something taped under that car's bumper.
luxury:1.line: 'A warm bun before sunrise — that is *luxury* enough for me.'

sentences.en: Lin sat on an upturned crate outside, eating a warm bun before her shift.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林坐在翻过来的木箱上，在值班前吃着热包子。

sentences.en: She watched a polished car idle at the traffic light, music drifting from its windows.
sentences.cn: 她看着一辆擦得锃亮的车在红绿灯前停下，音乐从车窗飘出来。

sentences.en: 'Clean socks every day is my *luxury*,' she told Tang, who had just arrived.
Tang looked at the car, then at Lin's worn shoes, and said nothing at all.
sentences.cn: 一条隔壁咖啡店的林说，每天穿上干净袜子就是我的奢侈，这时阿糖刚好来了。

announce:1.en: The Manager called me outside just before dawn. He pointed to a big paper sign taped to the lamp post across the street. 'I want to *announce* something,' he said, his breath making little clouds in the cold air. 'We are opening a second store next month, two blocks away.' He looked very pleased with himself.
announce:1.cnHint: 店长在店外向我____了一件大事：下个月要开新分店了。
announce:1.hook: But someone had already torn the bottom half of the sign away.
announce:1.line: 'I want to *announce* something important to the whole street.'

sentences.en: The Manager called me outside just before dawn.
sentences.cn: 店长在黎明前叫我出来。

sentences.en: He pointed to a big paper sign taped to the lamp post across the street.
sentences.cn: 他指着对街路灯杆上贴的一张大纸条。

sentences.en: 'I want to *announce* something,' he said, his breath making little clouds in the cold air.
'We are opening a second store next month, two blocks away.'
sentences.cn: 我们下个月要在隔两个街区的地方开第二家店。

sentences.en: He looked very pleased with himself.
sentences.cn: 他看起来很为自己感到骄傲。

appropriate:1.en: Tang and I stood outside arranging the new shelf display near the front window. A delivery driver stopped to ask if the pavement space we were using was ours. Tang smiled and said it was *appropriate* for a store to use a small area right outside its own door. The driver shrugged and walked on.
appropriate:1.cnHint: 阿糖认为店门口占用一小块路面展示商品是____的。
appropriate:1.hook: The driver came back ten minutes later, this time with a notebook.
appropriate:1.line: 'It is *appropriate* for the store to use this small space here.'

sentences.en: Tang and I stood outside arranging the new shelf display near the front window.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我站在外面，整理靠近前窗的新货架展示。

sentences.en: A delivery driver stopped to ask if the pavement space we were using was ours.
sentences.cn: 一位快递员停下来问我们用的人行道空间是不是我们的。

sentences.en: Tang smiled and said it was *appropriate* for a store to use a small area right outside its own door.
The driver shrugged and walked on.
sentences.cn: 快递员耸了耸肩走开了。

chief:1.en: Lin from the corner shop opposite crossed the street and stopped in front of me. 'What is your *chief* reason for adding an outside display?' she asked, arms folded. I said it helped people see the fresh fruit. She wrote something in her small notebook and walked back without another word.
chief:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林问我们在店外摆放展示台的____原因是什么。
chief:1.hook: She had been watching our store all morning, and I had just noticed.
chief:1.line: 'Tell me your *chief* reason for putting the display outside.'

sentences.en: Lin from the corner shop opposite crossed the street and stopped in front of me.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林穿过街道，停在我面前。

sentences.en: 'What is your *chief* reason for adding an outside display?' she asked, arms folded.
I said it helped people see the fresh fruit.
sentences.cn: 我说这样能让人们看到新鲜水果。

sentences.en: She wrote something in her small notebook and walked back without another word.
sentences.cn: 她在小本子上记了点东西，一言不发地走了回去。

clearly:1.en: The Manager taped a hand-drawn map to the front door showing where the new branch would be. He had written the address in large letters and drawn a big red arrow. 'People can *clearly* see it from here,' he said, stepping back to admire his work. A passing cat walked straight into the door.
clearly:1.cnHint: 店长把新分店的地图贴在门上，这样路人就能____看到地址。
clearly:1.hook: A phone number on the map was missing its last digit.
clearly:1.line: 'From the pavement, people can *clearly* read every word on this sign.'

sentences.en: The Manager taped a hand-drawn map to the front door showing where the new branch would be.
sentences.cn: 店长在前门贴了一张手绘地图，标注新分店的位置。

sentences.en: He had written the address in large letters and drawn a big red arrow.
sentences.cn: 他用大字写下了地址，还画了一支红箭头。

sentences.en: 'People can *clearly* see it from here,' he said, stepping back to admire his work.
A passing cat walked straight into the door.
sentences.cn: 一只路过的猫径直撞上了门。

communicate:1.en: Tang handed me a walkie-talkie before my shift. 'The Manager wants us to *communicate* between the main store and the new one during the first week,' she said. I pressed the button to test it. A very confused voice from a nearby taxi answered back.
communicate:1.cnHint: 阿糖给了我一个对讲机，让我们能在两家店之间____。
communicate:1.hook: The taxi driver now knew exactly how many boxes of milk we had in stock.
communicate:1.line: 'We need to *communicate* between the two stores every hour.'

sentences.en: Tang handed me a walkie-talkie before my shift.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在我上班前递给我一部对讲机。

sentences.en: 'The Manager wants us to *communicate* between the main store and the new one during the first week,' she said.
I pressed the button to test it.
sentences.cn: 我按了按按钮测试一下。

sentences.en: A very confused voice from a nearby taxi answered back.
sentences.cn: 附近一辆出租车里传来了一个非常困惑的声音。

emphasis:1.en: The Manager gathered Tang and me outside to talk about the new branch. He spoke slowly and put a strong *emphasis* on the word 'cleanliness', tapping the wall each time he said it. A pigeon landed on his head during the third tap. He did not break eye contact once.
emphasis:1.cnHint: 店长在店外开会时，特别把____放在了'整洁'这个词上。
emphasis:1.hook: The pigeon seemed to be listening more carefully than I was.
emphasis:1.line: 'I want to put the *emphasis* on keeping the new store spotless.'

sentences.en: The Manager gathered Tang and me outside to talk about the new branch.
sentences.cn: 店长把阿糖和我叫到外面谈新分店的事。

sentences.en: He spoke slowly and put a strong *emphasis* on the word 'cleanliness', tapping the wall each time he said it.
A pigeon landed on his head during the third tap.
sentences.cn: 第三次敲墙的时候，一只鸽子落在了他头上。

sentences.en: He did not break eye contact once.
sentences.cn: 他始终没有移开视线。

emphasize:1.en: Lin appeared at our door again, this time holding a small sign of her own. 'I just want to *emphasize* that my shop has been on this corner for nine years,' she said in a very calm voice. Then she smiled, turned around, and walked back across the empty street.
emphasize:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林再次来到我们门口，____说她的店已经在这个街角开了九年。
emphasize:1.hook: Her shop window was now lit up brighter than ever before.
emphasize:1.line: 'I want to *emphasize* that my store was here long before yours.'

sentences.en: Lin appeared at our door again, this time holding a small sign of her own.
sentences.cn: 林又出现在我们门口，这次手里拿着一个自己做的小牌子。

sentences.en: 'I just want to *emphasize* that my shop has been on this corner for nine years,' she said in a very calm voice.
Then she smiled, turned around, and walked back across the empty street.
sentences.cn: 然后她笑了，转身走回了空荡荡的街道对面。

newspaper:1.en: Early that morning I found a soaked *newspaper* pressed flat against the door of the new branch, left by someone before dawn. The headline was about rising rents on this street. I peeled it off carefully and read it on the step, a cold wind turning the pages for me.

sentences.en: The Manager asked me to walk with him after my shift.
sentences.cn: 我下班后店长请我和他一起走。

sentences.en: We stopped at a dusty corner lot two blocks away.
sentences.cn: 我们在两个街区外的一个尘土飞扬的角落停了下来。

sentences.en: 'This is the *site* for our new store,' he said, eyes bright.
A torn paper sign on the fence read the same address — but in someone else's handwriting.
sentences.cn: 栅栏上一张撕破的纸牌上写着同样的地址——但笔迹是别人的。

absorb:1.en: Tang handed me a thick folder on my third night. 'Read this — store layout, regular orders, supplier names,' she said. 'Try to *absorb* it before the weekend rush.' I nodded and opened page one. By page three I found a note that was not part of any training guide.
absorb:1.cnHint: 同事让我____这本厚厚的资料，但翻到第三页时我发现了一张奇怪的便条。
absorb:1.hook: The note had no name on it, only a time: 2:47 a.m.
absorb:1.line: 'You need to *absorb* all of this before Saturday night.'

sentences.en: Tang handed me a thick folder on my third night.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在我上班的第三个晚上递给我一个厚厚的文件夹。

sentences.en: 'Read this — store layout, regular orders, supplier names,' she said.
sentences.cn: "看这个——店铺平面图、常客订单、供货商名单，"她说。

sentences.en: 'Try to *absorb* it before the weekend rush.'
I nodded and opened page one.
sentences.cn: 我点了点头，翻开了第一页。

sentences.en: By page three I found a note that was not part of any training guide.
sentences.cn: 翻到第三页时，我发现了一张纸条，那不是任何培训资料的一部分。

advance:1.en: The Manager called a small meeting before dawn. 'Our new store opens in two weeks,' he said. 'This is a big *advance* for us.' Tang clapped softly. I smiled too — but Lin had been standing just outside the glass door, and now he was gone.
advance:1.cnHint: 店长宣布新店开张是一大____，但竞争对手林已悄悄离开了门口。
advance:1.hook: Lin's coffee cup was still warm on the step outside.
advance:1.line: 'Opening a second store is a real *advance* for this little shop.'

sentences.en: The Manager called a small meeting before dawn.
sentences.cn: 店长在天亮前召集了一个小会议。

sentences.en: 'Our new store opens in two weeks,' he said.
sentences.cn: "我们的新店要在两周后开业，"他说。

sentences.en: 'This is a big *advance* for us.'
Tang clapped softly.
sentences.cn: 阿糖轻轻鼓了鼓掌。

sentences.en: I smiled too — but Lin had been standing just outside the glass door, and now he was gone.
sentences.cn: 我也笑了——但隔壁咖啡店的林一直站在玻璃门外，现在他已经走了。

capable:1.en: A delivery driver dropped six heavy boxes at once and looked at me. 'New kid, can you handle these alone?' Tang crossed her arms and smiled. 'He is more than *capable*,' she said firmly. I stacked all six without dropping a single one. The driver raised an eyebrow and left a tip on the counter.
capable:1.cnHint: 送货员质疑我，同事说我完全____胜任，结果我证明了自己。
capable:1.hook: The driver came back ten minutes later with one more box.
capable:1.line: 'Trust me, the new clerk is perfectly *capable* of handling this.'

sentences.en: A delivery driver dropped six heavy boxes at once and looked at me.
sentences.cn: 一个送货司机一次性放下六个沉甸甸的箱子，朝我看了一眼。

sentences.en: 'New kid, can you handle these alone?'
sentences.cn: "新来的，你能一个人搞定这些吗？"

sentences.en: Tang crossed her arms and smiled.
sentences.cn: 阿糖交叉双臂，微笑着。

sentences.en: 'He is more than *capable*,' she said firmly.
I stacked all six without dropping a single one.
sentences.cn: 我把全部六个箱子堆好了，一个都没掉。

sentences.en: The driver raised an eyebrow and left a tip on the counter.
sentences.cn: 司机挑了挑眉毛，在柜台上留下了小费。

dollar:1.en: An old man counted coins on the counter every Tuesday, buying the same rice ball. Tonight he was one *dollar* short and stared at his palm. I quietly added it from the small tip jar Tang kept by the register. He looked up, said nothing, and placed a folded paper crane on the counter.
dollar:1.cnHint: 老人每次差一____买饭团，我悄悄补上了，他留下了一只纸鹤。
dollar:1.hook: Next Tuesday, three paper cranes were waiting on the doorstep.
dollar:1.line: 'Just one *dollar* short again — same as every week, I know.'

sentences.en: An old man counted coins on the counter every Tuesday, buying the same rice ball.
sentences.cn: 一个老人每周二都在柜台上数硬币，买同一种饭团。

sentences.en: Tonight he was one *dollar* short and stared at his palm.
I quietly added it from the small tip jar Tang kept by the register.
sentences.cn: 我悄悄从阿糖放在收银机旁的小费罐里补上了。

sentences.en: He looked up, said nothing, and placed a folded paper crane on the counter.
sentences.cn: 他抬起头，什么都没说，在柜台上放下了一只折好的纸鹤。

double:1.en: The Manager showed me the new store plan. The floor space was nearly *double* that of our current shop, with room for a small seating area by the window. I was excited until I noticed the delivery schedule pinned behind it — Lin's store had booked the same suppliers a day earlier.
double:1.cnHint: 新店面积几乎是现在的____，但竞争对手已提前一天预订了同样的供应商。
double:1.hook: Same suppliers, same street, one day apart — this was no accident.
double:1.line: 'The new place is almost *double* the size of what we have now.'

sentences.en: The Manager showed me the new store plan.
sentences.cn: 店长给我看了新店的平面图。

sentences.en: The floor space was nearly *double* that of our current shop, with room for a small seating area by the window.
I was excited until I noticed the delivery schedule pinned behind it — Lin's store had booked the same suppliers a day earlier.
sentences.cn: 我很兴奋，直到我注意到钉在后面的配送时间表——隔壁咖啡店的林的店提前一天预订了同样的供货商。

federal:1.en: A tired woman in a neat coat came in just before three in the morning, bought a coffee, and spread papers across the small side table. I could see the words '*federal* grant' on the top sheet. She circled a number, exhaled slowly, and smiled at the wall. I wondered what she was building.
federal:1.cnHint: 一位女士深夜在店里查看____补贴文件，悄悄地微笑，像是找到了什么答案。
federal:1.hook: She left the cap of her pen on the table, perhaps on purpose.
federal:1.line: 'This *federal* grant could change everything for our project.'

sentences.en: A tired woman in a neat coat came in just before three in the morning, bought a coffee, and spread papers across the small side table.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着整洁大衣、看起来很疲惫的女人在凌晨三点前来了，买了一杯咖啡，在边上的小桌子上铺开了一些文件。

sentences.en: I could see the words '*federal* grant' on the top sheet.
She circled a number, exhaled slowly, and smiled at the wall.
sentences.cn: 她圈了一个数字，慢慢呼了口气，朝着墙笑了。

sentences.en: I wondered what she was building.
sentences.cn: 我想知道她在建造什么。

insist:1.en: The Manager stood outside the newly rented corner unit, pointing at the sign above the door. Lin crossed her arms and shook her head. 'Too small,' she said. The Manager chose to *insist* that the spot was perfect — the foot traffic alone would double our sales.
insist:1.cnHint: 店长____说转角新店的位置绝对没问题，但隔壁咖啡店的林不这么认为。
insist:1.hook: Lin pulled out her phone and showed him something alarming.
insist:1.line: I *insist* this corner is the best spot on the street.

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the newly rented corner unit, pointing at the sign above the door.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新租下的转角店铺外面，指着门上的招牌。

sentences.en: Lin crossed her arms and shook her head.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林交叉双臂，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'Too small,' she said.
sentences.cn: "太小了，"她说。

sentences.en: The Manager chose to *insist* that the spot was perfect — the foot traffic alone would double our sales.

investigation:1.en: A city inspector arrived at the corner plot where our new store would be built. She walked slowly around the fence, writing notes and taking photos. 'This is a routine *investigation*,' she told me, though her eyes kept stopping on the same crack in the ground.
investigation:1.cnHint: 一位检查员来对新店地块进行____，她的目光一直落在地上那道裂缝上。
investigation:1.hook: She circled the crack a third time, then called someone quietly.
investigation:1.line: Our *investigation* of this site will take the whole morning.

sentences.en: A city inspector arrived at the corner plot where our new store would be built.
sentences.cn: 一个城市检查员来到了我们新店将要建造的转角地块。

sentences.en: She walked slowly around the fence, writing notes and taking photos.
sentences.cn: 她在围栏周围缓缓走着，记笔记、拍照片。

sentences.en: 'This is a routine *investigation*,' she told me, though her eyes kept stopping on the same crack in the ground.

limited:1.en: Tang spread the budget sheet across the hood of the delivery van outside. Only three weeks until the new branch opened, and the numbers looked thin. 'Our time is *limited*, our money is more limited, and the Manager still wants a coffee machine,' Tang said, laughing without joy.
limited:1.cnHint: 阿糖在车外查看预算单，发现开新店的资金和时间都十分____。
limited:1.hook: Then Tang spotted a line item neither of us had approved.
limited:1.line: Our budget is *limited*, so we must choose very carefully.

sentences.en: Tang spread the budget sheet across the hood of the delivery van outside.
sentences.cn: 阿糖把预算表铺在外面送货车的车盖上。

sentences.en: Only three weeks until the new branch opened, and the numbers looked thin.
sentences.cn: 距离新分店开业只有三周了，数字看起来很紧张。

sentences.en: 'Our time is *limited*, our money is more limited, and the Manager still wants a coffee machine,' Tang said, laughing without joy.

listen:1.en: I stood on the pavement as the Manager gave instructions to two workers fitting the new shop window. He spoke fast, waving his hands. One worker leaned close to *listen*, while the other quietly did the opposite of everything the Manager said, and the window tilted left.
listen:1.cnHint: 店长在店外指挥工人安装橱窗，其中一个工人根本不____他的话。
listen:1.hook: A loud crack came from above, and everyone froze.
listen:1.line: Please *listen* — the sign goes on the left side, not the right.

sentences.en: I stood on the pavement as the Manager gave instructions to two workers fitting the new shop window.
sentences.cn: 我站在人行道上，店长在给两个装新店橱窗的工人下指令。

sentences.en: He spoke fast, waving his hands.
sentences.cn: 他说得很快，挥舞着双手。

sentences.en: One worker leaned close to *listen*, while the other quietly did the opposite of everything the Manager said, and the window tilted left.

master:1.en: The old man who repaired locks on our street watched the workers struggle with the new store door for twenty minutes. Finally he walked over, took the tool, and fixed it in seconds. Tang whispered to me, 'He is a true *master*. Every lock on this block knows his hands.'
master:1.cnHint: 街上的老修锁人出手帮忙，阿糖悄悄告诉我他是这一行真正的____。
master:1.hook: The old man winked and slipped a small key into his pocket.
master:1.line: A true *master* never needs more than one try.

sentences.en: The old man who repaired locks on our street watched the workers struggle with the new store door for twenty minutes.
sentences.cn: 街上那个开锁的老师傅看着工人们在新店门口折腾了二十分钟。

sentences.en: Finally he walked over, took the tool, and fixed it in seconds.
sentences.cn: 最后他走了过去，接过工具，几秒钟就搞定了。

sentences.en: Tang whispered to me, 'He is a true *master*.
Every lock on this block knows his hands.'
sentences.cn: 阿糖在我耳边低声说，"这块街上的每把锁都认识他的手。"

newly:1.en: The *newly* painted sign above the branch hung bright yellow in the morning sun. I had walked past this corner a hundred times, but the colour made everything feel different — bigger, more real. Lin stood beside me, coffee in hand, and for once said nothing critical at all.
newly:1.cnHint: 新店____刷好的招牌在阳光下格外醒目，连一贯挑剔的隔壁咖啡店的林也沉默了。
newly:1.hook: Then a pigeon landed on the sign and refused to move.
newly:1.line: The *newly* painted wall looks perfect from across the street.

sentences.en: The *newly* painted sign above the branch hung bright yellow in the morning sun.
I had walked past this corner a hundred times, but the colour made everything feel different — bigger, more real.
sentences.cn: 我已经经过这个转角一百次了，但这个颜色让一切都感觉不同——更大、更真实了。

sentences.en: Lin stood beside me, coffee in hand, and for once said nothing critical at all.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在我身边，手里拿着咖啡，这一次难得什么批评的话都没说。

north:1.en: The Manager unfolded a city map on the pavement and stabbed his finger at a dot. 'Our main store is here. The new branch is *north*, near the university.' Lin looked at the distance between the two dots and quietly calculated how long the supply run would take each morning.
north:1.cnHint: 店长在路边摊开地图，指着____边那家新分店的位置给大家看。
north:1.hook: Lin's calculation ended with a soft, unhappy whistle.
north:1.line: The new branch is *north* of here, close to the university gate.

sentences.en: The Manager unfolded a city map on the pavement and stabbed his finger at a dot.
sentences.cn: 店长在人行道上展开了一张城市地图，用手指戳了戳其中一个点。

sentences.en: 'Our main store is here.
sentences.cn: 我们的主店就在这儿。

sentences.en: The new branch is *north*, near the university.'
Lin looked at the distance between the two dots and quietly calculated how long the supply run would take each morning.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林看着两个点之间的距离，默默计算着每天早上送货要花多长时间。

obviously:1.en: The delivery truck stopped in front of the new branch, blocking the entire lane. Cars began to pile up. The driver shrugged at me. '*Obviously* there is nowhere else to park,' he said cheerfully. A cyclist squeezed past, shouting words I chose not to repeat to the Manager.
obviously:1.cnHint: 送货车堵住了新店门前的整条路，司机却____觉得这很合理。
obviously:1.hook: A traffic officer turned the corner, notebook already open.
obviously:1.line: '*Obviously* the truck must stop here — there is no other space.'

sentences.en: The delivery truck stopped in front of the new branch, blocking the entire lane.
sentences.cn: 送货车停在新分店门前，堵住了整条巷子。

sentences.en: Cars began to pile up.
sentences.cn: 车子开始排队堵塞。

sentences.en: The driver shrugged at me. '*Obviously* there is nowhere else to park,' he said cheerfully.
A cyclist squeezed past, shouting words I chose not to repeat to the Manager.
sentences.cn: 一个骑自行车的人挤过去，喊了些我决定不转述给店长听的话。

pose:1.en: Outside the new branch store, the Manager asked everyone to stand together for a photo. Lin crossed his arms and turned sideways. Tang stood on tiptoe. I had no idea what to do with my hands. 'Hold your *pose*,' the Manager said, squinting at his phone screen, 'the light is perfect.'
pose:1.cnHint: 店长让大家在新分店门口摆好____，准备拍照留念。
pose:1.hook: Then a pigeon landed on the Manager's head.
pose:1.line: 'Hold your *pose* — don't move until I count to three!'

sentences.en: Outside the new branch store, the Manager asked everyone to stand together for a photo.
sentences.cn: 在新分店外，店长让大家站到一起拍照。

sentences.en: Lin crossed his arms and turned sideways.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林交叉起双臂，侧过身去。

sentences.en: Tang stood on tiptoe.
sentences.cn: 阿糖踮起脚尖。

sentences.en: I had no idea what to do with my hands.
sentences.cn: 我完全不知道该怎么放我的手。

sentences.en: 'Hold your *pose*,' the Manager said, squinting at his phone screen, 'the light is perfect.'

stimulate:1.en: The Manager hung a bright new sign above the branch store door. Passing students stopped and stared. 'A little colour can *stimulate* curiosity,' he told me proudly, smoothing his jacket. Tang leaned against the wall eating a rice ball, looking completely unstimulated. I decided not to mention that.
stimulate:1.cnHint: 店长认为鲜艳的新招牌能____路人的好奇心，吸引他们进店。
stimulate:1.hook: One student walked in, bought nothing, and left a note.
stimulate:1.line: 'Bright colours *stimulate* people — trust me, I read a whole article.'

sentences.en: The Manager hung a bright new sign above the branch store door.
sentences.cn: 店长在分店门上挂上了一块崭新的招牌。

sentences.en: Passing students stopped and stared.
sentences.cn: 过路的学生停下来盯着看。

sentences.en: 'A little colour can *stimulate* curiosity,' he told me proudly, smoothing his jacket.
Tang leaned against the wall eating a rice ball, looking completely unstimulated.
sentences.cn: 阿糖靠着墙吃米团，看起来完全没有被激起好奇心。

sentences.en: I decided not to mention that.
sentences.cn: 我决定不提这件事。

switch:1.en: The branch store stood one street over from ours. On busy nights the Manager would *switch* Tang and me between the two locations without warning. Tang always got the quiet one. I always got the queue that stretched to the corner. I was starting to notice a pattern.
switch:1.cnHint: 忙碌的夜晚，店长会悄悄把我和阿糖____到不同的门店。
switch:1.hook: Tonight the Manager smiled at me with unusual kindness.
switch:1.line: 'We need to *switch* you two again — starting right now.'

sentences.en: The branch store stood one street over from ours.
sentences.cn: 分店所在的街道离我们的店只隔一条街。

sentences.en: On busy nights the Manager would *switch* Tang and me between the two locations without warning.
Tang always got the quiet one.
sentences.cn: 阿糖总是分到安静的那家店。

sentences.en: I always got the queue that stretched to the corner.
sentences.cn: 我总是分到排队排到街角的那家店。

sentences.en: I was starting to notice a pattern.
sentences.cn: 我开始注意到一种模式。

treatment:1.en: Lin arrived at the branch store opening carrying a small cactus as a gift. The Manager accepted it with great ceremony. Tang and I had brought nothing and received a sharp look. 'Different *treatment* for different effort,' the Manager said quietly. Lin smiled. The cactus looked smug too.
treatment:1.cnHint: 开业那天，隔壁咖啡店的林带了礼物，店长对他和我们的____明显不同。
treatment:1.hook: The cactus was later found on my workstation.
treatment:1.line: 'Same work, same hours — we deserve equal *treatment*, don't we?'

sentences.en: Lin arrived at the branch store opening carrying a small cactus as a gift.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林提着一株小仙人掌作为礼物来到分店开业现场。

sentences.en: The Manager accepted it with great ceremony.
sentences.cn: 店长非常隆重地收下了它。

sentences.en: Tang and I had brought nothing and received a sharp look.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我什么都没带，得到了一个尖锐的眼神。

sentences.en: 'Different *treatment* for different effort,' the Manager said quietly.
Lin smiled.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林笑了。

sentences.en: The cactus looked smug too.
sentences.cn: 那仙人掌看起来也很得意。

union:1.en: Three neighbourhood store clerks stood outside comparing receipts in the early morning cold. Tang called it a *union* meeting. The Manager called it loitering. The woman from the flower shop said she just wanted someone to talk to. We agreed to meet every Thursday. The Manager pretended not to hear.
union:1.cnHint: 几个街区的店员在门外自发组成____，定期交流心得。
union:1.hook: The flower-shop woman mentioned she had once managed fifty people.
union:1.line: 'A small *union* of clerks — that's all we are, nothing scary.'

sentences.en: Three neighbourhood store clerks stood outside comparing receipts in the early morning cold.
sentences.cn: 三个街边店的店员站在早晨的寒冷中比较着收据。

sentences.en: Tang called it a *union* meeting.
