The Manager called it loitering.
sentences.cn: 店长叫它闲逛。

sentences.en: The woman from the flower shop said she just wanted someone to talk to.
sentences.cn: 花店的女老板说她只是想找个人说话。

sentences.en: We agreed to meet every Thursday.
sentences.cn: 我们同意每周四见面。

sentences.en: The Manager pretended not to hear.
sentences.cn: 店长假装没听见。

acknowledge:1.en: After the branch store ribbon was cut, a regular customer named Old Mr Fang clapped loudly from across the street. The Manager gave a small bow. He did not *acknowledge* that Fang had predicted the opening date three weeks ago — correctly, down to the hour. Fang just winked at me.
acknowledge:1.cnHint: 店长没有____一位老顾客早就准确预测了开业日期这件事。
acknowledge:1.hook: Old Mr Fang pulled a folded paper from his coat pocket.
acknowledge:1.line: 'You should *acknowledge* when someone gets it exactly right.'

sentences.en: After the branch store ribbon was cut, a regular customer named Old Mr Fang clapped loudly from across the street.
sentences.cn: 分店剪彩后，一个叫方老爷子的常客从街对面大声鼓掌。

sentences.en: The Manager gave a small bow.
sentences.cn: 店长微微鞠了一躬。

sentences.en: He did not *acknowledge* that Fang had predicted the opening date three weeks ago — correctly, down to the hour.
Fang just winked at me.
sentences.cn: 方老爷子只是朝我眨了眨眼。

alike:1.en: Standing outside the new branch store, Tang and I wore the same uniform, the same tired eyes, and the same lukewarm smile. A child tugged her mother's sleeve. 'They look *alike*,' she whispered. Tang and I turned to each other slowly. We had never noticed before. It was mildly alarming.
alike:1.cnHint: 一个小孩发现我和阿糖看起来____，我们俩都有点惊到了。
alike:1.hook: The Manager later admitted he had hired us on the same day.
alike:1.line: 'You two dress *alike*, stand alike — are you sure you're not related?'

sentences.en: Standing outside the new branch store, Tang and I wore the same uniform, the same tired eyes, and the same lukewarm smile.
sentences.cn: 站在新分店外，阿糖和我穿着同样的制服，顶着同样疲惫的眼睛，露出同样不冷不热的笑容。

sentences.en: A child tugged her mother's sleeve.
sentences.cn: 一个小孩拉了拉妈妈的袖子。

sentences.en: 'They look *alike*,' she whispered.
Tang and I turned to each other slowly.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我慢慢转向彼此。

sentences.en: We had never noticed before.
sentences.cn: 我们之前从没注意过。

sentences.en: It was mildly alarming.
sentences.cn: 这多少有点吓人。

analyze:1.en: Lin stood on the pavement across from the new branch store with a small notebook, watching customers go in and out. 'I *analyze* the foot traffic before every shift,' he told me seriously. I looked at his notebook. It was full of tiny drawings of clouds. He closed it very quickly.
analyze:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林声称自己会____新店的人流量，但他的笔记本里另有玄机。
analyze:1.hook: He offered to show me page one, then immediately changed his mind.
analyze:1.line: 'I always *analyze* the street before I go in — old habit.'

sentences.en: Lin stood on the pavement across from the new branch store with a small notebook, watching customers go in and out.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在新分店对面的人行道上，拿着一本小笔记本，看着顾客进出。

sentences.en: 'I *analyze* the foot traffic before every shift,' he told me seriously.
I looked at his notebook.
sentences.cn: 我看了看他的笔记本。

sentences.en: It was full of tiny drawings of clouds.
sentences.cn: 里面全是小云朵的画。

sentences.en: He closed it very quickly.
sentences.cn: 他很快就合上了。

belong:1.en: The Manager led me outside at dawn to look at the empty shop across the street. 'That corner *belongs* to us now,' he said, pointing at a sign in the window. Workers were already unloading boxes from a truck. I had no idea the store was growing. Neither, it seemed, did the woman watching from the doorway opposite.
belong:1.cnHint: 店长在黎明时带我出去，指着对面空店铺说那个角落____我们了。
belong:1.hook: The woman across the street had a key in her hand.
belong:1.line: 'That corner *belongs* to us now,' the Manager said quietly.

sentences.en: The Manager led me outside at dawn to look at the empty shop across the street.
sentences.cn: 店长在黎明时分领我走出门外，看对街那家空着的店铺。

sentences.en: 'That corner *belongs* to us now,' he said, pointing at a sign in the window.
Workers were already unloading boxes from a truck.
sentences.cn: 工人们已经在从货车上卸箱子了。

sentences.en: I had no idea the store was growing.
sentences.cn: 我不知道店铺在扩张。

sentences.en: Neither, it seemed, did the woman watching from the doorway opposite.
sentences.cn: 看来对面门口看着的那个女人也不知道。

beneficial:1.en: Tang handed me a warm cup outside the back door. 'The morning air is *beneficial*,' she said, stretching her arms wide. 'Breathe before the rush starts.' The street was still quiet, just a cat and one old man with a bag. The old man paused, looked at our new sign, and walked away very fast.
beneficial:1.cnHint: 阿糖在后门外说清晨的空气对人____，但那位老人看到新招牌后却快步离开了。
beneficial:1.hook: The old man turned the corner and pulled out a phone.
beneficial:1.line: 'Fresh air is *beneficial* — trust me,' Tang said, smiling.

sentences.en: Tang handed me a warm cup outside the back door.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在后门外递给我一杯热饮。

sentences.en: 'The morning air is *beneficial*,' she said, stretching her arms wide.
'Breathe before the rush starts.'
sentences.cn: 在奔忙开始前深呼吸。

sentences.en: The street was still quiet, just a cat and one old man with a bag.
sentences.cn: 街道还很安静，只有一只猫和一个拎着袋子的老人。

sentences.en: The old man paused, looked at our new sign, and walked away very fast.
sentences.cn: 老人停了下来，看了看我们的新招牌，然后很快走开了。

characteristic:1.en: Lin stood on the pavement studying our new branch with his arms crossed. His slow, careful nod was a *characteristic* I had learned to watch for — it meant he was thinking hard and saying little. He picked up a flyer from the ground, read both sides, and set it back down gently before walking away.
characteristic:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在人行道上仔细打量新分店，他那慢慢点头的____意味着他在认真思考。
characteristic:1.hook: The flyer he had read was gone the next morning.
characteristic:1.line: 'That slow nod is his *characteristic* — watch out,' Tang whispered.

sentences.en: Lin stood on the pavement studying our new branch with his arms crossed.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在人行道上，双臂交叉，打量着我们的新店。

sentences.en: His slow, careful nod was a *characteristic* I had learned to watch for — it meant he was thinking hard and saying little.
He picked up a flyer from the ground, read both sides, and set it back down gently before walking away.
sentences.cn: 他从地上捡起一张传单，两面都看过，然后轻轻放回去，转身离开了。

director:1.en: A man in a dark coat stopped outside and asked if the Manager was in. 'I am the *director* of the building company,' he said, handing me a card through the open door. He glanced at the half-built shelves inside, then at the street, as if measuring something. He said he would return at noon. He did not look like someone who forgot appointments.
director:1.cnHint: 一位穿深色外套的男士自称是建筑公司的____，他打量了半天后说中午还会再来。
director:1.hook: His card had two phone numbers, but one was crossed out in pen.
director:1.line: 'Tell your manager the *director* of the building company called.'

sentences.en: A man in a dark coat stopped outside and asked if the Manager was in.
sentences.cn: 一个穿深色大衣的男人停在外面，问店长在不在。

sentences.en: 'I am the *director* of the building company,' he said, handing me a card through the open door.
He glanced at the half-built shelves inside, then at the street, as if measuring something.
sentences.cn: 他瞥了一眼里面半搭好的架子，又看了看街道，仿佛在测量什么。

sentences.en: He said he would return at noon.
sentences.cn: 他说他会在中午回来。

sentences.en: He did not look like someone who forgot appointments.
sentences.cn: 他看起来不像会忘记约定的人。

emerge:1.en: We had been stacking boxes in the new branch all morning when the Manager told us to stop. He wanted to see the shop *emerge* slowly, one shelf at a time. 'Rushing makes the whole thing feel cheap,' he said. Outside, a group of students pressed their faces to the glass, fogging it with their breath.
emerge:1.cnHint: 店长让我们慢慢来，想看着新店一点一点____，而不是着急赶工。
emerge:1.hook: One student was quietly drawing the shop layout in a notebook.
emerge:1.line: 'Let the shop *emerge* slowly — don't rush it,' the Manager said.

sentences.en: We had been stacking boxes in the new branch all morning when the Manager told us to stop.
sentences.cn: 我们整个上午都在新店里堆纸箱，直到店长让我们停下来。

sentences.en: He wanted to see the shop *emerge* slowly, one shelf at a time.
'Rushing makes the whole thing feel cheap,' he said.
sentences.cn: "急赶快做什么都显得便宜，"他说。

sentences.en: Outside, a group of students pressed their faces to the glass, fogging it with their breath.
sentences.cn: 外面，一群学生把脸贴在玻璃上，呼出一片雾气。

exact:1.en: Tang measured the new sign three times before she was happy. 'The *exact* centre matters,' she told me, holding the ruler flat against the wall. I held one end and tried not to laugh. When we finally stepped back, the sign was perfect — and Lin was standing on the pavement, already taking notes on a small pad.
exact:1.cnHint: 阿糖反复测量新招牌，坚持说____的中心位置很重要，而隔壁咖啡店的林已经在旁边做笔记了。
exact:1.hook: Lin's notes were written in a hand too small to read from the door.
exact:1.line: 'The *exact* centre matters — hold the ruler still,' Tang said.

sentences.en: Tang measured the new sign three times before she was happy.
sentences.cn: 阿糖测了三次新招牌才满意。

sentences.en: 'The *exact* centre matters,' she told me, holding the ruler flat against the wall.
I held one end and tried not to laugh.
sentences.cn: 我拿住一头，努力忍着不笑。

sentences.en: When we finally stepped back, the sign was perfect — and Lin was standing on the pavement, already taking notes on a small pad.
sentences.cn: 我们最后退后一看，招牌完美无缺——隔壁咖啡店的林正站在人行道上，已经在小便签本上记起笔记。

guest:1.en: The first *guest* to walk into the new branch was a girl with a backpack and muddy boots. She looked around slowly, as if she had been here before, though we had only opened the doors an hour ago. She bought one bottle of water, paid, and said, 'Nice place.' Then she asked when the old shop had moved.
guest:1.cnHint: 新分店的第一位____背着包、穿着沾泥的靴子，她问的那个问题让我们都愣了一下。
guest:1.hook: None of us knew what old shop she meant.
guest:1.line: 'Welcome — you're our very first *guest* today,' I told her.

sentences.en: The first *guest* to walk into the new branch was a girl with a backpack and muddy boots.
She looked around slowly, as if she had been here before, though we had only opened the doors an hour ago.
sentences.cn: 她慢慢环顾四周，仿佛曾经来过这里，尽管我们才开门一小时。

sentences.en: She bought one bottle of water, paid, and said, 'Nice place.'
sentences.cn: 她买了一瓶水，付了钱，说："不错的地方。"

sentences.en: Then she asked when the old shop had moved.
sentences.cn: 然后她问起老店什么时候搬的。

massive:1.en: The delivery truck that arrived at the new branch was *massive*, far too wide for the narrow lane beside the shop. The driver climbed down, looked at the gap, and shrugged at me with a smile. Tang called the Manager. The Manager called someone else. Half the street stopped to watch. Lin watched too, from across the road, not smiling at all.
massive:1.cnHint: 送货卡车____得根本开不进小巷，整条街的人都停下来看热闹，只有隔壁咖啡店的林没有笑。
massive:1.hook: Lin crossed the street and spoke quietly to the driver.
massive:1.line: 'That *massive* truck will never fit in the lane,' Tang said flatly.

sentences.en: The delivery truck that arrived at the new branch was *massive*, far too wide for the narrow lane beside the shop.
The driver climbed down, looked at the gap, and shrugged at me with a smile.
sentences.cn: 司机爬下来，看看缝隙，对我耸了耸肩，带着微笑。

sentences.en: Tang called the Manager.
sentences.cn: 阿糖给店长打电话。

sentences.en: The Manager called someone else.
sentences.cn: 店长给别人打电话。

sentences.en: Half the street stopped to watch.
sentences.cn: 半条街的人都停下来看。

sentences.en: Lin watched too, from across the road, not smiling at all.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林也在街对面看，表情冷淡。

mix:1.en: The Manager hands me a small cup outside the new branch site. 'Try this,' he says. It is a *mix* of hot barley tea and lemon juice — his test drink for the second store menu. I sip it slowly. The street is cold, but the cup is warm.
mix:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址外让我尝一杯他为新店菜单设计的____。
mix:1.hook: He watches my face like my answer decides everything.
mix:1.line: 'This *mix* took me three weeks to get right.'

sentences.en: The Manager hands me a small cup outside the new branch site.
sentences.cn: 店长在新店地点外递给我一个小杯子。

sentences.en: 'Try this,' he says.
sentences.cn: "尝尝，"他说。

sentences.en: It is a *mix* of hot barley tea and lemon juice — his test drink for the second store menu.
I sip it slowly.
sentences.cn: 我慢慢啜饮。

sentences.en: The street is cold, but the cup is warm.
sentences.cn: 街道很冷，但杯子很热。

necessity:1.en: Tang and I stand outside the empty shop unit the Manager is considering. Tang points at the narrow door. 'A wider entrance is a *necessity*,' she says firmly. 'People carrying bags will just walk past.' The Manager nods slowly and writes something down in his small notebook.
necessity:1.cnHint: 唐在查看新店铺位时强调，宽敞的入口是____。
necessity:1.hook: Then the Manager crosses out a number on the rent page.
necessity:1.line: 'A wider door is a *necessity*, not a luxury.'

sentences.en: Tang and I stand outside the empty shop unit the Manager is considering.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我站在店长考虑的空店铺外。

sentences.en: Tang points at the narrow door.
sentences.cn: 阿糖指着狭窄的门。

sentences.en: 'A wider entrance is a *necessity*,' she says firmly.
'People carrying bags will just walk past.'
sentences.cn: "拎着包的人就会直接走过。"

sentences.en: The Manager nods slowly and writes something down in his small notebook.
sentences.cn: 店长缓缓点头，在小笔记本上写了什么。

stuff:1.en: I help the Manager carry boxes of sample products to the new branch building early one morning. There are bottles, cups, small tools, and paper bags — all sorts of *stuff* piled into a cart. A passer-by stops and asks if we are moving house. We both laugh.
stuff:1.cnHint: 一大早，我帮店长把各种样品____推到新店去。
stuff:1.hook: One box, taped shut, has no label at all.
stuff:1.line: 'This *stuff* all needs to be sorted before noon.'

sentences.en: I help the Manager carry boxes of sample products to the new branch building early one morning.
sentences.cn: 一大早我帮店长把样品盒子搬到新店房子里。

sentences.en: There are bottles, cups, small tools, and paper bags — all sorts of *stuff* piled into a cart.
A passer-by stops and asks if we are moving house.
sentences.cn: 一个路人停下来，问我们是不是在搬家。

sentences.en: We both laugh.
sentences.cn: 我们都笑了。

translate:1.en: Lin arrives at the new branch corner holding a printed sign. 'The display needs to *translate* the cosy feeling of the old store,' she says, pinning the sign to the board outside. She steps back, tilts her head, and frowns. Something is still not quite right.
translate:1.cnHint: 林认为新店的展示需要____老店那种温馨的感觉。
translate:1.hook: She pulls the sign down and reaches for a red pen.
translate:1.line: 'We need to *translate* that warmth into the new space.'

sentences.en: Lin arrives at the new branch corner holding a printed sign.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿着一张打印的标牌来到新店角落。

sentences.en: 'The display needs to *translate* the cosy feeling of the old store,' she says, pinning the sign to the board outside.
She steps back, tilts her head, and frowns.
sentences.cn: 她退后一步，歪头皱眉。

sentences.en: Something is still not quite right.
sentences.cn: 还是有什么地方不太对。

wander:1.en: Business is slow on the first preview day of the new branch. I *wander* along the block, slipping a small flyer under each shop door. A noodle stall owner reads it, raises an eyebrow, and asks how late the new store will stay open. I tell him: all night.
wander:1.cnHint: 新店预览日客流稀少，我在附近街区____派发传单。
wander:1.hook: The noodle stall owner folds the flyer and puts it in his pocket.
wander:1.line: 'I always *wander* this block after closing — I will stop by.'

sentences.en: Business is slow on the first preview day of the new branch.
sentences.cn: 新店首个预览日生意清淡。

sentences.en: I *wander* along the block, slipping a small flyer under each shop door.
A noodle stall owner reads it, raises an eyebrow, and asks how late the new store will stay open.
sentences.cn: 一个面摊老板读了传单，挑了挑眉毛，问新店会开到多晚。

sentences.en: I tell him: all night.
sentences.cn: 我告诉他：通宵。

warn:1.en: Tang calls me from the new branch door just before the preview opens. 'I need to *warn* you,' she says, 'the coffee machine here runs hotter than ours. The first cup will surprise you.' I reach for the handle anyway. Tang steps back with a small smile.
warn:1.cnHint: 唐____我新店的咖啡机温度比老店高，小心第一杯。
warn:1.hook: The cup burns my fingers before it even reaches my lips.
warn:1.line: 'I *warn* everyone once — after that it is their own fault.'

sentences.en: Tang calls me from the new branch door just before the preview opens.
sentences.cn: 预览开始前，阿糖从新店门口给我打电话。

sentences.en: 'I need to *warn* you,' she says, 'the coffee machine here runs hotter than ours.
The first cup will surprise you.'
sentences.cn: "第一杯会让你吃惊。"

sentences.en: I reach for the handle anyway.
sentences.cn: 我还是伸手去开了。

sentences.en: Tang steps back with a small smile.
sentences.cn: 阿糖退后一步，带着淡淡的笑。

advocate:1.en: Outside the new branch, a regular customer named Old Chen tells the Manager he is a strong *advocate* of keeping the store open past midnight. 'Night workers need somewhere,' he says, pressing his point with a raised finger. The Manager listens, then quietly asks me to note it down.
advocate:1.cnHint: 常客老陈在新店外积极做深夜营业的____，说夜班工人需要这样的地方。
advocate:1.hook: Old Chen then mentions he knows twelve other night workers on this street.
advocate:1.line: 'I am an *advocate* for every person who works the night shift.'

sentences.en: Outside the new branch, a regular customer named Old Chen tells the Manager he is a strong *advocate* of keeping the store open past midnight.
'Night workers need somewhere,' he says, pressing his point with a raised finger.
sentences.cn: '夜班的人需要有个去处，'他说，竖起一根手指强调自己的观点。

sentences.en: The Manager listens, then quietly asks me to note it down.
sentences.cn: 店长听着，然后轻声让我把这句话记下来。

cite:1.en: Lin stands at the corner near the new branch with a printed chart. She *cites* three nearby stores that failed in the past two years. 'Location, location, location,' she says, tapping each failed store name with her pen. The Manager listens without blinking. Then he taps our chosen spot on the map.
cite:1.cnHint: 林____了附近三家倒闭店铺的案例，提醒大家注意选址风险。
cite:1.hook: The Manager's finger stays on that spot for a long moment.
cite:1.line: 'I *cite* these three cases so we do not repeat their mistakes.'

sentences.en: Lin stands at the corner near the new branch with a printed chart.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在新门店附近的拐角，手里拿着一份打印的图表。

sentences.en: She *cites* three nearby stores that failed in the past two years.
'Location, location, location,' she says, tapping each failed store name with her pen.
sentences.cn: '地点、地点、还是地点，'她用笔尖一个个点着那些倒闭的店名说。

sentences.en: The Manager listens without blinking.
sentences.cn: 店长没眨眼地听着。

sentences.en: Then he taps our chosen spot on the map.
sentences.cn: 接着他在地图上点了点我们选中的那个位置。

writer:1.en: Outside the store, a street *writer* sits under the lamp, filling a notebook with quick pen strokes. Tang waves through the window. The writer looks up, nods, then returns to the page. I wonder what story is growing there. Ten minutes later, the writer closes the notebook and walks toward our door.
writer:1.cnHint: 街边有位____在灯下写东西，阿糖跟他打招呼。
writer:1.hook: The writer is coming inside with that mysterious notebook.
writer:1.line: 'That street *writer* comes here every Tuesday night,' Tang whispered.

sentences.en: Outside the store, a street *writer* sits under the lamp, filling a notebook with quick pen strokes.
Tang waves through the window.
sentences.cn: 阿糖隔着窗户挥了挥手。

sentences.en: The writer looks up, nods, then returns to the page.
sentences.cn: 那个写作者抬起头，点了点头，又低下头继续写。

sentences.en: I wonder what story is growing there.
sentences.cn: 我在想，一个什么样的故事正在那本子里生长。

sentences.en: Ten minutes later, the writer closes the notebook and walks toward our door.
sentences.cn: 十分钟后，那个写作者合上本子，朝我们的门走了过来。

addition:1.en: The Manager stands on the corner with a measuring tape, marking the ground with chalk. 'Perfect spot for the new store,' he says. Lin from the rival shop across the street watches with crossed arms. The *addition* of a second location means double the work but also double the chance to serve this neighborhood. Lin's expression darkens.
addition:1.cnHint: 店长在街角测量，准备____一家新店，对面隔壁咖啡店的林看起来不高兴。
addition:1.hook: Lin is walking over, and he does not look happy.
addition:1.line: 'This *addition* will help more customers,' the Manager said cheerfully.

sentences.en: The Manager stands on the corner with a measuring tape, marking the ground with chalk.
sentences.cn: 店长站在拐角，拿着卷尺，用粉笔在地上做着标记。

sentences.en: 'Perfect spot for the new store,' he says.
sentences.cn: '新店的完美位置，'他说。

sentences.en: Lin from the rival shop across the street watches with crossed arms.
sentences.cn: 街对面竞争对手的林挎着胳膊看着。

sentences.en: The *addition* of a second location means double the work but also double the chance to serve this neighborhood.
Lin's expression darkens.
sentences.cn: 林的脸色暗了下来。

alternative:1.en: Rain pours down outside. A customer stands under our awning, staring at two buses stopped at the corner. 'Which one goes downtown?' she asks me. I point left, then right. 'That one is faster, but this one is a quieter *alternative*.' She bites her lip, choosing. Behind her, both buses start their engines.
alternative:1.cnHint: 下雨天，顾客在屋檐下问哪路车去市中心，我告诉她有两个____。
alternative:1.hook: Both buses are leaving—she must decide now.
alternative:1.line: 'Is there an *alternative* route?' the customer asked nervously.

sentences.en: Rain pours down outside.
sentences.cn: 外面下起了大雨。

sentences.en: A customer stands under our awning, staring at two buses stopped at the corner.
sentences.cn: 一个顾客站在我们的雨棚下，盯着停在拐角的两辆公交车。

sentences.en: 'Which one goes downtown?' she asks me.
sentences.cn: '哪一辆去市中心？'她问我。

sentences.en: I point left, then right.
sentences.cn: 我指了指左边，又指了指右边。

sentences.en: 'That one is faster, but this one is a quieter *alternative*.'
She bites her lip, choosing.
sentences.cn: 她咬着嘴唇，在思考选择。

sentences.en: Behind her, both buses start their engines.
sentences.cn: 她身后，两辆公交车同时发动了引擎。

amazing:1.en: Outside, a street musician plays a small wooden flute. The melody floats through the night air, clear and bright. People slow their steps to listen. Even Lin, standing in his own shop doorway across the street, tilts his head. '*Amazing*,' Tang breathes beside me. Then the musician stops and bows. What happens next surprises everyone.
amazing:1.cnHint: 街头音乐家吹笛子，连隔壁咖啡店的林都停下来听，阿糖说真____。
amazing:1.hook: The musician opens the flute case—it is completely empty.
amazing:1.line: 'That sound is *amazing*!' Tang said, eyes wide with delight.

sentences.en: Outside, a street musician plays a small wooden flute.
sentences.cn: 外面，一个街头音乐人在吹一支小木笛。

sentences.en: The melody floats through the night air, clear and bright.
sentences.cn: 旋律浮过夜空，清脆而明亮。

sentences.en: People slow their steps to listen.
sentences.cn: 人们放慢脚步去听。

sentences.en: Even Lin, standing in his own shop doorway across the street, tilts his head. '*Amazing*,' Tang breathes beside me.
Then the musician stops and bows.
sentences.cn: 然后那个音乐人停了下来，鞠了一躬。

sentences.en: What happens next surprises everyone.
sentences.cn: 接下来发生的事让所有人都吃了一惊。

ease:1.en: The Manager leans against the lamp post outside, phone to his ear, nodding slowly. His shoulders relax. 'Good, good,' he says. Tang whispers that the bank approved the loan for the new store. I watch the Manager's face soften with *ease*. He ends the call, takes a deep breath, and smiles. Then his phone rings again.
ease:1.cnHint: 店长靠着路灯打电话，得知贷款批了，整个人放松下来，很____。
ease:1.hook: The second call wipes the smile off his face.
ease:1.line: 'I can finally breathe with *ease* now,' the Manager sighed happily.

sentences.en: The Manager leans against the lamp post outside, phone to his ear, nodding slowly.
sentences.cn: 店长靠在外面的灯柱上，手机贴在耳边，缓缓点头。

sentences.en: His shoulders relax.
sentences.cn: 他的肩膀放松了。

sentences.en: 'Good, good,' he says.
sentences.cn: '好的，好的，'他说。

sentences.en: Tang whispers that the bank approved the loan for the new store.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在我耳边说，银行批准了新店的贷款。

sentences.en: I watch the Manager's face soften with *ease*.
He ends the call, takes a deep breath, and smiles.
sentences.cn: 他挂断电话，深深吸了一口气，然后笑了。

sentences.en: Then his phone rings again.
sentences.cn: 接着他的电话又响了。

frequent:1.en: I sweep the sidewalk outside when I notice the same delivery truck parked at the corner for the third time today. '*Frequent* visitor,' Tang jokes, carrying out the trash. The driver waves. But this time, instead of driving off, he steps out and walks toward Lin's shop across the street. Tang and I exchange a glance.
frequent:1.cnHint: 我在外面扫地，注意到同一辆货车今天第三次停在街角，很____。
frequent:1.hook: The driver is carrying a thick envelope into Lin's shop.
frequent:1.line: 'That truck is a *frequent* visitor today,' Tang said suspiciously.

sentences.en: I sweep the sidewalk outside when I notice the same delivery truck parked at the corner for the third time today. '*Frequent* visitor,' Tang jokes, carrying out the trash.
The driver waves.
sentences.cn: 司机挥了挥手。

sentences.en: But this time, instead of driving off, he steps out and walks toward Lin's shop across the street.
sentences.cn: 但这一次，他没有直接开走，而是下了车，朝街对面隔壁咖啡店的林的店走去。

sentences.en: Tang and I exchange a glance.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我互相看了一眼。

hope:1.en: A small girl stands outside our store, clutching a coin purse and staring at the vending machine on the corner. She counts her coins twice. Not enough. Her face falls. Tang notices and steps outside with a smile and a candy bar. 'My treat,' he says. The girl's eyes fill with *hope*. She bows and runs off. But she forgets something.
hope:1.cnHint: 小女孩在外面数硬币不够买东西，阿糖送她糖果，她眼中充满____。
hope:1.hook: Her coin purse lies open on the ground.
hope:1.line: 'Maybe next time,' the girl whispered, voice small with fading *hope*.

sentences.en: A small girl stands outside our store, clutching a coin purse and staring at the vending machine on the corner.
sentences.cn: 一个小女孩站在我们店外，紧紧握着一个钱包，盯着拐角的自动贩卖机。

sentences.en: She counts her coins twice.
sentences.cn: 她数了两遍她的硬币。

sentences.en: Not enough.
sentences.cn: 不够。

sentences.en: Her face falls.
sentences.cn: 她的脸沮丧了下来。

sentences.en: Tang notices and steps outside with a smile and a candy bar.
sentences.cn: 阿糖注意到了，带着微笑拿着一根糖果走了出去。

sentences.en: 'My treat,' he says.
sentences.cn: '我请你，'他说。

sentences.en: The girl's eyes fill with *hope*.
She bows and runs off.
sentences.cn: 她鞠了一躬，跑开了。

sentences.en: But she forgets something.
sentences.cn: 但她忘了什么东西。

imply:1.en: Lin stands outside his shop, arms folded, watching the Manager post a sign on the corner: 'New Store Opening Soon!' Lin does not speak, but his silence seems to *imply* a challenge. The Manager nods politely and walks back. Tang mutters that trouble is coming. That evening, a city inspector arrives on our street.
imply:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在外面看店长贴新店广告，虽然没说话但似乎____不满。
imply:1.hook: The inspector is heading straight for our door.
imply:1.line: 'His look seemed to *imply* he was not pleased,' I told Tang.

sentences.en: Lin stands outside his shop, arms folded, watching the Manager post a sign on the corner: 'New Store Opening Soon!'
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在自己的店外，挎着胳膊，看着店长在拐角贴一张标志：'新店即将开业！'

sentences.en: Lin does not speak, but his silence seems to *imply* a challenge.
The Manager nods politely and walks back.
sentences.cn: 店长礼貌地点了点头，走了回来。

sentences.en: Tang mutters that trouble is coming.
sentences.cn: 阿糖嘟囔着麻烦要来了。

sentences.en: That evening, a city inspector arrives on our street.
sentences.cn: 那天傍晚，一个城市检查员来到了我们这条街。

gather:1.en: Outside the store, a crowd begins to *gather* near the crosswalk. I step out to see what is happening. A street musician has set up with a small keyboard, playing a cheerful tune. People stop, smile, and a few drop coins into his hat. The Manager waves at me from inside, pointing at his watch.
gather:1.cnHint: 人群在便利店外的人行横道____，因为有街头音乐家在表演。
gather:1.hook: But the musician keeps glancing nervously at someone across the street.
gather:1.line: 'When people *gather* like this, we should put a sign outside,' the Manager says.

sentences.en: Outside the store, a crowd begins to *gather* near the crosswalk.
I step out to see what is happening.
sentences.cn: 我走出去看看发生了什么。

sentences.en: A street musician has set up with a small keyboard, playing a cheerful tune.
sentences.cn: 一个街头音乐人架好了一架小型电子琴，弹着一首欢快的曲子。

sentences.en: People stop, smile, and a few drop coins into his hat.
sentences.cn: 人们停下脚步，笑着，有些人把硬币丢进他的帽子。

sentences.en: The Manager waves at me from inside, pointing at his watch.
sentences.cn: 店长从店里朝我挥手，指了指他的手表。

imagine:1.en: Lin stands across the street, staring at our store with folded arms. I cannot *imagine* why she looks so upset today. Her own shop is doing well. Tang whispers that Lin heard a rumor about us expanding. The Manager just smiles and keeps arranging the fruit display by the door, completely calm.
imagine:1.cnHint: 林站在街对面盯着我们的店，我无法____她为什么这么生气。
imagine:1.hook: Then Lin pulls out her phone and makes a call.
imagine:1.line: 'I can't *imagine* why she's worried,' Tang says quietly. 'We're not her enemy.'

sentences.en: Lin stands across the street, staring at our store with folded arms.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在街对面，挎着胳膊，盯着我们的店。

sentences.en: I cannot *imagine* why she looks so upset today.
Her own shop is doing well.
sentences.cn: 她自己的店生意不错。

sentences.en: Tang whispers that Lin heard a rumor about us expanding.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在我耳边说，隔壁咖啡店的林听到了关于我们扩张的传言。

sentences.en: The Manager just smiles and keeps arranging the fruit display by the door, completely calm.
sentences.cn: 店长只是笑了笑，继续在门边整理着水果的陈列，表情完全平静。

instance:1.en: The Manager teaches me how to handle difficult customers on the street corner. He gives me an *instance* from last month: a man demanded a refund for a drink he had already finished. The Manager stayed polite, offered him a coupon instead, and the man left happy. I take notes carefully.
instance:1.cnHint: 店长给我讲了一个上个月的____：如何处理难缠的顾客。
instance:1.hook: Just then, that same customer walks toward our door again.
instance:1.line: 'Let me give you one *instance*,' the Manager says. 'Kindness costs us nothing.'

sentences.en: The Manager teaches me how to handle difficult customers on the street corner.
sentences.cn: 店长在街角教我怎么应对难缠的顾客。

sentences.en: He gives me an *instance* from last month: a man demanded a refund for a drink he had already finished.
The Manager stayed polite, offered him a coupon instead, and the man left happy.
sentences.cn: 店长始终保持礼貌，改成送了他一张优惠券，那个人就高高兴兴地离开了。

sentences.en: I take notes carefully.
sentences.cn: 我认真地做笔记。

numerous:1.en: I sweep the sidewalk in front of the store and find *numerous* small items: a hair clip, a button, a toy car, even a single earring. People drop things without noticing. I collect them in a small box by the register. Tang says someone always comes back looking for something they lost.
numerous:1.cnHint: 我在店门口的人行道上发现了____件小东西，都是顾客掉的。
numerous:1.hook: A young woman rushes up, breathless, searching the ground frantically.
numerous:1.line: 'We get *numerous* lost things every week,' Tang tells me. 'Keep the box handy.'

sentences.en: I sweep the sidewalk in front of the store and find *numerous* small items: a hair clip, a button, a toy car, even a single earring.
People drop things without noticing.
sentences.cn: 人们掉东西从来没注意到。

sentences.en: I collect them in a small box by the register.
sentences.cn: 我把它们都收到收银台旁的一个小盒子里。

sentences.en: Tang says someone always comes back looking for something they lost.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说总有人回来找他们丢失的东西。

puzzle:1.en: A delivery truck parks outside, but the driver looks confused. He holds a map and scratches his head. The street signs here *puzzle* many newcomers because two roads share similar names. I step outside and point him toward the correct turn. He thanks me and drives off with a relieved smile.
puzzle:1.cnHint: 送货司机看起来很困惑，因为这里的路牌____了很多新来的人。
puzzle:1.hook: But he left a small package on our doorstep by mistake.
puzzle:1.line: 'These street names *puzzle* everyone,' I say. 'Even I got lost my first day.'

sentences.en: A delivery truck parks outside, but the driver looks confused.
sentences.cn: 一辆送货车停在外面，但司机看起来很困惑。

sentences.en: He holds a map and scratches his head.
sentences.cn: 他拿着地图挠头。

sentences.en: The street signs here *puzzle* many newcomers because two roads share similar names.
I step outside and point him toward the correct turn.
sentences.cn: 我走出去，给他指了正确的方向。

sentences.en: He thanks me and drives off with a relieved smile.
sentences.cn: 他松了口气，笑着谢我，开车离开了。

remind:1.en: An elderly man stops outside and peers through the window. He does not come in, just stands there smiling. Tang says he used to run a shop on this exact corner forty years ago. The sight of our store seems to *remind* him of old times. He waves at us and continues his evening walk.
remind:1.cnHint: 一位老人站在店外，我们的店似乎____了他很多往事。
remind:1.hook: But tonight, he turns back and reaches for the door handle.
remind:1.line: 'This place must *remind* him of something important,' Tang says softly.

sentences.en: An elderly man stops outside and peers through the window.
sentences.cn: 一位老人停在窗外往里看。

sentences.en: He does not come in, just stands there smiling.
sentences.cn: 他没有进来，就站在那里微笑。

sentences.en: Tang says he used to run a shop on this exact corner forty years ago.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说他四十年前在这个街角开过一家店。

sentences.en: The sight of our store seems to *remind* him of old times.
He waves at us and continues his evening walk.
sentences.cn: 他朝我们挥了挥手，继续散步。

truly:1.en: I watch the morning light touch the street corner, turning everything gold. After a long quiet night, I *truly* understand why the Manager loves this shift. Outside, a jogger waves at me through the window. A cat stretches on the warm pavement. The city wakes up gently here, one person at a time.
truly:1.cnHint: 经过一整夜安静的夜班，我____明白了店长为什么喜欢这个班次。
truly:1.hook: Then I notice someone has been sleeping in the doorway next door.
truly:1.line: 'You *truly* see the neighborhood on the night shift,' the Manager told me once.

sentences.en: I watch the morning light touch the street corner, turning everything gold.
sentences.cn: 我看着晨光洒满街角，把一切都镀成了金色。

sentences.en: After a long quiet night, I *truly* understand why the Manager loves this shift.
Outside, a jogger waves at me through the window.
sentences.cn: 窗外，一个慢跑的人透过玻璃朝我挥手。

sentences.en: A cat stretches on the warm pavement.
sentences.cn: 一只猫在温暖的人行道上伸懒腰。

sentences.en: The city wakes up gently here, one person at a time.
sentences.cn: 这座城市在这里温柔地醒来，一次一个人。

valuable:1.en: A businessman rushes out of a taxi and runs to our door. He left something *valuable* in the cab: his laptop bag. I help him call the taxi company while Tang checks our security camera to get the car number. We find the footage and the man relaxes. Ten minutes later, the driver returns with the bag.
valuable:1.cnHint: 一位商人把____的东西落在了出租车里，我们帮他找回来。
valuable:1.hook: The businessman pulls out his wallet, but hesitates over which bill to choose.
valuable:1.line: 'Thank you for keeping something so *valuable* safe,' the businessman says, clearly relieved.

sentences.en: A businessman rushes out of a taxi and runs to our door.
sentences.cn: 一个商人从出租车上冲下来，跑向我们的门。

sentences.en: He left something *valuable* in the cab: his laptop bag.
I help him call the taxi company while Tang checks our security camera to get the car number.
sentences.cn: 我帮他打电话给出租车公司，阿糖去查我们的安全摄像头找车牌号。

sentences.en: We find the footage and the man relaxes.
sentences.cn: 我们找到了录像，那个人放松了。

sentences.en: Ten minutes later, the driver returns with the bag.
sentences.cn: 十分钟后，司机拿着包回来了。

therefore:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, clipboard in hand. The street was narrow and the nearest bus stop was two blocks away. Fewer people passed here each hour, *therefore* he counted heads for twenty minutes before making any decision.
therefore:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址的街道上数人流，因为____他要先观察再决定。
therefore:1.hook: His pen stopped moving when a familiar face appeared.
therefore:1.line: Foot traffic is low, *therefore* we open at six, not eight.

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, clipboard in hand.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新分店的地址外，手里拿着记录板。

sentences.en: The street was narrow and the nearest bus stop was two blocks away.
sentences.cn: 街道很窄，最近的公交站点在两个街区外。

sentences.en: Fewer people passed here each hour, *therefore* he counted heads for twenty minutes before making any decision.

truth:1.en: Lin arrived early and walked the same block three times. She pulled out her notebook and wrote one line at the top: the *truth* is that this corner gets morning crowd but loses everyone by noon. She underlined it twice and kept walking.
truth:1.cnHint: 林在街上反复观察，在笔记本上写下了关于这个街角的____。
truth:1.hook: What she wrote next made her close the notebook fast.
truth:1.line: I checked the numbers — the *truth* is the rent is too high.

sentences.en: Lin arrived early and walked the same block three times.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林很早就到了，在同一条街上走了三遍。

sentences.en: She pulled out her notebook and wrote one line at the top: the *truth* is that this corner gets morning crowd but loses everyone by noon.
She underlined it twice and kept walking.
sentences.cn: 她停下来继续散步。

protein:1.en: Tang was handing out small sample cups near the door of the new site. Each cup held a warm soy drink. A passing student stopped, sipped, and asked what was in it. Tang said it was high in *protein* and good for morning classes. The student took two cups.
protein:1.cnHint: 唐在新店门口派发豆浆样品，向路过的学生介绍饮品富含____。
protein:1.hook: The student came back with five friends ten minutes later.
protein:1.line: One cup of this has more *protein* than your breakfast sandwich.

sentences.en: Tang was handing out small sample cups near the door of the new site.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在新店址的门口发送小样杯。

sentences.en: Each cup held a warm soy drink.
sentences.cn: 每个杯子里装着温热的豆浆。

sentences.en: A passing student stopped, sipped, and asked what was in it.
sentences.cn: 一个路过的学生停下来，喝了一口，问里面是什么。

sentences.en: Tang said it was high in *protein* and good for morning classes.
The student took two cups.
sentences.cn: 那个学生要了两杯。

traffic:1.en: The Manager asked Tang to stand at the corner for one full hour and count. By the end, Tang's notebook was full. The morning *traffic* was surprisingly heavy — office workers, students, delivery riders — all pouring past the empty shopfront like a small river.
traffic:1.cnHint: 唐在街角数了一小时的____，结果让店长眼睛一亮。
traffic:1.hook: One delivery rider slowed down and stared at the empty shop.
traffic:1.line: The *traffic* here at eight in the morning beats our old spot.

sentences.en: The Manager asked Tang to stand at the corner for one full hour and count.
sentences.cn: 店长让阿糖在街角站了整整一个小时来数人。

sentences.en: By the end, Tang's notebook was full.
sentences.cn: 最后，阿糖的笔记本满满的。

sentences.en: The morning *traffic* was surprisingly heavy — office workers, students, delivery riders — all pouring past the empty shopfront like a small river.

cat:1.en: A small orange *cat* sat on the window ledge of the empty shopfront all morning. People stopped to look at it, smiled, and then noticed the 'coming soon' sign behind it. Lin watched from across the street and wrote: best free advertisement we never planned.
cat:1.cnHint: 一只橘猫坐在新店橱窗上，意外地吸引了许多路人注意到____的开业公告。
cat:1.hook: Nobody knew who the cat belonged to.
cat:1.line: That *cat* has done more for us today than any flyer.

sentences.en: A small orange *cat* sat on the window ledge of the empty shopfront all morning.
People stopped to look at it, smiled, and then noticed the 'coming soon' sign behind it.
sentences.cn: 人们停下来看它，微笑，然后注意到后面的"即将开业"的标牌。

sentences.en: Lin watched from across the street and wrote: best free advertisement we never planned.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在街对面看着，写下：最好的免费广告，我们从没想过。

sugar:1.en: A grandmother stopped Tang outside and pointed at the sample drinks. She asked, very seriously, how much *sugar* was inside each cup. Tang checked the label and read the number out loud. She nodded, took a cup, and said that was exactly the right amount.
sugar:1.cnHint: 一位老奶奶在街上拦住唐，认真询问样品饮料里的____含量。
sugar:1.hook: She then asked how many cups she could take home.
sugar:1.line: Less *sugar* than a candy bar — I checked the label myself.

sentences.en: A grandmother stopped Tang outside and pointed at the sample drinks.
sentences.cn: 一位奶奶在外面拦住了阿糖，指着那些样品饮料。

sentences.en: She asked, very seriously, how much *sugar* was inside each cup.
Tang checked the label and read the number out loud.
sentences.cn: 阿糖查了标签，大声读出数字。

sentences.en: She nodded, took a cup, and said that was exactly the right amount.
sentences.cn: 她点了点头，拿了一杯，说那正好是完美的量。

balance:1.en: Lin set up a small folding table outside to test a display stand for bottled drinks. The bottles kept sliding. She shifted them left, then right, then added a rubber mat underneath. Finally, the whole row held its *balance* perfectly, even when a bus rumbled past.
balance:1.cnHint: 林在店外调整展示架上的瓶装饮料，反复摆弄才让它们保持____。
balance:1.hook: Then a cyclist clipped the edge of the table on the way by.
balance:1.line: Move the big bottles to the back and the stand will *balance*.

sentences.en: Lin set up a small folding table outside to test a display stand for bottled drinks.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在门外支起一张小折叠桌，想要测试一个装瓶饮料的展示架。

sentences.en: The bottles kept sliding.
sentences.cn: 瓶子老是滑下来。

sentences.en: She shifted them left, then right, then added a rubber mat underneath.
sentences.cn: 她把它们往左挪，再往右挪，最后在下面垫了一块橡胶垫。

sentences.en: Finally, the whole row held its *balance* perfectly, even when a bus rumbled past.

baby:1.en: A young father pushed a stroller past the new shop and slowed down. His *baby* was asleep inside, one small fist curled around a soft toy. The man looked at the 'opening next week' sign and whispered, so as not to wake her, 'good, we live just around the corner.'
baby:1.cnHint: 一位年轻爸爸推着婴儿车路过新店，看到开业告示后轻声说了一句话，没有吵醒____。
baby:1.hook: He came back alone that evening and stood there for a long time.
baby:1.line: Keep your voice down — there is a *baby* sleeping right there.

sentences.en: A young father pushed a stroller past the new shop and slowed down.
sentences.cn: 一个年轻父亲推着婴儿车经过这家新店，放慢了脚步。

sentences.en: His *baby* was asleep inside, one small fist curled around a soft toy.
The man looked at the 'opening next week' sign and whispered, so as not to wake her, 'good, we live just around the corner.'
sentences.cn: 这个男人看了看"下周开业"的牌子，压低了声音，"好啊，我们就住在转角附近。"

store:1.en: The Manager stopped me outside the new corner lot and pointed at the empty building. 'We are opening a second *store* here next month,' he said proudly, sweeping his arm wide. Painters were already mixing colours on the pavement. I stared at the peeling walls and wondered who had agreed to this plan.
store:1.cnHint: 店长在街角空房子前告诉我们，新____要开张了。
store:1.hook: But the building permit was nowhere to be found.
store:1.line: 'This *store* will be bigger and better than the first one.'

sentences.en: The Manager stopped me outside the new corner lot and pointed at the empty building.
sentences.cn: 店长在新转角空铺外头拦住我，指着那栋空楼。

sentences.en: 'We are opening a second *store* here next month,' he said proudly, sweeping his arm wide.
Painters were already mixing colours on the pavement.
sentences.cn: 油漆工已经在人行道上调色了。

sentences.en: I stared at the peeling walls and wondered who had agreed to this plan.
sentences.cn: 我盯着那些剥落的墙皮，想知道谁同意了这个计划。

budget:1.en: Tang spread a large sheet of paper on the bonnet of the Manager's old car. Columns of numbers covered every corner. 'The *budget* for the new branch is already gone,' Tang whispered, tapping the bottom line with one finger. Passing scooters drowned out the Manager's reply, but his face said everything.
budget:1.cnHint: 同事在路边发现新分店的____已经花光了。
budget:1.hook: Someone had been buying far too many decorative plants.
budget:1.line: 'Our *budget* ran out before we even bought the shelves.'

sentences.en: Tang spread a large sheet of paper on the bonnet of the Manager's old car.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在店长那辆旧车的引擎盖上铺开了一大张纸。

sentences.en: Columns of numbers covered every corner.
sentences.cn: 数字栏目覆盖了四面八方。

sentences.en: 'The *budget* for the new branch is already gone,' Tang whispered, tapping the bottom line with one finger.
Passing scooters drowned out the Manager's reply, but his face said everything.
sentences.cn: 路过的摩托车淹没了店长的回答声，但他的脸说明了一切。

grant:1.en: Lin arrived waving a thin envelope above her head. 'The city gave us a small *grant* to help with the new branch,' she announced on the pavement outside our shop. The Manager grabbed the letter, read it twice, and let out a long breath. The amount was helpful, though nowhere near enough.
grant:1.cnHint: 竞争对手兴冲冲地带来了一份城市____的消息。
grant:1.hook: Lin's smile suggested she already knew how to spend it.
grant:1.line: 'A city *grant* like this does not come around very often.'

sentences.en: Lin arrived waving a thin envelope above her head.
sentences.cn: 林拎着一个薄薄的信封，挥舞着冲进来。

sentences.en: 'The city gave us a small *grant* to help with the new branch,' she announced on the pavement outside our shop.
The Manager grabbed the letter, read it twice, and let out a long breath.
sentences.cn: 店长抓起那封信，读了两遍，长长地呼出一口气。

sentences.en: The amount was helpful, though nowhere near enough.
sentences.cn: 那笔钱有帮助，但远远不够。

hospital:1.en: A tired nurse in a white coat stopped at our pavement display of snacks on his way home from the *hospital* across the road. He bought four rice balls without a word. I noticed bandages on his left hand and mud on his shoes. Tang said the night shift there ended at exactly three in the morning.
hospital:1.cnHint: 一位从对面____下班的护士在门口买了东西。
hospital:1.hook: He would return every night at the same hour, saying nothing.
hospital:1.line: 'I walk past from the *hospital* and your light is always on.'

sentences.en: A tired nurse in a white coat stopped at our pavement display of snacks on his way home from the *hospital* across the road.
He bought four rice balls without a word.
sentences.cn: 他一句话没说就买了四个饭团。

sentences.en: I noticed bandages on his left hand and mud on his shoes.
sentences.cn: 我注意到他左手上有绷带，鞋上有泥土。

sentences.en: Tang said the night shift there ended at exactly three in the morning.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说那家医院的夜班恰好在早上三点结束。

island:1.en: An old woman set up a small card table on the pavement and laid out hand-painted postcards of a green *island* surrounded by blue water. She told me she had grown up there and painted every card from memory. Tourists stopped, pointed, and smiled. I bought one without asking the price.
island:1.cnHint: 一位老奶奶在街边摆出一张画满故乡____的明信片摊。
island:1.hook: The island on the cards did not appear on any map I knew.
island:1.line: 'Every card shows the *island* where I was born and raised.'

sentences.en: An old woman set up a small card table on the pavement and laid out hand-painted postcards of a green *island* surrounded by blue water.
She told me she had grown up there and painted every card from memory.
sentences.cn: 她告诉我她在那个岛上长大，每一张卡都是凭记忆画出来的。

sentences.en: Tourists stopped, pointed, and smiled.
sentences.cn: 游客们停下来，指着，微笑。

sentences.en: I bought one without asking the price.
sentences.cn: 我没问价格就买了一张。

native:1.en: Tang introduced me to a cheerful man leaning on the lamp-post outside. 'He is a *native* of this neighbourhood,' Tang said. 'He remembers when this corner was a cabbage field.' The man laughed and patted the wall of our shop as if greeting an old friend. I felt like the only stranger on the street.
native:1.cnHint: 同事向我介绍了一位街区____居民，他还记得这里以前的样子。
native:1.hook: He then mentioned something strange buried beneath the old field.
native:1.line: 'As a *native* here, I have seen this corner change three times.'

sentences.en: Tang introduced me to a cheerful man leaning on the lamp-post outside.
sentences.cn: 阿糖给我介绍了一个靠在路灯外的开朗男人。

sentences.en: 'He is a *native* of this neighbourhood,' Tang said.
'He remembers when this corner was a cabbage field.'
sentences.cn: "他还记得这个转角曾经是一片白菜地。"

sentences.en: The man laughed and patted the wall of our shop as if greeting an old friend.
sentences.cn: 那个男人笑了，像问候老朋友一样拍了拍我们店的墙。

sentences.en: I felt like the only stranger on the street.
sentences.cn: 我感觉自己像这条街上唯一的陌生人。

tradition:1.en: A group of elderly neighbours gathered on the pavement at dawn, doing slow morning exercises in neat rows. Tang told me it was a long-standing *tradition* on this street, going back forty years. The Manager watched from the doorway, nodding. I joined the back row, stumbled twice, and received polite applause anyway.
tradition:1.cnHint: 同事告诉我街边的晨练是这条街几十年来的____。
tradition:1.hook: One of the elders then invited me to lead next Friday.
tradition:1.line: 'This morning exercise is a *tradition* nobody wants to break.'

sentences.en: A group of elderly neighbours gathered on the pavement at dawn, doing slow morning exercises in neat rows.
sentences.cn: 一群年长的邻居在黎明时在人行道上聚集，排成整齐的队伍做着缓慢的晨练。

sentences.en: Tang told me it was a long-standing *tradition* on this street, going back forty years.
The Manager watched from the doorway, nodding.
sentences.cn: 店长在门口看着，不住地点头。

sentences.en: I joined the back row, stumbled twice, and received polite applause anyway.
sentences.cn: 我加入了最后一排，绊倒了两次，但还是得到了礼貌的掌声。

africa:1.en: A tall student stood at the corner reading a map, his backpack covered in small flag patches. Lin pointed out one patch of the continent of *Africa* and said he had just returned from a teaching programme there. He was trying to find a place to stay for one night. The Manager glanced at our stockroom and nodded slowly.
africa:1.cnHint: 一位刚从____回来的学生在街角迷了路，店长似乎有个主意。
africa:1.hook: The stockroom had not been empty for a very good reason.
africa:1.line: 'I spent three months in *Africa* and just arrived back tonight.'

sentences.en: A tall student stood at the corner reading a map, his backpack covered in small flag patches.
sentences.cn: 一个高个子学生站在转角读地图，背包上贴满了小旗帜补丁。

sentences.en: Lin pointed out one patch of the continent of *Africa* and said he had just returned from a teaching programme there.
He was trying to find a place to stay for one night.
sentences.cn: 他想找个地方住一晚。

sentences.en: The Manager glanced at our stockroom and nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 店长看了看我们的库房，慢慢地点了点头。

teenager:1.en: Just after midnight, a *teenager* in a school uniform pushed open the door and dropped a heavy bag on the counter. 'Just five minutes of warm air, please,' he said. He looked exhausted, like someone who had been studying since dawn. I handed him a hot drink and asked nothing.
teenager:1.cnHint: 一个深夜还穿着校服的____走进店里，只想借一点暖气歇脚。
teenager:1.hook: But his uniform had the wrong school's name on it.
teenager:1.line: 'I'm only a *teenager*, but I work harder than most adults I know.'

sentences.en: Just after midnight, a *teenager* in a school uniform pushed open the door and dropped a heavy bag on the counter.
'Just five minutes of warm air, please,' he said.
sentences.cn: "就五分钟的温暖空气，拜托了，"他说。

sentences.en: He looked exhausted, like someone who had been studying since dawn.
sentences.cn: 他看起来筋疲力尽，像是从天亮就开始学习的人。

sentences.en: I handed him a hot drink and asked nothing.
sentences.cn: 我递给他一杯热饮，什么都没问。

patient:1.en: The Manager stood outside in the cold, waiting for the new sign to be delivered. An hour passed. Then two. He did not check his phone or pace the pavement. He was remarkably *patient*, arms folded, eyes calm, watching the empty street as though he had all the time in the world.
patient:1.cnHint: 店长在寒风中____地等候新招牌送到，一动不动地站了好几个小时。
patient:1.hook: The delivery van that finally arrived was carrying the wrong sign.
patient:1.line: 'You have to be *patient* when you run a shop — rushing breaks more than it fixes.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside in the cold, waiting for the new sign to be delivered.
sentences.cn: 店长在冷风中站在门外，等着新招牌的送达。

sentences.en: An hour passed.
sentences.cn: 一个小时过去了。

sentences.en: Then two.
sentences.cn: 然后是两个小时。

sentences.en: He did not check his phone or pace the pavement.
sentences.cn: 他没有查看手机，也没有在人行道上踱步。

sentences.en: He was remarkably *patient*, arms folded, eyes calm, watching the empty street as though he had all the time in the world.

classroom:1.en: Tang pointed up at the empty building across the street. 'That used to be a *classroom*,' she said, 'where I failed my first English test.' Now the windows were dark and the door was sealed with tape. She said it quietly, like she was reading a small sad notice pinned to her own heart.
classroom:1.cnHint: 唐指着对面废弃的建筑，说那里曾是她经历失败的____。
classroom:1.hook: She then slipped a folded test paper out of her pocket.
classroom:1.line: 'Every *classroom* I ever sat in smelled exactly like chalk and cold tea.'

sentences.en: Tang pointed up at the empty building across the street.
sentences.cn: 阿糖抬头指向对面那栋空荡荡的楼。

sentences.en: 'That used to be a *classroom*,' she said, 'where I failed my first English test.'
Now the windows were dark and the door was sealed with tape.
sentences.cn: 现在窗户都黑了，门被胶带封死了。

sentences.en: She said it quietly, like she was reading a small sad notice pinned to her own heart.
sentences.cn: 她说得很轻，像是在读一张钉在自己心上的小小讣告。

vehicle:1.en: A large *vehicle* blocked the pavement outside at two in the morning, engine running, no driver in sight. I stepped out to look. Boxes were stacked in the back — all labelled with our store's address but a branch number I did not recognise. I stood in the yellow streetlight, very still.
vehicle:1.cnHint: 深夜一辆无人驾驶的____停在门外，车里装着写有陌生分店编号的箱子。
vehicle:1.hook: Then the engine cut out, and a phone inside one of the boxes began to ring.
vehicle:1.line: 'Every *vehicle* that stops here at night makes me a little nervous, honestly.'

sentences.en: A large *vehicle* blocked the pavement outside at two in the morning, engine running, no driver in sight.
I stepped out to look.
sentences.cn: 我走出去看。

sentences.en: Boxes were stacked in the back — all labelled with our store's address but a branch number I did not recognise.
sentences.cn: 后面堆着纸箱——都写着我们店的地址，但是个我没见过的分店号。

sentences.en: I stood in the yellow streetlight, very still.
sentences.cn: 我站在黄色的街灯下，一动不动。

remote:1.en: Lin arrived just before three, shaking rain off her jacket. 'The new branch site is confirmed,' she said, spreading a map on the counter. She tapped a spot far from the city centre, surrounded by empty land. 'It is quite *remote*,' I said. She smiled in a way that meant she already knew that.
remote:1.cnHint: 林摊开地图，指着新分店选址——一个离市区非常____的地方。
remote:1.hook: She folded the map before I could read the street name.
remote:1.line: '*Remote* is fine — the quieter the street, the more loyal the customers.'

sentences.en: Lin arrived just before three, shaking rain off her jacket.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在快三点时到了，一边甩掉夹克上的雨水。

sentences.en: 'The new branch site is confirmed,' she said, spreading a map on the counter.
sentences.cn: 她说："新分店的地址定了。"铺开一张地图放在柜台上。

sentences.en: She tapped a spot far from the city centre, surrounded by empty land.
sentences.cn: 她敲了敲一个远离市中心的地点，周围都是空地。

sentences.en: 'It is quite *remote*,' I said.
She smiled in a way that meant she already knew that.
sentences.cn: 她笑了，那种笑说明她早就知道了。

zoo:1.en: A small boy pressed his face to our window at six in the morning, fogging the glass with his breath. He had a paper wristband on that said '*zoo*' in green letters. He had clearly been walking a long time. He looked at the shelf of toy animals we kept by the door and went very quiet.
zoo:1.cnHint: 一个戴着____门票手环的小男孩，大清早独自出现在店门口。
zoo:1.hook: He knew every animal's name but could not say where his parents were.
zoo:1.line: 'The *zoo* lets you in free before seven — that part was great, at least.'

sentences.en: A small boy pressed his face to our window at six in the morning, fogging the glass with his breath.
sentences.cn: 一个小男孩一大早就把脸贴在我们的窗玻璃上，呼出的气雾蒙了一层。

sentences.en: He had a paper wristband on that said '*zoo*' in green letters.
He had clearly been walking a long time.
sentences.cn: 他显然已经走了很久。

sentences.en: He looked at the shelf of toy animals we kept by the door and went very quiet.
sentences.cn: 他看着我们放在门边的玩具动物架，忽然安静了下来。

card:1.en: A woman in a long coat asked me to hold a small envelope at the counter. 'Someone will come for it,' she said. Inside, I could see the corner of a *card* — hand-drawn flowers, careful writing. She was gone before I could ask a single question. The envelope sat there all night, uncollected.
card:1.cnHint: 一位神秘女士托我保管一个信封，里面露出一张手绘____的一角。
card:1.hook: At closing time, I noticed the name on the front was mine.
card:1.line: 'Leave the *card* exactly where it is — they will know where to find it.'

sentences.en: A woman in a long coat asked me to hold a small envelope at the counter.
sentences.cn: 一个穿长外套的女人让我在柜台上帮她拿着一个小信封。

sentences.en: 'Someone will come for it,' she said.
sentences.cn: 她说："会有人来取。"

sentences.en: Inside, I could see the corner of a *card* — hand-drawn flowers, careful writing.
She was gone before I could ask a single question.
sentences.cn: 她在我还没来得及问一个问题前就走了。

sentences.en: The envelope sat there all night, uncollected.
sentences.cn: 那个信封整晚都放在那儿，没人来收。

gene:1.en: The Manager and his sister stood side by side in the morning light, arguing about where the new branch should go. They had the same frown, the same folded arms, the same stubborn tilt of the chin. 'It must be a *gene*,' Tang whispered from behind the coffee machine. I decided not to laugh out loud.
gene:1.cnHint: 店长和他妹妹争执时，唐悄悄说他们固执的样子简直像同一个____。
gene:1.hook: Then his sister turned and asked me to cast the deciding vote.
gene:1.line: 'Stubbornness might just be a *gene* in our family — Mum is exactly the same.'

sentences.en: The Manager and his sister stood side by side in the morning light, arguing about where the new branch should go.
sentences.cn: 店长和他的妹妹肩并肩站在早晨的光线里，在新分店该开在哪儿的问题上吵架。

sentences.en: They had the same frown, the same folded arms, the same stubborn tilt of the chin.
sentences.cn: 他们有着同样的皱眉，同样交叉的胳膊，同样倔强的下巴角度。

sentences.en: 'It must be a *gene*,' Tang whispered from behind the coffee machine.
I decided not to laugh out loud.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在咖啡机后面小声说："这肯定是遗传。"

content:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, arms crossed, studying the new sign above the door. He had spent three days picking the right colour. Now he stepped back, tilted his head, and smiled. He looked *content* — the way a person looks when a long effort finally lands exactly right. I watched from inside, holding a mop, feeling oddly proud too.
content:1.cnHint: 店长在门外看着新招牌，脸上露出____的神情。
content:1.hook: But across the street, someone was taking photos of the sign.
content:1.line: 'I am finally *content* with how this place looks,' the Manager said softly.

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, arms crossed, studying the new sign above the door.
sentences.cn: 店长站在人行道上，两臂交叉，盯着门上新挂的招牌。

sentences.en: He had spent three days picking the right colour.
sentences.cn: 他花了三天时间挑选合适的颜色。

sentences.en: Now he stepped back, tilted his head, and smiled.
sentences.cn: 现在他往后退了一步，歪了歪头，笑了。

sentences.en: He looked *content* — the way a person looks when a long effort finally lands exactly right.
I watched from inside, holding a mop, feeling oddly proud too.
sentences.cn: 我从里面看着他，拿着拖把，心里也奇怪地感到骄傲。

divide:1.en: The Manager paced the pavement outside, measuring with his feet. He wanted to *divide* the front step into a waiting zone and a pick-up zone with just a strip of yellow tape. Tang watched from the doorway, trying not to laugh. I handed the Manager the tape. He laid it down with the focus of a person building something important.
divide:1.cnHint: 店长用黄色胶带把门前的台阶____成两个区域。
divide:1.hook: By midnight, someone had peeled up one end of the tape.
divide:1.line: 'We need to *divide* the space so customers stop bumping into each other,' the Manager said.

sentences.en: The Manager paced the pavement outside, measuring with his feet.
sentences.cn: 店长在人行道上踱步，用脚测量距离。

sentences.en: He wanted to *divide* the front step into a waiting zone and a pick-up zone with just a strip of yellow tape.
Tang watched from the doorway, trying not to laugh.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在门口看着，努力忍住不笑。

sentences.en: I handed the Manager the tape.
sentences.cn: 我把胶带递给了店长。

sentences.en: He laid it down with the focus of a person building something important.
sentences.cn: 他铺下去的时候很专注，就像在铺设什么重要的东西。

generate:1.en: The Manager hammered a small chalkboard sign into the flower box beside the door. 'Daily special — one new item every night,' he announced. His plan was to *generate* fresh interest from people walking past after midnight. Tang gave me a look that said this might actually work. By two in the morning, four strangers had stopped to read it.
generate:1.cnHint: 店长在门口立了小黑板，希望每晚____新的客流。
generate:1.hook: One of those strangers asked a question none of us could answer.
generate:1.line: 'A good sign outside will *generate* more foot traffic,' the Manager said firmly.

sentences.en: The Manager hammered a small chalkboard sign into the flower box beside the door.
sentences.cn: 店长在门边花盆旁边的黑板牌上敲了几下钉子。

sentences.en: 'Daily special — one new item every night,' he announced.
sentences.cn: 他宣布说："每天特价——每晚一款新品。"

sentences.en: His plan was to *generate* fresh interest from people walking past after midnight.
Tang gave me a look that said this might actually work.
sentences.cn: 阿糖给了我一个眼神，说这事儿说不定真能成。

sentences.en: By two in the morning, four strangers had stopped to read it.
sentences.cn: 到了凌晨两点，已经有四个陌生人停下来看了。

operate:1.en: Lin appeared on the pavement across the street, turning a key in the door of the empty shop unit opposite. I had not noticed that unit before. Tang leaned out of our doorway and whispered that Lin had been planning to *operate* a small store there for months. The Manager heard this from inside and went very quiet for a moment.
operate:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林打开对面空铺子的门，打算在那里____一家小店。
operate:1.hook: The Manager then picked up his phone and made a call.
operate:1.line: 'I plan to *operate* the new place seven days a week,' Lin said with a calm smile.

sentences.en: Lin appeared on the pavement across the street, turning a key in the door of the empty shop unit opposite.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林出现在对面人行道上，转动着对面那个空店铺单元门上的钥匙。

sentences.en: I had not noticed that unit before.
sentences.cn: 我之前没注意到那个店铺。

sentences.en: Tang leaned out of our doorway and whispered that Lin had been planning to *operate* a small store there for months.
The Manager heard this from inside and went very quiet for a moment.
sentences.cn: 店长从里面听到这些，安静了一会儿。

properly:1.en: Before the Manager arrived for his morning check, Tang and I rushed to arrange the new outdoor display stand *properly* — bottles in a straight line, price cards facing forward, nothing leaning. We finished one second before the door opened. The Manager looked at the stand, then at us, then nodded once. That single nod felt like a certificate.
properly:1.cnHint: 我和阿糖赶在店长到来前把门外展示架____地整理好。
properly:1.hook: The Manager then pointed at one bottle we had missed.
properly:1.line: 'If you set things up *properly* outside, customers trust the whole store,' Tang said.

sentences.en: Before the Manager arrived for his morning check, Tang and I rushed to arrange the new outdoor display stand *properly* — bottles in a straight line, price cards facing forward, nothing leaning.
We finished one second before the door opened.
sentences.cn: 我们在门打开前一秒钟搞完了。

sentences.en: The Manager looked at the stand, then at us, then nodded once.
sentences.cn: 店长看了看那个架子，又看了看我们，然后点了一下头。

sentences.en: That single nod felt like a certificate.
sentences.cn: 那单单一个点头感觉就像一张证书。

render:1.en: Rain started just as the Manager finished taping a new poster to the outside wall. Within a minute, the ink began to run. The water did not *render* the whole poster unreadable — the price and the arrow stayed clear — but the cheerful drawing of a rice ball melted into a soft blur. Tang bit her lip. I offered to reprint it.
render:1.cnHint: 突如其来的雨水把门外的海报____得模糊不清。
render:1.hook: The Manager said to leave it, and gave no reason why.
render:1.line: 'A little rain should not *render* our hard work useless,' the Manager said quietly.

sentences.en: Rain started just as the Manager finished taping a new poster to the outside wall.
sentences.cn: 店长刚贴完外墙上的新海报，雨就下了起来。

sentences.en: Within a minute, the ink began to run.
sentences.cn: 不到一分钟，墨水就开始晕开了。

sentences.en: The water did not *render* the whole poster unreadable — the price and the arrow stayed clear — but the cheerful drawing of a rice ball melted into a soft blur.
Tang bit her lip.
sentences.cn: 阿糖咬着嘴唇。

sentences.en: I offered to reprint it.
sentences.cn: 我主动说我来重新打印一张。

resolve:1.en: Tang and I stood on the pavement watching Lin measure the frontage of the new shop across the road. I felt uncertain. Tang, however, had a look of calm *resolve* — chin up, arms loose at her sides. 'We have been here longer,' she said simply. She walked back inside and began rearranging the window display with fresh energy.
resolve:1.cnHint: 看到对面的竞争对手，阿糖脸上却显出一种____的神情。
resolve:1.hook: Lin glanced over and gave Tang a small, knowing nod.
resolve:1.line: 'Our *resolve* to do better is worth more than any new sign,' Tang said.

sentences.en: Tang and I stood on the pavement watching Lin measure the frontage of the new shop across the road.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我站在人行道上，看着隔壁咖啡店的林测量对面新店的门面宽度。

sentences.en: I felt uncertain.
sentences.cn: 我心里没底。

sentences.en: Tang, however, had a look of calm *resolve* — chin up, arms loose at her sides.
'We have been here longer,' she said simply.
sentences.cn: "我们在这儿的时间更长，"她简单地说。

sentences.en: She walked back inside and began rearranging the window display with fresh energy.
sentences.cn: 她走回店里，干劲十足地重新布置起橱窗。

seemingly:1.en: Lin stood outside the new shop, *seemingly* relaxed — chatting with a delivery driver, laughing easily, checking nothing. But I noticed Lin's eyes move to our window every thirty seconds. Tang noticed too. We said nothing to each other. We just made sure the display looked perfect, the lights were bright, and the door was wide open.
seemingly:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林____很悠闲地站在对面，其实眼神一直瞟向我们这边。
seemingly:1.hook: That night Lin came in and bought a coffee without a word.
seemingly:1.line: 'Lin is *seemingly* calm, but watch the eyes,' Tang whispered to me.

sentences.en: Lin stood outside the new shop, *seemingly* relaxed — chatting with a delivery driver, laughing easily, checking nothing.
But I noticed Lin's eyes move to our window every thirty seconds.
sentences.cn: 但我注意到林的眼睛每三十秒就往我们的窗口看一次。

sentences.en: Tang noticed too.
sentences.cn: 阿糖也注意到了。

sentences.en: We said nothing to each other.
sentences.cn: 我们彼此什么都没说。

sentences.en: We just made sure the display looked perfect, the lights were bright, and the door was wide open.
sentences.cn: 我们只是确保橱窗看起来完美，灯亮得很足，门开得很敞。

childhood:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, staring at the empty lot. 'This corner,' he said quietly, 'is where I used to buy ice pops after school.' His *childhood* memory of this street was exactly why he chose it. I watched his face soften in a way I had never seen before.
childhood:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店选址前，回忆起他在这条街度过的____时光。
childhood:1.hook: Then he pointed to the wall and said, 'Dig carefully.'
childhood:1.line: 'This street holds my *childhood*, so this is where we build.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, staring at the empty lot.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新分店的空地前，盯着那片空荡荡的地方。

sentences.en: 'This corner,' he said quietly, 'is where I used to buy ice pops after school.'
sentences.cn: "这个角落，"他轻声说，"是我放学后买冰棍的地方。"

sentences.en: His *childhood* memory of this street was exactly why he chose it.
I watched his face soften in a way I had never seen before.
sentences.cn: 我看着他的脸柔和下来，这是我从未见过的样子。

equal:1.en: Lin and I carried supply boxes from the truck to the new branch entrance. She counted every trip with sharp eyes. After an hour she stopped and said the work was not *equal* — she had made twelve trips and I had made nine. I had no argument. I picked up two boxes at once.
equal:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林搬货时发现两人的工作量不____，当场指出来。
equal:1.hook: She smiled, but her next words were not a compliment.
equal:1.line: 'Twelve against nine is not *equal*, so carry two boxes next time.'

sentences.en: Lin and I carried supply boxes from the truck to the new branch entrance.
sentences.cn: 林和我从卡车上往新分店的入口搬供应箱。

sentences.en: She counted every trip with sharp eyes.
sentences.cn: 她用犀利的眼神数着每一趟。

sentences.en: After an hour she stopped and said the work was not *equal* — she had made twelve trips and I had made nine.
I had no argument.
sentences.cn: 我没有异议。

sentences.en: I picked up two boxes at once.
sentences.cn: 我一次拿起两个箱子。

inspire:1.en: A small girl stopped outside the new branch site and watched the workers paste the bright store sign onto the wall. 'I want to work in a place like that one day,' she told her mother. The Manager overheard her and turned to me. 'Moments like that *inspire* me to do this right,' he said.
inspire:1.cnHint: 一个小女孩在店外驻足，她的话深深____了店长。
inspire:1.hook: The girl left, but the Manager wrote something down in his notebook.
inspire:1.line: 'Little moments like that truly *inspire* me to keep going.'

sentences.en: A small girl stopped outside the new branch site and watched the workers paste the bright store sign onto the wall.
sentences.cn: 一个小女孩停在新分店的门前，看着工人们把亮晶晶的店招贴到墙上。

sentences.en: 'I want to work in a place like that one day,' she told her mother.
sentences.cn: "我长大了也想在这样的地方工作，"她对妈妈说。

sentences.en: The Manager overheard her and turned to me.
sentences.cn: 店长听见了，转向我。

sentences.en: 'Moments like that *inspire* me to do this right,' he said.

narrow:1.en: The delivery truck could not park near the new branch because the side road was too *narrow* for it to turn. The driver leaned out and shook his head. We ended up carrying every box by hand from the main street, four trips each, under the bright morning sun.
narrow:1.cnHint: 送货车因为小路太____，无法靠近新分店，大家只能徒步搬运。
narrow:1.hook: On the last trip, Tang found one box had already been opened.
narrow:1.line: 'That road is too *narrow*; we carry everything by hand today.'

sentences.en: The delivery truck could not park near the new branch because the side road was too *narrow* for it to turn.
The driver leaned out and shook his head.
sentences.cn: 司机探出头，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: We ended up carrying every box by hand from the main street, four trips each, under the bright morning sun.
sentences.cn: 我们最后只能一个一个地从大街上手工搬每一个箱子，每人四趟，顶着炽烈的晨阳。

quantity:1.en: Outside the new branch, Tang ticked items off a clipboard as workers unloaded the truck. She stopped and frowned. The *quantity* of bottled water on the list was eighty, but only fifty-three bottles sat on the pavement. She called the supplier at once, her voice calm but very firm.
quantity:1.cnHint: 阿糖在门外清点货物，发现瓶装水的____对不上单据。
quantity:1.hook: The supplier's answer made Tang go very quiet for a moment.
quantity:1.line: 'The *quantity* on this sheet is eighty, but I count fifty-three.'

sentences.en: Outside the new branch, Tang ticked items off a clipboard as workers unloaded the truck.
sentences.cn: 在新分店外面，阿糖拿着一张清单，一边打勾一边看着工人们卸货。

sentences.en: She stopped and frowned.
sentences.cn: 她停了下来，皱起了眉头。

sentences.en: The *quantity* of bottled water on the list was eighty, but only fifty-three bottles sat on the pavement.
She called the supplier at once, her voice calm but very firm.
sentences.cn: 她立刻给供应商打了电话，声音平静但很坚定。

sustainable:1.en: The Manager unrolled a poster on the pavement outside the new branch. It showed bins for paper, plastic, and glass. 'A store that wastes nothing is a *sustainable* store,' he told the small crowd of curious neighbours. One old man nodded slowly. I made a note to learn the recycling rules before opening day.
sustainable:1.cnHint: 店长在店外向邻居们介绍新分店的环保理念，强调经营要____。
sustainable:1.hook: The old man then asked a question nobody had an easy answer for.
sustainable:1.line: 'A shop that wastes nothing is a *sustainable* shop, neighbours.'

sentences.en: The Manager unrolled a poster on the pavement outside the new branch.
sentences.cn: 店长在新分店门前的人行道上铺开一张海报。

sentences.en: It showed bins for paper, plastic, and glass.
sentences.cn: 上面分别画着纸张、塑料和玻璃的垃圾桶。

sentences.en: 'A store that wastes nothing is a *sustainable* store,' he told the small crowd of curious neighbours.
One old man nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 一位老大爷慢慢地点了点头。

sentences.en: I made a note to learn the recycling rules before opening day.
sentences.cn: 我记了个备忘录，提醒自己在开业前要学会回收规则。

delay:1.en: Rain started just as we were about to hang the new branch sign above the door. The Manager looked at the sky and sighed. 'We will *delay* the sign until tomorrow,' he said. We covered the sign with a cloth and stood under the awning, watching the street fill with puddles and hurrying umbrellas.
delay:1.cnHint: 突然下起雨来，店长决定____招牌的安装工作到明天。
delay:1.hook: Under one umbrella, a stranger paused and stared at the covered sign.
delay:1.line: 'Rain means we *delay* the sign — cover it carefully, please.'

sentences.en: Rain started just as we were about to hang the new branch sign above the door.
sentences.cn: 我们正要挂新分店门上的招牌时，开始下雨了。

sentences.en: The Manager looked at the sky and sighed.
sentences.cn: 店长抬头看了看天，叹了口气。

sentences.en: 'We will *delay* the sign until tomorrow,' he said.
We covered the sign with a cloth and stood under the awning, watching the street fill with puddles and hurrying umbrellas.
sentences.cn: 我们用布盖住招牌，站在遮阳棚下，看着街道积满了水洼，行人打着伞匆匆忙忙地走过。

identity:1.en: A reporter stopped me outside the new branch and asked whether this store had a clear *identity* that set it apart from every other convenience store on the street. I hesitated, then pointed to the handwritten menu in the window and the recycling bins by the door. She wrote something down and smiled.
identity:1.cnHint: 一位记者在门外问新分店有什么能体现自身____的特色。
identity:1.hook: Her article, the Manager later told us, was already half-written.
identity:1.line: 'Every good shop needs an *identity* that people remember clearly.'

sentences.en: A reporter stopped me outside the new branch and asked whether this store had a clear *identity* that set it apart from every other convenience store on the street.
I hesitated, then pointed to the handwritten menu in the window and the recycling bins by the door.
sentences.cn: 我犹豫了一下，指向窗里的手写菜单和门边的垃圾分类桶。

sentences.en: She wrote something down and smiled.
sentences.cn: 她写下了什么，笑了笑。

modern:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, pointing at the glass front. 'This is going to be *modern*,' he said, arms wide. Tang and I looked at the old stone wall next to it and then at each other. The building did not look ready to agree with him.
modern:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店选址前，自豪地描述他心中____的新店。
modern:1.hook: Then Tang noticed the sign still on the door.
modern:1.line: 'This store will be *modern* — clean lines, bright lights, the works.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, pointing at the glass front.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新分店的工地前，指着玻璃店面。

sentences.en: 'This is going to be *modern*,' he said, arms wide.
Tang and I looked at the old stone wall next to it and then at each other.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我看了看它旁边的老石墙，又互相看了一眼。

sentences.en: The building did not look ready to agree with him.
sentences.cn: 这栋楼好像不太想同意他的看法。

officer:1.en: A city *officer* in a dark jacket stopped in front of our new branch sign, clipboard in hand. He read every word slowly, then wrote something down. The Manager hurried out from inside, smoothing his shirt, his smile about three sizes too big for his face.
officer:1.cnHint: 一名____来到新分店门前，仔细查看招牌，店长赶紧跑出来迎接。
officer:1.hook: The officer tore off a yellow sheet and held it out.
officer:1.line: 'Good morning, *officer* — can I offer you a free coffee?'

sentences.en: A city *officer* in a dark jacket stopped in front of our new branch sign, clipboard in hand.
He read every word slowly, then wrote something down.
sentences.cn: 他逐字逐句地读了一遍，然后写下了什么。

sentences.en: The Manager hurried out from inside, smoothing his shirt, his smile about three sizes too big for his face.
sentences.cn: 店长从里面匆匆跑了出来，拉平衣服，脸上的笑容大得不成比例。

convince:1.en: Lin stood across the street, arms crossed, watching workers hang our new branch sign. I walked over to try to *convince* her the two stores could share the same block. She listened, then looked at the sign, then at me. 'You believe that?' she asked. I paused a little too long.
convince:1.cnHint: 我试图____隔壁咖啡店的林，两家店开在同一条街上没有问题。
convince:1.hook: She pulled out her phone and made a call.
convince:1.line: 'Nothing you say will *convince* me this is good for either of us.'

sentences.en: Lin stood across the street, arms crossed, watching workers hang our new branch sign.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在街对面，双臂交叉，看着工人挂我们新店的招牌。

sentences.en: I walked over to try to *convince* her the two stores could share the same block.
She listened, then looked at the sign, then at me.
sentences.cn: 她听了听，然后看看招牌，又看看我。

sentences.en: 'You believe that?' she asked.
sentences.cn: "你真的相信这个？"她问道。

sentences.en: I paused a little too long.
sentences.cn: 我停顿了有点太久。

directly:1.en: The Manager called me *directly* on my day off and said the branch door lock was broken. I was still in my pyjamas. Tang had the day off too, so it was just me, a bus ride, and a screwdriver I was not sure how to use. The street was very quiet and very cold.
directly:1.cnHint: 店长____打电话给我，让我去处理新分店的门锁问题。
directly:1.hook: When I arrived, the door was already wide open.
directly:1.line: 'I'm calling you *directly* because Tang is not picking up.'

sentences.en: The Manager called me *directly* on my day off and said the branch door lock was broken.
I was still in my pyjamas.
sentences.cn: 我还穿着睡衣。

sentences.en: Tang had the day off too, so it was just me, a bus ride, and a screwdriver I was not sure how to use.
sentences.cn: 阿糖那天也休息，所以就我一个人，坐了一趟公车，带着一把我不太会用的螺丝刀。

sentences.en: The street was very quiet and very cold.
sentences.cn: 街上静得很，冷得很。

extend:1.en: The Manager decided to *extend* the awning over the new branch entrance so customers could stand outside without getting wet. He measured twice, ordered once, and the awning arrived two metres too short. We stood in the light rain looking at it. It covered exactly the recycling bin.
extend:1.cnHint: 店长决定____新分店门口的遮雨棚，结果尺寸出了问题。
extend:1.hook: A regular walked up, umbrella in hand, and said nothing.
extend:1.line: 'We need to *extend* it at least another metre — maybe two.'

sentences.en: The Manager decided to *extend* the awning over the new branch entrance so customers could stand outside without getting wet.
He measured twice, ordered once, and the awning arrived two metres too short.
sentences.cn: 他量了两次，只下了一次单，结果遮阳棚到货时短了两米。

sentences.en: We stood in the light rain looking at it.
sentences.cn: 我们站在小雨里看着它。

sentences.en: It covered exactly the recycling bin.
sentences.cn: 它正好罩住了回收桶。

rat:1.en: Tang screamed from the back of the new branch at six in the morning. I ran in to find her standing on a box, pointing at a corner. A single small *rat* sat there looking equally surprised. The Manager arrived eight minutes later, slightly out of breath, holding a broom he clearly had no plan for.
rat:1.cnHint: 阿糖在新分店后仓发现了一只____，大家都乱成一团。
rat:1.hook: The rat disappeared before anyone moved again.
rat:1.line: 'There is a *rat* back here and I am NOT dealing with it alone.'

sentences.en: Tang screamed from the back of the new branch at six in the morning.
sentences.cn: 早上六点，阿糖在新店后面尖叫。

sentences.en: I ran in to find her standing on a box, pointing at a corner.
sentences.cn: 我冲进去，发现她站在一个纸箱上，指着角落。

sentences.en: A single small *rat* sat there looking equally surprised.
The Manager arrived eight minutes later, slightly out of breath, holding a broom he clearly had no plan for.
sentences.cn: 店长八分钟后赶到，有点喘不上气来，手里拿着一把他显然没想好怎么用的扫帚。

saturday:1.en: The branch soft opening was set for *Saturday*, which the Manager said was perfect because foot traffic would be high. It rained all day. Tang and I stood near the door, handing out small flyers to three people and one dog. The dog seemed the most interested.
saturday:1.cnHint: 新分店选在____试营业，但当天的情况和预期差了很远。
saturday:1.hook: Lin's store across the street looked very busy.
saturday:1.line: 'Why did we pick *Saturday*? Everyone is at the market on Saturday.'

sentences.en: The branch soft opening was set for *Saturday*, which the Manager said was perfect because foot traffic would be high.
It rained all day.
sentences.cn: 下了一整天的雨。
