sentences.en: Tang and I stood near the door, handing out small flyers to three people and one dog.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我站在门边，把小传单发给三个人和一条狗。

sentences.en: The dog seemed the most interested.
sentences.cn: 那条狗看起来最感兴趣。

april:1.en: By *April* the branch still had no working heater, but the Manager said summer was coming so it did not matter. Tang disagreed loudly. I taped an extra layer of cardboard over the gap in the back wall and considered it a small personal win. Outside, the trees were just starting to show green.
april:1.cnHint: 到了____，新分店还没装好暖气，大家对此看法不一。
april:1.hook: Then the Manager mentioned the air-con was also not ordered yet.
april:1.line: 'It is *April* — cold in the morning still, and you want to wait?'

sentences.en: By *April* the branch still had no working heater, but the Manager said summer was coming so it did not matter.
Tang disagreed loudly.
sentences.cn: 阿糖大声反对。

sentences.en: I taped an extra layer of cardboard over the gap in the back wall and considered it a small personal win.
sentences.cn: 我在后墙的缝隙上贴了一层纸板，当作自己的一点小胜利。

sentences.en: Outside, the trees were just starting to show green.
sentences.cn: 外面，树上开始冒出新绿。

artificial:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, frowning at a row of plastic flowers by the door. 'These look cheap,' he said. The *artificial* blooms caught no sunlight, gave no scent, and fooled nobody. A real garden would cost more, but first he needed to count what was left in the budget.
artificial:1.cnHint: 店长看着新店门口那排假花，觉得它们毫无生气，开始盘算预算还剩多少。
artificial:1.hook: Then he noticed someone had already pulled one flower out.
artificial:1.line: These *artificial* flowers make the whole entrance look fake.

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, frowning at a row of plastic flowers by the door.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新店外，皱着眉头看着门边一排塑料花。

sentences.en: 'These look cheap,' he said.
sentences.cn: "这些看起来很廉价，"他说。

sentences.en: The *artificial* blooms caught no sunlight, gave no scent, and fooled nobody.
A real garden would cost more, but first he needed to count what was left in the budget.
sentences.cn: 真的花园花费更多，但首先他得清点一下预算还剩多少。

confirm:1.en: Tang rushed out of the new branch just as the delivery truck was pulling away. She waved both arms and shouted until the driver stopped. 'I need you to *confirm* the order,' she said, holding up her clipboard. 'Three boxes of rice balls, not thirty.' The driver checked his sheet and went pale.
confirm:1.cnHint: 唐冲出新店门口，拦住送货司机，要求对方____订单数量是否正确。
confirm:1.hook: The driver's list showed a number nobody had ever written down.
confirm:1.line: Please *confirm* the rice ball count before you leave.

sentences.en: Tang rushed out of the new branch just as the delivery truck was pulling away.
sentences.cn: 配送车正要驶离的时候，阿糖冲出了新店。

sentences.en: She waved both arms and shouted until the driver stopped.
sentences.cn: 她挥舞双臂喊到司机停了下来。

sentences.en: 'I need you to *confirm* the order,' she said, holding up her clipboard.
'Three boxes of rice balls, not thirty.'
sentences.cn: "三盒饭团，不是三十盒。"

sentences.en: The driver checked his sheet and went pale.
sentences.cn: 司机看了看单子，脸色发白。

context:1.en: Lin leaned against the wall outside, reading a note the Manager had taped to the new branch door. The words alone sounded odd, but Lin had worked here long enough to understand the *context*: new staff, tight budget, and a grand opening in three days. She folded the note and slipped it into her pocket.
context:1.cnHint: 林靠在新店门外，读着店长贴的告示，凭借____理解了那些听起来奇怪的指示。
context:1.hook: The note had a second line that Lin chose not to mention.
context:1.line: You need the *context* to understand what the Manager really means.

sentences.en: Lin leaned against the wall outside, reading a note the Manager had taped to the new branch door.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林靠在外墙上，读着店长贴在新店门上的一张纸条。

sentences.en: The words alone sounded odd, but Lin had worked here long enough to understand the *context*: new staff, tight budget, and a grand opening in three days.
She folded the note and slipped it into her pocket.
sentences.cn: 她折起纸条，塞进了口袋。

date:1.en: Tang knelt on the pavement outside the new branch, turning a box of milk cartons toward the morning light. She checked every carton carefully. 'The *date* on these is tomorrow,' she called up to the Manager on the step above her. He rubbed his eyes. One day of margin was not enough for a grand opening.
date:1.cnHint: 唐在新店门外检查牛奶保质期，发现____只剩明天，立刻告诉了店长。
date:1.hook: The Manager turned the box over and found a second stamp underneath.
date:1.line: The *date* on every carton is tomorrow — that is too close.

sentences.en: Tang knelt on the pavement outside the new branch, turning a box of milk cartons toward the morning light.
sentences.cn: 阿糖跪在新店外的人行道上，把一箱牛奶朝着晨光转动。

sentences.en: She checked every carton carefully.
sentences.cn: 她仔细检查了每一盒。

sentences.en: 'The *date* on these is tomorrow,' she called up to the Manager on the step above her.
He rubbed his eyes.
sentences.cn: 他揉了揉眼睛。

sentences.en: One day of margin was not enough for a grand opening.
sentences.cn: 一天的提前量对盛大开业来说还不够。

flexible:1.en: The Manager spread a long paper schedule across the bonnet of his car, parked just outside the new branch. 'Our hours have to be *flexible* for the first month,' he told Tang, tapping the chart. 'Some mornings quiet, some nights mad busy.' Tang nodded, already doing the maths on how little sleep that left her.
flexible:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门外摊开排班表，告诉唐第一个月的上班时间必须____。
flexible:1.hook: Tang spotted her name in every single weekend box.
flexible:1.line: The schedule must stay *flexible* until we know the busy hours.

sentences.en: The Manager spread a long paper schedule across the bonnet of his car, parked just outside the new branch.
sentences.cn: 店长在停在新店外的车引盖上铺开了一张长长的纸质日程表。

sentences.en: 'Our hours have to be *flexible* for the first month,' he told Tang, tapping the chart.
'Some mornings quiet, some nights mad busy.'
sentences.cn: "有些早上客少，有些晚上忙得不行。"

sentences.en: Tang nodded, already doing the maths on how little sleep that left her.
sentences.cn: 阿糖点点头，已经在心里算着这样能睡多少觉了。

fly:1.en: A single *fly* circled the tray of sample dumplings Tang had set out on the folding table in front of the new branch. She fanned it away three times. Each time it returned. A small crowd had gathered, watching the fly more than the dumplings. Tang smiled anyway and held out a toothpick.
fly:1.cnHint: 唐在新店门外摆出试吃饺子，却有一只____一直在旁边打转，引来路人围观。
fly:1.hook: One old man in the crowd seemed to be cheering for the fly.
fly:1.line: That *fly* has been here longer than any of our customers.

sentences.en: A single *fly* circled the tray of sample dumplings Tang had set out on the folding table in front of the new branch.
She fanned it away three times.
sentences.cn: 她扇了三次。

sentences.en: Each time it returned.

sentences.cn: 我看着这条繁忙的街道，慢慢明白了为什么他总是这么谨慎地选择地点。

vacation:1.en: I had taken this night-shift job during my summer *vacation*, expecting a quiet few weeks. Instead, the Manager announced plans for a new branch and pulled everyone into the project. Tang looked just as surprised as I felt. The sleepy corner store had suddenly turned into something much busier than I had bargained for.
vacation:1.cnHint: 我只是想在____期间打份轻松的工，没想到赶上了店长决定开分店。
vacation:1.hook: The Manager then handed me a map and said, 'You scout it.'
vacation:1.line: I joined during my *vacation* — I did not sign up for this.

sentences.en: I had taken this night-shift job during my summer *vacation*, expecting a quiet few weeks.
Instead, the Manager announced plans for a new branch and pulled everyone into the project.
sentences.cn: 结果店长宣布了开新店的计划，把所有人都拉进了这个项目。

sentences.en: Tang looked just as surprised as I felt.
sentences.cn: 阿糖看起来跟我一样吃惊。

sentences.en: The sleepy corner store had suddenly turned into something much busier than I had bargained for.
sentences.cn: 这个昏昏欲睡的角落店突然变成了比我预想中忙碌得多的地方。

acquire:1.en: The Manager explained that the plan was to *acquire* the lease on the old tea shop two streets away before anyone else moved on it. Time was short. Tang nodded and immediately left to make calls. I realised this was not a casual idea — the Manager had been planning this quietly for weeks.
acquire:1.cnHint: 店长打算抢在别人前面____那家旧茶铺的租约。
acquire:1.hook: Tang came back pale-faced — someone had already called about the lease.
acquire:1.line: We need to *acquire* that lease before the end of the week.

sentences.en: The Manager explained that the plan was to *acquire* the lease on the old tea shop two streets away before anyone else moved on it.
Time was short.
sentences.cn: 时间紧迫。

sentences.en: Tang nodded and immediately left to make calls.
sentences.cn: 阿糖点了点头，立刻离开去打电话。

sentences.en: I realised this was not a casual idea — the Manager had been planning this quietly for weeks.
sentences.cn: 我意识到这不是一个随随便便的想法——店长已经安安静静地计划了好几周。

adequate:1.en: Tang measured the floor space of the candidate site and reported back. 'Storage is *adequate*, maybe just enough for our usual stock,' she said carefully. The Manager nodded, but his eyes were already measuring the back wall. I got the feeling that 'just enough' was not going to satisfy him for long.
adequate:1.cnHint: 阿糖说新店的储物空间____，勉强够用，但店长显然想要更多。
adequate:1.hook: He then asked about the basement, and Tang went very quiet.
adequate:1.line: The storage is *adequate* for now, but only just.

sentences.en: Tang measured the floor space of the candidate site and reported back.
sentences.cn: 阿糖测量了候选地点的面积，回来汇报。

sentences.en: 'Storage is *adequate*, maybe just enough for our usual stock,' she said carefully.
The Manager nodded, but his eyes were already measuring the back wall.
sentences.cn: 店长点了点头，但他的眼神已经在量那面后墙了。

sentences.en: I got the feeling that 'just enough' was not going to satisfy him for long.
sentences.cn: 我有种感觉，"刚好够"这个说法不会让他满意太久。

conventional:1.en: The Manager stood on the pavement outside the new store site, shaking his head at the empty shopfront. 'A *conventional* corner store won't survive here,' he said, pointing at the busy night market across the street. He wanted something different — something that would pull people in before they even knew why.
conventional:1.cnHint: 店长觉得在这条街开一家____的便利店根本活不下去。
conventional:1.hook: He pulled out a notebook and began writing something none of us expected.
conventional:1.line: 'A *conventional* store will just disappear into the street, trust me.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood on the pavement outside the new store site, shaking his head at the empty shopfront.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新店铺门前的人行道上，对着空荡荡的店面摇头。

sentences.en: 'A *conventional* corner store won't survive here,' he said, pointing at the busy night market across the street.
He wanted something different — something that would pull people in before they even knew why.
sentences.cn: 他想要点不一样的东西——能在人们还没反应过来前就吸引他们进来的东西。

disappear:1.en: We carried boxes of stock from the van to the new branch at dawn. One moment Tang was right beside me, arms full of instant noodles — then he seemed to *disappear* around the corner. I called his name twice. The street stayed quiet. The box he had been carrying sat alone on the kerb.
disappear:1.cnHint: 搬货时，同事突然____了，只留下一箱东西放在路边。
disappear:1.hook: When Tang finally came back, he was holding a small, folded piece of paper.
disappear:1.line: 'You can't just *disappear* like that — I nearly called the Manager!'

sentences.en: We carried boxes of stock from the van to the new branch at dawn.
sentences.cn: 天亮的时候，我们从车里往新分店搬箱子。

sentences.en: One moment Tang was right beside me, arms full of instant noodles — then he seemed to *disappear* around the corner.
I called his name twice.
sentences.cn: 我喊了他两次。

sentences.en: The street stayed quiet.
sentences.cn: 街上安静得很。

sentences.en: The box he had been carrying sat alone on the kerb.
sentences.cn: 他放下的那个箱子孤零零地坐在路边。

district:1.en: The new branch sat at the edge of the old shopping *district*, where teahouses and noodle stalls had stood for decades. Walking there for the first time, I noticed how different it felt from our quiet corner — louder, brighter, and full of people even at midnight. This part of the city never seemed to sleep.
district:1.cnHint: 新分店开在老商业____的边缘，那里热闹得连午夜都不安静。
district:1.hook: Somewhere in that crowd, a face I recognised was watching the store.
district:1.line: 'This *district* is tough — every shop here has been fighting for years.'

sentences.en: The new branch sat at the edge of the old shopping *district*, where teahouses and noodle stalls had stood for decades.
Walking there for the first time, I noticed how different it felt from our quiet corner — louder, brighter, and full of people even at midnight.
sentences.cn: 第一次走那条路，我注意到这边和我们那个安静的角落有多不一样——更吵，更亮，即使半夜也人山人海。

sentences.en: This part of the city never seemed to sleep.
sentences.cn: 城市的这一块似乎从不睡觉。

greatly:1.en: The Manager had *greatly* underestimated how hard it would be to find a good location. Three streets, two arguments with landlords, and one very long afternoon later, he sat on a low wall outside a vacant shop, staring at his own shoes. Tang and I exchanged a look. Nobody said anything for a while.
greatly:1.cnHint: 店长____低估了找到合适店面的难度，坐在墙边沉默了很久。
greatly:1.hook: Then the Manager's phone rang, and his whole face changed.
greatly:1.line: 'I *greatly* underestimated this neighbourhood — it is far harder than I thought.'

sentences.en: The Manager had *greatly* underestimated how hard it would be to find a good location.
Three streets, two arguments with landlords, and one very long afternoon later, he sat on a low wall outside a vacant shop, staring at his own shoes.
sentences.cn: 三条街、两次和房东吵架，还有一个特别长的下午之后，他坐在一家空铺门前的矮墙上，低头看着自己的鞋。

sentences.en: Tang and I exchanged a look.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我互相看了一眼。

sentences.en: Nobody said anything for a while.
sentences.cn: 没人说话，过了一会儿。

imitate:1.en: Lin showed up at the new site uninvited, walking slowly around the outside of the building, looking at every detail. 'He's trying to *imitate* whatever we build here,' Tang whispered to me, watching from across the street. Lin paused at the door, took a photo, smiled to himself, and walked away without a word.
imitate:1.cnHint: 竞争对手林来到新店外围转悠，似乎想____我们的设计。
imitate:1.hook: What Lin didn't notice was that the Manager had been watching him the whole time.
imitate:1.line: 'If he wants to *imitate* us, let him — we'll just keep moving ahead.'

sentences.en: Lin showed up at the new site uninvited, walking slowly around the outside of the building, looking at every detail.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林不请自来地出现在新店址，缓缓走过楼外，看着每一个细节。

sentences.en: 'He's trying to *imitate* whatever we build here,' Tang whispered to me, watching from across the street.
Lin paused at the door, took a photo, smiled to himself, and walked away without a word.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在门口停了停，拍了张照，对自己笑了笑，然后一句话都没说就走了。

implement:1.en: The Manager laid every *implement* out on the folding table outside the new store: price tags, a label gun, a measuring tape, a screwdriver. He picked up each one, checked it, and set it down again with quiet care. It was the same routine he followed at our main store every single time a new shelf went up.
implement:1.cnHint: 店长把所有____整齐地摆在桌上，一件件检查，就像开第一家店时一样。
implement:1.hook: One tool was missing, and the Manager's jaw tightened when he noticed.
implement:1.line: 'Every *implement* has its place — a tidy kit means a tidy store.'

sentences.en: The Manager laid every *implement* out on the folding table outside the new store: price tags, a label gun, a measuring tape, a screwdriver.
He picked up each one, checked it, and set it down again with quiet care.
sentences.cn: 他拿起每一个，检查一下，再轻手轻脚地放回去。

sentences.en: It was the same routine he followed at our main store every single time a new shelf went up.
sentences.cn: 这跟他每次在老店装新架子时的做法一模一样。

mood:1.en: Tang arrived at the new branch site kicking a small stone ahead of him, which told me everything about his *mood*. The Manager had asked him to repaint the outside wall alone. It was hot, the wall was long, and the paint was the wrong shade of white. He picked up the brush anyway and started at the far end.
mood:1.cnHint: 同事今天____很差，因为被安排一个人粉刷外墙。
mood:1.hook: By noon, someone unexpected had picked up a second brush and joined him.
mood:1.line: 'My *mood* is terrible today, but the wall won't paint itself, will it.'

sentences.en: Tang arrived at the new branch site kicking a small stone ahead of him, which told me everything about his *mood*.
The Manager had asked him to repaint the outside wall alone.
sentences.cn: 店长让他一个人重新刷外面的墙。

sentences.en: It was hot, the wall was long, and the paint was the wrong shade of white.
sentences.cn: 天很热，墙很长，涂料的白色调子还不对。

sentences.en: He picked up the brush anyway and started at the far end.
sentences.cn: 他拿起刷子，从最远的那头开始了。

motivation:1.en: I asked the Manager why he was working so hard to open a second store when the first one barely broke even. He was quiet for a moment, straightening a sign above the new door. 'The *motivation* isn't money,' he said at last, without turning around. He didn't explain further, and I didn't ask again.
motivation:1.cnHint: 我问店长开分店的____到底是什么，他的回答让我意外。
motivation:1.hook: Later, Tang told me he had heard the Manager say a name — just once, softly.
motivation:1.line: 'My *motivation* has nothing to do with money — remember that.'

sentences.en: I asked the Manager why he was working so hard to open a second store when the first one barely broke even.
sentences.cn: 我问店长，第一家店都快收不了呢，为什么还要这么努力开第二家。

sentences.en: He was quiet for a moment, straightening a sign above the new door.
sentences.cn: 他安静了一会儿，整理着新门上的招牌。

sentences.en: 'The *motivation* isn't money,' he said at last, without turning around.
He didn't explain further, and I didn't ask again.
sentences.cn: 他没有继续解释，我也没再问。

attribute:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, studying the busy corner with folded arms. 'People walk past here all day,' he said. I could *attribute* his confidence to experience — he had opened three stores before. But something in his careful eyes made me wonder if he saw a problem he was not sharing yet.
attribute:1.cnHint: 店长在新分店选址外，把人流量____为成功的关键因素。
attribute:1.hook: He checked his watch twice, then looked north.
attribute:1.line: I *attribute* the foot traffic here to the night market two blocks away.

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, studying the busy corner with folded arms.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新店址外，两臂交叉，研究着这个繁忙的角落。

sentences.en: 'People walk past here all day,' he said.
sentences.cn: "人们整天从这儿走过，"他说。

sentences.en: I could *attribute* his confidence to experience — he had opened three stores before.
But something in his careful eyes made me wonder if he saw a problem he was not sharing yet.
sentences.cn: 但他那双谨慎的眼睛让我怀疑他看出了什么问题，只是没有说出来。

badly:1.en: Tang and I were sent to count the foot traffic outside the site on a cold morning. Tang forgot his coat. He *badly* wanted to go back for it, hopping from foot to foot on the pavement, but the Manager had said to stay until noon. I offered him half my scarf and he accepted with a grateful, shivering grin.
badly:1.cnHint: 外出勘察新店选址时，同事____需要一件外套来御寒。
badly:1.hook: Then Tang pointed at a figure crossing the road.
badly:1.line: I *badly* need a hot drink right now — any store nearby?

sentences.en: Tang and I were sent to count the foot traffic outside the site on a cold morning.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我被派去在一个寒冷的早上数这个地方的客流。

sentences.en: Tang forgot his coat.
sentences.cn: 阿糖没带外套。

sentences.en: He *badly* wanted to go back for it, hopping from foot to foot on the pavement, but the Manager had said to stay until noon.
I offered him half my scarf and he accepted with a grateful, shivering grin.
sentences.cn: 我把围巾分了他一半，他乐呵呵地接受了，还冻得发抖。

bridge:1.en: The new branch sat at the end of a narrow *bridge* over a small canal. Every morning, workers and students crossed it in a steady stream. The Manager watched them from the railings, counting heads under his breath. 'A bridge is not just concrete,' he told me. 'It is a promise that people will arrive.'
bridge:1.cnHint: 新分店就在一座____旁边，店长认为这是绝佳的客流保障。
bridge:1.hook: That evening, a cyclist stopped halfway across and stared at the door.
bridge:1.line: This *bridge* carries more people than that main road does.

sentences.en: The new branch sat at the end of a narrow *bridge* over a small canal.
Every morning, workers and students crossed it in a steady stream.
sentences.cn: 每天早上，工人和学生络绎不绝地穿过它。

sentences.en: The Manager watched them from the railings, counting heads under his breath.
sentences.cn: 店长靠在栏杆上看着他们，轻声数着人头。

sentences.en: 'A bridge is not just concrete,' he told me.
sentences.cn: "桥不只是混凝土，"他对我说。

sentences.en: 'It is a promise that people will arrive.'
sentences.cn: "它是一个承诺——人们会到达。"

casual:1.en: Lin appeared outside the site in a *casual* jacket and trainers, pretending to check her phone. She was clearly studying the same corner we had chosen. The Manager noticed her and simply smiled, straightening the small 'Coming Soon' sign on the door. Neither of them spoke. The street felt oddly quiet for a moment.
casual:1.cnHint: 竞争对手穿着____的衣服在新店选址附近假装路过，其实在暗中观察。
casual:1.hook: Lin took one photo before walking away without looking back.
casual:1.line: Oh, I was just taking a *casual* walk — nice spot you picked.

sentences.en: Lin appeared outside the site in a *casual* jacket and trainers, pretending to check her phone.
She was clearly studying the same corner we had chosen.
sentences.cn: 她显然在研究我们选中的那个角落。

sentences.en: The Manager noticed her and simply smiled, straightening the small 'Coming Soon' sign on the door.
sentences.cn: 店长注意到她，只是笑了笑，整了整门上那块"即将开业"的小牌子。

sentences.en: Neither of them spoke.
sentences.cn: 他们都没有说话。

sentences.en: The street felt oddly quiet for a moment.
sentences.cn: 街道在那一刻显得奇异地安静。

closely:1.en: I was asked to observe the morning crowd *closely* and write down what people carried — bags, umbrellas, hot cups from other stores. The Manager wanted to know what gap we could fill. By ten o'clock my notebook was full. Across the street, I noticed Lin doing exactly the same thing from a doorway.
closely:1.cnHint: 我被要求____观察早晨的人流，记录潜在顾客的消费习惯。
closely:1.hook: Our notes would turn out to be completely different.
closely:1.line: Watch *closely* — see how many people carry breakfast bags already.

sentences.en: I was asked to observe the morning crowd *closely* and write down what people carried — bags, umbrellas, hot cups from other stores.
The Manager wanted to know what gap we could fill.
sentences.cn: 店长想知道我们能填补什么空缺。

sentences.en: By ten o'clock my notebook was full.
sentences.cn: 到十点钟时，我的笔记本已经满了。

sentences.en: Across the street, I noticed Lin doing exactly the same thing from a doorway.
sentences.cn: 街对面，我注意到林正在门廊里做同样的事情。

commit:1.en: The Manager gathered Tang and me outside the site after lunch. 'I will not *commit* to this location until we check the evening crowd,' he said, tapping the door frame. We nodded. A woman with a folded map stopped, read the 'Coming Soon' sign, and asked us when we would open. We all looked at the Manager.
commit:1.cnHint: 店长说要等看过晚间人流后，才肯____确定这个新分店的选址。
commit:1.hook: The Manager smiled at the woman but gave no date.
commit:1.line: I never *commit* to a site until I see it after dark.

sentences.en: The Manager gathered Tang and me outside the site after lunch.
sentences.cn: 午餐后，店长在工地外聚集了阿糖和我。

sentences.en: 'I will not *commit* to this location until we check the evening crowd,' he said, tapping the door frame.
We nodded.
sentences.cn: 我们点了头。

sentences.en: A woman with a folded map stopped, read the 'Coming Soon' sign, and asked us when we would open.
sentences.cn: 一个拿着折好地图的女人停下来，看了"即将开业"的牌子，问我们什么时候开业。

sentences.en: We all looked at the Manager.
sentences.cn: 我们都看向店长。

concentrate:1.en: Setting up the small outdoor display table, I tried to *concentrate* on aligning the sample cups in a neat row. But the street noise, a barking dog, and Tang humming tunelessly behind me made it hard. The Manager appeared, fixed one cup with a single finger, and said nothing. The row was suddenly perfect.
concentrate:1.cnHint: 在店外摆设展示台时，我努力____于工作，但周围的噪音让人分心。
concentrate:1.hook: A child stopped and reached for one of the cups.
concentrate:1.line: Could you please *concentrate* — every cup needs to face the same way.

sentences.en: Setting up the small outdoor display table, I tried to *concentrate* on aligning the sample cups in a neat row.
But the street noise, a barking dog, and Tang humming tunelessly behind me made it hard.
sentences.cn: 但街上的噪音、一条狗的吠叫声，还有阿糖在我身后离调地哼唱，让这一切变得困难。

sentences.en: The Manager appeared, fixed one cup with a single finger, and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 店长出现了，用一根手指拨动了一个杯子，什么也没说。

sentences.en: The row was suddenly perfect.
sentences.cn: 那一排突然完美了。

conscious:1.en: Walking the block around the new site, I became *conscious* of how many people glanced at the 'Coming Soon' sign without slowing down. I started counting glances the way the Manager counted footsteps. By the third lap I noticed one man had done the same lap twice, reading the sign each time. He was not one of us.
conscious:1.cnHint: 在新店附近巡查时，我逐渐____到有个陌生人在反复打量我们的告示牌。
conscious:1.hook: On his third lap, the man finally took out a notebook.
conscious:1.line: I'm *conscious* that at least three people have photographed our sign today.

sentences.en: Walking the block around the new site, I became *conscious* of how many people glanced at the 'Coming Soon' sign without slowing down.
I started counting glances the way the Manager counted footsteps.
sentences.cn: 我开始像店长数脚步一样计数瞥见的次数。

sentences.en: By the third lap I noticed one man had done the same lap twice, reading the sign each time.
sentences.cn: 到第三圈时，我注意到一个男人做了同样的一圈，每次都读那个牌子。

sentences.en: He was not one of us.
sentences.cn: 他不是我们中的一员。

obvious:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site on a cold morning, staring at the empty shopfront. A big sign had fallen sideways overnight. It was *obvious* to every passerby that something had gone wrong — people slowed down, pointed, and whispered before hurrying on. I arrived late and found him already sweeping broken glass alone.
obvious:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店门口，看着倾斜的招牌，路人纷纷驻足——____就摆在眼前。
obvious:1.hook: He swept without a word, but his hands would not stop shaking.
obvious:1.line: 'It is *obvious* we have a problem — help me move this sign.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site on a cold morning, staring at the empty shopfront.
sentences.cn: 店长在一个寒冷的早晨站在新分店的工地外，盯着空荡荡的店面。

sentences.en: A big sign had fallen sideways overnight.
sentences.cn: 一块大牌子在一夜之间侧倒了。

sentences.en: It was *obvious* to every passerby that something had gone wrong — people slowed down, pointed, and whispered before hurrying on.
I arrived late and found him already sweeping broken glass alone.
sentences.cn: 我迟到了，发现他已经独自在那里扫碎玻璃。

ordinary:1.en: From the outside, the new branch looked like any *ordinary* corner shop: a small lit sign, a rack of umbrellas by the door, neat rows of drinks in the window. But the Manager had spent three months choosing every shelf position. I watched him stand back and smile at it the way a painter smiles at a finished wall.
ordinary:1.cnHint: 新分店从外面看和____的便利店没什么两样，但店长在门口站了很久，若有所思。
ordinary:1.hook: Then a stranger walked up and asked if the old branch had finally closed.
ordinary:1.line: 'It may look *ordinary*, but every shelf is exactly where I want it.'

sentences.en: From the outside, the new branch looked like any *ordinary* corner shop: a small lit sign, a rack of umbrellas by the door, neat rows of drinks in the window.
But the Manager had spent three months choosing every shelf position.
sentences.cn: 但店长花了三个月时间选择每个货架的位置。

sentences.en: I watched him stand back and smile at it the way a painter smiles at a finished wall.
sentences.cn: 我看着他退后一步，像画家对着一面完成的墙那样对它微笑。

pace:1.en: Tang *paced* up and down the pavement outside the new branch, checking the clock every few steps. The delivery truck was thirty minutes late, and the grand opening was in one hour. A small crowd had already gathered by the door, holding discount coupons the Manager had handed out the week before. I counted the coupons and felt my own stomach tighten.
pace:1.cnHint: 唐在新分店门外____来____去，送货车迟迟未到，开业就要开始了。
pace:1.hook: The truck turned the corner — but it was carrying the wrong store's order.
pace:1.line: 'Stop watching me *pace* — go and call the driver again.'

sentences.en: Tang *paced* up and down the pavement outside the new branch, checking the clock every few steps.
The delivery truck was thirty minutes late, and the grand opening was in one hour.
sentences.cn: 送货车迟到了三十分钟，盛大开业还有一小时。

sentences.en: A small crowd had already gathered by the door, holding discount coupons the Manager had handed out the week before.
sentences.cn: 一小群人已经聚集在门口，拿着店长上周发出的折扣券。

sentences.en: I counted the coupons and felt my own stomach tighten.
sentences.cn: 我数了数折扣券，感觉自己的胃也紧了起来。

participate:1.en: The Manager invited everyone on the street to *participate* in a simple game outside the new branch: guess the number of sweets in a glass jar and win a store voucher. A long, cheerful line formed within minutes. Lin arrived last, studied the jar for a long time, then wrote a number so precise that the Manager raised an eyebrow.
participate:1.cnHint: 店长邀请街上的路人____猜糖果数量的小游戏，林是最后一个来的。
participate:1.hook: Lin's number was only one away from correct, and he did not look surprised at all.
participate:1.line: 'I did not come to *participate* — I came to win.'

sentences.en: The Manager invited everyone on the street to *participate* in a simple game outside the new branch: guess the number of sweets in a glass jar and win a store voucher.
A long, cheerful line formed within minutes.
sentences.cn: 几分钟内就排起了一条长长的、欢快的队伍。

sentences.en: Lin arrived last, studied the jar for a long time, then wrote a number so precise that the Manager raised an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 林最后来了，长时间研究那个罐子，然后写了一个如此精确的数字，以至于店长扬起了眉毛。

pilot:1.en: A man in a neat uniform stopped at the new branch just after dawn, bought a hot coffee, and stood reading the community board by the door. Someone had pinned up a photo of the old store from ten years ago. He pointed at it and told me he was a *pilot* who had grown up on this very street and used to buy sweets here as a child.
pilot:1.cnHint: 一位____在天亮后停在新分店门口买咖啡，指着公告栏上的旧照片发了会儿呆。
pilot:1.hook: He asked quietly whether the woman in the photo still worked the morning shift.
pilot:1.line: 'I am a *pilot*, but this little store always felt like home base to me.'

sentences.en: A man in a neat uniform stopped at the new branch just after dawn, bought a hot coffee, and stood reading the community board by the door.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着整洁制服的男人在清晨时分停在新分店，买了一杯热咖啡，站在门边读社区公告板。

sentences.en: Someone had pinned up a photo of the old store from ten years ago.
sentences.cn: 有人钉上了十年前老店的一张照片。

sentences.en: He pointed at it and told me he was a *pilot* who had grown up on this very street and used to buy sweets here as a child.

primary:1.en: The Manager explained his *primary* reason for choosing this street corner: three schools within five minutes' walk, a bus stop right opposite, and a park where families gathered every weekend. He drew a rough map on the back of a receipt and handed it to me outside the empty shop. The logic was so clean it was almost beautiful.
primary:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门口向我解释选这个街角的____原因，还在收据背面画了张简图。
primary:1.hook: Lin appeared behind us and photographed the map before either of us noticed.
primary:1.line: 'Location is the *primary* thing — get it wrong and nothing else matters.'

sentences.en: The Manager explained his *primary* reason for choosing this street corner: three schools within five minutes' walk, a bus stop right opposite, and a park where families gathered every weekend.
He drew a rough map on the back of a receipt and handed it to me outside the empty shop.
sentences.cn: 他在一张收据的背面给我画了一张粗略的地图，然后在空店外递给我。

sentences.en: The logic was so clean it was almost beautiful.
sentences.cn: 逻辑是如此清晰，几乎美得令人惊叹。

priority:1.en: Tang and I carried a heavy promotional banner out to the pavement, but the wind kept folding it the wrong way. The Manager came outside, looked at our struggle, and said that getting the banner straight was not the *priority* — the open door and the warm smell of fresh bread coming out were. He propped the door wide open and walked back in without another word.
priority:1.cnHint: 店长走出来看我们挂横幅，说这不是最重要的____，然后把店门敞开就走了。
priority:1.hook: A small girl outside immediately followed the bread smell straight through the door.
priority:1.line: 'The banner can wait — the open door is the *priority* right now.'

sentences.en: Tang and I carried a heavy promotional banner out to the pavement, but the wind kept folding it the wrong way.
sentences.cn: 我和阿糖抬着一条沉重的宣传横幅走到人行道上，可风一个劲儿地把它吹反了。

sentences.en: The Manager came outside, looked at our struggle, and said that getting the banner straight was not the *priority* — the open door and the warm smell of fresh bread coming out were.
He propped the door wide open and walked back in without another word.
sentences.cn: 他把门撑得很开，转身走了进去，一句话都没说。

throughout:1.en: *Throughout* the first morning outside the new branch, a steady stream of curious neighbours stopped to peer through the window, read the menu board, and collect the small free samples Tang handed out on a tray. By noon the tray was empty, Tang's feet hurt, and a short queue had formed at the door before we had even officially opened.
throughout:1.cnHint: 新店开业第一个上午，____都有好奇的街坊在外面张望，唐的托盘很快就空了。
throughout:1.hook: The last person in line was holding a coupon printed with yesterday's date.
throughout:1.line: 'I was here *throughout* the whole morning — do I get an extra sample?'

sentences.en: *Throughout* the first morning outside the new branch, a steady stream of curious neighbours stopped to peer through the window, read the menu board, and collect the small free samples Tang handed out on a tray.
By noon the tray was empty, Tang's feet hurt, and a short queue had formed at the door before we had even officially opened.
sentences.cn: 到了中午，托盘空了，阿糖的脚疼了，门口已经排起了一条小队伍，而我们还没正式开门呢。

dinner:1.en: The Manager called us outside at sunset. A folding table stood on the pavement, covered with small dishes. 'Before we open the new branch,' he said, 'we share a *dinner* together.' Tang passed the chopsticks. I looked at the empty building across the street and felt, for the first time, like part of the team.
dinner:1.cnHint: 店长在街边摆了一桌菜，说要在____之前大家聚一聚。
dinner:1.hook: But one chair at the table was never explained.
dinner:1.line: 'I always *dinner* with my crew before a big day,' the Manager said.

sentences.en: The Manager called us outside at sunset.
sentences.cn: 店长在日落时叫我们走到外面。

sentences.en: A folding table stood on the pavement, covered with small dishes.
sentences.cn: 人行道上放着一张折叠桌，上面铺满了小菜。

sentences.en: 'Before we open the new branch,' he said, 'we share a *dinner* together.'
Tang passed the chopsticks.
sentences.cn: 阿糖递过筷子。

sentences.en: I looked at the empty building across the street and felt, for the first time, like part of the team.
sentences.cn: 我看着对面空荡荡的楼房，第一次觉得自己真的属于这个团队了。

embrace:1.en: I stepped outside to sweep the doorstep and found Lin standing across the street, staring at the empty shopfront. She didn't look angry. She looked almost sad. Then the Manager walked out, put a hand on her shoulder, and said we should *embrace* the change together — both stores could make this corner something special.
embrace:1.cnHint: 店长走出来，说大家应该____新的变化，把这个街角变得更好。
embrace:1.hook: Lin's answer was a smile that never quite reached her eyes.
embrace:1.line: 'We should *embrace* this new start,' the Manager told Lin quietly.

sentences.en: I stepped outside to sweep the doorstep and found Lin standing across the street, staring at the empty shopfront.
sentences.cn: 我走到外面扫门前的台阶，发现隔壁咖啡店的林站在街对面，盯着那间空店铺。

sentences.en: She didn't look angry.
sentences.cn: 她看起来不生气。

sentences.en: She looked almost sad.
sentences.cn: 她看起来几乎有点伤心。

sentences.en: Then the Manager walked out, put a hand on her shoulder, and said we should *embrace* the change together — both stores could make this corner something special.

explanation:1.en: A delivery van stopped in front of the wrong address and blocked our doorway for twenty minutes. The driver gave no *explanation*, just shrugged and scrolled his phone. Tang stood outside, arms folded, while customers squeezed past. When the van finally left, a small round of applause came from the bus stop.
explanation:1.cnHint: 送货车堵住了门口，司机没有任何____，坦然刷着手机。
explanation:1.hook: Tang wrote something in a notebook that I was not meant to see.
explanation:1.line: 'No *explanation* at all — just parked and walked off,' Tang said.

sentences.en: A delivery van stopped in front of the wrong address and blocked our doorway for twenty minutes.
sentences.cn: 一辆送货车停在了错误的地址前，挡了我们门口整整二十分钟。

sentences.en: The driver gave no *explanation*, just shrugged and scrolled his phone.
Tang stood outside, arms folded, while customers squeezed past.
sentences.cn: 阿糖站在外面，双臂交叉，而顾客们从旁边挤了过去。

sentences.en: When the van finally left, a small round of applause came from the bus stop.
sentences.cn: 货车终于开走了，公交站那边响起了一阵小小的掌声。

intend:1.en: The Manager pinned a paper map on the lamp post outside and circled two spots with a red pen. 'I *intend* to open the second branch on this corner,' he told us. A woman walking her dog stopped, read the map over his shoulder, and asked if there would be better coffee than the current store.
intend:1.cnHint: 店长在路灯柱上贴出地图，宣布他____在那个街角开新分店。
intend:1.hook: The woman left without giving her name, but she took a photo of the map.
intend:1.line: 'I *intend* to make the new store even cosier,' the Manager said firmly.

sentences.en: The Manager pinned a paper map on the lamp post outside and circled two spots with a red pen.
sentences.cn: 店长在外面的路灯柱上钉了一张纸质地图，用红笔圈出了两个点。

sentences.en: 'I *intend* to open the second branch on this corner,' he told us.
A woman walking her dog stopped, read the map over his shoulder, and asked if there would be better coffee than the current store.
sentences.cn: 一个遛狗的女人停下来，靠在他肩膀上读着地图，问是不是要开出比现在这家店更好的咖啡。

leadership:1.en: While we set up the outdoor sign for the new branch, a school group walked by. Their teacher pointed at the Manager and told the students that real *leadership* means doing the hard work yourself. The Manager was on a step-ladder at the time, fixing a crooked letter, and he bowed from up there with great dignity.
leadership:1.cnHint: 路过的老师指着正在梯子上干活的店长，夸他展现了真正的____。
leadership:1.hook: One student stayed behind and asked the Manager for a job application.
leadership:1.line: 'True *leadership* is climbing the ladder yourself,' the teacher said.

sentences.en: While we set up the outdoor sign for the new branch, a school group walked by.
sentences.cn: 我们在给新店铺安装室外招牌的时候，一群学生走了过来。

sentences.en: Their teacher pointed at the Manager and told the students that real *leadership* means doing the hard work yourself.
The Manager was on a step-ladder at the time, fixing a crooked letter, and he bowed from up there with great dignity.
sentences.cn: 店长正站在梯子上修一个歪了的字母，他从上面恭恭敬敬地鞠了一躬。

locate:1.en: Tang spread a city map on the bonnet of a parked car and tried to *locate* the exact site of our new branch. A stranger stopped, looked at the map upside down, and confidently pointed to the river. Tang thanked him, waited until he left, and then pointed to the correct block three streets away.
locate:1.cnHint: 阿糖在停着的车上摊开地图，试图____新分店的准确位置。
locate:1.hook: The stranger came back ten minutes later with a second, older map.
locate:1.line: 'I need to *locate* the new site before the Manager asks,' Tang muttered.

sentences.en: Tang spread a city map on the bonnet of a parked car and tried to *locate* the exact site of our new branch.
A stranger stopped, looked at the map upside down, and confidently pointed to the river.
sentences.cn: 一个陌生人停下来，把地图倒过来看，很有把握地指向河的方向。

sentences.en: Tang thanked him, waited until he left, and then pointed to the correct block three streets away.
sentences.cn: 阿糖谢了他，等他走远了，然后指向了三条街外的正确街区。

original:1.en: Lin stood outside studying our store front, then looked at the empty unit next door. 'Your sign design is nice,' she admitted to me, 'but my *original* plan was to open here first.' She said it without bitterness, just a quiet fact, the way you state the weather. Then she bought a coffee and walked away.
original:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林坦言，她____的计划是第一个在这里开店。
original:1.hook: She left a folded note under the coffee cup.
original:1.line: 'My *original* plan had this corner all to myself,' Lin said quietly.

sentences.en: Lin stood outside studying our store front, then looked at the empty unit next door.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在我们店铺前研究了一会儿，又看了看隔壁那间空着的店面。

sentences.en: 'Your sign design is nice,' she admitted to me, 'but my *original* plan was to open here first.'
She said it without bitterness, just a quiet fact, the way you state the weather.
sentences.cn: 她说这话的时候没有一点怨气，就像在陈述天气一样，平平淡淡。

sentences.en: Then she bought a coffee and walked away.
sentences.cn: 然后她买了杯咖啡，走开了。

overcome:1.en: The new sign was too wide for the doorway and nobody had measured twice. Tang and I stood outside in the evening air, turning it sideways, then diagonal. Small crowds gathered, offered advice, and cheered every attempt. We finally *overcome* the problem by removing one bolt and sliding the sign in at an angle, to loud applause.
overcome:1.cnHint: 招牌太宽进不了门，我们费了好大劲才____这个难题。
overcome:1.hook: The Manager filmed the whole thing without helping once.
overcome:1.line: 'We *overcome* every problem if we stay calm,' Tang said, out of breath.

sentences.en: The new sign was too wide for the doorway and nobody had measured twice.
sentences.cn: 新招牌太宽了，门框放不进去，而且没人量过两次。

sentences.en: Tang and I stood outside in the evening air, turning it sideways, then diagonal.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我站在傍晚的空气里，把招牌竖着试、斜着试。

sentences.en: Small crowds gathered, offered advice, and cheered every attempt.
sentences.cn: 小群众聚集了起来，出主意，每次尝试都欢呼。

sentences.en: We finally *overcome* the problem by removing one bolt and sliding the sign in at an angle, to loud applause.

partly:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, studying the empty shop front across the street. He had been watching it for days. 'The rent is low,' he said, 'and it is *partly* because the landlord wants a quick deal.' I looked at the dusty windows and wondered what he was planning.
partly:1.cnHint: 店长在街对面的空铺子前徘徊，觉得低租金____是因为房东急于出手。
partly:1.hook: He pulled out a tape measure and smiled at me.
partly:1.line: The low price is *partly* because they need the space filled fast.

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, studying the empty shop front across the street.
sentences.cn: 店长站在人行道上，盯着对面那间空店铺。

sentences.en: He had been watching it for days.
sentences.cn: 他已经看了好几天了。

sentences.en: 'The rent is low,' he said, 'and it is *partly* because the landlord wants a quick deal.'
I looked at the dusty windows and wondered what he was planning.
sentences.cn: 我看着那扇布满灰尘的窗户，琢磨着他在计划什么。

practical:1.en: Tang spread a hand-drawn map on the bonnet of a parked bicycle outside. Little squares marked possible sites for the new branch. 'Forget the pretty spots,' Tang said. 'We need something *practical*—close to the bus stop, with a loading bay.' I circled one square with a pen and Tang raised an eyebrow.
practical:1.cnHint: 阿糖在外面铺开地图，坚持选址要____，离公交站近才行。
practical:1.hook: The circled spot belonged to someone none of us expected.
practical:1.line: A place near the bus stop is far more *practical* for deliveries.

sentences.en: Tang spread a hand-drawn map on the bonnet of a parked bicycle outside.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在外面停着的自行车上铺开了一张手绘地图。

sentences.en: Little squares marked possible sites for the new branch.
sentences.cn: 小方块标记了新店铺的几个可能地点。

sentences.en: 'Forget the pretty spots,' Tang said.
sentences.cn: "忘了那些漂亮的地方吧，"阿糖说。

sentences.en: 'We need something *practical*—close to the bus stop, with a loading bay.'
I circled one square with a pen and Tang raised an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 我用笔圈了一个方块，阿糖挑了挑眉毛。

profit:1.en: Lin was already outside before dawn, counting the breakfast crowd walking past the empty corner lot. She wrote numbers in a small notebook. 'If we sell rice boxes and coffee here,' she said quietly, almost to herself, 'the *profit* in one month pays the deposit.' I stood beside her, watching the same crowd, doing the same sums.
profit:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在拐角空地旁计算早餐人流，默默估算一个月的____能否付清押金。
profit:1.hook: But Lin's notebook had a second column I had not noticed.
profit:1.line: One month of rice-box sales brings enough *profit* to cover the deposit.

sentences.en: Lin was already outside before dawn, counting the breakfast crowd walking past the empty corner lot.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林天还没亮就已经在外面了，数着经过这块空地的早餐人流。

sentences.en: She wrote numbers in a small notebook.
sentences.cn: 她在小本子上记下数字。

sentences.en: 'If we sell rice boxes and coffee here,' she said quietly, almost to herself, 'the *profit* in one month pays the deposit.'
I stood beside her, watching the same crowd, doing the same sums.
sentences.cn: 我站在她身边，看着同样的人流，做着同样的账目。

promise:1.en: Outside the old post office, the Manager shook hands with a landlord in a grey coat. I waited by the kerb. 'You have my *promise*,' the Manager said, standing straight and calm. 'We open within sixty days.' The landlord nodded slowly, folded his copy of the agreement, and walked away without a word.
promise:1.cnHint: 店长在旧邮局外握手，郑重地给了房东一个____：六十天内开业。
promise:1.hook: The landlord paused at the corner and looked back once.
promise:1.line: You have my *promise*—the store opens in sixty days.

sentences.en: Outside the old post office, the Manager shook hands with a landlord in a grey coat.
sentences.cn: 在旧邮局外，店长和一个穿灰大衣的房东握了手。

sentences.en: I waited by the kerb.
sentences.cn: 我在路边等着。

sentences.en: 'You have my *promise*,' the Manager said, standing straight and calm.
'We open within sixty days.'
sentences.cn: 我们在六十天内开业。

sentences.en: The landlord nodded slowly, folded his copy of the agreement, and walked away without a word.
sentences.cn: 房东缓缓点头，折好协议书的副本，无言地走开了。

rarely:1.en: The side street behind the market was quiet that morning. Tang pointed to a small unit wedged between a laundry and a hardware stall. 'Customers *rarely* come this deep in,' Tang admitted, kicking a loose stone, 'but the people who do are regulars—every single day.' I looked at the narrow lane and tried to imagine a neon sign here.
rarely:1.cnHint: 阿糖带我去市场后的小巷看铺位，承认顾客____走到这么深的地方。
rarely:1.hook: Just then, a familiar regular walked out of that very lane.
rarely:1.line: People *rarely* wander this far, but loyal ones do every day.

sentences.en: The side street behind the market was quiet that morning.
sentences.cn: 那天早上，市场后面的小街很安静。

sentences.en: Tang pointed to a small unit wedged between a laundry and a hardware stall.
sentences.cn: 阿糖指了指夹在洗衣店和五金铺之间的小店铺。

sentences.en: 'Customers *rarely* come this deep in,' Tang admitted, kicking a loose stone, 'but the people who do are regulars—every single day.'
I looked at the narrow lane and tried to imagine a neon sign here.
sentences.cn: 我看着这条窄巷，试图想象一块霓虹灯牌在这里会是什么样子。

severe:1.en: A *severe* overnight frost had left thin ice on the doorstep of the site the Manager liked most. We arrived early to check the pipes. Tang pressed a hand to the outside wall and frowned. 'If the insulation is this poor in spring,' Tang said, 'we will lose stock every winter.' The Manager knocked on the wall and said nothing.
severe:1.cnHint: 夜里的____霜冻让店长看中的铺子台阶结了薄冰，阿糖担心冬天货物受损。
severe:1.hook: There was a damp patch on the ceiling nobody had mentioned.
severe:1.line: A frost this *severe* means the insulation is far too weak.

sentences.en: A *severe* overnight frost had left thin ice on the doorstep of the site the Manager liked most.
We arrived early to check the pipes.
sentences.cn: 我们早早赶到，检查管道。

sentences.en: Tang pressed a hand to the outside wall and frowned.
sentences.cn: 阿糖把手按在外墙上，皱起眉头。

sentences.en: 'If the insulation is this poor in spring,' Tang said, 'we will lose stock every winter.'
sentences.cn: 阿糖说，要是春天的隔热效果这么差，我们冬天每年都得亏货。

sentences.en: The Manager knocked on the wall and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 店长敲了敲墙，什么也没说。

smell:1.en: We visited the candidate site near the night market just after the food stalls packed up. The air was still thick with the *smell* of fried dough and spice. I breathed it in and thought it was wonderful. Tang wrinkled their nose. 'Strong neighbours,' Tang said. 'Our snacks will have to fight hard to stand out.'
smell:1.cnHint: 夜市收摊后，我们去看附近的铺位，空气里弥漫着油炸食品的____。
smell:1.hook: Tang pointed to the stall directly next door and went silent.
smell:1.line: That *smell* from next door will compete with everything we sell.

sentences.en: We visited the candidate site near the night market just after the food stalls packed up.
sentences.cn: 我们在食摊收摊后，去看夜市附近的候选地点。

sentences.en: The air was still thick with the *smell* of fried dough and spice.
I breathed it in and thought it was wonderful.
sentences.cn: 我呼吸着这股气味，觉得很棒。

sentences.en: Tang wrinkled their nose.
sentences.cn: 阿糖皱起鼻子。

sentences.en: 'Strong neighbours,' Tang said.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说，强劲的邻居啊。

sentences.en: 'Our snacks will have to fight hard to stand out.'

socialize:1.en: Lin had chosen the Sunday morning visit on purpose. The small plaza in front of the site was full of older residents doing slow exercises and young parents watching children play. 'Look,' Lin said, sweeping a hand across the square. 'People come here to *socialize* every single day. They will need water, snacks, a warm drink.' I started counting heads immediately.
socialize:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林特意选在周日带我们来，广场上全是来____的街坊邻居，她认为生意差不了。
socialize:1.hook: One woman with a pram stopped and peered through our window.
socialize:1.line: They come here to *socialize* daily—every one of them is a customer.

sentences.en: Lin had chosen the Sunday morning visit on purpose.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林故意选了周日早上去看。

sentences.en: The small plaza in front of the site was full of older residents doing slow exercises and young parents watching children play.
sentences.cn: 店铺前的小广场上挤满了做太极的老人和看孩子玩耍的年轻家长。

sentences.en: 'Look,' Lin said, sweeping a hand across the square.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林指着广场说，你看。

sentences.en: 'People come here to *socialize* every single day.
They will need water, snacks, a warm drink.'
sentences.cn: 他们会需要水、小食、一杯热饮。

sentences.en: I started counting heads immediately.
sentences.cn: 我立刻开始数人头。

threaten:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site at dawn, arms crossed. A rival shop owner from across the street marched over and began to *threaten* him, jabbing a finger at the sign. The Manager did not step back even one centimetre.
threaten:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址外被人____，却纹丝不动。
threaten:1.hook: The rival's last word hung in the cold air like a warning.
threaten:1.line: 'You can *threaten* me all you like — this sign stays.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site at dawn, arms crossed.
sentences.cn: 天亮时，店长双臂交叉站在新分店址外。

sentences.en: A rival shop owner from across the street marched over and began to *threaten* him, jabbing a finger at the sign.
The Manager did not step back even one centimetre.
sentences.cn: 店长往后退了哪怕一厘米都没有。

throw:1.en: Opening a second branch on this street was a real *throw* — the rent was high, the foot traffic unknown, and two other shops had already failed here. The Manager studied the empty shopfront anyway, turning the key over in his hand with a quiet, determined look.
throw:1.cnHint: 在这条街开分店是一次大胆的____，风险不小。
throw:1.hook: He pocketed the key, and nobody saw him smile.
throw:1.line: 'Every good business starts as a *throw*, doesn't it?'

sentences.en: Opening a second branch on this street was a real *throw* — the rent was high, the foot traffic unknown, and two other shops had already failed here.
The Manager studied the empty shopfront anyway, turning the key over in his hand with a quiet, determined look.
sentences.cn: 店长还是研究着这间空店铺，手里转着钥匙，脸上带着安静而坚定的神情。

unlike:1.en: The new branch corner felt *unlike* anything near our usual store — wider pavements, taller trees, a slower kind of morning. I stood there holding a measuring tape for the Manager and tried to picture a second little shop of ours sitting quietly between the old bookshop and the flower stall.
unlike:1.cnHint: 新店的街角环境与我们原来的门店____。
unlike:1.hook: Then I noticed something odd taped to the bookshop door.
unlike:1.line: 'This place is *unlike* anywhere I expected us to open.'

sentences.en: The new branch corner felt *unlike* anything near our usual store — wider pavements, taller trees, a slower kind of morning.
I stood there holding a measuring tape for the Manager and tried to picture a second little shop of ours sitting quietly between the old bookshop and the flower stall.
sentences.cn: 我站在那里给店长拿着卷尺，试图想象我们的第二家小店安静地坐在旧书店和花店之间会是什么样子。

vast:1.en: From the rooftop of the proposed building I could see a *vast* stretch of the city — towers, rooftops, tiny figures on bikes below. The Manager spread a hand-drawn map on the ledge and said the new store had to serve all those people out there, every quiet hungry one of them.
vast:1.cnHint: 从楼顶望去，城市____，店长指着远处说新店要服务所有人。
vast:1.hook: One tiny figure on a bike stopped and looked straight up.
vast:1.line: 'Look at that *vast* crowd — they all need a good night clerk.'

sentences.en: From the rooftop of the proposed building I could see a *vast* stretch of the city — towers, rooftops, tiny figures on bikes below.
The Manager spread a hand-drawn map on the ledge and said the new store had to serve all those people out there, every quiet hungry one of them.
sentences.cn: 店长在窗台上摊开了一张手画的地图，说新店必须为外面那些人服务，每一个安静饥饿的人。

absolutely:1.en: Lin from the rival shop leaned against the lamppost and told me *absolutely* nothing useful — every question about the local customer habits got a cheerful shrug or a change of subject. I wrote 'zero data from Lin' in my notebook and decided to count passing customers myself.
absolutely:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林对我的问题____没有给出任何有用的信息。
absolutely:1.hook: Lin's smile, though, suggested she knew far more than she let on.
absolutely:1.line: 'I *absolutely* have no idea what time people eat around here.'

sentences.en: Lin from the rival shop leaned against the lamppost and told me *absolutely* nothing useful — every question about the local customer habits got a cheerful shrug or a change of subject.
I wrote 'zero data from Lin' in my notebook and decided to count passing customers myself.
sentences.cn: 我在本子上记下"从隔壁咖啡店的林那儿没问出什么有用的"，决定自己数行人。

accumulate:1.en: Every morning before the new branch opened, I would walk past and watch the Manager *accumulate* small clues — a coffee cup left on the step, a bus ticket caught in the doorway, chalk marks children drew on the kerb. He was building a picture of the street one tiny detail at a time.
accumulate:1.cnHint: 店长每天在新店门口____关于这条街的各种细节。
accumulate:1.hook: That morning's clue, though, was not a small one at all.
accumulate:1.line: 'You have to *accumulate* evidence before you trust a street.'

sentences.en: Every morning before the new branch opened, I would walk past and watch the Manager *accumulate* small clues — a coffee cup left on the step, a bus ticket caught in the doorway, chalk marks children drew on the kerb.
He was building a picture of the street one tiny detail at a time.
sentences.cn: 他一点一点地积累这条街的细节，慢慢拼成一幅完整的图景。

breakfast:1.en: Tang arrived early to help measure the new shop space and stopped to *breakfast* at the old couple's stall next door — a bowl of warm rice porridge, eaten standing up, watching the street wake. 'Good neighbours,' Tang said, nodding at the couple, 'that is the best sign for any new store.'
breakfast:1.cnHint: 阿糖在新店隔壁的小摊____，觉得有好邻居是好兆头。
breakfast:1.hook: The old couple exchanged a glance that Tang did not catch.
breakfast:1.line: 'I always *breakfast* near a future shop — tells you everything.'

sentences.en: Tang arrived early to help measure the new shop space and stopped to *breakfast* at the old couple's stall next door — a bowl of warm rice porridge, eaten standing up, watching the street wake.
'Good neighbours,' Tang said, nodding at the couple, 'that is the best sign for any new store.'
sentences.cn: 阿糖点了点头说，"好邻居，"他看着那对夫妇，"这是开新店最好的兆头。"

capacity:1.en: The Manager paced the empty floor of the new branch, counting steps. 'The *capacity* is just right,' he murmured — enough shelves for the essentials, enough counter space for two clerks on a busy night, and one small corner where a tired customer could stand and breathe for a moment.
capacity:1.cnHint: 店长测量新店空间，觉得____恰到好处。
capacity:1.hook: He paused at that small corner and did not move for a long time.
capacity:1.line: 'The *capacity* is right — but is the street ready for us?'

sentences.en: The Manager paced the empty floor of the new branch, counting steps.
sentences.cn: 店长在新分店空荡荡的地板上踱步，数着步子。

sentences.en: 'The *capacity* is just right,' he murmured — enough shelves for the essentials, enough counter space for two clerks on a busy night, and one small corner where a tired customer could stand and breathe for a moment.

consideration:1.en: The Manager stood at the corner of Maple Street, studying the empty shop across the road. 'Location, foot traffic, rent,' he muttered, ticking items off on his fingers. Every *consideration* mattered when opening a second store. I held the measuring tape and tried to look useful. Then a familiar face appeared in the window opposite.
consideration:1.cnHint: 店长在街角评估新店地址时，窗户里出现了一张熟悉的脸，令他____了很多因素。
consideration:1.hook: The face in the window belonged to someone the Manager clearly feared.
consideration:1.line: 'Cost is only one *consideration* — the neighbours matter more.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood at the corner of Maple Street, studying the empty shop across the road.
sentences.cn: 店长站在枫树街的拐角处，研究着对面那家空店铺。

sentences.en: 'Location, foot traffic, rent,' he muttered, ticking items off on his fingers.
sentences.cn: "位置、人流、租金，"他嘟囔着，在手指上一一数过。

sentences.en: Every *consideration* mattered when opening a second store.
I held the measuring tape and tried to look useful.
sentences.cn: 我拿着卷尺，试图让自己看起来有点用处。

sentences.en: Then a familiar face appeared in the window opposite.
sentences.cn: 突然一张熟悉的脸出现在对面的窗户里。

disaster:1.en: Rain had been falling since dawn, and the outdoor sign we had just put up for the new branch lay flat in a puddle. Paint was running down the pavement in little coloured rivers. The Manager stared at the soggy mess and whispered, 'What a *disaster*.' A passing cyclist slowed down, read the ruined sign, and laughed.
disaster:1.cnHint: 新店招牌被大雨冲倒，店长看着一片狼藉，感叹这真是一场____。
disaster:1.hook: The cyclist pulled out a phone and started recording.
disaster:1.line: 'One wet morning and it is already a *disaster* — great start.'

sentences.en: Rain had been falling since dawn, and the outdoor sign we had just put up for the new branch lay flat in a puddle.
sentences.cn: 从天亮开始就一直下雨，我们刚刚为新分店竖起来的户外招牌已经平躺在水坑里。

sentences.en: Paint was running down the pavement in little coloured rivers.
sentences.cn: 油漆沿着人行道流成一条条彩色的小河。

sentences.en: The Manager stared at the soggy mess and whispered, 'What a *disaster*.'
A passing cyclist slowed down, read the ruined sign, and laughed.
sentences.cn: 一个骑自行车的人放慢了速度，看着那块报废的招牌，笑了。

emergency:1.en: A small boy ran up to me outside the new branch site and grabbed my sleeve. 'Mister, my bike wheel is stuck in the drain and I am late for school!' It felt like a real *emergency* to him, and honestly to me too. I found a stick, levered the wheel free, and he pedalled away without a single thank-you.
emergency:1.cnHint: 一个小男孩冲到店外求助，对他来说这是一场真正的____。
emergency:1.hook: Three seconds later the boy skidded to a stop and turned back.
emergency:1.line: 'This is an *emergency* — please help me right now!'

sentences.en: A small boy ran up to me outside the new branch site and grabbed my sleeve.
sentences.cn: 一个小男孩在新分店门口跑过来，抓住了我的袖子。

sentences.en: 'Mister, my bike wheel is stuck in the drain and I am late for school!'
sentences.cn: "先生，我的自行车轮子卡在下水道里了，我要迟到了！"

sentences.en: It felt like a real *emergency* to him, and honestly to me too.
I found a stick, levered the wheel free, and he pedalled away without a single thank-you.
sentences.cn: 我找了根树枝，撬开了车轮，他蹬着自行车跑了，没说一声谢谢。

familiar:1.en: I had walked past this street corner a hundred times before joining the store, yet it felt different now that we were about to open a branch here. The smell of the bread stall, the sound of the tram — everything was *familiar* and strange at once. Tang nudged me: 'You look like you have seen a ghost.'
familiar:1.cnHint: 我走在即将开新店的街角，一切既____又陌生，唐同事发现了我奇怪的表情。
familiar:1.hook: Tang had gone pale too, and was staring at the bread stall.
familiar:1.line: 'This corner feels *familiar* — I think I have been here in a dream.'

sentences.en: I had walked past this street corner a hundred times before joining the store, yet it felt different now that we were about to open a branch here.
sentences.cn: 我加入店里之前已经走过这条街角一百次了，可现在我们要在这儿开分店了，一切感觉都不一样了。

sentences.en: The smell of the bread stall, the sound of the tram — everything was *familiar* and strange at once.
Tang nudged me: 'You look like you have seen a ghost.'
sentences.cn: 阿糖推了我一下："你看起来就像见了鬼一样。"

furthermore:1.en: Lin had arrived at the new site before any of us and had already taped a neat list of problems to the front door: the window was too small, the ceiling was too low, and, *furthermore*, the nearest bus stop was a full ten minutes away on foot. The Manager read the list slowly, folded it in half, and put it in his pocket.
furthermore:1.cnHint: 林提前列出了新店的问题，____连公交站也太远，店长默默把清单收进了口袋。
furthermore:1.hook: No one mentioned that Lin had also brought a rival store's brochure.
furthermore:1.line: 'The rent is high, and *furthermore*, there is no parking at all.'

sentences.en: Lin had arrived at the new site before any of us and had already taped a neat list of problems to the front door: the window was too small, the ceiling was too low, and, *furthermore*, the nearest bus stop was a full ten minutes away on foot.
The Manager read the list slowly, folded it in half, and put it in his pocket.
sentences.cn: 店长慢慢读完那张单子，把它折成两半，放进了口袋。

hardly:1.en: By nine in the morning a small crowd had gathered to watch us hang the new branch sign. My arms ached from holding the ladder steady, and I could *hardly* keep my eyes open after the long night shift. Then the Manager called up, 'A little to the left.' A little. He said that eleven more times.
hardly:1.cnHint: 挂招牌时我熬了一夜，____睁得开眼，店长却不停叫我往左移一点。
hardly:1.hook: On the twelfth adjustment, the ladder gave a quiet, worrying creak.
hardly:1.line: 'I can *hardly* read the address on this map — the print is tiny.'

sentences.en: By nine in the morning a small crowd had gathered to watch us hang the new branch sign.
sentences.cn: 早上九点，一小群人聚在一起看我们挂新分店的招牌。

sentences.en: My arms ached from holding the ladder steady, and I could *hardly* keep my eyes open after the long night shift.
Then the Manager called up, 'A little to the left.'
sentences.cn: 然后店长在上面喊，"靠左一点。"

sentences.en: A little.
sentences.cn: 一点点。

sentences.en: He said that eleven more times.
sentences.cn: 他这样说了又说，一共十一次。

hinder:1.en: A delivery truck had parked right in front of the new branch entrance, blocking the whole pavement. The driver was nowhere to be seen. 'This will *hinder* everything,' Tang said, waving at the crowd of workers waiting to carry boxes inside. I slipped a note under the windscreen wiper and hoped the driver had a conscience.
hinder:1.cnHint: 一辆货车堵住了新店入口，____了所有工作，我只好在雨刷下留了张纸条。
hinder:1.hook: The note blew away before I even turned around.
hinder:1.line: 'Please move your truck — it will *hinder* our whole morning.'

sentences.en: A delivery truck had parked right in front of the new branch entrance, blocking the whole pavement.
sentences.cn: 一辆送货卡车停在了新分店的入口正前方，堵住了整条人行道。

sentences.en: The driver was nowhere to be seen.
sentences.cn: 司机不见了踪影。

sentences.en: 'This will *hinder* everything,' Tang said, waving at the crowd of workers waiting to carry boxes inside.
I slipped a note under the windscreen wiper and hoped the driver had a conscience.
sentences.cn: 我在挡风玻璃下塞了张纸条，希望司机还有良心。

injury:1.en: While helping stack display shelves on the pavement outside the new branch, I dropped a corner unit onto my foot. It was not serious, but I hopped around for a full minute. Tang handed me a small bandage from her bag without a word. 'Old *injury*,' I told a curious passer-by, trying to sound dignified. Nobody believed me.
injury:1.cnHint: 我在店外搬货架时伤了脚，唐递给我创可贴，我硬撑着对路人解释这是旧____。
injury:1.hook: The passer-by turned out to be the landlord coming to sign our lease.
injury:1.line: 'It is just a small *injury* — I can still carry the boxes, really.'

sentences.en: While helping stack display shelves on the pavement outside the new branch, I dropped a corner unit onto my foot.
sentences.cn: 在新分店外面的人行道上堆放展示架的时候，我不小心把一个角柜砸在了自己的脚上。

sentences.en: It was not serious, but I hopped around for a full minute.
sentences.cn: 伤得不严重，但我跳了一整分钟。

sentences.en: Tang handed me a small bandage from her bag without a word.
sentences.cn: 阿糖二话不说从包里递给我一张小创可贴。

sentences.en: 'Old *injury*,' I told a curious passer-by, trying to sound dignified.
Nobody believed me.
sentences.cn: 没人信。

lift:1.en: The new branch store was on the third floor of a corner building. I carried two heavy boxes of milk up the stairs because the *lift* was broken. My legs burned by the top step. The Manager watched from below, arms folded, saying nothing at all.
lift:1.cnHint: 新分店在三楼，我扛着牛奶箱走楼梯，因为____坏了。
lift:1.hook: The Manager's silence felt heavier than the boxes.
lift:1.line: 'The *lift* has been broken for a week — welcome to the new store.'

sentences.en: The new branch store was on the third floor of a corner building.

sentences.en: I carried two heavy boxes of milk up the stairs because the *lift* was broken.
My legs burned by the top step.
sentences.cn: 我的腿在最后一级台阶处已经酸得不行。

sentences.en: The Manager watched from below, arms folded, saying nothing at all.
sentences.cn: 店长在下面看着，双臂交叉，一句话都没说。

mainly:1.en: The Manager explained the new branch to me outside on the pavement. It would serve the office workers across the street, she said. The customers here were *mainly* young people in suits who needed coffee and a quick bite before nine o'clock every morning.
mainly:1.cnHint: 店长在街边向我介绍新分店，顾客____是附近的上班族。
mainly:1.hook: One regular had not shown up in three days.
mainly:1.line: 'Our customers are *mainly* office workers, so mornings will be very busy.'

sentences.en: The Manager explained the new branch to me outside on the pavement.
sentences.cn: 店长在外面的人行道上给我讲解新分店。

sentences.en: It would serve the office workers across the street, she said.
sentences.cn: 她说这家店会服务对面的上班族。

sentences.en: The customers here were *mainly* young people in suits who needed coffee and a quick bite before nine o'clock every morning.

moral:1.en: Tang told me a story about the old branch on our walk to the new store. A clerk once kept extra change instead of returning it and was fired the same afternoon. 'The *moral* is simple,' Tang said, kicking a pebble off the kerb, 'the Manager counts everything.'
moral:1.cnHint: 阿糖边走边讲了个老店的故事，最后点出其中的____。
moral:1.hook: Tang's voice dropped when we reached the new front door.
moral:1.line: 'The *moral* of that story? Never think the Manager is not watching.'

sentences.en: Tang told me a story about the old branch on our walk to the new store.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在我们去新门店的路上给我讲了一个关于老店的故事。

sentences.en: A clerk once kept extra change instead of returning it and was fired the same afternoon.
sentences.cn: 从前有个店员把多收的零钱留了下来，结果当天下午就被开除了。

sentences.en: 'The *moral* is simple,' Tang said, kicking a pebble off the kerb, 'the Manager counts everything.'

nor:1.en: The new branch sat between a dry cleaner and a florist. There was no bus stop nearby, *nor* was there a car park. I stood outside wondering how anyone would find us. Then a crowd rounded the corner, heading straight for the glass door like they already knew.
nor:1.cnHint: 新分店位置偏，附近没有公交站，____有停车场，但顾客却纷至沓来。
nor:1.hook: Someone at the front of the crowd seemed to know my name.
nor:1.line: 'There is no bus stop here, *nor* a car park — people still come every day.'

sentences.en: The new branch sat between a dry cleaner and a florist.
sentences.cn: 新门店夹在一家干洗店和一家花店之间。

sentences.en: There was no bus stop nearby, *nor* was there a car park.
I stood outside wondering how anyone would find us.
sentences.cn: 我站在门外琢磨着怎么会有人找到我们。

sentences.en: Then a crowd rounded the corner, heading straight for the glass door like they already knew.
sentences.cn: 紧接着一群人转过了街角，径直朝玻璃门走来，好像他们早就知道这个地方。

pick:1.en: Before the new branch opened, the Manager let the two clerks *pick* which shift they wanted. Tang chose days without a word of thanks. I chose nights, mostly because the street outside looked wonderfully quiet after midnight. I did not know about the man who came at two every morning.
pick:1.cnHint: 开业前店长让我们____班次，我选了夜班，没想到凌晨会有个神秘常客。
pick:1.hook: The man always ordered the same thing and never paid by phone.
pick:1.line: 'You can *pick* your shift — but nights here are never really quiet.'

sentences.en: Before the new branch opened, the Manager let the two clerks *pick* which shift they wanted.
Tang chose days without a word of thanks.
sentences.cn: 阿糖没有道谢，直接选了白班。

sentences.en: I chose nights, mostly because the street outside looked wonderfully quiet after midnight.
sentences.cn: 我选了夜班，主要是因为午夜后外面的街道看起来安静得令人舒服。

sentences.en: I did not know about the man who came at two every morning.
sentences.cn: 我还不知道有个人每天早上两点会来。

pollution:1.en: The new store faced a wide road, and lorries rolled past all morning. Lin propped the door open to air out the stockroom and then quickly shut it again. 'The *pollution* from those engines is terrible,' she said, waving a hand in front of her face. I noticed she still stood outside on her break.
pollution:1.cnHint: 新店门口大货车不断，隔壁咖啡店的林感叹路上的____很严重，却还是跑到外面休息。

pollution:1.line: 'Close the door — the *pollution* from those lorries gets into everything.'

sentences.en: The new store faced a wide road, and lorries rolled past all morning.
sentences.cn: 新店面朝着一条宽敞的马路，大货车整个上午都在来回轰隆隆地驶过。

sentences.en: Lin propped the door open to air out the stockroom and then quickly shut it again.
sentences.cn: 林把门打开来给储藏室通风，然后又迅速关上了。

sentences.en: 'The *pollution* from those engines is terrible,' she said, waving a hand in front of her face.

sentences.cn: 我注意到她休息的时候还是会站到外面去。

quit:1.en: A man in a paint-stained jacket leaned against the wall outside, staring at the new store sign. He had worked here before, Tang whispered, but he chose to *quit* the week the branch was announced. Now he came by every evening and just looked. He never came in. He never explained why.
quit:1.cnHint: 一个穿旧夹克的男人每晚在门外驻足，阿糖说他在新店宣布前____了工作。
quit:1.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he stepped toward the door.
quit:1.line: 'He used to work here, then chose to *quit* — nobody knows the real reason.'

sentences.en: A man in a paint-stained jacket leaned against the wall outside, staring at the new store sign.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着沾满油漆的夹克的男人靠在外面的墙上，目不转睛地盯着新门店的招牌。

sentences.en: He had worked here before, Tang whispered, but he chose to *quit* the week the branch was announced.
Now he came by every evening and just looked.
sentences.cn: 现在他每天傍晚都会过来看一眼。
