separate:1.cnHint: 阿糖和我在店外测量，确认入口和送货通道能否____开来。
separate:1.hook: The pigeons, I felt, were judging our technique.
separate:1.line: 'We need to keep the entrance and the delivery door *separate*, right?'

sentences.en: Tang and I were sent to measure the pavement outside the new site.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我被派去量新店址外的人行道。

sentences.en: The Manager wanted to know if there was enough room to keep the entrance and the delivery door *separate*.
We used a broom handle as a ruler and argued cheerfully about every centimetre while pigeons watched us with great interest.
sentences.cn: 我们用扫帚把当尺子，为每一厘米的尺寸欢快地争论，鸽子在一旁饶有兴味地看着我们。

tie:1.en: A man in a neat suit and a bright orange *tie* stopped in front of the future store window and stared at the paper sign that read 'Opening Soon'. He checked his watch three times in one minute. I had never seen anyone look so personally offended by a construction delay.
tie:1.cnHint: 一个打着____的男士在新店橱窗前驻足，对"即将开业"的牌子愣神许久。
tie:1.hook: He slid a business card under the door and left.
tie:1.line: 'I have been walking past this corner in my lucky *tie* for a month.'

sentences.en: A man in a neat suit and a bright orange *tie* stopped in front of the future store window and stared at the paper sign that read 'Opening Soon'.
He checked his watch three times in one minute.
sentences.cn: 他一分钟内看了三次手表。

sentences.en: I had never seen anyone look so personally offended by a construction delay.
sentences.cn: 我从未见过有人对施工延误感到这么个人的冒犯。

jam:1.en: The morning the Manager announced the new branch, a delivery truck broke down right outside, turning the narrow street into a solid *jam*. Horns, voices, and the smell of warm exhaust filled the air. We handed out free coffee cups to the stuck cyclists, and three of them said they would come to the opening.
jam:1.cnHint: 新店宣布开业那天，门口偏偏发生了交通____，我们趁机向被堵的骑手派发咖啡。
jam:1.hook: One cyclist stayed to help direct traffic — and never left.
jam:1.line: 'Every opening has a little *jam*; think of it as free advertising.'

sentences.en: The morning the Manager announced the new branch, a delivery truck broke down right outside, turning the narrow street into a solid *jam*.
Horns, voices, and the smell of warm exhaust filled the air.
sentences.cn: 汽笛声、人声和温热的尾气味道充满了空气。

sentences.en: We handed out free coffee cups to the stuck cyclists, and three of them said they would come to the opening.
sentences.cn: 我们给被困的自行车手分发了免费咖啡杯，其中三人说他们会来参加开业。

supermarket:1.en: The big *supermarket* at the end of the road had put up a banner saying 'Everything You Need' right on the day we posted our 'New Branch Coming' notice. The Manager read their banner, straightened his collar, and said simply, 'Good. Competition keeps us awake.' I was not sure if he meant that literally.
supermarket:1.cnHint: 街头的大____在我们贴出新店告示的同一天打出了竞争横幅。
supermarket:1.hook: Their banner was twice the size of our door.
supermarket:1.line: 'A *supermarket* banner will not scare us — small stores have sharper smiles.'

sentences.en: The big *supermarket* at the end of the road had put up a banner saying 'Everything You Need' right on the day we posted our 'New Branch Coming' notice.
The Manager read their banner, straightened his collar, and said simply, 'Good.
sentences.cn: 店长读了他们的横幅，理了理领口，简单地说："很好。

sentences.en: Competition keeps us awake.'
sentences.cn: 竞争让我们保持清醒。

sentences.en: I was not sure if he meant that literally.
sentences.cn: 我不确定他是字面上的意思还是别的意思。

debate:1.en: Tang and I stood on the pavement outside the new site, locked in a serious *debate* about which window faced better light for the snack display. We drew diagrams in the dust with a stick. A passing grandmother stopped, studied our drawings for a moment, and gave a verdict we both immediately accepted.
debate:1.cnHint: 阿糖和我在新店门外____摆放零食货架哪面朝光更合适，一位路过的老奶奶帮我们拍了板。
debate:1.hook: The grandmother asked if we were hiring.
debate:1.line: 'This *debate* about the window matters more than you think — light sells snacks.'

sentences.en: Tang and I stood on the pavement outside the new site, locked in a serious *debate* about which window faced better light for the snack display.
We drew diagrams in the dust with a stick.
sentences.cn: 我们用树枝在灰尘里画了图。

sentences.en: A passing grandmother stopped, studied our drawings for a moment, and gave a verdict we both immediately accepted.
sentences.cn: 一位路过的奶奶停了下来，研究了我们的画一会儿，给了一个我们都立即接受的判断。

anyway:1.en: The Manager called me at noon to say the new branch location was decided. I had not slept yet after my night shift, but I dragged myself outside *anyway*. Standing on the corner, I watched him point at an empty shopfront across the street. His eyes were bright with plans. Behind him, a small figure in a red coat wrote something in a notebook and slipped away before I could see her face.
anyway:1.cnHint: 店长在街角宣布新分店选址，叙述者____赶来见证这一刻。
anyway:1.hook: The woman in the red coat knew the address before the Manager said it.
anyway:1.line: 'It is raining and I am tired, but I came *anyway*.'

sentences.en: The Manager called me at noon to say the new branch location was decided.
sentences.cn: 店长在中午给我打电话，说新分店的位置定了。

sentences.en: I had not slept yet after my night shift, but I dragged myself outside *anyway*.
Standing on the corner, I watched him point at an empty shopfront across the street.
sentences.cn: 站在街角，我看着他指向对街的一个空店面。

sentences.en: His eyes were bright with plans.
sentences.cn: 他的眼睛闪闪发光，充满了计划。

sentences.en: Behind him, a small figure in a red coat wrote something in a notebook and slipped away before I could see her face.
sentences.cn: 他身后，一个穿红外套的小个子在笔记本上写了什么，在我看清她的脸之前就溜走了。

besides:1.en: Tang and I walked the block twice, checking foot traffic. The corner unit had good light and a wide door. *Besides*, the bus stop right outside meant customers every fifteen minutes. Tang ticked boxes on a clipboard and looked pleased. I noticed she kept glancing at the closed flower shop next door, whose owner, an old man with paint-stained gloves, watched us without blinking.
besides:1.cnHint: 叙述者和阿糖考察街角店面时，发现它____有公交站的优势。
besides:1.hook: The old man with paint-stained gloves had not moved in twenty minutes.
besides:1.line: 'The rent is fair, and *besides*, the location is perfect.'

sentences.en: Tang and I walked the block twice, checking foot traffic.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我走了两遍街区，检查行人流量。

sentences.en: The corner unit had good light and a wide door.
sentences.cn: 角落单位光线充足，门也宽敞。

sentences.en: *Besides*, the bus stop right outside meant customers every fifteen minutes.
Tang ticked boxes on a clipboard and looked pleased.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在剪贴板上打勾，看起来很满意。

sentences.en: I noticed she kept glancing at the closed flower shop next door, whose owner, an old man with paint-stained gloves, watched us without blinking.
sentences.cn: 我注意到她一直在看隔壁关闭的花店，花店老板是个手上沾满油漆的老人，眼睛一眨不眨地看着我们。

certainly:1.en: A city inspector arrived while the Manager was measuring the front window. She flipped through her papers, asked three sharp questions, and then smiled. 'You may *certainly* open here,' she said, stamping a form, 'as long as the side alley stays clear.' The Manager exhaled loudly. I quietly moved two boxes of stock that were already sitting in the alley, hoping nobody had noticed they were ours.
certainly:1.cnHint: 城市检查员告诉店长，新店____可以开业，但有一个条件。
certainly:1.hook: Someone had already photographed those boxes in the alley.
certainly:1.line: 'You may *certainly* open here,' she said with a firm nod.

sentences.en: A city inspector arrived while the Manager was measuring the front window.
sentences.cn: 城市检查员在店长量前窗时来了。

sentences.en: She flipped through her papers, asked three sharp questions, and then smiled.
sentences.cn: 她翻过她的文件，问了三个尖锐的问题，然后微笑了。

sentences.en: 'You may *certainly* open here,' she said, stamping a form, 'as long as the side alley stays clear.'
The Manager exhaled loudly.
sentences.cn: 店长大声呼出一口气。

sentences.en: I quietly moved two boxes of stock that were already sitting in the alley, hoping nobody had noticed they were ours.
sentences.cn: 我静静地移开了两箱已经堆在小巷里的存货，希望没人注意到它们是我们的。

challenging:1.en: Walking back from the new site, Tang said finding good night staff for two stores would be *challenging*. The Manager shrugged and said he had someone in mind. He looked at me. I looked at the pavement. Three pigeons looked at the pavement too, which felt like solidarity. Later, Tang texted me a single question mark, and I still have not replied.
challenging:1.cnHint: 阿糖认为同时管理两家店的夜班员工是件____的事，店长却看向了叙述者。
challenging:1.hook: Tang's single question mark sat unanswered in my phone all night.
challenging:1.line: 'Running two stores at once will be *challenging*, but we can do it.'

sentences.en: Walking back from the new site, Tang said finding good night staff for two stores would be *challenging*.
The Manager shrugged and said he had someone in mind.
sentences.cn: 店长耸了耸肩，说他有个人选。

sentences.en: He looked at me.
sentences.cn: 他看着我。

sentences.en: I looked at the pavement.
sentences.cn: 我看着人行道。

sentences.en: Three pigeons looked at the pavement too, which felt like solidarity.
sentences.cn: 三只鸽子也看着人行道，这感觉像是团结。

sentences.en: Later, Tang texted me a single question mark, and I still have not replied.
sentences.cn: 后来，阿糖给我发了一条短信，只有一个问号，我至今还没回复。

circumstance:1.en: Lin appeared at the corner just as the Manager was locking up the new unit. They stood two metres apart, both pretending to check their phones. Under any other *circumstance* I would have walked on, but Tang nudged me to stay. Nobody spoke for a long minute. Then Lin pointed at the sign the Manager had just taped to the window and said, very quietly, 'Nice font.'
circumstance:1.cnHint: 在任何其他____下，叙述者都会走开，但这次目睹了隔壁咖啡店的林和店长的奇异相遇。
circumstance:1.hook: 'Nice font' was the first thing Lin had said to the Manager in two years.
circumstance:1.line: 'Under this *circumstance*, I think we should talk.'

sentences.en: Lin appeared at the corner just as the Manager was locking up the new unit.
sentences.cn: 林恰好在店长上锁新店时出现在街角。

sentences.en: They stood two metres apart, both pretending to check their phones.
sentences.cn: 他们相隔两米站着，都假装在查看手机。

sentences.en: Under any other *circumstance* I would have walked on, but Tang nudged me to stay.
Nobody spoke for a long minute.
sentences.cn: 没人说话，沉默了很久。

sentences.en: Then Lin pointed at the sign the Manager had just taped to the window and said, very quietly, 'Nice font.'
sentences.cn: 然后林指着店长刚贴在窗户上的招牌，很轻声地说："字体不错。"

comfort:1.en: The Manager sat on the kerb after everyone else had gone, staring at the empty shopfront. I brought him a warm can of tea from our store. He took it without looking up. It was a small *comfort*, but his shoulders dropped a little and his breathing slowed. Down the street, a light went on in Lin's shop, then off again, as if someone had thought better of it.
comfort:1.cnHint: 叙述者给疲惫的店长送去一杯热茶，这成为他今晚小小的____。
comfort:1.hook: Lin's light turned on, then off — one second of hesitation, no more.
comfort:1.line: 'A hot drink is a small *comfort*, but it helps on hard days.'

sentences.en: The Manager sat on the kerb after everyone else had gone, staring at the empty shopfront.
sentences.cn: 其他人都走后，店长坐在路边，盯着空荡荡的店面。

sentences.en: I brought him a warm can of tea from our store.
sentences.cn: 我从我们的店里拿了一罐温热的茶给他。

sentences.en: He took it without looking up.
sentences.cn: 他接过去，头都没抬。

sentences.en: It was a small *comfort*, but his shoulders dropped a little and his breathing slowed.
Down the street, a light went on in Lin's shop, then off again, as if someone had thought better of it.
sentences.cn: 街道那边，隔壁咖啡店的林开了盏灯，又关了，好像有人想到了更好的主意。

enrich:1.en: The Manager told us the new branch would *enrich* the whole street, not just our business. He waved his arm at the bakery, the flower shop, and the phone-repair stall, as if welcoming them to a party they had not agreed to attend. The stall owner gave a careful thumbs-up. Later I found a handwritten note on our door that said: 'Please do not play music after midnight.'
enrich:1.cnHint: 店长豪言新分店将____整条街，但附近商户的反应却耐人寻味。
enrich:1.hook: The handwritten note had no name, but the ink matched Lin's pen.
enrich:1.line: 'A new store will *enrich* this street and bring us all closer.'

sentences.en: The Manager told us the new branch would *enrich* the whole street, not just our business.
He waved his arm at the bakery, the flower shop, and the phone-repair stall, as if welcoming them to a party they had not agreed to attend.
sentences.cn: 他挥舞着手臂指向面包店、花店和手机修理摊，好像在邀请他们参加一场他们根本没同意的派对。

sentences.en: The stall owner gave a careful thumbs-up.
sentences.cn: 摊主小心翼翼地竖起了大拇指。

sentences.en: Later I found a handwritten note on our door that said: 'Please do not play music after midnight.'
sentences.cn: 后来我在我们门上发现了一张手写纸条，上面写着："请不要在午夜后放音乐。"

egg:1.en: The Manager called me outside just after midnight. He pointed at the new shop window across the street, where someone had thrown a raw *egg* against the glass. 'That happened on our first week too,' he said, almost proudly. I looked at the yellow mess and wondered who would do such a thing.
egg:1.cnHint: 店长带我出门，指着对面新店的橱窗——上面沾着一个____留下的痕迹。
egg:1.hook: The Manager smiled too calmly for someone looking at a mess.
egg:1.line: 'A raw *egg* on the window — that means someone is already scared of them.'

sentences.en: The Manager called me outside just after midnight.
sentences.cn: 店长在午夜刚过不久叫我出来。

sentences.en: He pointed at the new shop window across the street, where someone had thrown a raw *egg* against the glass.
'That happened on our first week too,' he said, almost proudly.
sentences.cn: "我们第一周也发生过这种事，"他说，几乎带着几分骄傲。

sentences.en: I looked at the yellow mess and wondered who would do such a thing.
sentences.cn: 我看着那黄色的一团烂糊，想知道谁会做这种事。

hire:1.en: A woman in a bright yellow jacket stopped me on the pavement while I was putting out the morning papers. She asked if the new shop down the road was really going to *hire* twenty people from the neighbourhood. I said I had no idea. She nodded slowly, like that answer told her everything.
hire:1.cnHint: 一位穿黄夹克的女士问我，听说那家新店要____很多本地人，是真的吗？
hire:1.hook: She glanced back at our store before she walked away.
hire:1.line: 'They say they will *hire* local people — every single one.'

sentences.en: A woman in a bright yellow jacket stopped me on the pavement while I was putting out the morning papers.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着亮黄色夹克的女人在我摆放早报时在人行道上拦住了我。

sentences.en: She asked if the new shop down the road was really going to *hire* twenty people from the neighbourhood.
I said I had no idea.
sentences.cn: 我说我不知道。

sentences.en: She nodded slowly, like that answer told her everything.
sentences.cn: 她缓缓点头，仿佛那个答案已经告诉了她一切。

aid:1.en: Tang and I were stacking boxes outside when an old man tripped on the uneven pavement near the corner. Tang moved fast, offering a hand. 'Night-shift *aid* service,' Tang joked, helping the man steady himself. The old man laughed, then looked up at our sign with warm eyes.
aid:1.cnHint: 唐迅速上前____一位在转角绊倒的老人，还开了个玩笑。
aid:1.hook: The old man whispered something to Tang that made Tang go very quiet.
aid:1.line: 'Think of it as free *aid* — we are open all night anyway.'

sentences.en: Tang and I were stacking boxes outside when an old man tripped on the uneven pavement near the corner.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我在外面堆箱子，一个老人在角落附近不平坦的人行道上绊倒了。

sentences.en: Tang moved fast, offering a hand.
sentences.cn: 阿糖反应很快，伸出手去扶。

sentences.en: 'Night-shift *aid* service,' Tang joked, helping the man steady himself.
The old man laughed, then looked up at our sign with warm eyes.
sentences.cn: 老人笑了起来，然后用温暖的眼神抬头看着我们的招牌。

bill:1.en: Lin from the shop across the street walked over at dawn and handed me a folded piece of paper. 'Your Manager left this on our door,' Lin said, cool and polite. It was a water *bill* — the Manager had paid it for the wrong address by mistake. Lin watched my face the whole time.
bill:1.cnHint: 林把一张____递给我，说是店长错放在他们门上的。
bill:1.hook: Lin did not leave straight away.
bill:1.line: 'This *bill* has your store name on it — I think there has been a mistake.'

sentences.en: Lin from the shop across the street walked over at dawn and handed me a folded piece of paper.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在黎明时走了过来，递给我一张折起来的纸。

sentences.en: 'Your Manager left this on our door,' Lin said, cool and polite.
sentences.cn: "你们店长把这个留在我们门上，"林说得冷静而有礼。

sentences.en: It was a water *bill* — the Manager had paid it for the wrong address by mistake.
Lin watched my face the whole time.
sentences.cn: 林一直看着我的脸。

paint:1.en: I arrived early to find the Manager on a ladder, touching up the front wall with a small brush. The new shop down the road had clean white walls, so the Manager had decided to *paint* ours a warm yellow. He climbed down and looked pleased. 'First impression,' he said, 'is everything.'
paint:1.cnHint: 店长爬上梯子，决定把店面____成暖黄色，说第一印象最重要。
paint:1.hook: Lin stood at the corner, watching every brushstroke.
paint:1.line: 'I will *paint* it yellow — yellow means we are open and we are happy.'

sentences.en: I arrived early to find the Manager on a ladder, touching up the front wall with a small brush.
sentences.cn: 我提前到达，发现店长站在梯子上，用小刷子触笔描绘前墙。

sentences.en: The new shop down the road had clean white walls, so the Manager had decided to *paint* ours a warm yellow.
He climbed down and looked pleased.
sentences.cn: 他爬了下来，看起来很满意。

sentences.en: 'First impression,' he said, 'is everything.'
sentences.cn: "第一印象，"他说，"就是一切。"

bean:1.en: Just before sunrise, a student sat on the kerb outside eating a cup of warm *bean* soup she had bought inside. She looked tired, books piled beside her. She told me she had been studying all night for an exam. I brought her a plastic spoon she had forgotten to take.
bean:1.cnHint: 一个学生坐在路边喝____汤，旁边放着一堆书，说她通宵复习了。
bean:1.hook: The title on top of her notes was the same subject I had failed once.
bean:1.line: 'This *bean* soup is the only thing keeping me awake right now.'

sentences.en: Just before sunrise, a student sat on the kerb outside eating a cup of warm *bean* soup she had bought inside.
She looked tired, books piled beside her.
sentences.cn: 她看起来很疲惫，书堆在她身边。

sentences.en: She told me she had been studying all night for an exam.
sentences.cn: 她告诉我她整夜都在为考试复习。

sentences.en: I brought her a plastic spoon she had forgotten to take.
sentences.cn: 我给了她一个她忘了拿的塑料勺子。

birthday:1.en: Tang came rushing out of the store to catch a little girl who had just dropped her bag on the pavement. Inside was a small cake box, slightly crushed. 'It is my grandpa's *birthday*,' she said, her eyes wide with worry. Tang straightened the box carefully and told her it would still taste wonderful.
birthday:1.cnHint: 唐帮一个小女孩捡起掉落的袋子，里面是给爷爷____用的蛋糕，有点压扁了。
birthday:1.hook: The girl ran off, then turned back and smiled at Tang like she knew a secret.
birthday:1.line: 'Today is grandpa's *birthday* — this cake has to be perfect.'

sentences.en: Tang came rushing out of the store to catch a little girl who had just dropped her bag on the pavement.
sentences.cn: 阿糖冲出店外去接住一个刚把袋子掉在人行道上的小女孩。

sentences.en: Inside was a small cake box, slightly crushed.
sentences.cn: 里面是一个小蛋糕盒，有点压扁了。

sentences.en: 'It is my grandpa's *birthday*,' she said, her eyes wide with worry.
Tang straightened the box carefully and told her it would still taste wonderful.
sentences.cn: 阿糖小心地把盒子摆正，告诉她蛋糕还是会很好吃的。

flight:1.en: A man in a coat stood outside checking his watch every thirty seconds. He asked me which bus went to the airport. He had a very early *flight* and was afraid of missing it. I pointed him to the stop one corner down. He thanked me and sprinted away, coat flying behind him.
flight:1.cnHint: 一个男人问我去机场怎么坐车，说他有一个早班____，快赶不上了。
flight:1.hook: He left a small notebook on the bench outside, still open.
flight:1.line: 'My *flight* is at five — if I miss it, six months of work disappears.'

sentences.en: A man in a coat stood outside checking his watch every thirty seconds.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着外套的男人站在外面，每三十秒检查一次手表。

sentences.en: He asked me which bus went to the airport.
sentences.cn: 他问我哪辆公交车去机场。

sentences.en: He had a very early *flight* and was afraid of missing it.
I pointed him to the stop one corner down.
sentences.cn: 我指了指下一个角落的车站。

sentences.en: He thanked me and sprinted away, coat flying behind him.
sentences.cn: 他道了谢，然后冲了过去，外套在身后飞扬。

housing:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new corner lot, pointing at the empty building next door. 'This block has good *housing* for staff,' he said, 'cheap rent, close walk.' I looked up at the dark windows and tried to imagine living so near the store. Something felt both cosy and a little strange.
housing:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址附近查看____，觉得员工住在附近很方便。
housing:1.hook: But one window on the third floor already had a light on.
housing:1.line: 'Good *housing* near the store means staff arrive on time.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new corner lot, pointing at the empty building next door.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新角落地段外，指着隔壁的空楼。

sentences.en: 'This block has good *housing* for staff,' he said, 'cheap rent, close walk.'
I looked up at the dark windows and tried to imagine living so near the store.
sentences.cn: 我抬起头看着那些黑暗的窗户，试着想象住得离店铺这么近会是什么样子。

sentences.en: Something felt both cosy and a little strange.
sentences.cn: 感觉既舒服又有点奇怪。

behaviour:1.en: A small dog sat outside the new branch site, perfectly still while its owner argued with a city worker. Everyone nearby watched the dog, not the argument. Its calm *behaviour* made me feel a little ashamed — I had been pacing nervously all morning about the opening plan. The dog glanced at me once, then looked away.
behaviour:1.cnHint: 店外一只小狗的____让叙述者感到有些惭愧。
behaviour:1.hook: Then the dog stood up and walked straight through the unlocked front door.
behaviour:1.line: 'That dog's *behaviour* is better than half my staff.'

sentences.en: A small dog sat outside the new branch site, perfectly still while its owner argued with a city worker.
sentences.cn: 一只小狗坐在新分店地段外，完全静止不动，它的主人在和一个城市工作人员争论。

sentences.en: Everyone nearby watched the dog, not the argument.
sentences.cn: 附近的人都看着那只狗，而不是那场争论。

sentences.en: Its calm *behaviour* made me feel a little ashamed — I had been pacing nervously all morning about the opening plan.
The dog glanced at me once, then looked away.
sentences.cn: 那只狗看了我一眼，然后转开了视线。

husband:1.en: A woman stopped me on the pavement near the new site and asked if we sold hot soup. I said not yet. She sighed and said her *husband* always bought soup here on cold nights, back when this corner had an old noodle stall. She touched the bare wall gently, then smiled and walked away.
husband:1.cnHint: 一位女士提到她的____曾常在这个街角买热汤。
husband:1.hook: She left behind a folded paper with a soup recipe on it.
husband:1.line: 'My *husband* used to stop here every single cold night.'

sentences.en: A woman stopped me on the pavement near the new site and asked if we sold hot soup.
sentences.cn: 一个女人在新地段附近的人行道上拦住我，问我们是否卖热汤。

sentences.en: I said not yet.
sentences.cn: 我说还没有。

sentences.en: She sighed and said her *husband* always bought soup here on cold nights, back when this corner had an old noodle stall.
She touched the bare wall gently, then smiled and walked away.
sentences.cn: 她触了一下光秃秃的墙，然后微笑着走开了。

tourist:1.en: A young *tourist* with a large backpack stood at the future store entrance, map in hand, looking very lost. I was checking the site for the Manager and felt sorry for him. I gave him directions to the old street market three blocks east. He thanked me twice, then asked if we had cold drinks yet.
tourist:1.cnHint: 一位____在新店门口迷路，叙述者帮助了他。
tourist:1.hook: He pulled out a camera and took a photo of the empty shopfront instead.
tourist:1.line: 'Excuse me, every *tourist* guide shows a shop on this corner.'

sentences.en: A young *tourist* with a large backpack stood at the future store entrance, map in hand, looking very lost.
I was checking the site for the Manager and felt sorry for him.
sentences.cn: 我在帮店长查看地址的时候，看到他可怜兮兮的样子。

sentences.en: I gave him directions to the old street market three blocks east.
sentences.cn: 我给他指了向东三个街区的老街市。

sentences.en: He thanked me twice, then asked if we had cold drinks yet.
sentences.cn: 他谢了我两次，然后问我们有没有冷饮。

agent:1.en: A woman in a neat grey coat arrived at the new branch corner with a clipboard and a measuring tape. 'I'm the property *agent*,' she told me briskly, 'here to sign the final papers.' She measured the doorway three times, wrote something down, and frowned at her notes. The Manager had said nothing about final papers today.
agent:1.cnHint: 一位____来到新店签署最终文件，叙述者感到意外。
agent:1.hook: The clipboard had two different store names on the top sheet.
agent:1.line: 'As your *agent*, I need to see the Manager right now.'

sentences.en: A woman in a neat grey coat arrived at the new branch corner with a clipboard and a measuring tape.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着整洁灰色大衣的女人拿着剪贴板和卷尺来到新店的角落。

sentences.en: 'I'm the property *agent*,' she told me briskly, 'here to sign the final papers.'
She measured the doorway three times, wrote something down, and frowned at her notes.
sentences.cn: 她把门框量了三遍，记下什么东西，皱着眉看着笔记。

sentences.en: The Manager had said nothing about final papers today.
sentences.cn: 店长今天根本没说过什么最终文件的事。

cash:1.en: Tang met me outside the new site carrying a small envelope. 'Deposit,' she whispered, patting it. 'All *cash*, the way the landlord wanted.' She looked left and right like someone in a spy film, which made me laugh. The morning street was empty except for a pigeon. Tang did not find it funny at all.
cash:1.cnHint: 阿糖带着一个装有____的信封来到新店，举止十分神秘。
cash:1.hook: When she opened the envelope, it held only a handwritten note.
cash:1.line: 'He said bring *cash*, so I brought every note I had.'

sentences.en: Tang met me outside the new site carrying a small envelope.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在新店址外面见我，手里拿着个小信封。

sentences.en: 'Deposit,' she whispered, patting it.
sentences.cn: "定金，"她小声说，拍了拍信封。

sentences.en: 'All *cash*, the way the landlord wanted.'
She looked left and right like someone in a spy film, which made me laugh.
sentences.cn: 她左看右看的样子就像在看谍报片，逗得我直笑。

sentences.en: The morning street was empty except for a pigeon.
sentences.cn: 早上的街道空荡荡的，只有一只鸽子。

sentences.en: Tang did not find it funny at all.
sentences.cn: 阿糖一点都没觉得好笑。

competition:1.en: Lin was already standing outside the new branch site when I arrived, arms crossed, studying the street. 'Nice corner,' she said without looking at me. 'The *competition* for this block was fierce — three other chains wanted it.' She finally turned and gave me a small, tight smile. I was not sure if she was pleased or warning me.
competition:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在新店门口提到，这个街角曾面临激烈的____。
competition:1.hook: She then pointed to a store two doors down that had just opened.
competition:1.line: 'We won the *competition* for this corner, but only just.'

sentences.en: Lin was already standing outside the new branch site when I arrived, arms crossed, studying the street.
sentences.cn: 我到的时候隔壁咖啡店的林已经站在新店址外面，双臂交叉，盯着这条街。

sentences.en: 'Nice corner,' she said without looking at me.
sentences.cn: "不错的角落，"她说，眼睛没看我。

sentences.en: 'The *competition* for this block was fierce — three other chains wanted it.'
She finally turned and gave me a small, tight smile.
sentences.cn: 她终于转过身，给了我一个淡淡的、紧绷的笑容。

sentences.en: I was not sure if she was pleased or warning me.
sentences.cn: 我不太确定她是高兴还是在警告我。

farmer:1.en: An old man sat on a crate beside the future store, selling small bags of dried peppers from a worn basket. He told me he was a *farmer* from a village two hours away and came every weekend to sell here. He gave me one bag for free and said the corner had always been lucky. I hoped he was right.
farmer:1.cnHint: 一位____在新店门口卖干辣椒，并说这个街角一直很吉利。
farmer:1.hook: He mentioned he had sold here thirty years ago, before the last store burned down.
farmer:1.line: 'I am a *farmer*, but I know a good corner when I see one.'

sentences.en: An old man sat on a crate beside the future store, selling small bags of dried peppers from a worn basket.
sentences.cn: 一个老人坐在未来店铺旁边的板条箱上，用一个旧篮子卖装在小袋子里的干辣椒。

sentences.en: He told me he was a *farmer* from a village two hours away and came every weekend to sell here.
He gave me one bag for free and said the corner had always been lucky.
sentences.cn: 他送了我一袋，说这个角落一直都很幸运。

sentences.en: I hoped he was right.
sentences.cn: 我希望他是对的。

collection:1.en: The Manager spread a large paper map across the counter and pointed to six red dots. 'Each dot is a possible site for the new branch,' he said. I looked at the *collection* of locations — a park corner, two bus stops, a school gate, a hospital entrance, and our own street — and suddenly felt the weight of the decision.
collection:1.cnHint: 店长把六个备选新店地址的____摆在柜台上，让我感受到了这个决定的分量。
collection:1.hook: But one of those red dots already had a visitor waiting there every night.
collection:1.line: 'Look at this *collection* of spots — one of them will be our next store.'

sentences.en: The Manager spread a large paper map across the counter and pointed to six red dots.
sentences.cn: 店长在柜台上铺开一张大纸质地图，指向六个红点。

sentences.en: 'Each dot is a possible site for the new branch,' he said.
sentences.cn: "每个点都是新店的一个可能地址，"他说。

sentences.en: I looked at the *collection* of locations — a park corner, two bus stops, a school gate, a hospital entrance, and our own street — and suddenly felt the weight of the decision.

depression:1.en: Tang and I walked the block near the old cinema to check a possible branch site. The pavement dipped sharply in front of an empty unit — a wide *depression* filled with last night's rain. Tang jumped it easily. I did not. We stood there, soaked and laughing, until a passing woman gave us a look of deep pity.
depression:1.cnHint: 唐和我去勘察新店选址时，遇到了路面上一处积满雨水的____，结果我跳过去时失败了。
depression:1.hook: The woman who pitied us stopped, turned back, and handed Tang a business card.
depression:1.line: 'Watch that *depression* in the road — I landed in it this morning and ruined my shoes.'

sentences.en: Tang and I walked the block near the old cinema to check a possible branch site.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我在老电影院附近的街区走了一圈，检查一个可能的店址。

sentences.en: The pavement dipped sharply in front of an empty unit — a wide *depression* filled with last night's rain.
Tang jumped it easily.
sentences.cn: 阿糖轻轻一跳就跳过去了。

sentences.en: I did not.
sentences.cn: 我没有。

sentences.en: We stood there, soaked and laughing, until a passing woman gave us a look of deep pity.
sentences.cn: 我们站在那里，浑身湿漉漉的，笑个不停，直到一个路过的女人用深深的同情眼神看了我们一眼。

foot:1.en: The Manager paced the empty shopfront on Maple Lane, measuring the width by counting steps. 'About thirty *foot* across,' he said, more to himself than to me. I wrote it down. A small girl on a bicycle rode past, glanced at us, then circled back as if we were the most interesting thing on the street.
foot:1.cnHint: 店长用脚步丈量枫树街空铺的宽度，估算出大约三十____，一个小女孩骑车路过后又折了回来。
foot:1.hook: The girl stopped and said she came here every single day — and why.
foot:1.line: 'Roughly thirty *foot* wide — that is just enough for our layout.'

sentences.en: The Manager paced the empty shopfront on Maple Lane, measuring the width by counting steps.
sentences.cn: 店长在枫树巷的空店铺里踱步，用数脚步的方式量宽度。

sentences.en: 'About thirty *foot* across,' he said, more to himself than to me.
I wrote it down.
sentences.cn: 我记下来了。

sentences.en: A small girl on a bicycle rode past, glanced at us, then circled back as if we were the most interesting thing on the street.
sentences.cn: 一个骑自行车的小女孩骑过，瞥了我们一眼，然后折了回来，好像我们是街上最有趣的东西。

graduate:1.en: Outside the university gate, Tang and I counted passing faces to judge foot traffic for a possible branch. A young man in a new shirt stopped us and asked if we were hiring. 'I am a fresh *graduate*,' he said, smiling nervously. Tang looked at me. I looked at Tang. We both looked at our very understaffed store.
graduate:1.cnHint: 在大学门口考察客流时，一位刚刚成为____的年轻人主动向我们询问是否招人。
graduate:1.hook: He pulled out a folded resume that somehow already listed our store's address.
graduate:1.line: 'I am a new *graduate* and I have wanted to work here since my first year.'

sentences.en: Outside the university gate, Tang and I counted passing faces to judge foot traffic for a possible branch.
sentences.cn: 在大学门口，阿糖和我通过数经过的人脸来判断可能店址的人流量。

sentences.en: A young man in a new shirt stopped us and asked if we were hiring.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着崭新衬衣的年轻人拦住我们，问我们是不是在招人。

sentences.en: 'I am a fresh *graduate*,' he said, smiling nervously.
Tang looked at me.
sentences.cn: 阿糖看了看我。

sentences.en: I looked at Tang.
sentences.cn: 我看了看阿糖。

sentences.en: We both looked at our very understaffed store.
sentences.cn: 我们都看了看我们严重缺人的店。

intake:1.en: The Manager stood on the pavement outside the hospital site and watched people enter. He counted quietly, then nodded. 'High *intake* of visitors every morning — families, nurses, patients picking up small things.' I wrote down his words and noticed a woman across the road had been watching us count for ten minutes, arms folded.
intake:1.cnHint: 店长在医院门口观察每日____的人流量，却没注意到对面有个女人一直盯着我们看。
intake:1.hook: The woman crossed the road and told us she had been planning the same branch herself.
intake:1.line: 'The daily *intake* of people here is three times what we get on our street.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood on the pavement outside the hospital site and watched people enter.
sentences.cn: 店长站在医院店址外的人行道上，看着人们进去。

sentences.en: He counted quietly, then nodded.
sentences.cn: 他默默地数着，然后点了点头。

sentences.en: 'High *intake* of visitors every morning — families, nurses, patients picking up small things.'
I wrote down his words and noticed a woman across the road had been watching us count for ten minutes, arms folded.
sentences.cn: 我记下了他的话，突然注意到马路对面有个女人已经盯着我们数了十分钟，双臂交叉。

screen:1.en: Lin from the shop across the street appeared at the corner just as Tang and I were photographing a possible branch site. She held up her phone like a *screen* between her face and ours. 'Just checking the area,' she said, not very convincingly. The corner was quiet. We all stood there pretending not to notice each other.
screen:1.cnHint: 当我和唐在勘察新址时，竞争对手林出现了，她举着手机像一块____挡住了自己的脸。
screen:1.hook: Lin's phone screen, facing us by accident, showed the exact same location pinned on a map.
screen:1.line: 'I am just using my phone as a *screen* from the sun — nothing suspicious at all.'

sentences.en: Lin from the shop across the street appeared at the corner just as Tang and I were photographing a possible branch site.
sentences.cn: 我和阿糖在给一个可能的店址拍照的时候，隔壁的林从角落出现了。

sentences.en: She held up her phone like a *screen* between her face and ours.
'Just checking the area,' she said, not very convincingly.
sentences.cn: "就是来看看这一带，"她说，听起来不太有说服力。

sentences.en: The corner was quiet.
sentences.cn: 这个角落很安静。

sentences.en: We all stood there pretending not to notice each other.
sentences.cn: 我们都站在那儿假装没注意到彼此。

chair:1.en: The Manager had somehow dragged a folding *chair* to the pavement outside the empty unit on Bridge Street and was sitting in it, drinking tea, watching people walk by. 'Research,' he told me firmly when I arrived. Two neighbours had already joined him with their own stools, and one was offering suggestions about shelf layout.
chair:1.cnHint: 店长搬了把____坐在候选新店门口喝茶"做调研"，附近居民也凑了过来出主意。
chair:1.hook: One neighbour then mentioned they owned the building and had been waiting for a tenant.
chair:1.line: 'Bring a *chair* and sit with me — the foot traffic tells you everything in one hour.'

sentences.en: The Manager had somehow dragged a folding *chair* to the pavement outside the empty unit on Bridge Street and was sitting in it, drinking tea, watching people walk by.
'Research,' he told me firmly when I arrived.
sentences.cn: "调查，"我来的时候他坚定地对我说。

sentences.en: Two neighbours had already joined him with their own stools, and one was offering suggestions about shelf layout.
sentences.cn: 已经有两个邻居加入他，带来了自己的小凳子，其中一个还在出主意怎么摆货架。

court:1.en: The last site on the list was beside a community basketball *court*. Even at midnight it was bright and loud, players calling to each other between shots. Tang grinned. 'Late-night snacks, cold drinks, instant noodles,' she said. I was already imagining the queue. Then the ball bounced out and rolled to a stop at my feet.
court:1.cnHint: 候选地址中最后一处位于社区篮球____旁，深夜依然热闹，唐已经开始畅想营业场景了。
court:1.hook: The player who chased the ball looked up and said he had been hoping for years someone would open a store right here.
court:1.line: 'A store next to a *court* like this one would sell out every night, trust me.'

sentences.en: The last site on the list was beside a community basketball *court*.
Even at midnight it was bright and loud, players calling to each other between shots.
sentences.cn: 即使在午夜,这里还是亮堂堂的,闹哄哄的,球员们在投篮间隙互相喊话。

sentences.en: Tang grinned.
sentences.cn: 阿糖咧嘴笑了。

sentences.en: 'Late-night snacks, cold drinks, instant noodles,' she said.
sentences.cn: "夜宵、冷饮、速冻面,"她说。

sentences.en: I was already imagining the queue.
sentences.cn: 我已经在脑子里想象排队的人潮了。

sentences.en: Then the ball bounced out and rolled to a stop at my feet.
sentences.cn: 然后篮球弹了出去,滚到我脚边停下了。

female:1.en: The Manager pointed at a cat sitting outside the door. 'She has been here every night this week,' he said. I looked closer. A small *female* with bright eyes stared back at me, calm as if she owned the place. Tang left a bowl of water out. The cat did not touch it.
female:1.cnHint: 店长指着门外的猫说，这只____每晚都来。
female:1.hook: But the next night, she brought a friend.
female:1.line: 'She is a *female*, so she will probably bring kittens soon,' Tang said quietly.

sentences.en: The Manager pointed at a cat sitting outside the door.
sentences.cn: 店长指了指门外坐着的一只猫。

sentences.en: 'She has been here every night this week,' he said.
sentences.cn: "她每晚都来,这整个礼拜都在,"他说。

sentences.en: I looked closer.
sentences.cn: 我凑近看。

sentences.en: A small *female* with bright eyes stared back at me, calm as if she owned the place.
Tang left a bowl of water out.
sentences.cn: 阿糖留了一碗水。

sentences.en: The cat did not touch it.
sentences.cn: 猫没有碰它。

holiday:1.en: It was the first day of a long *holiday*, and the street outside was almost empty. I expected a quiet shift. Instead, by midnight, every seat near the window was taken by people who had nowhere else to go. Tang smiled and said some folks just did not like being home alone.
holiday:1.cnHint: ____期间街上冷清，但店里却坐满了无处可去的人。
holiday:1.hook: One of them had been sitting there for three nights straight.
holiday:1.line: 'Every *holiday* is the same — lonely people find us,' Tang said with a warm shrug.

sentences.en: It was the first day of a long *holiday*, and the street outside was almost empty.
I expected a quiet shift.
sentences.cn: 我以为这会是个清静的班次。

sentences.en: Instead, by midnight, every seat near the window was taken by people who had nowhere else to go.
sentences.cn: 反而到了午夜,窗边的每个座位都坐满了无处可去的人。

sentences.en: Tang smiled and said some folks just did not like being home alone.
sentences.cn: 阿糖笑着说有些人就是不想一个人呆在家里。

pain:1.en: An old man came in just after two in the morning, moving slowly and holding his back. He bought a small bottle of hot water and pressed it against his side. 'The *pain* starts when it gets cold,' he told me, without my asking. He stayed an hour, said nothing more, and left with a small nod.
pain:1.cnHint: 一位老人深夜进来，用热水瓶贴着背部缓解____。
pain:1.hook: He came back the next night, and the night after that.
pain:1.line: 'The *pain* is not so bad when there is a warm place to sit,' he said softly.

sentences.en: An old man came in just after two in the morning, moving slowly and holding his back.
sentences.cn: 一个老男人在凌晨两点多走了进来,动作很慢,捂着腰。

sentences.en: He bought a small bottle of hot water and pressed it against his side.
sentences.cn: 他买了一小瓶热水,贴在身侧。

sentences.en: 'The *pain* starts when it gets cold,' he told me, without my asking.
He stayed an hour, said nothing more, and left with a small nod.
sentences.cn: 他呆了一个小时,没再说什么,走的时候冲我轻轻点了点头。

player:1.en: A young man in a sports jacket dropped three energy drinks on the counter at midnight. 'Big match tomorrow,' he said. I asked if he was a *player* on the team. He laughed and said no — he just never missed a game. Tang gave him a thumbs up. He bought four more drinks and jogged away.
player:1.cnHint: 一个年轻人买了好几瓶功能饮料，自称是球队的____。
player:1.hook: He came back the next week looking much less cheerful.
player:1.line: 'Every *player* on our team drinks two of these before warm-up,' he said proudly.

sentences.en: A young man in a sports jacket dropped three energy drinks on the counter at midnight.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着运动夹克的年轻男人在午夜时分把三罐能量饮料摔到柜台上。

sentences.en: 'Big match tomorrow,' he said.
sentences.cn: "明天有大赛,"他说。

sentences.en: I asked if he was a *player* on the team.
He laughed and said no — he just never missed a game.
sentences.cn: 他笑了,说不是——他就是从不错过任何一场比赛。

sentences.en: Tang gave him a thumbs up.
sentences.cn: 阿糖竖起了大拇指。

sentences.en: He bought four more drinks and jogged away.
sentences.cn: 他又买了四罐,一溜烟地跑了。

production:1.en: Lin walked in carrying a big cardboard box and set it on the counter without a word. Inside were small jars of sauce — her own *production*, she said, from a recipe her grandmother used. She wanted the Manager to sell them. He picked one up, read the label, and raised an eyebrow.
production:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了一箱自制酱料，说这是她自己的____，希望店里代卖。
production:1.hook: The Manager's eyebrow stayed raised for a very long time.
production:1.line: 'This *production* took me three weeks to get right,' Lin said, crossing her arms.

sentences.en: Lin walked in carrying a big cardboard box and set it on the counter without a word.
sentences.cn: 林从隔壁咖啡店走进来,拎着一个大纸箱,什么话都没说就放在了柜台上。

sentences.en: Inside were small jars of sauce — her own *production*, she said, from a recipe her grandmother used.
She wanted the Manager to sell them.
sentences.cn: 她想让店长卖这些。

sentences.en: He picked one up, read the label, and raised an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 店长拿起一罐,看了看标签,眉头一挑。

secure:1.en: After the new shelves arrived, the Manager spent an hour making sure every bracket was *secure*. He shook each shelf twice, then a third time. Tang caught my eye and tried not to laugh. 'If a shelf falls,' the Manager said without looking up, 'everything on it falls too.' He had a point.
secure:1.cnHint: 店长反复检查新货架是否____，阿糖和我差点忍不住笑出来。
secure:1.hook: One shelf wobbled just slightly, and the Manager went very quiet.
secure:1.line: 'I need every shelf to be *secure* before we put a single item on it,' the Manager said firmly.

sentences.en: After the new shelves arrived, the Manager spent an hour making sure every bracket was *secure*.
He shook each shelf twice, then a third time.
sentences.cn: 他摇了摇每一块架子,又摇了一遍。

sentences.en: Tang caught my eye and tried not to laugh.
sentences.cn: 阿糖朝我使眼色,努力憋住笑。

sentences.en: 'If a shelf falls,' the Manager said without looking up, 'everything on it falls too.'
sentences.cn: "要是架子掉下来,"店长头也没抬地说,"上面的东西全都得掉下来。"

sentences.en: He had a point.
sentences.cn: 他说得有道理。

audience:1.en: At three in the morning, a woman sat on the step outside and played a small instrument, very softly. I was the only *audience*. She did not seem to mind. After two songs she stood up, bought a warm tea, thanked me with a small bow, and walked away into the dark street.
audience:1.cnHint: 凌晨三点，一位女士在门口轻轻弹奏，我成了她唯一的____。
audience:1.hook: She left a folded note under the tea cup.
audience:1.line: 'You were a good *audience*,' she said, smiling before she turned to go.

sentences.en: At three in the morning, a woman sat on the step outside and played a small instrument, very softly.
sentences.cn: 凌晨三点,一个女人坐在外面的台阶上,吹着一件小乐器,声音很轻。

sentences.en: I was the only *audience*.
She did not seem to mind.
sentences.cn: 她似乎不在乎。

sentences.en: After two songs she stood up, bought a warm tea, thanked me with a small bow, and walked away into the dark street.
sentences.cn: 吹了两首曲子后她站起身,买了一杯温茶,冲我深深鞠了一躬,然后消失在黑黝黝的街道里。

borrow:1.en: A teenage boy knocked on the glass at four in the morning and held up a pen with a question on his face. I let him in. He needed to *borrow* a calculator — his exam was in five hours and his had stopped working. Tang found an old one under the counter. The boy sat down and did not look up for an hour.
borrow:1.cnHint: 一个男孩深夜敲窗，想____一个计算器，因为他的坏掉了。
borrow:1.hook: When he finally left, he forgot to take his student ID.
borrow:1.line: 'Can I *borrow* this until morning? I will bring it back, I promise,' he said.

sentences.en: A teenage boy knocked on the glass at four in the morning and held up a pen with a question on his face.
sentences.cn: 一个少年在凌晨四点时敲了敲玻璃,举起一支笔,用眼神问我。

sentences.en: I let him in.
sentences.cn: 我让他进来了。

sentences.en: He needed to *borrow* a calculator — his exam was in five hours and his had stopped working.
Tang found an old one under the counter.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在柜台下面翻出了一台旧计算器。

sentences.en: The boy sat down and did not look up for an hour.
sentences.cn: 男孩坐了下来,一个小时都没抬过头。

mile:1.en: The Manager spread a city map across the hood of his car. 'The new branch will be exactly one *mile* from here,' he said, tapping a red circle near the river. I stood on the pavement in the cold morning air, trying to picture a second store glowing in the dark.
mile:1.cnHint: 店长在车盖上摊开地图，指出新分店的____位置。
mile:1.hook: But why was Lin already standing at that exact spot?
mile:1.line: 'One *mile* south — that is where our future is.'

sentences.en: The Manager spread a city map across the hood of his car.
sentences.cn: 店长在车罩上铺开了一张城市地图。

sentences.en: 'The new branch will be exactly one *mile* from here,' he said, tapping a red circle near the river.
I stood on the pavement in the cold morning air, trying to picture a second store glowing in the dark.
sentences.cn: 我站在冷清的早晨的人行道上,试图想象第二家店在黑暗中闪闪发光的样子。

movement:1.en: I noticed a strange *movement* behind the half-built wall across the street — a shadow slipping between wooden boards. Tang grabbed my sleeve. 'Someone is watching us,' she whispered. The Manager kept talking about floor plans, but neither Tang nor I could look away from that wall.
movement:1.cnHint: 街对面的围墙后出现了奇怪的____，让我们心生警觉。
movement:1.hook: The shadow moved again, and this time it had a familiar shape.
movement:1.line: 'That *movement* behind the wall — did you see it too?'

sentences.en: I noticed a strange *movement* behind the half-built wall across the street — a shadow slipping between wooden boards.
Tang grabbed my sleeve.
sentences.cn: 阿糖拽住了我的袖子。

sentences.en: 'Someone is watching us,' she whispered.
sentences.cn: "有人在看我们,"她小声说。

sentences.en: The Manager kept talking about floor plans, but neither Tang nor I could look away from that wall.
sentences.cn: 店长还在滔滔不绝地讲着楼面设计,但我和阿糖都没法把眼神从那面墙移开。

party:1.en: A small crowd had gathered outside the empty shop the Manager wanted to rent. It turned out a local *party* committee had put up a notice claiming the building for a community centre. The Manager read the sign twice, then folded his arms. I quietly wondered whose name was at the bottom.
party:1.cnHint: 店长看中的店面门口贴着一个____的告示，声称要用作社区中心。
party:1.hook: Lin walked past, smiling just a little too widely.
party:1.line: 'The *party* notice went up last night — someone moved fast.'

sentences.en: A small crowd had gathered outside the empty shop the Manager wanted to rent.
sentences.cn: 店长想租的那间空店外面聚了一小群人。

sentences.en: It turned out a local *party* committee had put up a notice claiming the building for a community centre.
The Manager read the sign twice, then folded his arms.
sentences.cn: 店长读了两遍那张告示,然后交叉双臂。

sentences.en: I quietly wondered whose name was at the bottom.
sentences.cn: 我在心里暗暗想知道签名的是谁。

rescue:1.en: A delivery bicycle had tipped into the ditch beside the road, boxes of drinks scattered everywhere. Before I could think, Tang sprinted over. Her quick *rescue* of the goods meant nothing was broken. The driver kept bowing in thanks. I made a note: Tang is faster than she looks.
rescue:1.cnHint: 送货自行车翻进路边水沟，阿糖迅速____了那些货物。
rescue:1.hook: One box had a label that matched our store, not the new branch.
rescue:1.line: 'Lucky I was here for the *rescue*, or everything would be lost.'

sentences.en: A delivery bicycle had tipped into the ditch beside the road, boxes of drinks scattered everywhere.
sentences.cn: 一辆送货自行车翻进了路边的沟里，饮料箱散落一地。

sentences.en: Before I could think, Tang sprinted over.
sentences.cn: 我还没反应过来，阿糖就冲了过去。

sentences.en: Her quick *rescue* of the goods meant nothing was broken.
The driver kept bowing in thanks.
sentences.cn: 司机一个劲儿地鞠躬道谢。

sentences.en: I made a note: Tang is faster than she looks.
sentences.cn: 我记了一笔：阿糖比看上去的要快。

writing:1.en: Taped to the lamppost outside the future branch was a sheet of paper covered in neat *writing*. It listed reasons why the neighbourhood did not want a convenience store on that corner. I read every line. The arguments were careful, almost professional. Someone had spent real time on this.
writing:1.cnHint: 路灯柱上贴着一张满是____的纸，列出反对开分店的理由。
writing:1.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like Lin's.
writing:1.line: 'This *writing* is too neat to be just one angry neighbour.'

sentences.en: Taped to the lamppost outside the future branch was a sheet of paper covered in neat *writing*.
It listed reasons why the neighbourhood did not want a convenience store on that corner.
sentences.cn: 上面列举了这一带为什么不想在那个角落开便利店的种种理由。

sentences.en: I read every line.
sentences.cn: 我把每一行都读了。

sentences.en: The arguments were careful, almost professional.
sentences.cn: 论证很周密，几乎像是专业人士写的。

sentences.en: Someone had spent real time on this.
sentences.cn: 有人花了真功夫在这上面。

bite:1.en: Tang handed me a warm meat bun as we stood outside the half-empty building. I took one *bite* and immediately felt better about the cold and the long morning. 'Food first, problems second,' she said. The Manager appeared from around the corner, spotted the bun, and his face softened too.
bite:1.cnHint: 阿糖递来热包子，我____了一口，寒意顿时减轻了许多。
bite:1.hook: The Manager said the buns came from a shop that might become our rival.
bite:1.line: 'Go on, take a *bite* — you have been frowning for an hour.'

sentences.en: Tang handed me a warm meat bun as we stood outside the half-empty building.
sentences.cn: 阿糖递给我一个热汤包，我们站在空荡荡的楼外。

sentences.en: I took one *bite* and immediately felt better about the cold and the long morning.
'Food first, problems second,' she said.
sentences.cn: "先吃饭，后解决问题，"她说。

sentences.en: The Manager appeared from around the corner, spotted the bun, and his face softened too.
sentences.cn: 店长从拐角出现，看到汤包，脸色也柔和了。

capture:1.en: I tried to *capture* the whole scene on my phone — the half-finished sign, the Manager pointing at the roofline, Tang measuring the doorway with her arms spread wide. A photo could not hold the feeling, though. The street was quiet except for pigeons, and everything felt oddly important.
capture:1.cnHint: 我想用手机____眼前这一幕——店长和阿糖正在勘察新店面。
capture:1.hook: When I looked at the photo later, there was a face in the window above.
capture:1.line: 'Try to *capture* the sign in the shot — the Manager wants a record.'

sentences.en: I tried to *capture* the whole scene on my phone — the half-finished sign, the Manager pointing at the roofline, Tang measuring the doorway with her arms spread wide.
A photo could not hold the feeling, though.
sentences.cn: 照片拍不出那种感觉。

sentences.en: The street was quiet except for pigeons, and everything felt oddly important.
sentences.cn: 街上静得只能听见鸽子叫，一切都显得莫名其妙地重要。

cope:1.en: The building was dustier inside than the Manager had expected. Tang sneezed four times in a row. I tried to *cope* with the darkness by propping the door open with a brick. Light flooded in, and we all stood still for a moment, looking at the space that might soon become our second home.
cope:1.cnHint: 新店面里又黑又脏，我们各自想办法____眼前的困难。
cope:1.hook: In the far corner, someone had left a fresh cup of tea.
cope:1.line: 'How do you *cope* with the dark? I can barely see a thing.'

sentences.en: The building was dustier inside than the Manager had expected.
sentences.cn: 楼里面比店长预期的要尘土飞扬。

sentences.en: Tang sneezed four times in a row.
sentences.cn: 阿糖连打了四个喷嚏。

sentences.en: I tried to *cope* with the darkness by propping the door open with a brick.
Light flooded in, and we all stood still for a moment, looking at the space that might soon become our second home.
sentences.cn: 光亮涌了进来，我们都站着没动，看着这个很快就可能成为我们第二个家的空间。

burn:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site at dawn, watching workers pour hot tar on the road nearby. A careless splash landed on his wrist, leaving a small *burn* that he barely noticed. He kept his eyes on the signboard going up above the door, smiling quietly to himself.
burn:1.cnHint: 店长在新分店门口看招牌安装，手腕上不小心留下了一处____。
burn:1.hook: But the signboard spelled the store's name completely wrong.
burn:1.line: 'A little *burn* never stopped a grand opening,' the Manager said, wrapping his wrist.

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site at dawn, watching workers pour hot tar on the road nearby.
sentences.cn: 店长天亮的时候站在新店址外，看着工人在附近的路面上浇热沥青。

sentences.en: A careless splash landed on his wrist, leaving a small *burn* that he barely noticed.
He kept his eyes on the signboard going up above the door, smiling quietly to himself.
sentences.cn: 他的眼睛一直盯着门上方正在装上去的招牌，自己乐得很开心。

cook:1.en: Lin stood across the street from the new branch, watching a food cart owner *cook* noodles on an open flame right in front of the entrance. The smell drifted everywhere. Lin crossed her arms and thought: that cart was pulling in every hungry person who might have walked through their door instead.
cook:1.cnHint: 林站在新分店对面，看着一个摊主在门口____面条，抢走了不少客流。
cook:1.hook: Lin pulled out her phone and started making a very particular call.
cook:1.line: 'Why does he get to *cook* right outside our new branch?' Lin muttered.

sentences.en: Lin stood across the street from the new branch, watching a food cart owner *cook* noodles on an open flame right in front of the entrance.
The smell drifted everywhere.
sentences.cn: 气味飘得到处都是。

sentences.en: Lin crossed her arms and thought: that cart was pulling in every hungry person who might have walked through their door instead.
sentences.cn: 林双臂交叉，心想：那辆餐车把本该走进他们店里的每一个饿肚子的人都吸引过去了。

corporate:1.en: A man in a stiff suit arrived at the new branch before it even opened, sliding a thick envelope under the door. The Manager picked it up outside and read the header: it was a *corporate* notice from a large chain store two blocks away, warning them about a shared supplier agreement. The street felt very quiet suddenly.
corporate:1.cnHint: 一个西装男在新分店门口塞进一封____通知，让店长顿时沉默了。
corporate:1.hook: The Manager read the last line twice, then looked up the street slowly.
corporate:1.line: 'This is a *corporate* matter,' the suited man said, adjusting his tie firmly.

sentences.en: A man in a stiff suit arrived at the new branch before it even opened, sliding a thick envelope under the door.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着硬挺西装的男人在新店还没开张前就来了，在门下塞了一个厚厚的信封。

sentences.en: The Manager picked it up outside and read the header: it was a *corporate* notice from a large chain store two blocks away, warning them about a shared supplier agreement.
The street felt very quiet suddenly.
sentences.cn: 街道突然安静了下来。

dangerous:1.en: Tang was sent to hang a banner above the new branch entrance using a short ladder. The wind picked up fast, and the ladder began to sway against the wall. A woman passing by stopped and called out that the whole situation looked very *dangerous*. Tang laughed nervously and kept climbing anyway.
dangerous:1.cnHint: 唐在新分店门口爬梯子挂横幅，路过的人大喊这样做很____。
dangerous:1.hook: Then one ladder leg lifted clean off the pavement.
dangerous:1.line: 'This is *dangerous*, you should come down right now!' the woman shouted up.

sentences.en: Tang was sent to hang a banner above the new branch entrance using a short ladder.
sentences.cn: 阿糖被派去用一把小梯子在新店门口上方挂横幅。

sentences.en: The wind picked up fast, and the ladder began to sway against the wall.
sentences.cn: 风突然大了起来，梯子开始贴着墙摇晃。

sentences.en: A woman passing by stopped and called out that the whole situation looked very *dangerous*.
Tang laughed nervously and kept climbing anyway.
sentences.cn: 阿糖紧张地笑了笑，还是继续往上爬。

debt:1.en: Outside the new branch on opening morning, an old man sat on a folding chair and refused to leave. The Manager spoke to him gently and learned that the building's previous tenant had left without settling a *debt* with the old man's small supply shop. The old man just wanted someone to listen.
debt:1.cnHint: 开业当天，一位老人坐在新分店门口，原来前租户留下了一笔____未还。
debt:1.hook: The Manager sat down in a second chair and said nothing for a long moment.
debt:1.line: 'He left without clearing the *debt*, and nobody cared,' the old man said quietly.

sentences.en: Outside the new branch on opening morning, an old man sat on a folding chair and refused to leave.
sentences.cn: 开张那天早上，新店外坐着一个老大爷，死活不肯离开。

sentences.en: The Manager spoke to him gently and learned that the building's previous tenant had left without settling a *debt* with the old man's small supply shop.
The old man just wanted someone to listen.
sentences.cn: 老大爷只是想有人听他说话。

discipline:1.en: The Manager lined up the new branch staff on the pavement before the doors opened, running through every rule out loud. He told them that good *discipline* in a small store meant the difference between keeping customers and losing them in the first week. Lin watched from across the street, taking quiet notes in a little book.
discipline:1.cnHint: 店长在新分店门外给员工训话，强调良好的____是留住顾客的关键。
discipline:1.hook: Lin smiled and wrote one final note, then closed her little book with a snap.
discipline:1.line: '*Discipline* starts before the first customer even walks in,' the Manager said firmly.

sentences.en: The Manager lined up the new branch staff on the pavement before the doors opened, running through every rule out loud.
sentences.cn: 店长让新店的员工都排成一排站在人行道上，在门开之前把每一条规则都大声念了一遍。

sentences.en: He told them that good *discipline* in a small store meant the difference between keeping customers and losing them in the first week.
Lin watched from across the street, taking quiet notes in a little book.
sentences.cn: 林在对街看着，在一本小簿子里安静地记着笔记。

error:1.en: Tang was pasting the new branch's opening-hours sign onto the glass door when he noticed an *error*: someone had printed the closing time as two in the afternoon instead of two in the morning. A small crowd had gathered outside, reading the sign and already looking confused and a little disappointed.
error:1.cnHint: 唐在新分店玻璃门上贴营业时间告示时，发现上面有一处____，引来路人围观。
error:1.hook: Tang's phone rang — it was the Manager, calling from just inside the door.
error:1.line: 'There is an *error* on the sign — we close at two in the morning,' Tang said.

sentences.en: Tang was pasting the new branch's opening-hours sign onto the glass door when he noticed an *error*: someone had printed the closing time as two in the afternoon instead of two in the morning.
A small crowd had gathered outside, reading the sign and already looking confused and a little disappointed.
sentences.cn: 一小群人已经聚集在外面，读着这张牌子，看起来既困惑又有点失望。

gym:1.en: The new branch sat directly between a closed bakery and a *gym* whose members spilled onto the pavement every evening after their workouts, loud and cheerful and very thirsty. The Manager had chosen the location carefully. By the end of the first night, the sports drink shelf was already empty, and he was back on the phone with the supplier.
gym:1.cnHint: 新分店开在一家____旁边，店长选址很用心，第一晚运动饮料就卖空了。
gym:1.hook: But the gym's owner strolled in last, smiled, and asked for a word.
gym:1.line: 'The *gym* next door is our best neighbour,' the Manager told Tang happily.

sentences.en: The new branch sat directly between a closed bakery and a *gym* whose members spilled onto the pavement every evening after their workouts, loud and cheerful and very thirsty.
The Manager had chosen the location carefully.
sentences.cn: 店长精心选择了这个地址。

sentences.en: By the end of the first night, the sports drink shelf was already empty, and he was back on the phone with the supplier.
sentences.cn: 第一晚快要结束时，运动饮料架已经空了，他又拨通了供应商的电话。

salary:1.en: The Manager called me outside before my first shift. He pointed at the small sign above the door and said the store was opening a second branch nearby. Then he slid a paper across the hood of his car. My new *salary* was printed at the bottom — higher than I had expected for a night clerk.
salary:1.cnHint: 店长在外面告诉我，新分店开张，我的____也涨了。
salary:1.hook: But the number had a condition written in red ink.
salary:1.line: 'Your *salary* goes up the day the new branch opens,' he said.

sentences.en: The Manager called me outside before my first shift.
sentences.cn: 我第一班班前，店长把我叫到了外面。

sentences.en: He pointed at the small sign above the door and said the store was opening a second branch nearby.
sentences.cn: 他指着门上方的小牌子，说门店要在附近开一家分店。

sentences.en: Then he slid a paper across the hood of his car.
sentences.cn: 然后他把一张纸滑过他的车引擎盖。

sentences.en: My new *salary* was printed at the bottom — higher than I had expected for a night clerk.

shopping:1.en: On the corner opposite our store, Lin set up a small table and handed out flyers for the new branch. People passed by with bags already full from the weekend market. One older woman stopped, read the flyer, and nodded slowly. 'Good location,' she said. Lin smiled. All that morning *shopping* foot traffic walked straight past us toward the new site.
shopping:1.cnHint: 林在街角发传单，____的人群都被吸引向新店。
shopping:1.hook: Then Lin glanced back at our store with a very odd expression.
shopping:1.line: 'The *shopping* crowd this morning is bigger than I expected,' Lin said.

sentences.en: On the corner opposite our store, Lin set up a small table and handed out flyers for the new branch.
sentences.cn: 在我们店对面的街角，隔壁咖啡店的林摆了张小桌子，分发新分店的传单。

sentences.en: People passed by with bags already full from the weekend market.
sentences.cn: 人们提着周末市集的满满行囊走过。

sentences.en: One older woman stopped, read the flyer, and nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 一个年纪较大的女人停下来，读了传单，慢慢点点头。

sentences.en: 'Good location,' she said.
sentences.cn: "地理位置不错，"她说。

sentences.en: Lin smiled.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林笑了。

sentences.en: All that morning *shopping* foot traffic walked straight past us toward the new site.

tendency:1.en: Tang and I stood outside counting customers who entered Lin's new branch across the street. We had been tracking the numbers all week. Tang tapped her notebook. 'There is a clear *tendency*,' she said quietly. 'More people try a new place once, just for curiosity.' She closed the notebook and went back inside to restock the shelves.
tendency:1.cnHint: 唐观察后发现，顾客有一种明显的____去尝试新店。
tendency:1.hook: Tang had underlined one number three times and said nothing more.
tendency:1.line: 'I notice a *tendency* for new stores to win the first week,' Tang said.

sentences.en: Tang and I stood outside counting customers who entered Lin's new branch across the street.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我站在外面，数着进入街对面隔壁咖啡店的林新开分店的顾客。

sentences.en: We had been tracking the numbers all week.
sentences.cn: 我们整个星期都在追踪这些数字。

sentences.en: Tang tapped her notebook.
sentences.cn: 阿糖敲了敲她的笔记本。

sentences.en: 'There is a clear *tendency*,' she said quietly.
'More people try a new place once, just for curiosity.'
sentences.cn: "更多人只是出于好奇，第一次会尝试一家新店。"

sentences.en: She closed the notebook and went back inside to restock the shelves.
sentences.cn: 她合上笔记本，走回里面补货。

tough:1.en: The morning the second branch opened, the Manager asked me to carry a heavy folding sign two blocks down the road. The summer air was already thick and the pavement shone with heat. It was *tough* work, but I made it. I planted the sign on the corner and stood back to read it: grand opening, free coffee, today only.
tough:1.cnHint: 我扛着重广告牌走了两条街，这份活儿真____。
tough:1.hook: A stranger read the sign, then looked at me with sudden suspicion.
tough:1.line: 'It is *tough* to move that sign alone — let me help,' Tang said.

sentences.en: The morning the second branch opened, the Manager asked me to carry a heavy folding sign two blocks down the road.
sentences.cn: 第二家分店开业的那个早上，店长让我扛着一块沉重的折叠牌子走了两个街区。

sentences.en: The summer air was already thick and the pavement shone with heat.
sentences.cn: 夏日的空气已经又浓又热，路面闪闪发光。

sentences.en: It was *tough* work, but I made it.
I planted the sign on the corner and stood back to read it: grand opening, free coffee, today only.
sentences.cn: 我把牌子竖在街角，退后看了一眼：盛大开业，免费咖啡，仅限今天。

tour:1.en: The Manager decided to give the delivery driver a quick *tour* of the new branch before the first stock arrived. They walked the narrow aisles, tested the cold cabinet, and checked the back room. I waited outside with a clipboard. The driver said very little the whole time, only nodding at each item the Manager pointed to.
tour:1.cnHint: 店长带司机参观了新店，我站在外面等候，做了一次____。
tour:1.hook: The driver paused at the back door and asked one strange question.
tour:1.line: 'Let me *tour* the storage room one more time,' the driver said quietly.

sentences.en: The Manager decided to give the delivery driver a quick *tour* of the new branch before the first stock arrived.
They walked the narrow aisles, tested the cold cabinet, and checked the back room.
sentences.cn: 他们走过狭窄的过道，测试冷柜，检查了后房间。

sentences.en: I waited outside with a clipboard.
sentences.cn: 我在外面等着，手拿着夹板。

sentences.en: The driver said very little the whole time, only nodding at each item the Manager pointed to.
sentences.cn: 司机整个时间几乎一言不发，只是在店长指向每一项时点点头。

wake:1.en: After the opening ceremony the small crowd drifted away down the street. In the *wake* of all that noise and ribbon and free samples, the block felt suddenly empty. A single flyer turned slow circles in the gutter. Tang picked it up, smoothed it flat, and tucked it into her apron pocket without a word.
wake:1.cnHint: 热闹结束后，街道在喧嚣的____中变得出奇地安静。
wake:1.hook: Tang had kept one item from the ceremony that no one else noticed.
wake:1.line: 'In the *wake* of the opening, something feels different about this street,' Tang said.

imagination:1.en: I was sweeping the pavement outside when a small boy stopped and stared at the store's dark back room. 'Is there a dragon in there?' he asked. I said no. He looked disappointed. 'Use your *imagination*,' his grandmother told him, pulling him along. He glanced back at the door with wide eyes.

imagination:1.line: 'Use your *imagination* — a good store can be anything you want,' the grandmother said.

nearby:1.hook: She stopped counting at sixty — in under ten minutes.

perspective:1.cnHint: 林和我从街道两端看新店，因为____不同，看到的效果完全不一样。

perspective:1.line: 'From my *perspective*, this site has one serious problem,' Lin said, pointing at the sun.
