sentences.cn: 街对面有个身影在观察。

procedure:1.en: Tang arrived early and found a long queue already forming outside the new branch site. The permit officer explained every *procedure* required before the doors could open: inspection, signature, stamp, and a final walkthrough. Tang wrote it all down on a notepad, biting the pen in concentration.
procedure:1.cnHint: 唐发现开新店需要走一套复杂的____，认真地记录着每个步骤。
procedure:1.hook: The last item on the list made Tang go very quiet.
procedure:1.line: 'Follow each *procedure* exactly, or the permit will be refused.'

sentences.en: Tang arrived early and found a long queue already forming outside the new branch site.
sentences.cn: 阿糖早到了，发现新店址外已经排起了长队。

sentences.en: The permit officer explained every *procedure* required before the doors could open: inspection, signature, stamp, and a final walkthrough.
Tang wrote it all down on a notepad, biting the pen in concentration.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在记事本上把一切都记下来，咬着笔，眉头紧皱。

reasonable:1.en: Lin set up a small table outside and offered free coffee to people passing by. A resident stopped and asked how much the new store would charge for late-night snacks. Lin smiled and said the prices would be very *reasonable*, maybe even lower than the old shop down the road. The resident looked interested.
reasonable:1.cnHint: 林向路人保证新店的价格非常____，吸引了附近居民驻足询问。
reasonable:1.hook: Just then the old shop's owner walked around the corner.
reasonable:1.line: 'Our prices are *reasonable* — you will not find cheaper nearby.'

sentences.en: Lin set up a small table outside and offered free coffee to people passing by.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在外面摆了张小桌子，给过路的人免费提供咖啡。

sentences.en: A resident stopped and asked how much the new store would charge for late-night snacks.
sentences.cn: 一位居民停下来问新店里半夜的小食要卖多少钱。

sentences.en: Lin smiled and said the prices would be very *reasonable*, maybe even lower than the old shop down the road.
The resident looked interested.
sentences.cn: 那位居民显得很感兴趣。

reduction:1.en: The Manager taped a large sign to the window of the future branch. It read: grand opening sale, big *reduction* on all drinks for the first week. A small crowd gathered on the pavement, people taking photos and pointing. One woman asked when exactly the doors would open.
reduction:1.cnHint: 店长在新店橱窗贴出告示，宣布开业期间饮料将有大幅____。
reduction:1.hook: Nobody noticed the rival store van parked just behind them.
reduction:1.line: 'A *reduction* like this in the first week will bring everyone in.'

sentences.en: The Manager taped a large sign to the window of the future branch.
sentences.cn: 店长在未来分店的窗户上贴了一张大告示。

sentences.en: It read: grand opening sale, big *reduction* on all drinks for the first week.
A small crowd gathered on the pavement, people taking photos and pointing.
sentences.cn: 一小群人聚集在人行道上，有人在拍照指点。

sentences.en: One woman asked when exactly the doors would open.
sentences.cn: 一个女人问门什么时候会开放。

season:1.en: It was the busy *season* for hot drinks, and the Manager had chosen this cold autumn stretch on purpose to open the new branch. Steam rose from cups being handed to workers on their morning walk past the site. The smell drifted all the way to the bus stop.
season:1.cnHint: 店长特意选在热饮____开新店，吸引了清晨上班的路人。
season:1.hook: A figure at the bus stop turned and began walking back toward the store.
season:1.line: 'This *season* is perfect — cold air makes everyone want something warm.'

sentences.en: It was the busy *season* for hot drinks, and the Manager had chosen this cold autumn stretch on purpose to open the new branch.
Steam rose from cups being handed to workers on their morning walk past the site.
sentences.cn: 蒸气从递给早间过路工人的杯子里升起。

sentences.en: The smell drifted all the way to the bus stop.
sentences.cn: 气味一直飘到公交站牌。

sector:1.en: Tang stood at the crossroads, map in hand, explaining to the Manager why this block was the right choice. 'Every food and drink *sector* in this district is squeezed into one street, but this corner has nothing,' Tang said, circling the spot with a finger. The Manager nodded slowly.
sector:1.cnHint: 唐向店长分析这个街角在餐饮____上的空白，认为这里是开新店的好地方。
sector:1.hook: Lin, standing nearby, quietly took out a phone and made a call.
sector:1.line: 'The food *sector* here is empty — we should move fast.'

sentences.en: Tang stood at the crossroads, map in hand, explaining to the Manager why this block was the right choice.
sentences.cn: 阿糖站在十字路口，手里拿着地图，向店长解释为什么这个街区是正确的选择。

sentences.en: 'Every food and drink *sector* in this district is squeezed into one street, but this corner has nothing,' Tang said, circling the spot with a finger.
The Manager nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 店长缓缓点了点头。

setting:1.en: The Manager walked around the outside of the building one last time, checking the light, the trees, the angle of the small bench near the door. 'The *setting* matters as much as the stock,' he told Tang quietly. 'People decide in three seconds whether to come in or keep walking.'
setting:1.cnHint: 店长仔细打量新店周围的____，认为环境对吸引顾客至关重要。
setting:1.hook: Tang glanced up and saw Lin measuring the same street from the far end.
setting:1.line: 'The *setting* here is perfect — warm light, quiet street, good bench.'

sentences.en: The Manager walked around the outside of the building one last time, checking the light, the trees, the angle of the small bench near the door.
sentences.cn: 店长在建筑物外面最后走了一圈，检查了光线、树木和门边小长椅的角度。

sentences.en: 'The *setting* matters as much as the stock,' he told Tang quietly.
'People decide in three seconds whether to come in or keep walking.'
sentences.cn: 人们三秒内就会决定是进来还是继续走。

shrink:1.en: A sudden cold wind swept down the street as Tang unrolled the banner for the new branch. Everyone seemed to *shrink* into their coats at once, shoulders rising, chins tucking down. Tang gripped the banner tighter and laughed. 'Free hot soup on opening day,' Tang called out. Several heads turned.
shrink:1.cnHint: 一阵冷风吹来，街上的人纷纷____进外套里，唐趁机宣传开业当天有免费热汤。
shrink:1.hook: One of the turning heads belonged to someone carrying a competitor's cup.
shrink:1.line: 'Watch them *shrink* from the cold — then our hot soup wins them over.'

sentences.en: A sudden cold wind swept down the street as Tang unrolled the banner for the new branch.
sentences.cn: 突然一阵冷风扫过街道，阿糖展开了新分店的横幅。

sentences.en: Everyone seemed to *shrink* into their coats at once, shoulders rising, chins tucking down.
Tang gripped the banner tighter and laughed.
sentences.cn: 阿糖紧紧握住横幅，笑了。

sentences.en: 'Free hot soup on opening day,' Tang called out.
sentences.cn: 阿糖大声喊道："开业当天免费汤！"

sentences.en: Several heads turned.
sentences.cn: 几个人转过了头。

beautiful:1.en: The Manager led me outside at 5 a.m. to show me the new sign above the door. Morning light caught the bright letters, and the whole corner of the street seemed to glow. 'Every new branch starts with a good sign,' he said. The empty street looked *beautiful* in that pale light, calm and full of quiet promise.
beautiful:1.cnHint: 清晨，店长带我出门欣赏新招牌，整条街在晨光中显得格外____。
beautiful:1.hook: Then a shadow appeared at the far end of the street, moving fast.
beautiful:1.line: 'This corner looks *beautiful* at dawn — that is why I chose it.'

sentences.en: The Manager led me outside at 5 a.m. to show me the new sign above the door.
sentences.cn: 店长早上五点带我出去看新店门上的招牌。

sentences.en: Morning light caught the bright letters, and the whole corner of the street seemed to glow.
sentences.cn: 晨光照在闪闪发光的字母上，整个街角似乎都在发光。

sentences.en: 'Every new branch starts with a good sign,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他说："每家新分店都从一块好招牌开始。"

sentences.en: The empty street looked *beautiful* in that pale light, calm and full of quiet promise.

combine:1.en: The Manager unrolled two paper maps on the hood of his car outside. One showed the new branch location; the other showed the bus routes nearby. 'We need to *combine* these ideas,' he said, tapping both sheets. 'Foot traffic plus late buses equals customers.' I nodded, pretending I understood business better than I did.
combine:1.cnHint: 店长在车外把两张地图摊开，想把两份信息____起来规划新店选址。
combine:1.hook: He had circled one corner in red ink three separate times.
combine:1.line: 'If we *combine* the two maps, the best spot becomes obvious.'

sentences.en: The Manager unrolled two paper maps on the hood of his car outside.
sentences.cn: 店长在车外的引擎盖上摊开了两张纸质地图。

sentences.en: One showed the new branch location; the other showed the bus routes nearby.
sentences.cn: 一张显示新分店的位置，另一张显示附近的公交路线。

sentences.en: 'We need to *combine* these ideas,' he said, tapping both sheets.
'Foot traffic plus late buses equals customers.'
sentences.cn: 脚流量加上深夜公交等于顾客。

sentences.en: I nodded, pretending I understood business better than I did.
sentences.cn: 我点了点头，假装自己比实际上更懂生意。

complicated:1.en: Standing outside the new branch on opening day, I tried to read the new electronic lock panel. There were twelve buttons and a tiny screen showing a code I had never seen before. 'Is this *complicated* on purpose?' I asked Tang. He laughed and said the Manager had changed the code that morning and forgotten to tell anyone.
complicated:1.cnHint: 新店门口的电子锁面板让我一头雾水，操作实在太____了。
complicated:1.hook: Inside, the Manager was pressing buttons with a worried look.
complicated:1.line: 'The lock is too *complicated* — even the Manager can't open it now.'

sentences.en: Standing outside the new branch on opening day, I tried to read the new electronic lock panel.
sentences.cn: 开业那天站在新分店外，我试图读懂新的电子门禁面板。

sentences.en: There were twelve buttons and a tiny screen showing a code I had never seen before.
sentences.cn: 有十二个按钮和一个小屏幕，显示着我从未见过的代码。

sentences.en: 'Is this *complicated* on purpose?'
I asked Tang.
sentences.cn: 我问阿糖。

sentences.en: He laughed and said the Manager had changed the code that morning and forgotten to tell anyone.
sentences.cn: 他笑着说店长那天早上改了密码，却忘记告诉任何人。

crash:1.en: Tang and I were carrying a heavy shelf unit through the side door of the new branch when my foot caught the step. There was a loud *crash* as one end hit the pavement. A cat on the wall above us blinked once and walked away without interest. 'Smooth,' said Tang. We checked the shelf. It was fine. We were not as fine.
crash:1.cnHint: 搬货架时我绊了一跤，货架落地发出巨大的____声，把街上的猫都惊到了。
crash:1.hook: The Manager appeared at the window, wearing a very calm expression.
crash:1.line: 'That *crash* was loud enough to wake the whole street, honestly.'

sentences.en: Tang and I were carrying a heavy shelf unit through the side door of the new branch when my foot caught the step.
sentences.cn: 我和阿糖正抬着一个沉重的架子从新店的侧门进去，我的脚绊到了台阶。

sentences.en: There was a loud *crash* as one end hit the pavement.
A cat on the wall above us blinked once and walked away without interest.
sentences.cn: 墙上的一只猫眨了一次眼睛，漫不经心地走开了。

sentences.en: 'Smooth,' said Tang.
sentences.cn: "不错啊，"阿糖说。

sentences.en: We checked the shelf.
sentences.cn: 我们检查了一下架子。

sentences.en: It was fine.
sentences.cn: 架子没事。

sentences.en: We were not as fine.
sentences.cn: 我们可没那么幸运。

creature:1.en: Before the new branch opened, I was sweeping the front step when I noticed a small, round *creature* sitting just inside the door — a turtle, very still, watching me with patient eyes. No one knew where it came from. Tang said it must be a sign of good luck. The Manager said it was probably Lin's fault somehow.
creature:1.cnHint: 新店开张前，我在门口扫地时发现一只小____静静地坐在门里看着我。
creature:1.hook: The next morning, the turtle had moved itself behind the cash register.
creature:1.line: 'A small *creature* like that in a new shop means good luck, I think.'

sentences.en: Before the new branch opened, I was sweeping the front step when I noticed a small, round *creature* sitting just inside the door — a turtle, very still, watching me with patient eyes.
No one knew where it came from.
sentences.cn: 没人知道它从哪儿来的。

sentences.en: Tang said it must be a sign of good luck.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说这肯定是好运的预兆。

sentences.en: The Manager said it was probably Lin's fault somehow.
sentences.cn: 店长说这多半是隔壁咖啡店的林搞出来的。

crime:1.en: Lin appeared outside the new branch just before we opened, arms folded, staring at our new sign. 'Opening here is basically a *crime* against the neighbourhood,' Lin said, nodding at the older shop down the road. I handed Lin a free sample of the new rice ball. Lin ate it in two bites and said nothing else for a while.
crime:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在新店门外，说我们在这里开店简直是对这条街的一种____。
crime:1.hook: Lin came back an hour later and asked for the recipe.
crime:1.line: 'Opening right here is a *crime* — this was supposed to be my corner!'

sentences.en: Lin appeared outside the new branch just before we opened, arms folded, staring at our new sign.
sentences.cn: 林在我们开业前出现在新店外面，双臂交叉，盯着我们的新招牌。

sentences.en: 'Opening here is basically a *crime* against the neighbourhood,' Lin said, nodding at the older shop down the road.
I handed Lin a free sample of the new rice ball.
sentences.cn: 我递给林一个新米团的免费试吃。

sentences.en: Lin ate it in two bites and said nothing else for a while.
sentences.cn: 林两口就吃完了，然后有一段时间什么都没说。

deeply:1.en: After the ribbon-cutting, the Manager stood outside for a long moment, hands in pockets, staring at the new sign. I had never seen him so still. '*Deeply* proud' was how Tang described it quietly beside me. It seemed right. The Manager had drawn the floor plan himself, carried boxes, and stayed up three nights for this small corner shop.
deeply:1.cnHint: 剪彩结束后，店长静静地望着新招牌，阿糖说他____地为此感到骄傲。
deeply:1.hook: Then the Manager sniffed once and said, 'The sign is two centimetres crooked.'
deeply:1.line: 'I am *deeply* proud of everyone who helped build this new branch.'

sentences.en: After the ribbon-cutting, the Manager stood outside for a long moment, hands in pockets, staring at the new sign.
sentences.cn: 剪彩仪式后，店长在外面站了很久，两手插在口袋里，盯着新招牌。

sentences.en: I had never seen him so still. '*Deeply* proud' was how Tang described it quietly beside me.
It seemed right.
sentences.cn: 感觉就该是这样。

sentences.en: The Manager had drawn the floor plan himself, carried boxes, and stayed up three nights for this small corner shop.
sentences.cn: 店长自己画了平面图，搬了无数箱子，为了这个小角落店连续熬了三个夜晚。

demonstrate:1.en: On the pavement outside the new branch, the Manager stopped a small group of passing students to *demonstrate* how the loyalty card app worked. He tapped his phone, scanned a card, and smiled. Three students downloaded the app on the spot. I stood nearby, holding a tray of samples, feeling like part of something that was actually going well for once.
demonstrate:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门外拦住几位路过的学生，现场____新会员积分App的使用方法。
demonstrate:1.hook: One of the students stared at the screen, then stared at me with wide eyes.
demonstrate:1.line: 'Let me *demonstrate* the new app — it takes less than one minute, I promise.'

sentences.en: On the pavement outside the new branch, the Manager stopped a small group of passing students to *demonstrate* how the loyalty card app worked.
He tapped his phone, scanned a card, and smiled.
sentences.cn: 他点了一下手机，扫了一张卡，然后笑了。

sentences.en: Three students downloaded the app on the spot.
sentences.cn: 三个学生当场下载了这个应用。

sentences.en: I stood nearby, holding a tray of samples, feeling like part of something that was actually going well for once.
sentences.cn: 我站在一旁，端着一盘试吃品，感觉自己好像是某件真正顺利进行的事情的一部分。

employment:1.en: The Manager called me outside just after midnight. He pointed across the street at a shiny new store under bright lights. 'That place opened last week,' he said quietly. 'They are offering *employment* to three more staff. Good pay.' He looked at me with calm eyes. I wasn't sure if it was a warning — or a test.
employment:1.cnHint: 店长在深夜把我叫到外面，指着对面新开的店，说那里正在____新员工。
employment:1.hook: He handed me a small key I had never seen before.
employment:1.line: 'They are offering *employment* to three new clerks across the street.'

sentences.en: The Manager called me outside just after midnight.
sentences.cn: 店长在午夜刚过不久叫我出去。

sentences.en: He pointed across the street at a shiny new store under bright lights.
sentences.cn: 他指向街对面一家闪闪发亮、灯火通明的新店。

sentences.en: 'That place opened last week,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "那家店上周开的，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: 'They are offering *employment* to three more staff.
Good pay.'
sentences.cn: 待遇不错。

sentences.en: He looked at me with calm eyes.
sentences.cn: 他用平静的眼神看着我。

sentences.en: I wasn't sure if it was a warning — or a test.
sentences.cn: 我说不准这是一个警告——还是一场考验。

entire:1.en: The Manager asked me to count stock before sunrise. I stepped outside to check the window display and stopped. Sometime in the night, someone had covered the *entire* front wall of our store in tiny paper stars. Every corner, every gap, filled with colour. The street was silent. No one was around.
entire:1.cnHint: 我走出去查看橱窗，发现____面墙都被人贴满了小纸星。
entire:1.hook: One star had a phone number written on the back.
entire:1.line: 'Someone covered the *entire* wall while we were not looking.'

sentences.en: The Manager asked me to count stock before sunrise.
sentences.cn: 店长让我在日出前点清库存。

sentences.en: I stepped outside to check the window display and stopped.
sentences.cn: 我走到外面检查窗口展示，突然停住了。

sentences.en: Sometime in the night, someone had covered the *entire* front wall of our store in tiny paper stars.
Every corner, every gap, filled with colour.
sentences.cn: 每个角落、每道缝隙，都被填满了色彩。

sentences.en: The street was silent.
sentences.cn: 街道一片寂静。

sentences.en: No one was around.
sentences.cn: 周围没有一个人。

gift:1.en: Around two in the morning, an old man came in and bought nothing. He just placed a small box on the counter, smiled, and walked back into the dark street. Inside the box was a warm meat bun, still soft. Tang picked it up and laughed. 'A *gift* with no name,' she said. 'That is the strangest and nicest thing.'
gift:1.cnHint: 一位老人深夜走进来，在柜台放下一个盒子就离开了，里面装着一个热乎乎的____。
gift:1.hook: The next night, a second box appeared before we even opened the door.
gift:1.line: 'A *gift* with no name — that is the strangest and nicest thing.'

sentences.en: Around two in the morning, an old man came in and bought nothing.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点左右，一个老人进来了，什么都没买。

sentences.en: He just placed a small box on the counter, smiled, and walked back into the dark street.
sentences.cn: 他只是在柜台上放了一个小盒子，笑了一下，然后走回了黑暗的街道。

sentences.en: Inside the box was a warm meat bun, still soft.
sentences.cn: 盒子里装着一个热肉包，还是软的。

sentences.en: Tang picked it up and laughed.
sentences.cn: 阿糖拿起来笑了。

sentences.en: 'A *gift* with no name,' she said.
'That is the strangest and nicest thing.'
sentences.cn: "那是最奇怪也最温暖的东西。"

kitchen:1.en: A food cart appeared on the corner just before three in the morning. The owner, a short woman with flour on her coat, knocked on our door and asked to borrow salt. 'My small *kitchen* on wheels ran out,' she said, laughing at herself. Tang gave her a full bag and refused money. The woman nodded once and went back to work.
kitchen:1.cnHint: 一位推着餐车的女士敲门借盐，说她的移动____里用完了。
kitchen:1.hook: She returned an hour later carrying something wrapped in brown paper.
kitchen:1.line: 'My small *kitchen* on wheels ran out of salt tonight.'

sentences.en: A food cart appeared on the corner just before three in the morning.
sentences.cn: 凌晨三点刚过，一辆小食车出现在街角。

sentences.en: The owner, a short woman with flour on her coat, knocked on our door and asked to borrow salt.
sentences.cn: 老板是个个子不高、衣服上沾着面粉的女人，她敲了敲我们的门，问能不能借点盐。

sentences.en: 'My small *kitchen* on wheels ran out,' she said, laughing at herself.
Tang gave her a full bag and refused money.
sentences.cn: 阿糖给了她一整袋，拒绝了钱。

sentences.en: The woman nodded once and went back to work.
sentences.cn: 女人点了点头，回去继续工作。

mystery:1.en: Every Tuesday, someone left a single coin on top of the newspaper stand outside our door. Not inside, not under — always on top, always one coin, always gone by morning. Tang called it a *mystery* and kept a notebook of dates. The Manager just shrugged. I started watching the street camera logs, but the timing was never quite right.
mystery:1.cnHint: 每周二都有人在报架顶上放一枚硬币，阿糖把这件____记录在笔记本里。
mystery:1.hook: This Tuesday, there were two coins.
mystery:1.line: 'It is a *mystery* — one coin, every Tuesday, gone by morning.'

sentences.en: Every Tuesday, someone left a single coin on top of the newspaper stand outside our door.
sentences.cn: 每个星期二，有人都会在外面报刊架的顶部放一枚硬币。

sentences.en: Not inside, not under — always on top, always one coin, always gone by morning.
sentences.cn: 不是放在里面，不是放在下面——总是在顶部，总是一枚硬币，总是到早上就消失了。

sentences.en: Tang called it a *mystery* and kept a notebook of dates.
The Manager just shrugged.
sentences.cn: 店长就是耸肩。

sentences.en: I started watching the street camera logs, but the timing was never quite right.
sentences.cn: 我开始查看街道摄像头的录像，但时间总是卡不准。

opposite:1.en: Lin runs the noodle shop *opposite* our store, and every night around four he sweeps his doorstep exactly when I sweep ours. We never speak. We just sweep in silence, two small lights facing each other across a quiet road. Tang says he once swept for an hour straight during a rainstorm, so I figure he has his reasons.
opposite:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在我们店____的面馆每晚都和我同时扫地，两家店隔街相望。
opposite:1.hook: Tonight Lin looked up and gave a very small nod.
opposite:1.line: 'His noodle shop is directly *opposite* — they sweep at the same time every night.'

sentences.en: Lin runs the noodle shop *opposite* our store, and every night around four he sweeps his doorstep exactly when I sweep ours.
We never speak.
sentences.cn: 我们从不说话。

sentences.en: We just sweep in silence, two small lights facing each other across a quiet road.
sentences.cn: 我们就在寂静的路上，两盏小灯相对地扫地。

sentences.en: Tang says he once swept for an hour straight during a rainstorm, so I figure he has his reasons.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说他有一次在暴雨中扫了整整一个小时，所以我觉得他肯定有他的理由。

permanent:1.en: The Manager showed me the staff board on the back wall. Most names had small paper tags, easy to remove. Mine was the only one written directly on the wood in black ink. 'I made yours *permanent*,' he said, turning back to his ledger without another word. Tang caught my eye from behind the snack shelf and gave a quiet thumbs-up.
permanent:1.cnHint: 店长把我的名字直接写在木板上，说要把它变成____的。
permanent:1.hook: Below my name, in very small letters, was a second name I did not recognise.
permanent:1.line: 'I made yours *permanent* — written right into the wood.'

sentences.en: The Manager showed me the staff board on the back wall.
sentences.cn: 店长给我看了后墙上的员工板。

sentences.en: Most names had small paper tags, easy to remove.
sentences.cn: 大多数名字都贴着小纸签，很容易撕掉。

sentences.en: Mine was the only one written directly on the wood in black ink.
sentences.cn: 我的是唯一一个直接用黑墨水写在木板上的。

sentences.en: 'I made yours *permanent*,' he said, turning back to his ledger without another word.
Tang caught my eye from behind the snack shelf and gave a quiet thumbs-up.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在零食架后面看着我，竖起了大拇指。

plenty:1.en: Just before dawn, a student sat down on the step outside with a big bag of chips from our shelf and an open notebook. She had *plenty* of notes already, pages thick with colour. Tang watched through the glass and whispered, 'She comes before every exam.' The girl never looked up. She just kept reading until the sky went pink.
plenty:1.cnHint: 一位女生在天亮前坐在门口台阶上复习，笔记本里已经有____的笔记了。
plenty:1.hook: She left a sticky note on the door that none of us could read.
plenty:1.line: 'She has *plenty* of notes — pages and pages of them every time.'

sentences.en: Just before dawn, a student sat down on the step outside with a big bag of chips from our shelf and an open notebook.
sentences.cn: 天还没亮，一个学生就坐在门外的台阶上，拿着从我们货架上拿的一大包薯片和一本摊开的笔记本。

sentences.en: She had *plenty* of notes already, pages thick with colour.
Tang watched through the glass and whispered, 'She comes before every exam.'

sentences.en: The girl never looked up.
sentences.cn: 那女孩始终没有抬头。

sentences.en: She just kept reading until the sky went pink.
sentences.cn: 她就一直读啊读，直到天空泛红。

strike:1.en: The morning I arrived to help scout the new store location, a group of workers outside the building next door had begun a *strike*. They stood in a long line, holding signs, chanting in low, steady voices. The Manager studied them and then studied the empty shop front, saying nothing for a long time.
strike:1.cnHint: 店长带我去考察新店选址，隔壁楼的工人正在进行____，场面让人有点不安。
strike:1.hook: The Manager finally smiled — and that made me more nervous.
strike:1.line: 'A *strike* next door means cheap rent for us, probably.'

sentences.en: The morning I arrived to help scout the new store location, a group of workers outside the building next door had begun a *strike*.
They stood in a long line, holding signs, chanting in low, steady voices.
sentences.cn: 他们排成一条长队，举着标语，用低沉而有节奏的嗓音喊着口号。

sentences.en: The Manager studied them and then studied the empty shop front, saying nothing for a long time.
sentences.cn: 店长看了看他们，又看了看空荡荡的店铺前面，沉默了很久。

television:1.en: The new site was a dusty shell, but someone had left an old *television* balanced on a stack of bricks in the corner. It was still on, showing a cooking programme, its light flickering blue across bare walls. The Manager stood in front of it for a moment, tilting his head as if reading a sign.
television:1.cnHint: 新店地址里废弃的____还亮着，店长盯着它若有所思。
television:1.hook: He muttered something, wrote one word in his notebook, and closed it fast.
television:1.line: 'That *television* — leave it exactly where it is, please.'

sentences.en: The new site was a dusty shell, but someone had left an old *television* balanced on a stack of bricks in the corner.
It was still on, showing a cooking programme, its light flickering blue across bare walls.
sentences.cn: 电视还开着，播放着一个烹饪节目，蓝色的光在裸露的墙壁上闪烁。

sentences.en: The Manager stood in front of it for a moment, tilting his head as if reading a sign.
sentences.cn: 店长在它面前站了一会儿，歪着头，就像在读什么标志似的。

youth:1.en: Two doors down from the new site was a small barbershop. A kid who looked barely eighteen sat outside on a plastic stool, arms folded, watching us measure the pavement. There was a quiet confidence about him — the kind of *youth* that does not know yet what it cannot do. I envied him a little.
youth:1.cnHint: 考察途中遇到一个坐在门口的少年，那股____的劲儿让我有点羡慕。
youth:1.hook: Later, Tang whispered that the kid owned the barbershop himself.
youth:1.line: '*Youth* is wasted on people who just sit and wait, I think.'

sentences.en: Two doors down from the new site was a small barbershop.
sentences.cn: 新店址往下两个门面是一家小理发店。

sentences.en: A kid who looked barely eighteen sat outside on a plastic stool, arms folded, watching us measure the pavement.
sentences.cn: 一个看起来才十八岁出头的小伙子坐在塑料凳子上，双臂交叉，看着我们测量人行道。

sentences.en: There was a quiet confidence about him — the kind of *youth* that does not know yet what it cannot do.
I envied him a little.
sentences.cn: 我有点羡慕他。

alter:1.en: The Manager paced the empty floor of the new site, then stopped at the main window. He said we would need to *alter* the layout of the shelves so that customers could see straight in from the street. He sketched a quick plan on the back of a receipt. Tang and I looked at each other.
alter:1.cnHint: 店长说必须____新店的货架布局，让街上的人一眼就能看进来。
alter:1.hook: Tang's quick look meant: this plan will change three more times before lunch.
alter:1.line: 'We have to *alter* the window side first — everything else follows that.'

sentences.en: The Manager paced the empty floor of the new site, then stopped at the main window.
sentences.cn: 店长在新店址的空地上踱步，然后停在了主窗口前。

sentences.en: He said we would need to *alter* the layout of the shelves so that customers could see straight in from the street.

sentences.en: Tang and I looked at each other.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我互相看了一眼。

approximately:1.en: Lin was already outside the new site when we arrived, leaning on a rival shop's van and looking pleased. She told the Manager, with a wide smile, that her company had signed a lease on a space *approximately* fifty metres further down the same street, and that she expected to open two weeks before us.
approximately:1.cnHint: 林出现在新店附近，说她的竞争门店距我们____五十米，开业还比我们早。
approximately:1.hook: The Manager just nodded, which is always the dangerous sign.
approximately:1.line: '*Approximately* fifty metres — close enough to share your customers, yes?'

sentences.en: Lin was already outside the new site when we arrived, leaning on a rival shop's van and looking pleased.
sentences.cn: 我们到达新店址时，隔壁咖啡店的林已经在外面了，靠着一辆竞争对手的货车，看起来很高兴。

sentences.en: She told the Manager, with a wide smile, that her company had signed a lease on a space *approximately* fifty metres further down the same street, and that she expected to open two weeks before us.

attractive:1.en: From the pavement outside, the corner location did look genuinely *attractive*: wide glass front, warm afternoon light, a bus stop almost touching the door. I found myself imagining the night shift here — a little quieter, a little gentler than our current street. Tang caught me daydreaming and laughed.

attractive:1.hook: Then Tang pointed out the all-night noodle stall directly opposite.
attractive:1.line: 'Honestly, the location is *attractive* enough — it sells itself at night.'

sentences.en: From the pavement outside, the corner location did look genuinely *attractive*: wide glass front, warm afternoon light, a bus stop almost touching the door.

sentences.cn: 阿糖看到我在发呆，笑了。

bag:1.en: The Manager produced a large paper *bag* from somewhere inside his coat and began handing out sandwiches on the pavement outside the new site. It felt less like a business trip and more like a school outing. Tang accepted his sandwich solemnly, as though receiving an important document.
bag:1.cnHint: 店长从大纸____里掏出三明治，在新店门口请大家吃东西，感觉像郊游。
bag:1.hook: At the bottom of the bag was a rolled-up lease agreement, already signed.
bag:1.line: 'I keep the contracts and the lunch in the same *bag* — saves trips.'

sentences.en: The Manager produced a large paper *bag* from somewhere inside his coat and began handing out sandwiches on the pavement outside the new site.
It felt less like a business trip and more like a school outing.
sentences.cn: 感觉不像是出差，倒像是学校春游。

sentences.cn: 阿糖郑重其事地接过三明治，就像在接一份重要文件。

beat:1.en: We had walked the whole street twice in the afternoon heat, and by the time we reached the bus stop to head back I was completely *beat*. My feet ached. The Manager, somehow fresh, was already calling someone on his phone. Tang sat down on the kerb and closed his eyes without a word.
beat:1.cnHint: 转了整整一下午，我和唐到站台等车时都____了，只有店长精神依旧。
beat:1.hook: The Manager ended his call and said, 'We open in three weeks.'
beat:1.line: 'I am absolutely *beat* — how does the Manager still look so alive?'

sentences.en: We had walked the whole street twice in the afternoon heat, and by the time we reached the bus stop to head back I was completely *beat*.

sentences.cn: 我的脚疼。

sentences.en: The Manager, somehow fresh, was already calling someone on his phone.
sentences.cn: 店长不知怎么还精神得很，已经在打电话了。

sentences.en: Tang sat down on the kerb and closed his eyes without a word.
sentences.cn: 阿糖坐在路缘上，一声不吭地闭上了眼睛。

bottom:1.en: The Manager taped a notice to the *bottom* of the store window, low enough that only people crouching to lock their bikes would spot it. It read: 'New branch opening soon — same corner, bigger space.' I read it twice, wondering what that meant for my night shift.
bottom:1.cnHint: 店长把一张告示贴在橱窗的____，只有蹲下锁车的人才能看到。
bottom:1.hook: Tang had already seen it — and said nothing to me.
bottom:1.line: 'I put it at the *bottom* so the right people would find it.'

sentences.en: The Manager taped a notice to the *bottom* of the store window, low enough that only people crouching to lock their bikes would spot it.

sentences.cn: 上面写着："新分店即将开业——同一街角，更大空间。"

sentences.en: I read it twice, wondering what that meant for my night shift.
sentences.cn: 我读了两遍，在想这对我的夜班意味着什么。

breed:1.en: Outside the store, an old man walked a small dog of a *breed* I had never seen — short legs, huge ears, serious face. He stopped, looked at the new branch sign the Manager had just posted on the lamp post, and shook his head slowly before walking on without a word.
breed:1.cnHint: 一位老人遛着一只奇特____的小狗，在新店告示牌前摇了摇头。
breed:1.hook: He came back ten minutes later — alone, without the dog.
breed:1.line: 'That *breed* always knows trouble before people do.'

sentences.en: Outside the store, an old man walked a small dog of a *breed* I had never seen — short legs, huge ears, serious face.
He stopped, looked at the new branch sign the Manager had just posted on the lamp post, and shook his head slowly before walking on without a word.
sentences.cn: 他停了下来，看了看店长刚才贴在灯杆上的新分店标志，缓缓摇头，然后无言地走了。

classify:1.en: Lin stood on the pavement comparing two hand-drawn maps, trying to *classify* each nearby shop as a threat or an opportunity for the new branch. She used red dots and blue dots. I passed by on my way to open the store and she covered the maps quickly, pretending to check her phone.
classify:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在人行道上用红蓝圆点____附近的每家店，却在我经过时迅速把地图藏了起来。
classify:1.hook: One red dot sat exactly where our store stood.
classify:1.line: 'I *classify* every shop before the Manager even asks me to.'

sentences.en: Lin stood on the pavement comparing two hand-drawn maps, trying to *classify* each nearby shop as a threat or an opportunity for the new branch.
She used red dots and blue dots.
sentences.cn: 她用红点和蓝点标记。

sentences.en: I passed by on my way to open the store and she covered the maps quickly, pretending to check her phone.
sentences.cn: 我在去开门前经过，她迅速盖住地图，假装在看手机。

comment:1.en: The Manager pinned the branch announcement to the community board outside and stepped back. A small crowd formed quickly. Someone wrote a *comment* on a sticky note and pressed it onto the poster before walking away. I caught a glimpse — it said only three words — but a bus passed and blocked my view.
comment:1.cnHint: 店长把开分店的通知贴到社区公告栏后，有人在上面贴了一张便利贴____。
comment:1.hook: When I reached the board, the sticky note was already gone.
comment:1.line: 'Every *comment* on that board ends up meaning something.'

sentences.en: The Manager pinned the branch announcement to the community board outside and stepped back.

sentences.en: A small crowd formed quickly.
sentences.cn: 很快就聚集了一小群人。

sentences.en: Someone wrote a *comment* on a sticky note and pressed it onto the poster before walking away.

sentences.cn: 我瞥到了一眼——只有三个字——但一辆公交车开过来挡住了我的视线。

component:1.en: Tang was kneeling beside a flat-pack shelf unit on the pavement outside the new branch site, sorting pieces by size. 'Each *component* has to go in order,' he said, 'or the whole thing falls apart.' A gust of wind sent the instruction sheet tumbling into the road at that exact moment.
component:1.cnHint: 阿糖在新店门外整理货架的每个____，一阵风却把说明书吹进了马路。
component:1.hook: A passing van rolled right over the instructions.
component:1.line: 'Miss one *component* and the whole shelf will lean.'

sentences.en: Tang was kneeling beside a flat-pack shelf unit on the pavement outside the new branch site, sorting pieces by size.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在新分店门口的人行道上跪着，正在给平板式货架零件按大小分类。

sentences.en: 'Each *component* has to go in order,' he said, 'or the whole thing falls apart.'
A gust of wind sent the instruction sheet tumbling into the road at that exact moment.
sentences.cn: 恰好这时一阵风把说明书吹到了马路上。

contrary:1.en: Everyone assumed the new branch would be on the busy main road. On the *contrary*, the Manager had chosen a quiet side street behind the old library. I found out only because I followed a delivery truck by accident one evening after my shift, and the truck stopped right in front of it.
contrary:1.cnHint: 大家以为新分店会开在主干道，____，店长选了图书馆后面的一条僻静小街。
contrary:1.hook: The delivery truck driver gave me a very long look.
contrary:1.line: 'On the *contrary*, a quiet street is exactly what we want.'

sentences.en: Everyone assumed the new branch would be on the busy main road.
sentences.cn: 大家都以为新分店会在繁忙的大街上。

sentences.en: On the *contrary*, the Manager had chosen a quiet side street behind the old library.
I found out only because I followed a delivery truck by accident one evening after my shift, and the truck stopped right in front of it.
sentences.cn: 我是在一天晚班后不小心跟着一辆送货车才发现的，车子在它前面停了下来。

deny:1.en: Lin caught me reading the address on the delivery notice posted to the future branch door. 'Were you following that truck?' she asked, stepping out of the shadow of the old library wall. I wanted to *deny* it, but the mud on my shoes from the side street said everything for me.
deny:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林从暗处走出来质问我是否跟踪了送货车，我想____，但鞋上的泥出卖了我。
deny:1.hook: She smiled and said, 'Good — now you owe me one.'
deny:1.line: 'Go ahead and *deny* it, but I saw you follow that truck.'

sentences.en: Lin caught me reading the address on the delivery notice posted to the future branch door.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林抓到我在读贴在未来分店门上的收货单地址。

sentences.en: 'Were you following that truck?' she asked, stepping out of the shadow of the old library wall.
sentences.cn: "你在跟踪那辆车吗？"她从老图书馆的墙影里走出来，问道。

sentences.en: I wanted to *deny* it, but the mud on my shoes from the side street said everything for me.

depth:1.en: The Manager unrolled the floor plan for the new branch on the bonnet of a parked car outside. I peered over her shoulder. The storage room had real *depth* — nearly double the one in our current store. She tapped it with her pen and said quietly, 'This is the part Lin must not see yet.'
depth:1.cnHint: 店长在停着的车上展开新店平面图，储藏室的____让我印象深刻，她叮嘱我不能让隔壁咖啡店的林看到。
depth:1.hook: Behind us, a familiar pair of red shoes rounded the corner.
depth:1.line: 'The *depth* of that back room changes everything for us.'

sentences.en: The Manager unrolled the floor plan for the new branch on the bonnet of a parked car outside.
sentences.cn: 店长在停在外面的一辆车的引擎盖上铺开了新分店的平面图。

document:1.cnHint: 城管来检查，我到处找那份开业____，险些误事。

fortune:1.en: Lin walked past our new branch and paused at the door. She studied the red ribbon the Manager had tied above the entrance for good luck. 'A ribbon won't bring *fortune*,' she said pleasantly. Then she smiled, took a photo, and strolled away down the sunny street.
fortune:1.cnHint: 林路过我们的新分店，对那条红绸带能带来____表示怀疑，然后笑着走开了。
fortune:1.hook: She uploaded the photo somewhere, and by evening a crowd had gathered outside.
fortune:1.line: 'A pretty ribbon alone will not bring you *fortune*, you know.'

sentences.en: Lin walked past our new branch and paused at the door.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林经过我们的新分店，在门前停了下来。

sentences.en: She studied the red ribbon the Manager had tied above the entrance for good luck.
sentences.cn: 她研究了店长在入口上方绑的红丝带，那是为了好运。

sentences.en: 'A ribbon won't bring *fortune*,' she said pleasantly.
Then she smiled, took a photo, and strolled away down the sunny street.
sentences.cn: 然后她笑了，拍了张照，悠闲地沿着阳光下的街道走了。

fulfil:1.en: The Manager pinned a handwritten list to the new branch door before opening: restock shelves, test the card reader, greet the first ten customers by name. 'Each of us must *fulfil* our part today,' he said quietly, tapping the list. Tang and I nodded and got to work.
fulfil:1.cnHint: 店长在门上贴了任务清单，说每个人都要____自己的职责，正式开张才能顺利。
fulfil:1.hook: The card reader beeped once, then went completely silent.
fulfil:1.line: 'We each must *fulfil* our task before we open those doors.'

sentences.en: The Manager pinned a handwritten list to the new branch door before opening: restock shelves, test the card reader, greet the first ten customers by name.
sentences.cn: 开店前，店长在新分店门上钉了一张手写的清单：补充货架、测试读卡器、按名字问候前十个顾客。

sentences.en: 'Each of us must *fulfil* our part today,' he said quietly, tapping the list.
Tang and I nodded and got to work.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我点了点头，开始工作。

gradually:1.en: The new branch started with just three customers all morning. Then a few office workers found us at lunch. By afternoon a small line formed at the counter. Business was *gradually* picking up, like a fire catching from a single match. Tang said this was the best sign possible.
gradually:1.cnHint: 新分店的生意____好转，从早上三个顾客到下午排起了小队。
gradually:1.hook: Then one regular looked at the shelf and frowned deeply at something missing.
gradually:1.line: 'See? Customers are *gradually* finding us — no need to worry yet.'

sentences.en: The new branch started with just three customers all morning.
sentences.cn: 新分店整个上午只有三个顾客。

sentences.en: Then a few office workers found us at lunch.
sentences.cn: 然后一些上班族在午餐时间找到了我们。

sentences.en: By afternoon a small line formed at the counter.
sentences.cn: 到了下午，收银台前排起了一条小队。

sentences.en: Business was *gradually* picking up, like a fire catching from a single match.
Tang said this was the best sign possible.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说这是最好的信号。

incentive:1.en: The Manager announced a small bonus for whichever branch sold more hot drinks before noon. Lin heard about it somehow and appeared at our door with a knowing look. 'That kind of *incentive* cuts both ways,' she said. Tang leaned over to me and whispered, 'She already won, didn't she.'
incentive:1.cnHint: 店长宣布卖热饮奖金制度作为____，林不知怎么听说了，意味深长地出现在门口。
incentive:1.hook: Tang checked our hot-drink counter and went very quiet indeed.
incentive:1.line: 'A small bonus is a fine *incentive*, but I have a better idea.'

sentences.en: The Manager announced a small bonus for whichever branch sold more hot drinks before noon.
sentences.cn: 店长宣布了一项小奖金，给中午前卖出最多热饮的分店。

sentences.en: Lin heard about it somehow and appeared at our door with a knowing look.
sentences.cn: 林从什么渠道听到了这个消息，带着一种了然于心的表情出现在我们的门口。

sentences.en: 'That kind of *incentive* cuts both ways,' she said.
Tang leaned over to me and whispered, 'She already won, didn't she.'
sentences.cn: 阿糖靠近我，低声说道，"她已经赢了，对吧。"

somewhat:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, clipboard in hand. The street was noisier than our usual corner — trucks rolled past every few minutes. He looked *somewhat* worried, checking his notes twice, then staring at the traffic as if counting each engine rumble.
somewhat:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店选址外，对周围环境感到____不安。
somewhat:1.hook: Then a truck stopped right in front of him.
somewhat:1.line: 'The noise is *somewhat* more than I expected,' he said quietly.

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, clipboard in hand.
sentences.cn: 店长站在新分店所在地的外面，手里拿着一个夹板。

sentences.en: The street was noisier than our usual corner — trucks rolled past every few minutes.
sentences.cn: 这条街比我们通常的角落要吵得多——卡车每隔几分钟就会驶过一次。

sentences.en: He looked *somewhat* worried, checking his notes twice, then staring at the traffic as if counting each engine rumble.

stable:1.en: Lin walked the whole block around the new site, testing the pavement with one foot. 'A good store needs a *stable* foundation,' she said, half to herself. She pressed a loose tile with her heel — it wobbled. She pulled out her phone and started taking photos.
stable:1.cnHint: 林在新选址附近检查地面，担心地基是否____。
stable:1.hook: One photo caught something no one else had noticed.
stable:1.line: 'Nothing feels very *stable* under this corner,' Lin warned.

sentences.en: Lin walked the whole block around the new site, testing the pavement with one foot.
sentences.cn: 林绕着新店址所在的整个街区走了一圈，用一只脚踩着人行道测试。

sentences.en: 'A good store needs a *stable* foundation,' she said, half to herself.
She pressed a loose tile with her heel — it wobbled.
sentences.cn: 她用脚跟按了按一块松动的瓷砖——它摇晃了。

sentences.en: She pulled out her phone and started taking photos.
sentences.cn: 她掏出手机开始拍照。

lower:1.en: The Manager pointed at the map spread on the hood of his car. 'The rent on Park Road is *lower* than anywhere else we checked,' he said, tapping the circled block. I leaned in, trying to look useful. A pigeon landed on the map and stared at us both.
lower:1.cnHint: 店长在街边看地图，说某条路的租金____，正当此时一只鸽子也凑了过来。
lower:1.hook: The pigeon refused to move, even when the Manager reached for the map.
lower:1.line: 'The rent here is *lower*, so this corner is our top choice.'

sentences.en: The Manager pointed at the map spread on the hood of his car.
sentences.cn: 店长指着摊在他车顶上的地图。

sentences.en: 'The rent on Park Road is *lower* than anywhere else we checked,' he said, tapping the circled block.
I leaned in, trying to look useful.
sentences.cn: 我靠近前去，试图显得有用。

sentences.en: A pigeon landed on the map and stared at us both.
sentences.cn: 一只鸽子落在了地图上，盯着我们两个。

naturally:1.en: Tang and I stood outside the empty shopfront on Maple Street. She walked the length of it once, then said the space felt right. '*Naturally*, a corner spot gets more foot traffic,' she added, already picturing shelves along the walls. I was just glad to be out of the store for an hour.
naturally:1.cnHint: 阿糖在空铺位外评估地点，____地说转角店面人流更多。
naturally:1.hook: Then Tang noticed the small sign taped to the inside of the glass.
naturally:1.line: '*Naturally*, the busiest corner will bring us the most customers.'

sentences.en: Tang and I stood outside the empty shopfront on Maple Street.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我站在枫树街的空店铺外面。

sentences.en: She walked the length of it once, then said the space felt right. '*Naturally*, a corner spot gets more foot traffic,' she added, already picturing shelves along the walls.
I was just glad to be out of the store for an hour.
sentences.cn: 我只是很高兴能离开店里一个小时。

passionate:1.en: Lin from the shop across the street watched us measure the pavement outside the new site. She crossed her arms. 'You are very *passionate* about expansion,' she called out, making the word sound like a warning. I waved politely. The Manager kept measuring and did not look up once.
passionate:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林看着我们在街上量尺寸，用____这个词讽刺地打了个招呼。
passionate:1.hook: Lin pulled out her phone and made a call right there on the pavement.
passionate:1.line: 'How *passionate* of you — measuring the street at seven in the morning.'

sentences.en: Lin from the shop across the street watched us measure the pavement outside the new site.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林从街对面看着我们在新店址外测量人行道。

sentences.en: She crossed her arms.
sentences.cn: 她交叉双臂。

sentences.en: 'You are very *passionate* about expansion,' she called out, making the word sound like a warning.
I waved politely.
sentences.cn: 我礼貌地挥了挥手。

sentences.en: The Manager kept measuring and did not look up once.
sentences.cn: 店长继续测量，一次都没有抬头。

pop:1.en: We were taping a bright sign to the new shopfront window when Tang said we needed something to catch passing eyes. She pressed a big yellow sticker to the glass — a *pop* of colour against the grey wall. Three people slowed down to look before we had even finished.
pop:1.cnHint: 阿糖在新店橱窗贴上亮黄色贴纸，用颜色____来吸引路人注意。
pop:1.hook: One of the three people who slowed down pressed their face to the glass.
pop:1.line: 'A *pop* of yellow on the window and everyone suddenly notices us.'

sentences.en: We were taping a bright sign to the new shopfront window when Tang said we needed something to catch passing eyes.
sentences.cn: 我们正在给新店铺的窗户贴一张明亮的标志，阿糖说我们需要什么东西来吸引路人的眼球。

sentences.en: She pressed a big yellow sticker to the glass — a *pop* of colour against the grey wall.
Three people slowed down to look before we had even finished.
sentences.cn: 我们还没有贴完，就已经有三个人慢了下来看。

possibly:1.en: I measured the distance from the main bus stop to the new site by counting my steps. Forty-three steps — *possibly* close enough for tired commuters to stop on their way home. The Manager watched from the doorway, nodding slowly. Across the road, Lin was also counting her steps.
possibly:1.cnHint: 我步测新店离公交站的距离，心想这____足够近，能吸引下班的通勤者。
possibly:1.hook: Lin stopped walking at exactly the same spot I had stopped.
possibly:1.line: 'Forty-three steps — *possibly* close enough to pull in the evening crowd.'

sentences.en: I measured the distance from the main bus stop to the new site by counting my steps.
sentences.cn: 我通过数步子来测量从主要公交车站到新店址的距离。

sentences.en: Forty-three steps — *possibly* close enough for tired commuters to stop on their way home.
The Manager watched from the doorway, nodding slowly.
sentences.cn: 店长从门口看着，缓缓点头。

sentences.en: Across the road, Lin was also counting her steps.
sentences.cn: 街对面，林也在数她的步子。

previously:1.en: The Manager showed us photos on his phone. The corner unit had *previously* been a tiny bookshop, its shelves still faintly visible where the paint was lighter on the walls. I liked the idea of a place with a quiet history. Tang was already redesigning it in her head out loud.
previously:1.cnHint: 店长展示照片，说这个铺面____是一家小书店，墙上还留有痕迹。
previously:1.hook: Tang stopped mid-sentence and pointed at something behind the old counter.
previously:1.line: 'This spot *previously* held a bookshop — good energy, I think.'

sentences.en: The Manager showed us photos on his phone.
sentences.cn: 店长给我们看了他手机上的照片。

sentences.en: The corner unit had *previously* been a tiny bookshop, its shelves still faintly visible where the paint was lighter on the walls.
I liked the idea of a place with a quiet history.
sentences.cn: 我喜欢一个有着安静历史的地方这个想法。

sentences.en: Tang was already redesigning it in her head out loud.
sentences.cn: 阿糖已经开始大声地在脑子里重新设计它了。

profession:1.en: A woman stopped to read our handwritten 'Opening Soon' sign. She asked what kind of store it would be. When I explained, she smiled and said retail was a tough *profession* but an honest one. Then she bought a bottle of water from my carry bag and walked on without another word.
profession:1.cnHint: 一位路过的女士称零售是艰辛却诚实的____，随后向我买了瓶水就离开了。
profession:1.hook: She left before I could ask how she knew the store was not open yet.
profession:1.line: 'Retail is a hard *profession*, but it suits an honest person well.'

sentences.en: A woman stopped to read our handwritten 'Opening Soon' sign.
sentences.cn: 一位女性停下来读我们手写的"即将开业"标志。

sentences.en: She asked what kind of store it would be.
sentences.cn: 她问这家店会是什么样的。

sentences.en: When I explained, she smiled and said retail was a tough *profession* but an honest one.
Then she bought a bottle of water from my carry bag and walked on without another word.
sentences.cn: 然后她从我的背包里买了一瓶水，没有再说一句话就走开了。

readily:1.en: When the Manager asked who would cover the new site on opening day, I *readily* raised my hand before thinking it through. Tang raised an eyebrow. The Manager smiled the smile of someone who had been waiting for exactly that answer. I realised I had just volunteered for a very long shift.
readily:1.cnHint: 店长问谁愿意负责新店开业当天，我____举了手，随即意识到自己可能麻烦了。
readily:1.hook: Tang leaned over and whispered something about the new store having no coffee machine.
readily:1.line: 'I *readily* volunteer — someone has to be there for the first customer.'

sentences.en: When the Manager asked who would cover the new site on opening day, I *readily* raised my hand before thinking it through.
Tang raised an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 阿糖扬起一边眉毛。

sentences.en: The Manager smiled the smile of someone who had been waiting for exactly that answer.
sentences.cn: 店长露出了那种一直在等这个答案的人才有的笑容。

sentences.en: I realised I had just volunteered for a very long shift.
sentences.cn: 我意识到自己刚刚报名参加了一个很长的班次。

vigorous:1.en: The Manager called us outside at six in the morning. He pointed at the empty lot across the street, where workers were already digging. 'A new branch,' he said, his voice *vigorous* and full of energy, as if he hadn't slept all night — or maybe he had slept just fine and we were the ones missing something.
vigorous:1.cnHint: 店长精神抖擞地宣布，对面空地正在为新分店破土动工。
vigorous:1.hook: Tang said nothing, but his hands went very still.
vigorous:1.line: 'Stay *vigorous*, team — the new branch opens in thirty days!'

sentences.en: The Manager called us outside at six in the morning.
sentences.cn: 店长在早上六点钟把我们叫出去。

sentences.en: He pointed at the empty lot across the street, where workers were already digging.
sentences.cn: 他指向街对面的空地，工人们已经在那里挖掘了。

sentences.en: 'A new branch,' he said, his voice *vigorous* and full of energy, as if he hadn't slept all night — or maybe he had slept just fine and we were the ones missing something.

wide:1.en: From the pavement outside I could see the whole street in one glance. The *wide* road was empty except for a delivery truck and a cat. The Manager had brought us out here to 'feel the location.' I wasn't sure what that meant, but the cat looked confident, so I tried to copy it.
wide:1.cnHint: 站在街角，店长让大家感受新分店选址的____视野与街道环境。
wide:1.hook: Then Lin pointed to a sign just two doors down that I hadn't noticed.
wide:1.line: 'The street is *wide* — foot traffic here will be double what we get now.'

sentences.en: From the pavement outside I could see the whole street in one glance.
sentences.cn: 站在人行道外面，我能一眼看完整条街。

sentences.en: The *wide* road was empty except for a delivery truck and a cat.
The Manager had brought us out here to 'feel the location.'
sentences.cn: 店长把我们带到这儿来是为了"感受这个位置"。

sentences.en: I wasn't sure what that meant, but the cat looked confident, so I tried to copy it.
sentences.cn: 我不太明白这是什么意思，但那只猫看起来很有把握，所以我试着模仿它。

agriculture:1.en: A customer stopped to read the notice taped to our door about the new branch. 'My family left *agriculture* years ago and came to this city,' he said quietly, almost to himself. 'Now even this small street is changing.' He bought a bottle of water and walked away before I could think of anything to say.
agriculture:1.cnHint: 一位顾客看着新分店公告，感叹自家当年从____进城，如今连这条街都在变化。
agriculture:1.hook: He came back an hour later and stood outside without coming in.
agriculture:1.line: 'We left *agriculture* behind, but I never thought I'd miss a quiet corner street.'

sentences.en: A customer stopped to read the notice taped to our door about the new branch.
sentences.cn: 一个顾客停下来读贴在我们门上关于新店的告示。

sentences.en: 'My family left *agriculture* years ago and came to this city,' he said quietly, almost to himself.
'Now even this small street is changing.'
sentences.cn: 连这条小街都在变了。

sentences.en: He bought a bottle of water and walked away before I could think of anything to say.
sentences.cn: 他买了瓶水就走了，我还没想好该说什么。

assign:1.en: The Manager lined us up on the pavement and began to *assign* roles for the new branch opening. Tang got the stock room. I got the front counter. He paused before Lin's name, tapping his clipboard, while Lin stared at the ground with an unreadable expression.
assign:1.cnHint: 店长在街上把大家召集起来，开始为新分店____各自的职位。
assign:1.hook: Lin's name stayed blank on the clipboard.
assign:1.line: 'I will *assign* your post by Friday — make sure you are ready.'

sentences.en: The Manager lined us up on the pavement and began to *assign* roles for the new branch opening.
Tang got the stock room.
sentences.cn: 阿糖分到了库房。

sentences.en: I got the front counter.
sentences.cn: 我分到了前台。

sentences.en: He paused before Lin's name, tapping his clipboard, while Lin stared at the ground with an unreadable expression.
sentences.cn: 他在隔壁咖啡店的林的名字前停顿了一下，敲了敲他的夹板，林低着头盯着地面，表情难以捉摸。

broad:1.en: The new site had a *broad* front window facing the street, much larger than ours. Standing outside with Tang, I could see how every passing person would be able to look straight in. 'Good for selling,' Tang said. 'Bad for hiding,' I said. Tang laughed for the first time in a week.
broad:1.cnHint: 新分店门面____宽阔，站在街上便能一眼看清店内，让人又喜又忧。
broad:1.hook: Someone had already taped a hand-written note to that big window.
broad:1.line: 'That *broad* front window will bring in customers we have never seen before.'

sentences.en: The new site had a *broad* front window facing the street, much larger than ours.
Standing outside with Tang, I could see how every passing person would be able to look straight in.
sentences.cn: 和阿糖站在外面，我能看出有多少过路的人能直接往里看。

sentences.en: 'Good for selling,' Tang said.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说，这样好卖。

sentences.en: 'Bad for hiding,' I said.
sentences.cn: 我说，这样不好躲。

sentences.en: Tang laughed for the first time in a week.
sentences.cn: 阿糖一周以来第一次笑了。

careful:1.en: The Manager walked the building site, *careful* with each step around the loose bricks and muddy ground. He checked every corner, measured a doorway with his arms, and wrote things in a small notebook. I watched from the pavement. I had never seen him look so focused, like the store was a living thing he was trying to understand.
careful:1.cnHint: 店长在工地上____地巡视每个角落，把一切细节记在小本子里。
careful:1.hook: He crossed out one line in his notebook and circled another.
careful:1.line: 'Be *careful* here — the floor plan must be right before we pour the concrete.'

sentences.en: The Manager walked the building site, *careful* with each step around the loose bricks and muddy ground.
He checked every corner, measured a doorway with his arms, and wrote things in a small notebook.
sentences.cn: 他检查了每个角落，用两臂丈量了一扇门，在一个小本子上记东西。

sentences.en: I watched from the pavement.
sentences.cn: 我在人行道上看着。

sentences.en: I had never seen him look so focused, like the store was a living thing he was trying to understand.
sentences.cn: 我从没见他这么专注过，就像那家店是个活物，他想要理解它。

combination:1.en: Outside the future branch, the Manager explained his vision: a *combination* of hot food, fresh drinks, and a small seating area. He drew it in the air with his hands. Passers-by slowed down to listen. For a moment the whole corner felt like it belonged to us, not to the empty lot or the dust.
combination:1.cnHint: 店长在街角描述新分店的设计——一种____美食、饮品与休闲座位的新形式。
combination:1.hook: One stranger in the small crowd took out a phone and started taking notes.
combination:1.line: 'The right *combination* of food and space — that is what this street is missing.'

sentences.en: Outside the future branch, the Manager explained his vision: a *combination* of hot food, fresh drinks, and a small seating area.
He drew it in the air with his hands.
sentences.cn: 他用手在空中画了出来。

sentences.en: Passers-by slowed down to listen.
sentences.cn: 过路的人放慢了脚步听。

sentences.en: For a moment the whole corner felt like it belonged to us, not to the empty lot or the dust.
sentences.cn: 那一刻整个街角都像属于我们了，不属于那片空地也不属于尘埃。

constant:1.en: Standing outside in the early morning, I noticed the *constant* hum of the city waking up — motorbikes, distant voices, a shop shutter rolling open. The new branch site was quiet by comparison, just a fence and a sign. It was strange to think that in a few months this silence would turn into something like the noise I was already used to.
constant:1.cnHint: 站在新分店工地旁，我感受着城市____不停的喧嚣，想象着这里未来的模样。
constant:1.hook: The fence had a small gap, and through it I could see a light already on inside.
constant:1.line: 'This street has *constant* foot traffic — that is exactly why we chose it.'

sentences.en: Standing outside in the early morning, I noticed the *constant* hum of the city waking up — motorbikes, distant voices, a shop shutter rolling open.
The new branch site was quiet by comparison, just a fence and a sign.
sentences.cn: 新分店的工地相比之下很安静，只有一道围栏和一块牌子。

sentences.en: It was strange to think that in a few months this silence would turn into something like the noise I was already used to.
sentences.cn: 想到再过几个月这份沉寂会变成我已经习惯的那种嘈杂，感觉有点奇怪。

relax:1.en: The Manager told me the street corner gets busy after midnight, but at two in the morning it was perfectly still. I leaned against the counter and let my shoulders *relax* for the first time all shift. A warm breeze drifted through the open door. Then footsteps. Someone was approaching very slowly, stopping to look at every item in the window display.
relax:1.cnHint: 深夜小店门前一片安静，店员终于能____一下，却听到外面有脚步声越来越近。
relax:1.hook: The figure outside pressed one hand flat against the glass.
relax:1.line: 'You can *relax* — the rush hour is long over,' the Manager said with a small smile.

sentences.en: The Manager told me the street corner gets busy after midnight, but at two in the morning it was perfectly still.
sentences.cn: 店长告诉我这个街角午夜以后会很忙，但凌晨两点的时候一片寂静。

sentences.en: I leaned against the counter and let my shoulders *relax* for the first time all shift.
A warm breeze drifted through the open door.
sentences.cn: 温暖的微风飘过敞开的门。

sentences.en: Then footsteps.
sentences.cn: 然后是脚步声。

sentences.en: Someone was approaching very slowly, stopping to look at every item in the window display.
sentences.cn: 有人走过来，走得很慢，停下来看橱窗里的每一样东西。

release:1.en: A delivery van stopped outside and the driver carried in three heavy boxes. He set them down, signed the form, and walked back into the dark street. I cut the tape and lifted the flaps to *release* the smell of fresh paper and new packaging — the new stock had finally arrived. Tang appeared from the back room exactly on cue.
release:1.cnHint: 快递员送来了新货，店员打开箱子，____出一股崭新商品的气味，同事阿糖也恰好走了出来。
release:1.hook: But one box had no label and no return address.
release:1.line: 'Pull that tab to *release* the seal,' Tang said, already reaching for a box cutter.

sentences.en: A delivery van stopped outside and the driver carried in three heavy boxes.
sentences.cn: 一辆送货车停在外面，司机搬进来三个沉甸甸的纸箱。

sentences.en: He set them down, signed the form, and walked back into the dark street.
sentences.cn: 他放下纸箱，签了单据，走回黑暗的街道。

sentences.en: I cut the tape and lifted the flaps to *release* the smell of fresh paper and new packaging — the new stock had finally arrived.
Tang appeared from the back room exactly on cue.
sentences.cn: 阿糖恰好从后间走了出来。

route:1.en: Lin from the store across the street knocked on our door just after three. She said her usual delivery *route* had changed and her supplier now passed our corner first. She wanted to know if she could leave a small parcel with us until morning. The Manager looked at me. I looked at the parcel.
route:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林来敲门，说她的货物____经过我们这里，想寄存一个包裹到天亮。
route:1.hook: The parcel made a faint ticking sound.
route:1.line: 'The new *route* brings the truck past your door at four,' Lin said, not quite meeting my eyes.

sentences.en: Lin from the store across the street knocked on our door just after three.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在三点刚过的时候敲了我们的门。

sentences.en: She said her usual delivery *route* had changed and her supplier now passed our corner first.
She wanted to know if she could leave a small parcel with us until morning.
sentences.cn: 她想知道能不能把一个小包裹放在我们这儿直到早上。

sentences.en: The Manager looked at me.
sentences.cn: 店长看着我。

sentences.en: I looked at the parcel.
sentences.cn: 我看着那个包裹。

sight:1.en: Just before dawn a thick fog rolled down the street. By four-thirty the streetlights were soft orange blurs and I could barely see the bins outside. Then, through all that white mist, a bicycle appeared — the most striking *sight* of my whole first week. The rider was wearing a full suit and a bow tie, pedalling calmly as if it were noon on a sunny day.
sight:1.cnHint: 黎明前大雾弥漫，能见度极低，一个骑车人突然出现，成了本周最令人难忘的____。
sight:1.hook: He stopped, looked straight at me, and slowly raised one finger to his lips.
sight:1.line: 'What a *sight* — fog this thick in May,' said Tang, pressing his face to the window.

sentences.en: Just before dawn a thick fog rolled down the street.
sentences.cn: 天亮前不久，浓雾沿着街道涌了下来。

sentences.en: By four-thirty the streetlights were soft orange blurs and I could barely see the bins outside.
sentences.cn: 到了四点半，路灯变成了柔和的橙色光晕，我几乎看不见外面的垃圾桶。

sentences.en: Then, through all that white mist, a bicycle appeared — the most striking *sight* of my whole first week.
The rider was wearing a full suit and a bow tie, pedalling calmly as if it were noon on a sunny day.
sentences.cn: 骑手穿着完整的西装和领结，踩着踏板，骑得就像中午的大晴天一样平静。

speaker:1.en: A woman set up a small folding table on the pavement just outside our door and placed a tiny wireless *speaker* on it. Soft music drifted in every time a customer opened the door. She sat with a notebook and wrote without looking up. The Manager said she appeared every Thursday night but had never once come inside.
speaker:1.cnHint: 一位女士在店门外摆了张桌子，放了个____播放音乐，她每周四深夜都会出现，却从未进过店里。
speaker:1.hook: Tonight, for the first time, she stood up and walked toward our door.
speaker:1.line: 'Turn the *speaker* down a little,' the Manager called out, though I suspected he rather liked it.

sentences.en: A woman set up a small folding table on the pavement just outside our door and placed a tiny wireless *speaker* on it.
Soft music drifted in every time a customer opened the door.
sentences.cn: 每次顾客推开门，柔和的音乐就飘进来。

sentences.en: She sat with a notebook and wrote without looking up.
sentences.cn: 她坐着，用笔记本记东西，头也不抬。

sentences.en: The Manager said she appeared every Thursday night but had never once come inside.
sentences.cn: 店长说她每个星期四晚上都会出现，但从来没进过店里。

species:1.en: A man in a wide hat came in and spent twenty minutes studying our pot plants near the window. He took notes in a small book. Finally he told me that two of them were a *species* he had been trying to find for three years, and asked, very politely, where we had bought them. I had no idea. The Manager was asleep in the back room.
species:1.cnHint: 一位戴帽子的男士仔细查看店里的盆栽，声称其中两株是他寻找了三年的某个____。
species:1.hook: He left his card, but the name on it matched no job I had ever heard of.
species:1.line: 'This *species* only grows in mountain soil — how did it end up here?' he whispered, almost to himself.

sentences.en: A man in a wide hat came in and spent twenty minutes studying our pot plants near the window.
sentences.cn: 一个宽帽子男人走了进来，在窗边的盆栽前研究了二十分钟。

sentences.en: He took notes in a small book.
sentences.cn: 他在一个小本子上记笔记。

sentences.en: Finally he told me that two of them were a *species* he had been trying to find for three years, and asked, very politely, where we had bought them.
I had no idea.
sentences.cn: 我一点也不知道。

sentences.en: The Manager was asleep in the back room.
sentences.cn: 店长在后间睡着了。

specifically:1.en: Tang left me a note before his shift ended: the Manager had called and asked me *specifically* to face all the drinks in the cooler before five. I finished the task with ten minutes to spare and found a twenty-dollar bill tucked behind a bottle in the very back row. No name, no note, nothing.
specifically:1.cnHint: 阿糖留下字条，说店长____叫我整理冷柜，我照做之后，在最里面发现了一张二十元钞票。
specifically:1.hook: The security camera above the cooler had been unplugged.
specifically:1.line: 'He said *specifically* you — not me, not anyone else,' Tang had written in big letters.

sentences.en: Tang left me a note before his shift ended: the Manager had called and asked me *specifically* to face all the drinks in the cooler before five.
I finished the task with ten minutes to spare and found a twenty-dollar bill tucked behind a bottle in the very back row.
sentences.cn: 我提前十分钟完成了任务，在最后一排瓶子后面发现了一张二十块的钞票。

sentences.en: No name, no note, nothing.
sentences.cn: 没有名字，没有纸条，什么都没有。

unfortunately:1.en: Around five a regular customer came in for his usual hot drink. *Unfortunately*, the machine had broken sometime in the night — a small red light blinked where the green one should have been. He stared at it. I stared at it. He pulled a folded repair manual from his coat pocket, as if he had been expecting this exact moment.
unfortunately:1.cnHint: 一位常客来买热饮，____机器坏了，但他从口袋里掏出一本维修手册，好像早有预料。
unfortunately:1.hook: The manual was dated fifteen years ago and had our store's old address on the cover.
unfortunately:1.line: '*Unfortunately* this model breaks every winter,' he said, already flipping to page twelve.

sentences.en: Around five a regular customer came in for his usual hot drink.
sentences.cn: 五点左右，一个常客进来买他平时要喝的热饮。

sentences.en: *Unfortunately*, the machine had broken sometime in the night — a small red light blinked where the green one should have been.
He stared at it.
sentences.cn: 他盯着它。

sentences.en: I stared at it.
sentences.cn: 我也盯着它。

sentences.en: He pulled a folded repair manual from his coat pocket, as if he had been expecting this exact moment.
sentences.cn: 他从大衣口袋里掏出一本折叠好的维修手册，仿佛早就在等这一刻。

consultant:1.en: A woman in a sharp coat stopped outside our store and studied the front window for a long time. The Manager stepped out and asked what she thought. She smiled and said she was a *consultant* hired to check whether this corner was a good place for a second branch.
consultant:1.cnHint: 一位女士在店外仔细打量橱窗，她是被雇来评估这个街角能否开____的。
consultant:1.hook: She wrote one word in her notebook, then walked away without showing us.
consultant:1.line: 'I am a *consultant* — I decide if your corner is worth anything.'

sentences.en: A woman in a sharp coat stopped outside our store and studied the front window for a long time.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着笔挺外套的女人在我们店外停了下来，长时间研究着橱窗。

sentences.en: The Manager stepped out and asked what she thought.
sentences.cn: 店长走出去问她在想什么。

sentences.en: She smiled and said she was a *consultant* hired to check whether this corner was a good place for a second branch.

direct:1.en: The Manager stood on the pavement with a city map and a cup of coffee, trying to work out the fastest route between our store and the possible new site three blocks away. Tang walked over, glanced at the map, and gave a *direct* answer: 'Turn left twice. Done.'
direct:1.cnHint: 店长在街上研究地图，阿糖给出了一个____的路线建议。
direct:1.hook: But Tang's shortcut passed right in front of Lin's rival store.
direct:1.line: 'My advice is *direct*: left, left, and you are there.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood on the pavement with a city map and a cup of coffee, trying to work out the fastest route between our store and the possible new site three blocks away.
sentences.cn: 店长站在人行道上，拿着一张市区地图和一杯咖啡，琢磨着从我们店到三个街区外那处可能的新址之间最快的路线。

sentences.en: Tang walked over, glanced at the map, and gave a *direct* answer: 'Turn left twice.
Done.'
sentences.cn: 搞定。”

discourage:1.en: Rain began to fall just as the Manager unrolled the hand-painted sign for the new branch outside. A passing neighbour shook her head and said the street was always wet and cold in autumn. The Manager refused to let the grey sky *discourage* him and kept the sign up all morning.
discourage:1.cnHint: 下雨天里，邻居的话让店长感到被____，但他还是坚持把新店的招牌立在雨中。
discourage:1.hook: By noon the sign had attracted one curious face — but it was Lin's.
discourage:1.line: 'Nothing will *discourage* me — not rain, not you, not anyone.'

sentences.en: Rain began to fall just as the Manager unrolled the hand-painted sign for the new branch outside.
sentences.cn: 店长在新店外展开手绘招牌时，雨下了起来。

sentences.en: A passing neighbour shook her head and said the street was always wet and cold in autumn.
sentences.cn: 一个路过的邻居摇了摇头，说这条街在秋天总是又湿又冷。

sentences.en: The Manager refused to let the grey sky *discourage* him and kept the sign up all morning.

essentially:1.en: Tang and I walked the block where the Manager wanted to open the second branch. The empty shop there had cracked tiles and one broken light. Tang looked around slowly and said the place was *essentially* just a big, cold box waiting for someone to believe in it.
essentially:1.cnHint: 阿糖看过新店选址后说，那里____就是一个等人改造的空盒子。
essentially:1.hook: Then we both noticed fresh footprints on the dusty floor — someone had been there tonight.
essentially:1.line: 'It is *essentially* an empty box, but maybe that is enough.'

sentences.en: Tang and I walked the block where the Manager wanted to open the second branch.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林和我走过店长想开第二家分店的街区。

sentences.en: The empty shop there had cracked tiles and one broken light.
sentences.cn: 那家空店铺地砖破裂，还有一盏坏了的灯。

sentences.en: Tang looked around slowly and said the place was *essentially* just a big, cold box waiting for someone to believe in it.

extent:1.en: The Manager asked me to walk the whole street and note how many people passed the corner each hour. I counted carefully for three hours in the cold. When I handed him the numbers he nodded slowly, finally seeing the *extent* of foot traffic we could expect at the new site.
extent:1.cnHint: 店长让我统计街角的人流量，以了解新店潜力的____。
extent:1.hook: The last number on my list made him go very quiet.
extent:1.line: 'Now I see the *extent* of what we could build here.'

sentences.en: The Manager asked me to walk the whole street and note how many people passed the corner each hour.
sentences.cn: 店长让我走遍整条街，记录每小时经过这个路口的人数。

sentences.en: I counted carefully for three hours in the cold.
sentences.cn: 我在寒风中仔细数了三小时。

sentences.en: When I handed him the numbers he nodded slowly, finally seeing the *extent* of foot traffic we could expect at the new site.

finance:1.en: Outside the old post office down the road, the Manager met a man carrying a thick folder. They talked in low voices beside a lamp post. Later the Manager told me the man helped small shops with *finance*, and that a loan for the second branch might actually be possible.
finance:1.cnHint: 店长在街边与一位专门做____的人悄悄会面，新分店的资金也许有了着落。
finance:1.hook: The man with the folder glanced back once and smiled in a way I could not read.
finance:1.line: 'Good *finance* advice is the only thing standing between us and that new store.'

sentences.en: Outside the old post office down the road, the Manager met a man carrying a thick folder.
sentences.cn: 店长在街道下面的老邮局外遇见了一个拿着厚厚文件夹的男人。

sentences.en: They talked in low voices beside a lamp post.
sentences.cn: 他们在路灯旁用低声交谈。

sentences.en: Later the Manager told me the man helped small shops with *finance*, and that a loan for the second branch might actually be possible.

freedom:1.en: After locking up one quiet Tuesday, I stood on the empty pavement and looked at the dark street ahead. The Manager came out and stood beside me. He said opening a second branch was never really about money — it was about the *freedom* to grow in any direction he chose.
freedom:1.cnHint: 店长站在街头说，开分店真正的意义是一种____，而不是钱。
freedom:1.hook: He then pointed down the road toward the exact block where Lin had just signed a lease.
freedom:1.line: 'This second store gives us *freedom* — to go anywhere we want.'

sentences.en: After locking up one quiet Tuesday, I stood on the empty pavement and looked at the dark street ahead.
sentences.cn: 一个安静的周二锁好店后，我站在空荡荡的人行道上，看着前面漆黑的街道。

sentences.en: The Manager came out and stood beside me.
sentences.cn: 店长走出来站在我身边。

sentences.en: He said opening a second branch was never really about money — it was about the *freedom* to grow in any direction he chose.

highlight:1.en: The city held a small street fair one Sunday morning, and the Manager set up a tiny table outside to draw attention to our planned new branch. He asked me to *highlight* the new address on a hand-drawn map and hand it to anyone who stopped. Most people took one and kept walking.
highlight:1.cnHint: 在街头集市上，店长让我在手绘地图上____新店地址，以吸引路人注意。
highlight:1.hook: One person took two maps, and I am almost certain it was Lin.
highlight:1.line: 'Please *highlight* the new address — make it impossible to miss.'

sentences.en: The city held a small street fair one Sunday morning, and the Manager set up a tiny table outside to draw attention to our planned new branch.
sentences.cn: 城市在一个周日上午举办了小型街头集市，店长在外面摆了张小桌子来吸引人们注意我们计划中的新分店。

sentences.en: He asked me to *highlight* the new address on a hand-drawn map and hand it to anyone who stopped.
Most people took one and kept walking.
sentences.cn: 大多数人拿了一张就继续走。

himself:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site at six in the morning, measuring the window space *himself* instead of waiting for the crew. He held the tape in one hand and a coffee cup in the other, muttering numbers under his breath. The street was empty except for a stray cat watching from a wall.
himself:1.cnHint: 店长天亮前独自来到新店门口，____丈量橱窗尺寸。
himself:1.hook: The cat knew something about that wall the Manager did not.
himself:1.line: 'I'll measure this *himself* — nobody else gets it right.'

sentences.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site at six in the morning, measuring the window space *himself* instead of waiting for the crew.
He held the tape in one hand and a coffee cup in the other, muttering numbers under his breath.
sentences.cn: 他一手拿着卷尺，一手拿着咖啡杯，用低沉的声音嘟囔着数字。

sentences.en: The street was empty except for a stray cat watching from a wall.
sentences.cn: 街道空荡荡的，只有一只野猫从墙上看着。

landscape:1.en: Lin arrived at the corner opposite the new branch and stood very still. The morning *landscape* — low rooftops, a bicycle leaning on a lamppost, pale sky — looked peaceful, but her eyes were fixed on the Manager's tape measure. She took a slow photograph with her phone and walked away without a word.
landscape:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在街角，把新店周边的____拍了下来。
landscape:1.hook: What exactly was she planning to do with that photograph?
landscape:1.line: 'Nice *landscape*, but I see something more interesting in it.'

sentences.en: Lin arrived at the corner opposite the new branch and stood very still.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林走到对面街角，静静地站着。

sentences.en: The morning *landscape* — low rooftops, a bicycle leaning on a lamppost, pale sky — looked peaceful, but her eyes were fixed on the Manager's tape measure.
She took a slow photograph with her phone and walked away without a word.
sentences.cn: 她用手机拍了张慢镜头，然后无声地走开了。

mentally:1.en: Tang sat on the store's back step, staring at the delivery list for the new branch. She was *mentally* sorting boxes into groups before the truck even arrived, lips moving slightly, fingers tapping the clipboard. A pigeon landed near her shoe and she did not blink once.
mentally:1.cnHint: 阿糖在台阶上____整理新店的货单，完全沉浸其中。
mentally:1.hook: She had counted one box twice — and that single mistake would matter later.
mentally:1.line: 'I'm *mentally* mapping every shelf before I touch a single box.'

sentences.en: Tang sat on the store's back step, staring at the delivery list for the new branch.
sentences.cn: 阿糖坐在店铺的后台阶上，盯着新分店的配送清单。

sentences.en: She was *mentally* sorting boxes into groups before the truck even arrived, lips moving slightly, fingers tapping the clipboard.
A pigeon landed near her shoe and she did not blink once.
sentences.cn: 一只鸽子在她鞋边落地，她眼都没眨一下。

neither:1.en: The Manager pointed at two possible signs leaning against the wall outside. One was bright red; the other was dark green. *Neither* colour matched the original store, and he frowned at both for a long moment. A delivery driver slowed his bicycle to look, then pedalled on, shaking his head.
neither:1.cnHint: 店长看着两块备选招牌，发现____颜色与原店相符。

sentences.en: The Manager pointed at two possible signs leaning against the wall outside.

onto:1.en: Tang carried a tall stack of sign boards out of the van and stepped carefully *onto* the low platform in front of the new branch. She balanced the stack with her chin and nudged the door open with her knee. The Manager watched from the pavement, arms folded, saying nothing.
onto:1.cnHint: 阿糖抱着一叠招牌，踩____门口的台子往里走。

onto:1.line: 'Step *onto* the platform slowly — those boards are not light.'

sentences.en: Tang carried a tall stack of sign boards out of the van and stepped carefully *onto* the low platform in front of the new branch.
She balanced the stack with her chin and nudged the door open with her knee.
sentences.cn: 她用下巴夹住那摞招牌板，用膝盖顶开了门。

plus:1.en: Lin had been counting on her fingers outside the rival site: foot traffic, corner position, bus stop nearby. She wrote it all in a small notebook and snapped it shut with a satisfied click.
sentences.cn: 她把这一切记在小本子上，啪的一声满意地合上了。

root:1.en: A large old tree stood just outside the new branch, its thick *root* pushing a ridge into the footpath. The Manager crouched down and traced the ridge with his finger, worried it would trip customers. He looked up at the tree, then at the store, as if asking one of them for advice.

root:1.line: 'This *root* is a problem — customers will trip before they even enter.'

sentences.en: A large old tree stood just outside the new branch, its thick *root* pushing a ridge into the footpath.
The Manager crouched down and traced the ridge with his finger, worried it would trip customers.
sentences.cn: 店长蹲下来，用手指沿着凸起的地方摸，担心它会绊到顾客。

sentences.cn: 他抬头看看树，再看看店铺，好像在向其中某一个征求意见。

satisfy:1.en: After a long morning on the street, the Manager stepped back and looked at the new branch from across the road. The sign was level, the windows were clean, and the small chalkboard menu stood straight by the door. Nothing grand — but enough to *satisfy* him for now. He allowed himself one small nod.

satisfaction:2.en: A folded note slipped under the back-room door read: 'New branch opens Friday. You will run it.' I read it twice, then set it on the shelf beside the cold coffee I had forgotten. A quiet warmth spread through my chest — a deep *satisfaction* I had not expected to feel at midnight.

cultivate:2.en: The Manager had left a thick folder on the counter before dawn. Inside were schedules, supplier lists, and a handwritten note: 'Study these. A good branch leader must *cultivate* the habit of noticing small things — a nearly empty shelf, a tired regular, a door that sticks.' I closed the folder slowly.
