sentences.en: Behind the back shelf I found a small cooler no one had mentioned.
sentences.cn: 在后架后面我找到了一个没人提过的小冰箱。

sentences.en: Inside: three sealed packs of salted *fish*, a price tag from a supplier I did not recognise, and a sticky note that said 'Do not sell — Lin.'
I put the cooler back exactly as I found it.
sentences.cn: 我把冰箱放回原来的位置。

fashion:2.en: Tang rushed in from the back room wearing a bright yellow apron covered in little stars. 'The Manager ordered these,' she said, handing me one. 'New store, new image.' In her *fashion*, she made even a silly apron look like a deliberate choice. I tied mine on without a word.
fashion:2.cnHint: 唐以她独特的____，让店里新订的围裙穿出了别样的感觉。
fashion:2.hook: The Manager's 'new image' plan turned out to be only the beginning.
fashion:2.line: 'In my *fashion*, I make anything look like it belongs here.'

sentences.en: Tang rushed in from the back room wearing a bright yellow apron covered in little stars.
sentences.cn: 阿糖穿着一件布满小星星的亮黄色围裙从后室冲了出来。

sentences.en: 'The Manager ordered these,' she said, handing me one.
sentences.cn: '店长订的，'她递给我一件说。

sentences.en: 'New store, new image.'
sentences.cn: '新店，新形象。'

sentences.en: In her *fashion*, she made even a silly apron look like a deliberate choice.
I tied mine on without a word.
sentences.cn: 我无言地系上围裙。

weather:2.en: The Manager called just after midnight. 'Check the roof door,' he said. 'It sticks in this *weather*.' I climbed the narrow back stairs, pushed the door open, and found a small folding table and two chairs no one had told me about. The night air was cool and completely still.
weather:2.cnHint: 店长来电让我检查屋顶的门，说这种____容易卡住。
weather:2.hook: On the table sat a cup of tea that was still warm.
weather:2.line: 'In this *weather*, the roof door always sticks — go check it now.'

sentences.en: The Manager called just after midnight.
sentences.cn: 店长在午夜刚过后打来电话。

sentences.en: 'Check the roof door,' he said.
sentences.cn: '检查一下屋顶门，'他说。

sentences.en: 'It sticks in this *weather*.'
I climbed the narrow back stairs, pushed the door open, and found a small folding table and two chairs no one had told me about.
sentences.cn: 我爬上狭窄的后楼梯，推开门，发现了一张小折叠桌和两把椅子，没人告诉过我。

sentences.en: The night air was cool and completely still.
sentences.cn: 夜晚的空气凉爽而绝对寂静。

device:2.en: A regular customer left a small *device* on the counter — flat, silver, with a single green light blinking slowly. No name, no receipt, no explanation. Tang picked it up, turned it over, and set it down carefully. 'Someone will come back for this,' she said. No one did. Not that night.
device:2.cnHint: 一位常客把一个奇怪的____落在了收银台上，没有留下任何说明。
device:2.hook: At three in the morning, the green light turned red.
device:2.line: 'This *device* has been here two hours — should we call someone?'

sentences.en: A regular customer left a small *device* on the counter — flat, silver, with a single green light blinking slowly.
No name, no receipt, no explanation.
sentences.cn: 没有名字，没有收据，没有解释。

sentences.en: Tang picked it up, turned it over, and set it down carefully.
sentences.cn: 阿糖拿起它，翻了翻，小心地放了下去。

sentences.en: 'Someone will come back for this,' she said.
sentences.cn: '会有人回来拿的，'她说。

sentences.en: No one did.
sentences.cn: 没人来。

sentences.en: Not that night.
sentences.cn: 那晚没有。

farm:2.en: An older woman came in just before dawn carrying a cloth bag that smelled of earth and green leaves. She set a jar of honey on the counter. 'From my *farm*, outside the city,' she said proudly. 'The Manager ordered it for the new shop.' I had not known there was a new shop yet.
farm:2.cnHint: 一位老太太送来了她____出产的蜂蜜，说是店长为新店订购的。
farm:2.hook: She mentioned the new shop's address before the Manager had told any of us.
farm:2.line: 'I grew this honey on my own *farm* — nothing added, nothing removed.'

sentences.en: An older woman came in just before dawn carrying a cloth bag that smelled of earth and green leaves.
sentences.cn: 一位年长的女士在天亮前不久走了进来，提着一个闻起来像土壤和绿叶的布袋。

sentences.en: She set a jar of honey on the counter.
sentences.cn: 她在柜台上放了一罐蜂蜜。

sentences.en: 'From my *farm*, outside the city,' she said proudly.
'The Manager ordered it for the new shop.'
sentences.cn: '店长为新店订的。'

sentences.en: I had not known there was a new shop yet.
sentences.cn: 我还不知道有新店呢。

drug:2.en: A young man in a white coat hurried in and asked for cold water. He set a small labelled bag on the counter while he paid. Tang glanced at it. 'Is that a *drug* sample?' she asked quietly. He nodded. 'New pharmacy opening next door,' he said. 'We move in Friday.' I looked at Tang. She looked at me.
drug:2.cnHint: 一位穿白大褂的年轻人来买水，顺口透露隔壁将开一家新药店，他带着____样品。
drug:2.hook: Tang said nothing, but she had already taken out her phone.
drug:2.line: 'It is just a *drug* sample — the new pharmacy opens on Friday.'

sentences.en: A young man in a white coat hurried in and asked for cold water.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着白大褂的年轻男子匆匆跑进来要冰水。

sentences.en: He set a small labelled bag on the counter while he paid.
sentences.cn: 他在付钱时在柜台上放了一个贴着标签的小袋子。

sentences.en: Tang glanced at it.
sentences.cn: 阿糖瞥了一眼。

sentences.en: 'Is that a *drug* sample?' she asked quietly.
He nodded.
sentences.cn: 他点了点头。

sentences.en: 'New pharmacy opening next door,' he said.
sentences.cn: '新药房就要在隔壁开了，'他说。

sentences.en: 'We move in Friday.'
sentences.cn: '我们周五搬进去。'

sentences.en: I looked at Tang.
sentences.cn: 我看了看阿糖。

sentences.en: She looked at me.
sentences.cn: 她看了看我。

heat:2.en: The small storage room at the back held old stock, a broken fan, and a thermometer fixed to the wall. I checked it at two in the morning: thirty-one degrees. The *heat* in there was enough to ruin the chocolate bars stacked by the door. I moved them to the front shelf and texted the Manager a photo.
heat:2.cnHint: 我发现储藏室里的____已经高到足以损坏货物，立刻把东西搬走并通知了店长。
heat:2.hook: The Manager's reply came in four seconds flat.
heat:2.line: 'The *heat* back there will ruin the stock — we need to fix that fan.'

sentences.en: The small storage room at the back held old stock, a broken fan, and a thermometer fixed to the wall.
sentences.cn: 后面的小储藏室里堆放着旧货、一个坏了的风扇和钉在墙上的温度计。

sentences.en: I checked it at two in the morning: thirty-one degrees.
sentences.cn: 我在凌晨两点检查了它：三十一度。

sentences.en: The *heat* in there was enough to ruin the chocolate bars stacked by the door.
I moved them to the front shelf and texted the Manager a photo.
sentences.cn: 我把它们挪到前面的架子上，给店长发了张照片。

announce:2.en: A folded note appeared under the store door just after two in the morning. I picked it up and read it by the counter light. It said the Manager planned to *announce* something big at the staff meeting on Friday — a second store, maybe, on the other side of town. My hands went a little cold.
announce:2.cnHint: 一张纸条悄悄塞进了门缝，说店长周五将____一件大事。
announce:2.hook: But the note was signed with only a question mark.
announce:2.line: 'The Manager will *announce* the news on Friday — every one of us should be there.'

sentences.en: A folded note appeared under the store door just after two in the morning.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点过后，一张折叠的纸条出现在店门下。

sentences.en: I picked it up and read it by the counter light.
sentences.cn: 我拿起来，在柜台灯光下读了。

sentences.en: It said the Manager planned to *announce* something big at the staff meeting on Friday — a second store, maybe, on the other side of town.
My hands went a little cold.
sentences.cn: 我的手有点发冷。

appropriate:2.en: Tang found a dusty cardboard box in the back room while stacking new stock. Inside was a set of spare keys, three old staff badges, and a small cash bag. Tang looked at me and said it did not feel *appropriate* to simply put it back. We called the Manager at three in the morning.
appropriate:2.cnHint: 阿糖在库房发现了一个旧箱子，觉得处理方式必须____。
appropriate:2.hook: The Manager went very quiet on the phone for a long time.
appropriate:2.line: 'It is not *appropriate* to ignore this — we have to report it tonight.'

sentences.en: Tang found a dusty cardboard box in the back room while stacking new stock.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在整理新货时在后室找到了一个满是灰尘的纸箱。

sentences.en: Inside was a set of spare keys, three old staff badges, and a small cash bag.
sentences.cn: 里面是一套备用钥匙、三个旧员工证和一个小现金袋。

sentences.en: Tang looked at me and said it did not feel *appropriate* to simply put it back.
We called the Manager at three in the morning.
sentences.cn: 我们在凌晨三点打给了店长。

chief:2.en: The delivery driver who came every Wednesday night finally told me his name: Old Wen. He said his *chief* reason for choosing the night route was the silence — no traffic, no crowds, just the dark road and the radio. He handed me a box of drinks and winked. I wondered what the second reason was.
chief:2.cnHint: 送货司机告诉我，他选择夜班路线的____原因是喜欢安静。
chief:2.hook: He never mentioned that second reason, not once.
chief:2.line: 'My *chief* reason for this job? The night is honest — it never pretends.'

sentences.en: The delivery driver who came every Wednesday night finally told me his name: Old Wen.
sentences.cn: 每个星期三晚上来送货的司机终于告诉了我他的名字——老文。

sentences.en: He said his *chief* reason for choosing the night route was the silence — no traffic, no crowds, just the dark road and the radio.
He handed me a box of drinks and winked.
sentences.cn: 他递给我一盒饮料，眨了眨眼。

sentences.en: I wondered what the second reason was.
sentences.cn: 我想知道第二个原因是什么。

clearly:2.en: Someone had written on the staff whiteboard in red marker, big and careful: NEW STORE COMING. Nothing else. Lin walked in from the cold, stared at it, then looked at me. I shrugged. The message was *clearly* meant for all of us, yet nobody seemed to know who had written it.
clearly:2.cnHint: 白板上用红笔写着一行字，____是写给所有人看的，但没人知道是谁写的。
clearly:2.hook: The red marker was still sitting right there, lid off, still wet.
clearly:2.line: 'This is *clearly* not a joke — look how carefully someone wrote every letter.'

sentences.en: Someone had written on the staff whiteboard in red marker, big and careful: NEW STORE COMING.
sentences.cn: 有人用红色马克笔在员工白板上写了很大很工整的字：新店即将开业。

sentences.en: Nothing else.
sentences.cn: 就这么一句话。

sentences.en: Lin walked in from the cold, stared at it, then looked at me.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林从寒风中走了进来，盯着那句话看，然后看向我。

sentences.en: I shrugged.
sentences.cn: 我耸了耸肩。

sentences.en: The message was *clearly* meant for all of us, yet nobody seemed to know who had written it.

communicate:2.en: The Manager left a voice message on the store phone instead of calling any of us directly. Tang played it twice on speaker. 'The best way to *communicate* big changes,' Tang said slowly, 'is apparently to talk to a machine.' We both looked at the little blinking light and said nothing for a while.
communicate:2.cnHint: 店长给门店电话留了语音，阿糖说这真是一种奇怪的____方式。
communicate:2.hook: The message had one sentence none of us could quite make out.
communicate:2.line: 'Why *communicate* news this way — are we not worth a real phone call?'

sentences.en: The Manager left a voice message on the store phone instead of calling any of us directly.
sentences.cn: 店长没有直接给我们任何人打电话，而是在店里的电话留言机上留了条语音。

sentences.en: Tang played it twice on speaker.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在扬声器上播放了两遍。

sentences.en: 'The best way to *communicate* big changes,' Tang said slowly, 'is apparently to talk to a machine.'
We both looked at the little blinking light and said nothing for a while.
sentences.cn: 我们俩都看着那盏小小的闪烁灯，有一阵子谁也没说话。

emphasis:2.en: The Manager's printed memo about the new branch had one line underlined twice and circled in pen: TEAMWORK IS EVERYTHING. Tang read it aloud and tapped the circled words. 'Notice the *emphasis*,' Tang said, sounding more worried than inspired. I noticed. The word EVERYTHING felt very large in that small break room.
emphasis:2.cnHint: 店长备忘录里有一句话被圈起来加重标注，阿糖说要注意这个____。
emphasis:2.hook: Tang folded the memo very slowly and slipped it into a pocket.
emphasis:2.line: 'The *emphasis* on teamwork here tells me someone already made a mistake.'

sentences.en: The Manager's printed memo about the new branch had one line underlined twice and circled in pen: TEAMWORK IS EVERYTHING.
sentences.cn: 店长关于新分店的打印备忘录上有一行被下划了两次，还用笔圈了起来：团队合作就是一切。

sentences.en: Tang read it aloud and tapped the circled words.
sentences.cn: 阿糖读了出来，拍了拍那圈起来的字。

sentences.en: 'Notice the *emphasis*,' Tang said, sounding more worried than inspired.
I noticed.
sentences.cn: 我注意到了。

sentences.en: The word EVERYTHING felt very large in that small break room.
sentences.cn: 那个"一切"在这间小小的休息室里显得特别大。

emphasize:2.en: Lin came in just before dawn carrying a folder of printouts. 'The Manager asked me to *emphasize* one thing at the briefing,' Lin said, spreading sheets across the counter. Every single sheet had the same bold heading: LOCATION IS FINAL. I looked at the address. It was two doors down from Lin's own flat.
emphasize:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来一叠文件，说店长让他特别____一件事：新店地址已定。
emphasize:2.hook: Lin's face gave absolutely nothing away.
emphasize:2.line: 'I am here to *emphasize* that the location decision is final — no more votes.'

sentences.en: Lin came in just before dawn carrying a folder of printouts.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在天亮前走了进来，手里拿着一文件夹的打印纸。

sentences.en: 'The Manager asked me to *emphasize* one thing at the briefing,' Lin said, spreading sheets across the counter.
Every single sheet had the same bold heading: LOCATION IS FINAL.
sentences.cn: 纸上每一张都用粗体写着同样的标题：地点已确定。

sentences.en: I looked at the address.
sentences.cn: 我看了看地址。

sentences.en: It was two doors down from Lin's own flat.
sentences.cn: 那是离隔壁咖啡店的林自己住的地方两门之外。

england:2.en: Tucked inside the new stock delivery was a small tin of biscuits with a red double-decker bus on the lid and tiny print reading MADE IN *ENGLAND*. No order slip, no name, nothing. Tang turned it over and over. An old regular shuffled in just then, glanced at the tin, and smiled in a way that seemed almost like recognition.
england:2.cnHint: 一批新货里夹着一盒印有"来自____"的饼干，没有任何来历说明。
england:2.hook: The old regular bought nothing else and left without a single word.
england:2.line: 'A tin from *England* with no label — someone sent this here on purpose.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside the new stock delivery was a small tin of biscuits with a red double-decker bus on the lid and tiny print reading MADE IN *ENGLAND*.
No order slip, no name, nothing.
sentences.cn: 没有订单单据，没有名字，什么都没有。

sentences.en: Tang turned it over and over.
sentences.cn: 阿糖把罐子翻来覆去地看。

sentences.en: An old regular shuffled in just then, glanced at the tin, and smiled in a way that seemed almost like recognition.
sentences.cn: 就在那时，一位老主顾拖着脚步走了进来，瞥了一眼那罐饼干，用一种几乎像是认出来了什么的方式微笑了。

immediately:2.en: A note appeared under the back-room door just after midnight. I picked it up and read it. The Manager had written that a second store would open across town, and that staff choices would be made *immediately* — no waiting, no long talks. My hands felt cold.
immediately:2.cnHint: 店长的纸条说，分店的员工名单会____确定。
immediately:2.hook: My name was circled in pencil — but so was Lin's.
immediately:2.line: 'We decide *immediately*, so be ready by morning,' the Manager said.

sentences.en: A note appeared under the back-room door just after midnight.
sentences.cn: 午夜刚过，一张纸条从后间门下面塞了进来。

sentences.en: I picked it up and read it.
sentences.cn: 我拿起来读了一遍。

sentences.en: The Manager had written that a second store would open across town, and that staff choices would be made *immediately* — no waiting, no long talks.
My hands felt cold.
sentences.cn: 我的手感到冰冷。

improvement:2.en: The Manager pinned a chart to the wall near the coffee machine one afternoon. It showed sales numbers for both stores — the new one and ours. Our numbers were higher, but the gap was small. 'Any *improvement* here,' he said quietly, pointing at our side, 'decides who runs the new branch.'
improvement:2.cnHint: 店长贴出对比图，说这边的____将决定谁去管分店。
improvement:2.hook: Tang had already started rearranging the snack shelf without being asked.
improvement:2.line: 'A small *improvement* now can change everything later,' Tang whispered.

sentences.en: The Manager pinned a chart to the wall near the coffee machine one afternoon.
sentences.cn: 店长在一个下午把一张表贴在了咖啡机旁的墙上。

sentences.en: It showed sales numbers for both stores — the new one and ours.
sentences.cn: 表上显示的是两家店的销售数字——新店和我们的店。

sentences.en: Our numbers were higher, but the gap was small.
sentences.cn: 我们的数字更高，但差距不大。

sentences.en: 'Any *improvement* here,' he said quietly, pointing at our side, 'decides who runs the new branch.'

afternoon:2.en: The delivery for the new store arrived on a bright *afternoon* when I was alone at the counter. Three large boxes sat outside the door, each one labelled with an address I did not know. I copied it down on a receipt slip before Tang came back from lunch.
afternoon:2.cnHint: 一个____，我独自收到了寄往新店的货物，偷偷记下了地址。
afternoon:2.hook: That address matched the street where Lin's cousin lived.
afternoon:2.line: 'Every *afternoon* this week, boxes come for the new place,' I told Tang.

sentences.en: The delivery for the new store arrived on a bright *afternoon* when I was alone at the counter.
Three large boxes sat outside the door, each one labelled with an address I did not know.
sentences.cn: 三个大纸箱放在门外，每个箱子上都标着我不认识的地址。

sentences.en: I copied it down on a receipt slip before Tang came back from lunch.
sentences.cn: 我在阿糖从午餐回来前把地址抄在了一张收据纸上。

expand:2.en: Lin spread a hand-drawn map across the counter during a slow hour. Little circles marked shops and bus stops. 'The Manager wants to *expand* into this block,' Lin said, almost to himself, tracing a route with one finger. He did not notice me leaning closer to read the small notes in the margin.
expand:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林展开地图，谈到店长想____进那片街区，没发现我在偷看。
expand:2.hook: One margin note read: 'Remove current night clerk if needed.'
expand:2.line: 'To *expand* well, you need someone who knows the neighbourhood,' Lin said.

sentences.en: Lin spread a hand-drawn map across the counter during a slow hour.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在闲散时光里把一张手绘的地图摊在了柜台上。

sentences.en: Little circles marked shops and bus stops.
sentences.cn: 小圆圈标记了商店和公交站。

sentences.en: 'The Manager wants to *expand* into this block,' Lin said, almost to himself, tracing a route with one finger.
He did not notice me leaning closer to read the small notes in the margin.
sentences.cn: 他没注意到我靠近了去读边缘处的小字。

regardless:2.en: Tang stayed past the end of the shift to face the new stock system, *regardless* of the late hour. I watched him enter each item twice, checking the screen after every line. He never complained. Outside, rain tapped the glass. The Manager watched from the office doorway without saying a word.
regardless:2.cnHint: 阿糖____时间多晚，坚持把新库存系统录完，店长在门口默默看着。
regardless:2.hook: The Manager then sent a message — to Lin, not Tang.
regardless:2.line: 'I will finish this *regardless*, even if it takes all night,' Tang said.

sentences.en: Tang stayed past the end of the shift to face the new stock system, *regardless* of the late hour.
I watched him enter each item twice, checking the screen after every line.
sentences.cn: 我看他输入每一项两次，每一行后都检查一遍屏幕。

sentences.en: He never complained.
sentences.cn: 他从不抱怨。

sentences.en: Outside, rain tapped the glass.
sentences.cn: 外面，雨敲打着玻璃。

sentences.en: The Manager watched from the office doorway without saying a word.
sentences.cn: 店长从办公室门口看着，一言不发。

rid:2.en: I found a damp cardboard sign at the bottom of the storage shelf, half hidden under empty bags. It read: 'Grand Opening — Sister Store.' Someone had tried to *rid* the shelf of it, pushing it deep into the corner. The tape on one edge was still fresh and sticky.
rid:2.cnHint: 我在储物架底部发现了分店开业的牌子，有人试图____它，但没彻底藏好。
rid:2.hook: The handwriting matched Lin's notebook exactly.
rid:2.line: 'I just wanted to *rid* the shelf of old junk,' Lin said, not meeting my eyes.

sentences.en: I found a damp cardboard sign at the bottom of the storage shelf, half hidden under empty bags.
sentences.cn: 我在储物架的底部找到了一张潮湿的硬纸板标牌，半隐在空塑料袋下面。

sentences.en: It read: 'Grand Opening — Sister Store.'
sentences.cn: 上面写着："盛大开业——姐妹店"。

sentences.en: Someone had tried to *rid* the shelf of it, pushing it deep into the corner.
The tape on one edge was still fresh and sticky.
sentences.cn: 其中一边的胶带还是新鲜的、粘糊糊的。

dog:2.en: A small *dog* trotted into the store just before three in the morning, collar tag jingling. It sniffed every corner, then sat squarely in front of the new-store brochure rack by the door, as if it belonged there. No owner followed. I checked the tag — the address was the new branch location.
dog:2.cnHint: 一只小____深夜跑进店里，径直坐到新店宣传架前，项圈上写着新店地址。
dog:2.hook: It looked at me with calm, knowing eyes, then trotted back into the dark.
dog:2.line: 'That *dog* shows up every night around three,' Tang said, sounding uneasy.

sentences.en: A small *dog* trotted into the store just before three in the morning, collar tag jingling.
It sniffed every corner, then sat squarely in front of the new-store brochure rack by the door, as if it belonged there.

living:2.line: 'This job is my *living*, so I take it seriously.'

sentences.cn: 阿糖在柜台后面一枚一枚地把硬币数进一个小罐子里。

sentences.en: 'Night shifts are not glamorous,' she admitted, 'but they are my *living* for now.'
She smiled without any self-pity, then slid a warm meat bun across to me.
sentences.cn: 她笑着，没有半分自怜，然后把一个热肉包推过来给我。

sentences.en: Outside, the street was completely silent.
sentences.cn: 外面，街道完全静寂。

proposal:2.en: The Manager taped a single sheet of paper to the fridge door and stepped back, arms folded. 'Read it,' he said. It was a *proposal* for a second store, two blocks east, with a hand-drawn map and a bold opening date circled in red. He looked very pleased with himself.
proposal:2.cnHint: 店长把一份开设新分店的____贴到冰箱门上，让我们仔细读。
proposal:2.hook: The opening date was only three weeks away.
proposal:2.line: 'I wrote this *proposal* myself — tell me honestly what you think.'

sentences.en: The Manager taped a single sheet of paper to the fridge door and stepped back, arms folded.
sentences.cn: 店长在冰箱门上贴了一张纸，然后退后一步，双臂交叉。

sentences.en: 'Read it,' he said.
sentences.cn: "读一下，"他说。

sentences.en: It was a *proposal* for a second store, two blocks east, with a hand-drawn map and a bold opening date circled in red.
He looked very pleased with himself.
sentences.cn: 他看起来对自己很满意。

relevant:2.en: Lin walked in just before two in the morning and dropped a folder on our counter without a word. Inside were printed pages about local rent prices, school calendars, and bus routes. 'Only the *relevant* facts,' she said coolly, tapping the folder. 'I know what the Manager is planning.'
relevant:2.cnHint: 林深夜走进店里，把一份只包含____信息的资料放在柜台上，暗示她知道店长的计划。
relevant:2.hook: Her folder was thicker than the Manager's entire plan.
relevant:2.line: 'I kept only the *relevant* data — nothing extra, nothing wasted.'

sentences.en: Lin walked in just before two in the morning and dropped a folder on our counter without a word.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在凌晨两点刚过的时候走进来，没说一句话就把一个文件夹放在我们的柜台上。

sentences.en: Inside were printed pages about local rent prices, school calendars, and bus routes.
sentences.cn: 里面是关于当地房租价格、学校日历和公交路线的打印页面。

sentences.en: 'Only the *relevant* facts,' she said coolly, tapping the folder.
'I know what the Manager is planning.'
sentences.cn: "我知道店长在计划什么。"

senior:2.en: A quiet man came in every Tuesday for warm soy milk and a small bread roll. Tang told me he was a *senior* at the university nearby, finishing his last semester. He always paid exact change and always said thank you twice. Tonight he left a handwritten note beside the till.
senior:2.cnHint: 一位即将毕业的大学____每周都来买同样的东西，今晚他在收银台旁留下了一张手写便条。
senior:2.hook: The note had the Manager's home address on it.
senior:2.line: 'He is a *senior* this year — graduating in two months,' Tang told me softly.

sentences.en: A quiet man came in every Tuesday for warm soy milk and a small bread roll.
sentences.cn: 有个安静的男人每周二都来买一杯热豆浆和一个小面包。

sentences.en: Tang told me he was a *senior* at the university nearby, finishing his last semester.
He always paid exact change and always said thank you twice.
sentences.cn: 他总是付好零钱，总是说两次谢谢。

sentences.en: Tonight he left a handwritten note beside the till.
sentences.cn: 今晚他在收银台旁留下了一张手写便条。

table:2.en: I found a folded map wedged under the leg of the small *table* in the store room. It showed the neighbourhood with three locations marked in different colours — red, blue, and green. Someone had been planning this quietly for a long time. The map was not the Manager's handwriting.
table:2.cnHint: 我在储藏室的小____腿下发现了一张折叠地图，上面标注了三个不同地点。
table:2.hook: The blue mark was our store — drawn there last.
table:2.line: 'Check under the *table* in the back room,' Tang said without looking up.

sentences.en: I found a folded map wedged under the leg of the small *table* in the store room.
It showed the neighbourhood with three locations marked in different colours — red, blue, and green.
sentences.cn: 地图上标着这个街区，用红、蓝、绿三种颜色标注了不同的位置。

sentences.en: Someone had been planning this quietly for a long time.
sentences.cn: 有人已经在这儿悄悄筹划了很久。

sentences.en: The map was not the Manager's handwriting.
sentences.cn: 这不是店长的笔迹。

campus:2.en: Just after midnight a tired student pushed through our door still wearing her university lanyard. 'The vending machines on *campus* all shut down,' she sighed, grabbing two bottles of water and a bag of crackers. She paid and was gone in ninety seconds. But she had left her student card on the counter.
campus:2.cnHint: 一个学生说____里的自动售货机都关了，匆忙买完东西后把学生证落在了柜台上。
campus:2.hook: The card showed she lived in the dorm nearest the red circle on the Manager's map.
campus:2.line: 'Nothing on *campus* is open past midnight — you are my only hope.'

sentences.en: Just after midnight a tired student pushed through our door still wearing her university lanyard.
sentences.cn: 午夜刚过，一个穿着大学证件的疲惫女生推门而入。

sentences.en: 'The vending machines on *campus* all shut down,' she sighed, grabbing two bottles of water and a bag of crackers.
She paid and was gone in ninety seconds.
sentences.cn: 她付完钱，九十秒内就消失了。

sentences.en: But she had left her student card on the counter.
sentences.cn: 但她在柜台上落下了学生卡。

campaign:2.en: A folded paper landed on the counter. I opened it: a neat hand-drawn map with arrows and timing notes. Someone had planned a whole *campaign* to place flyers in every building before the Manager arrived at dawn. The handwriting looked very familiar.
campaign:2.cnHint: 一份详细的行动计划书出现在收银台上，店长早上来之前就必须完成。
campaign:2.line: 'This *campaign* starts at three — don't be late.'

sentences.en: A folded paper landed on the counter.
sentences.cn: 一张折起来的纸掉在了柜台上。

sentences.en: I opened it: a neat hand-drawn map with arrows and timing notes.
sentences.cn: 我打开一看，是一张手绘的地图，上面标着箭头和时间备注。

sentences.en: Someone had planned a whole *campaign* to place flyers in every building before the Manager arrived at dawn.
The handwriting looked very familiar.
sentences.cn: 笔迹看起来很眼熟。

hurt:2.en: I found a small cactus on the back shelf with a torn sticky note: 'Please water me. I don't bite.' Below that, in tinier letters: 'The last clerk left me dry for a week. That really *hurt*.' I watered it immediately and felt oddly guilty.
hurt:2.cnHint: 店里的一盆小仙人掌留下了一张纸条，诉说着上一个店员的疏忽带来的____。
hurt:2.hook: Then I noticed a second note hidden underneath.
hurt:2.line: 'It *hurt* more than you'd think for a plant.'

sentences.en: I found a small cactus on the back shelf with a torn sticky note: 'Please water me.
sentences.cn: 我在后架子上发现了一盆小仙人掌，贴着一张破破的便签纸："请给我浇浇水。

sentences.en: I don't bite.'
sentences.cn: 我不会咬人。"

sentences.en: Below that, in tinier letters: 'The last clerk left me dry for a week.
sentences.cn: 下面用更小的字写着："上个员工放我干了一整个星期。

sentences.en: That really *hurt*.'
I watered it immediately and felt oddly guilty.
sentences.cn: 我立刻给它浇了水，莫名其妙地感到了内疚。

initiative:2.en: Nobody told me to restock the hot-drink shelf after the midnight rush. I just did it. When the Manager came in at six, she stopped, looked at the neat rows, and nodded slowly. 'Good *initiative*,' she said, then walked past without another word. That single nod felt like a trophy.
initiative:2.cnHint: 没人要求我补货，但我自己主动做了，店长只用一个词表扬了我的____。
initiative:2.hook: Tang later told me that nod was extremely rare.
initiative:2.line: 'Showing *initiative* on your first week — not bad.'

sentences.en: Nobody told me to restock the hot-drink shelf after the midnight rush.
sentences.cn: 午夜的冲刺过后，没人让我重新整理热饮料的架子。

sentences.en: I just did it.
sentences.cn: 我就自己整理了。

sentences.en: When the Manager came in at six, she stopped, looked at the neat rows, and nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 店长六点进来的时候，停下脚步，看着整齐的一排排饮料，慢慢点了点头。

sentences.en: 'Good *initiative*,' she said, then walked past without another word.
That single nod felt like a trophy.
sentences.cn: 那个点头让我感觉像拿到了奖杯。

jump:2.en: Lin slid a folded note under the stockroom door at two in the morning. It read: 'New branch opens Friday. Don't let your sales *jump* before then — it'll make our numbers look bad at the meeting.' I stared at it for a long time, unsure whether to laugh or worry.
jump:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林悄悄塞来一张纸条，提醒我别让销售额在新分店开业前____得太高。
jump:2.hook: The Manager's meeting was on Thursday.
jump:2.line: 'If your numbers *jump* now, we both look strange.'

sentences.en: Lin slid a folded note under the stockroom door at two in the morning.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点，隔壁咖啡店的林在储藏室门下塞了一张折好的纸条。

sentences.en: It read: 'New branch opens Friday.
sentences.cn: 纸条写着："新店周五开张。

sentences.en: Don't let your sales *jump* before then — it'll make our numbers look bad at the meeting.'
I stared at it for a long time, unsure whether to laugh or worry.
sentences.cn: 我盯着它看了很久，不知道该笑还是该担心。

lie:2.en: The new branch address *lies* three streets east of ours, right next to the university gate. I discovered this on a printed notice the Manager left under my keyboard, circled in red. Three streets felt close enough to be a problem. I folded the notice and slipped it into my pocket.
lie:2.cnHint: 新分店的地址____在离我们只有三条街的地方，店长留下的通知让我意识到这件事。
lie:2.hook: The university gate meant ten thousand students.
lie:2.line: 'The new store *lies* right where all the students pass.'

sentences.en: The new branch address *lies* three streets east of ours, right next to the university gate.
I discovered this on a printed notice the Manager left under my keyboard, circled in red.
sentences.cn: 我在店长放在我键盘下面的一张打印通知上发现了这个地址，周围被红笔圈了圈。

sentences.en: Three streets felt close enough to be a problem.
sentences.cn: 三条街的距离近到足以成为问题。

sentences.en: I folded the notice and slipped it into my pocket.
sentences.cn: 我把通知折起来塞进了口袋。

lunch:2.en: A delivery bag was left inside the door at noon with my name on it. Inside: one neat *lunch* box and a card that said 'Stay strong, night-shift friend.' I had never told anyone I sometimes skipped meals. I looked at the security camera in the corner and then at the card again.
lunch:2.cnHint: 一份午餐悄悄出现在店门口，附有一张鼓励我坚持的小卡片，我不知道是谁送的。
lunch:2.hook: The bag's knot was tied the way Tang always ties things.
lunch:2.line: 'A proper *lunch* matters more than you think it does.'

sentences.en: A delivery bag was left inside the door at noon with my name on it.
sentences.cn: 中午的时候，门里被放进了一个快递袋，上面写着我的名字。

sentences.en: Inside: one neat *lunch* box and a card that said 'Stay strong, night-shift friend.'
I had never told anyone I sometimes skipped meals.
sentences.cn: 我从没告诉任何人我有时会不吃饭。

sentences.en: I looked at the security camera in the corner and then at the card again.
sentences.cn: 我看了看角落里的监控摄像头，然后又看了看卡片。

necessarily:2.en: I told Tang I was worried the new branch would take all our regular customers. Tang shrugged. 'New competition doesn't *necessarily* mean we lose. It means we have to give people a reason to stay.' Then Tang pulled out a small notebook filled with ideas and dropped it on the counter.
necessarily:2.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我，新分店开业并不____意味着我们会失去老顾客，还拿出了一本小册子。
necessarily:2.hook: Page one was titled 'Why Our Store Feels Like Home.'
necessarily:2.line: 'More stores don't *necessarily* mean fewer friends here.'

sentences.en: I told Tang I was worried the new branch would take all our regular customers.
sentences.cn: 我跟阿糖说我担心新店会抢走我们的老顾客。

sentences.en: Tang shrugged.
sentences.cn: 阿糖耸了耸肩。

sentences.en: 'New competition doesn't *necessarily* mean we lose.
It means we have to give people a reason to stay.'
sentences.cn: 这意味着我们得给人们留下来的理由。

sentences.en: Then Tang pulled out a small notebook filled with ideas and dropped it on the counter.
sentences.cn: 然后阿糖拿出一个装满了想法的小笔记本，扔在了柜台上。

psychologist:2.en: A quiet regular who always bought warm milk left a business card by the register. It read: 'Certified *psychologist* — free first talk, any time.' On the back, in small neat writing: 'You looked like you needed to know that option existed.' I did not remember making any expression at all.
psychologist:2.cnHint: 一位常客在收银台留下了一张名片，原来她是一位____，还在背面写了一句贴心的话。
psychologist:2.hook: She was already gone before I could look up.
psychologist:2.line: 'A *psychologist* once told me: small stores heal people too.'

sentences.en: A quiet regular who always bought warm milk left a business card by the register.
sentences.cn: 一个总是买温牛奶的安静老顾客在收银机旁留下了一张名片。

sentences.en: It read: 'Certified *psychologist* — free first talk, any time.'
On the back, in small neat writing: 'You looked like you needed to know that option existed.'
sentences.cn: 背面用小小的整齐字迹写着："你看起来像是需要知道这个选项存在。"

sentences.en: I did not remember making any expression at all.
sentences.cn: 我根本不记得自己做过什么表情。

pursue:2.en: A folded note slipped under the back door read: 'Do not *pursue* the new branch plan. Some corners are not yours to take.' I showed the Manager. He read it twice, then tucked it into his shirt pocket without a word.
pursue:2.cnHint: 一张纸条悄悄塞进后门，警告店长不要____开分店的计划。
pursue:2.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like Lin's.
pursue:2.line: 'I will *pursue* this plan no matter what note appears.'

sentences.en: A folded note slipped under the back door read: 'Do not *pursue* the new branch plan.
Some corners are not yours to take.'
sentences.cn: 有人会采取一些不属于你的角落。

sentences.en: I showed the Manager.
sentences.cn: 我把纸条拿给了店长看。

sentences.en: He read it twice, then tucked it into his shirt pocket without a word.
sentences.cn: 他读了两遍，然后没说一句话就把它塞进了衬衫口袋。

site:2.en: The Manager unrolled a large paper map on the counter and tapped a red circle near the old library. 'This is the *site* for the new branch,' he said. I leaned in and noticed a small ink mark already on that spot, as if someone had circled it before him.
site:2.cnHint: 店长在地图上指出新分店的____，但那个地点似乎早有人做过标记。
site:2.hook: Who had seen this map before the Manager?
site:2.line: 'The *site* near the library was chosen three weeks ago.'

sentences.en: The Manager unrolled a large paper map on the counter and tapped a red circle near the old library.
sentences.cn: 店长在柜台上展开了一张大地图，敲了敲靠近老图书馆的一个红圈。

sentences.en: 'This is the *site* for the new branch,' he said.
I leaned in and noticed a small ink mark already on that spot, as if someone had circled it before him.
sentences.cn: 我靠近一看，发现那个位置上已经有一个小墨点了，好像有人早就在那儿圈过了。

absorb:2.en: The Manager dropped a thick folder of numbers on my desk. 'Read everything tonight,' he said. 'The new branch will *absorb* all the stock from this store first.' I stared at the pages. One column of figures had been circled in red pen — by someone else, long before tonight.
absorb:2.cnHint: 店长让我读一份文件，说新分店会____本店的全部库存，但文件上已有人做了标记。
absorb:2.hook: The red ink was still faintly wet.
absorb:2.line: 'The new branch will *absorb* our stock within a week.'

sentences.en: The Manager dropped a thick folder of numbers on my desk.
sentences.cn: 店长把厚厚一沓数字材料扔在我桌子上。

sentences.en: 'Read everything tonight,' he said.
sentences.cn: "今晚把这些全读了，"他说。

sentences.en: 'The new branch will *absorb* all the stock from this store first.'
I stared at the pages.
sentences.cn: 我盯着这些页面。

sentences.en: One column of figures had been circled in red pen — by someone else, long before tonight.
sentences.cn: 其中一列数字被红笔圈了起来——是别人很久以前圈的，不是今晚。

advance:2.en: Tang handed me a small envelope before my shift ended. 'The Manager left this — an *advance* on next month's pay, to say thank you,' she whispered. Inside were six crisp notes. Tucked beneath them was a tiny slip of paper that had nothing to do with money.
advance:2.cnHint: 唐交给我一个信封，说是薪水____，但信封里还藏着一张奇怪的纸条。
advance:2.hook: The slip read: 'Leave before the branch opens.'
advance:2.line: 'He asked me to give you this *advance* quietly, not at the register.'

sentences.en: Tang handed me a small envelope before my shift ended.
sentences.cn: 我的班快结束时，阿糖递给我一个小信封。

sentences.en: 'The Manager left this — an *advance* on next month's pay, to say thank you,' she whispered.
Inside were six crisp notes.
sentences.cn: 里面装着六张崭新的纸币。

sentences.en: Tucked beneath them was a tiny slip of paper that had nothing to do with money.
sentences.cn: 压在下面的是一张小纸条，和钱一点关系都没有。

capable:2.en: Lin walked in just after two in the morning and stood at the magazine shelf for a long time. 'You seem *capable*,' she said at last, not quite looking at me. 'Smart enough to know when a job is worth keeping.' She bought nothing and left before I could reply.
capable:2.cnHint: 林深夜走进店里，夸我____，话里似乎藏着某种警告。
capable:2.hook: Her smile never reached her eyes.
capable:2.line: 'A *capable* clerk always knows which side to stand on.'

sentences.en: Lin walked in just after two in the morning and stood at the magazine shelf for a long time.
sentences.cn: 凌晨刚过两点，隔壁咖啡店的林走了进来，在杂志架前站了很久。

sentences.en: 'You seem *capable*,' she said at last, not quite looking at me.
'Smart enough to know when a job is worth keeping.'
sentences.cn: "聪明人才知道什么工作值得守住。"

sentences.en: She bought nothing and left before I could reply.
sentences.cn: 她什么也没买，在我来得及回答前就走了。

dollar:2.en: Counting the till at midnight, I found one extra *dollar* coin tucked behind the receipt roll. Taped to it was a note in tiny letters: 'For your bus fare out of here.' Tang saw my face and came over. She turned the coin in her fingers and went very quiet.
dollar:2.cnHint: 我在收银机里发现一枚多出来的____硬币，上面贴着一张神秘字条。
dollar:2.hook: Tang said she had found the same coin last week.
dollar:2.line: 'One *dollar* and a warning — someone wants you gone.'

sentences.en: Counting the till at midnight, I found one extra *dollar* coin tucked behind the receipt roll.
Taped to it was a note in tiny letters: 'For your bus fare out of here.'
sentences.cn: 贴在上面的纸条用很小的字写着："给你坐公交滚蛋的车费。"

sentences.en: Tang saw my face and came over.
sentences.cn: 阿糖看到我的表情走了过来。

sentences.en: She turned the coin in her fingers and went very quiet.
sentences.cn: 她在手指间转动那枚硬币，忽然没出了声。

double:2.en: The delivery invoice showed *double* the usual order of bottled water — enough to fill the new branch on opening day. But the delivery address written at the bottom was not the new branch. It was somewhere I had never heard of. I photographed it quickly with my phone.
double:2.cnHint: 送货单上的瓶装水数量是平时的____，但收货地址却让人看不懂。
double:2.hook: The address led to a building that closed two years ago.
double:2.line: 'Why would anyone order *double* stock for a place that empty?'

sentences.en: The delivery invoice showed *double* the usual order of bottled water — enough to fill the new branch on opening day.
But the delivery address written at the bottom was not the new branch.
sentences.cn: 但填在下面的收货地址不是新店。

sentences.en: It was somewhere I had never heard of.
sentences.cn: 是个我从没听说过的地方。

sentences.en: I photographed it quickly with my phone.
sentences.cn: 我用手机快速拍了下来。

federal:2.en: A man in a plain grey jacket came in near dawn and bought only a pen. He left a business card on the counter by accident — or maybe on purpose. It read: *Federal* Trade Office, Regional Review. The Manager arrived an hour later and went pale when I showed it to him.
federal:2.cnHint: 一位神秘男子留下一张____贸易办公室的名片，店长看到后脸色大变。
federal:2.hook: The Manager made a phone call he did not want me to hear.
federal:2.line: 'A *federal* review now — right when we plan to expand?'

sentences.en: A man in a plain grey jacket came in near dawn and bought only a pen.
sentences.cn: 天快亮的时候，一个穿着素灰色夹克的男人进来，只买了一支笔。

sentences.en: He left a business card on the counter by accident — or maybe on purpose.
sentences.cn: 他不小心——或者是故意——在柜台留下了一张名片。

sentences.en: It read: *Federal* Trade Office, Regional Review.
The Manager arrived an hour later and went pale when I showed it to him.
sentences.cn: 店长一小时后到店，看到我递给他的名片时脸色苍白。

insist:2.en: A note arrived from the Manager: the new branch would open in two weeks. Lin dropped by the store to read it over my shoulder and *insist* that the corner location was wrong. 'Customers walk from the east,' she said, tapping the map firmly with one finger.
insist:2.cnHint: 林来店里看通知，____说新分店的位置选错了。
insist:2.hook: But the Manager had already signed the lease.
insist:2.line: 'I *insist* that corner will lose us every passing customer.'

sentences.en: A note arrived from the Manager: the new branch would open in two weeks.
sentences.cn: 店长发来纸条：新店两周后开业。

sentences.en: Lin dropped by the store to read it over my shoulder and *insist* that the corner location was wrong.

sentences.en: Old notes and hand-drawn maps *gather* in neat piles on the desk, each one labelled with a different street corner.
'I'm planning something big,' he says, smoothing a fold in his coat.
sentences.cn: "我在计划什么大的，"他说着，整理了一下衣服上的褶皱。

sentences.en: I count seven maps.
sentences.cn: 我数了数，七张地图。

sentences.en: Seven corners.
sentences.cn: 七个角落。

sentences.en: Our store only has one.
sentences.cn: 我们的店只有一个。

imagine:2.en: A folded note falls out of a supply box from the warehouse. It reads: 'Whoever finds this — good luck with the night shift.' I *imagine* the person who wrote it: tired, a little lonely, maybe smiling. Tang sees me holding it and laughs. 'That was me. Three years ago.'
imagine:2.cnHint: 店员在货箱里发现一张留言条，开始____留下纸条的人是谁，结果出乎意料。
imagine:2.hook: Tang's smile faded just a little too quickly.
imagine:2.line: 'Did you ever *imagine* someone would actually find it?' I asked.

sentences.en: A folded note falls out of a supply box from the warehouse.
sentences.cn: 一张折好的纸条从仓库里的供货箱掉了出来。

sentences.en: It reads: 'Whoever finds this — good luck with the night shift.'
sentences.cn: 上面写着："谁捡到这个——祝你夜班好运。"

sentences.en: I *imagine* the person who wrote it: tired, a little lonely, maybe smiling.
Tang sees me holding it and laughs.
sentences.cn: 阿糖看我拿着它，笑了。

sentences.en: 'That was me.
sentences.cn: "那是我写的。

sentences.en: Three years ago.'
sentences.cn: 三年前。"

instance:2.en: Lin slides a printed chart under our door. It lists every price difference between their store and ours, item by item. The Manager reads it slowly, then nods. 'This is a useful *instance* of knowing your competition,' he says, almost admiringly. He pins it to the wall next to our own price list.
instance:2.cnHint: 竞争对手把一份比价表塞进门缝，店长把它当作一个____贴在墙上。
instance:2.hook: By morning, three of our prices had quietly changed.
instance:2.line: 'This is a perfect *instance* of why we must pay attention,' the Manager said.

sentences.en: Lin slides a printed chart under our door.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林从门下塞进来一张打印的表格。

sentences.en: It lists every price difference between their store and ours, item by item.
sentences.cn: 上面逐项列出了他们店和我们店之间的每一个价格差。

sentences.en: The Manager reads it slowly, then nods.
sentences.cn: 店长慢慢读着，然后点了点头。

sentences.en: 'This is a useful *instance* of knowing your competition,' he says, almost admiringly.
He pins it to the wall next to our own price list.
sentences.cn: 他把它钉在了我们自己的价目表旁边。

numerous:2.en: I open the lost-and-found box under the counter for the first time. There are *numerous* small items inside: keys, a single earring, a folded umbrella, a child's drawing of a cat. Each one is a little mystery. The Manager says nobody has ever come back for the drawing. That feels wrong.
numerous:2.cnHint: 店员第一次打开失物招领箱，发现里面有____件无人认领的小物品。
numerous:2.hook: The cat in the drawing was wearing a tiny shop apron.
numerous:2.line: 'There are *numerous* stories in that box,' Tang said softly.

sentences.en: I open the lost-and-found box under the counter for the first time.
sentences.cn: 我打开了柜台下那个失物招领箱，这还是第一次。

sentences.en: There are *numerous* small items inside: keys, a single earring, a folded umbrella, a child's drawing of a cat.
Each one is a little mystery.
sentences.cn: 每一件都是个小谜团。

sentences.en: The Manager says nobody has ever come back for the drawing.
sentences.cn: 店长说从来没人来领过那张画。

sentences.en: That feels wrong.
sentences.cn: 这感觉不太对。

puzzle:2.en: A regular customer leaves exact change every night — always correct, always silent — but tonight the coins add up to three cents more than the total. I check twice. Tang shrugs. The Manager just smiles. This small *puzzle* stays with me until sunrise, turning over and over like a coin itself.
puzzle:2.cnHint: 一位老顾客今晚多付了三分钱，这个小小的____让店员整晚都在想。
puzzle:2.hook: The same customer came back at 5 a.m. and said nothing.
puzzle:2.line: 'Every regular here is a *puzzle* you slowly solve,' the Manager told me.

sentences.en: A regular customer leaves exact change every night — always correct, always silent — but tonight the coins add up to three cents more than the total.
sentences.cn: 一个常客每晚付的都是整钱——总是对得上，总是无声的——但今晚硬币加起来比总价多了三分钱。

sentences.en: I check twice.
sentences.cn: 我检查了两遍。

sentences.en: Tang shrugs.
sentences.cn: 阿糖耸了耸肩。

sentences.en: The Manager just smiles.
sentences.cn: 店长只是笑了。

sentences.en: This small *puzzle* stays with me until sunrise, turning over and over like a coin itself.

remind:2.en: Tang sticks a small note to the register: 'Check the back fridge at 2 a.m.' I almost miss it. The fridge holds one box of rice pudding, nearly out of date, marked with a smiley face. A note inside says: 'For the night clerk.' These little things *remind* me that someone cared about this job before me.
remind:2.cnHint: 阿糖贴的一张便条____店员去查冰箱，里面有一份留给夜班的惊喜。
remind:2.hook: The handwriting on the smiley face matched the warehouse note exactly.
remind:2.line: 'I always leave a note to *remind* the next person they matter,' Tang said.

sentences.en: Tang sticks a small note to the register: 'Check the back fridge at 2 a.m.'
sentences.cn: 阿糖在收银机上贴了张小纸条："凌晨两点检查后面的冰箱。"

sentences.en: I almost miss it.
sentences.cn: 我差点没看到。

sentences.en: The fridge holds one box of rice pudding, nearly out of date, marked with a smiley face.
sentences.cn: 冰箱里放着一盒米布丁，快过期了，上面画了个笑脸。

sentences.en: A note inside says: 'For the night clerk.'
sentences.cn: 里面的纸条写着："给夜班的店员。"

sentences.en: These little things *remind* me that someone cared about this job before me.

truly:2.en: The Manager hands me a spare key at the end of my first week. It is old and a little bent. 'This store is *truly* yours now, on the night shift,' he says. It sounds simple. But the weight of the key in my hand feels like something much larger than metal. Tang gives me a small nod from the snack aisle.
truly:2.cnHint: 第一周结束时，店长把备用钥匙交给店员，说这家店____属于他了。
truly:2.hook: The key had two faint scratches on it — like a tally.
truly:2.line: 'You are *truly* part of this place now,' the Manager said, and meant it.

sentences.en: The Manager hands me a spare key at the end of my first week.
sentences.cn: 工作的第一周快结束时，店长把一把备用钥匙递给我。

sentences.en: It is old and a little bent.
sentences.cn: 它很旧，微微弯曲。

sentences.en: 'This store is *truly* yours now, on the night shift,' he says.
It sounds simple.
sentences.cn: 听起来很简单。

sentences.en: But the weight of the key in my hand feels like something much larger than metal.
sentences.cn: 但那把钥匙在我手心的重量，感觉远超一块金属该有的分量。

sentences.en: Tang gives me a small nod from the snack aisle.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林从零食货架那边朝我轻轻点了下头。

valuable:2.en: Lin comes in just before dawn — not as a rival, just as a customer. They buy a hot drink and leave a small envelope on the counter. Inside is a handwritten list of the three nearest bus stops and their schedules. 'Foot traffic timing,' Tang whispers. 'That is *valuable*.' I agree. It is also surprisingly kind.
valuable:2.cnHint: 竞争对手来买东西，悄悄留下一份____的公交时刻表，让人意外地感到温暖。
valuable:2.hook: Lin paused at the door and looked back, just once.
valuable:2.line: 'Good information is always *valuable*, even between rivals,' Lin said.

sentences.en: Lin comes in just before dawn — not as a rival, just as a customer.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在天亮前不久走进来——不是作为竞争对手，只是作为一个顾客。

sentences.en: They buy a hot drink and leave a small envelope on the counter.
sentences.cn: 他们买了一杯热饮，在柜台上留下了一个小信封。

sentences.en: Inside is a handwritten list of the three nearest bus stops and their schedules.
sentences.cn: 里面是手写的最近三个公交站点和它们的班次表。

sentences.en: 'Foot traffic timing,' Tang whispers.
sentences.cn: "客流高峰时段，"阿糖低声说。

sentences.en: 'That is *valuable*.'
I agree.
sentences.cn: 我同意。

sentences.en: It is also surprisingly kind.
sentences.cn: 这也出乎意料地善良。

belong:2.en: While restocking shelves at two in the morning, I found a small notebook behind the instant-noodle boxes. The cover had no name. I flipped through it and saw careful columns of numbers — daily sales figures, sketched floor plans, and one circled question: 'Does this corner *belong* to us, or to them?' I quietly put it back.
belong:2.cnHint: 我在货架后发现一本无名笔记本，里面记满数字和一个关于这家店____给谁的问题。
belong:2.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like the Manager's.
belong:2.line: 'This store *belongs* to the whole street, not just one person.'

sentences.en: While restocking shelves at two in the morning, I found a small notebook behind the instant-noodle boxes.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点补货时，我在速冻面条纸箱后面发现了一本小笔记本。

sentences.en: The cover had no name.
sentences.cn: 封面上没有名字。

sentences.en: I flipped through it and saw careful columns of numbers — daily sales figures, sketched floor plans, and one circled question: 'Does this corner *belong* to us, or to them?'
I quietly put it back.
sentences.cn: 我没出声地把它放了回去。

beneficial:2.en: Tang slid a printed chart across the counter during our break. It showed that staying open until six in the morning was *beneficial* to weekly profits by nearly thirty percent. She tapped the page twice, eyebrows raised, clearly proud. I nodded slowly. The Manager had not seen this report yet — and Tang seemed fine keeping it that way.
beneficial:2.cnHint: 阿糖拿出一份图表，证明延长营业时间对利润____，但她似乎不急着让店长看到。
beneficial:2.hook: She folded the chart and slipped it into her own bag.
beneficial:2.line: 'More hours open is *beneficial* — trust the numbers.'

sentences.en: Tang slid a printed chart across the counter during our break.
sentences.cn: 休息时，阿糖把一张打印好的图表推过柜台。

sentences.en: It showed that staying open until six in the morning was *beneficial* to weekly profits by nearly thirty percent.
She tapped the page twice, eyebrows raised, clearly proud.
sentences.cn: 她在纸上敲了两下，眉毛挑起，看起来很骄傲。

sentences.en: I nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 我缓缓点了点头。

sentences.en: The Manager had not seen this report yet — and Tang seemed fine keeping it that way.
sentences.cn: 店长还没看过这份报告——阿糖似乎很乐意这样瞒着他。

characteristic:2.en: Lin walked in just before dawn carrying a tray of small sample cups. That confident half-smile was a *characteristic* I had already learned to notice. She set the tray on the counter without asking, poured one cup for me, and said nothing. The drink was good — almost exactly like the one we sold in aisle three.
characteristic:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带着试喝样品走进来，那个自信的笑容是她____的标志，饮料的口味让我有点担心。
characteristic:2.hook: Our aisle-three supplier called ten minutes later.
characteristic:2.line: 'That calm look is her most dangerous *characteristic*.'

sentences.en: Lin walked in just before dawn carrying a tray of small sample cups.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在天亮前走了进来，拿着一盘小试喝杯。

sentences.en: That confident half-smile was a *characteristic* I had already learned to notice.
She set the tray on the counter without asking, poured one cup for me, and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 她没问一声就把盘子放在了柜台上，给我倒了一杯，什么都没说。

sentences.en: The drink was good — almost exactly like the one we sold in aisle three.
sentences.cn: 咖啡很不错——几乎和我们第三货架卖的那种一模一样。

director:2.en: A woman in a neat grey coat came in at midnight and asked for three bottles of water and a bag of salted nuts. She paid, then paused. 'Tell your Manager,' she said quietly, 'that the *director* of the new branch project has already chosen this block.' She left before I could ask a single question.
director:2.cnHint: 一位神秘女士深夜来买东西，临走时说新分店项目的____已经看中了这条街。
director:2.hook: Her business card said only a room number, nothing else.

sentences.en: A woman in a neat grey coat came in at midnight and asked for three bottles of water and a bag of salted nuts.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着整洁灰色大衣的女人在午夜走了进来，要了三瓶水和一袋咸坚果。

sentences.en: She paid, then paused.
sentences.cn: 她付了钱，然后停顿了一下。

sentences.en: 'Tell your Manager,' she said quietly, 'that the *director* of the new branch project has already chosen this block.'
She left before I could ask a single question.
sentences.cn: 她在我还没来得及问任何问题前就离开了。

emerge:2.en: I was checking the stock room when I heard the back door creak. A hand, then a shoulder, then the whole Manager *emerged* from behind a tower of boxed drinks. He was holding a rolled-up paper — building plans, by the look of it — and he froze when he saw me standing there with a clipboard.
emerge:2.cnHint: 店长从仓库的饮料箱后____出来，手里拿着一张像是建筑图纸的卷轴。
emerge:2.hook: He smiled, but the paper disappeared behind his back.
emerge:2.line: 'Good — you *emerge* from the back just in time.'

sentences.en: I was checking the stock room when I heard the back door creak.
sentences.cn: 我在检查库房时听到后门吱呀一声打开了。

sentences.en: A hand, then a shoulder, then the whole Manager *emerged* from behind a tower of boxed drinks.
He was holding a rolled-up paper — building plans, by the look of it — and he froze when he saw me standing there with a clipboard.
sentences.cn: 他拿着一卷纸——看起来是建筑图纸——看到我站在那儿拿着夹板时整个人僵住了。

exact:2.en: Tang was on the phone near the freezer aisle when I passed. She was reading figures aloud in a low voice. 'The *exact* address — yes, corner of Mei Road and Qing Street, ground floor.' She noticed me, ended the call fast, and began straightening yoghurt cups that were already perfectly straight.
exact:2.cnHint: 阿糖在电话里报出了一个____地址，看见我后迅速挂断并假装整理货架。
exact:2.hook: That address was the same as ours.

sentences.en: Tang was on the phone near the freezer aisle when I passed.
sentences.cn: 我经过冷柜货架时，阿糖正在打电话。

sentences.en: She was reading figures aloud in a low voice.
sentences.cn: 她用低沉的声音朗读着数字。

sentences.en: 'The *exact* address — yes, corner of Mei Road and Qing Street, ground floor.'
She noticed me, ended the call fast, and began straightening yoghurt cups that were already perfectly straight.
sentences.cn: 她注意到我，很快挂了电话，开始整理已经整整齐齐的酸奶杯。

guest:2.en: A quiet man came in every night at eleven and bought one green tea. He never spoke. Tonight he left a folded note on the counter beside his coins. It read: 'Thank you for the light.' I looked up, but he was already gone. The Manager later told me the man was a *guest* speaker at the college nearby, far from home.
guest:2.cnHint: 一位每晚来买绿茶的沉默男士留下了一张便条，店长说他是附近高校的____，离家很远。
guest:2.hook: The note had a second line I had not noticed before.
guest:2.line: 'Every *guest* carries a story we have not heard yet.'

sentences.en: A quiet man came in every night at eleven and bought one green tea.
sentences.cn: 一个安静的男人每晚十一点准时来买一杯绿茶。

sentences.en: He never spoke.
sentences.cn: 他从不说话。

sentences.en: Tonight he left a folded note on the counter beside his coins.
sentences.cn: 今晚他在柜台上的硬币旁边留了一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: It read: 'Thank you for the light.'
sentences.cn: 纸条上写着："感谢你的灯光。"

sentences.en: I looked up, but he was already gone.
sentences.cn: 我抬起头，但他已经走了。

sentences.en: The Manager later told me the man was a *guest* speaker at the college nearby, far from home.

massive:2.en: The delivery arrived at three in the morning — not the usual two trolleys, but a *massive* stack that filled the entire doorway and spilled onto the pavement outside. The driver shrugged and handed me a slip. The order was three times the normal size. At the top, in red ink, someone had written 'new branch — trial stock.'
massive:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点来了一批____的货物，送货单上用红笔写着"新分店——试销库存"。
massive:2.hook: No one had told me we were opening a second store.
massive:2.line: 'That *massive* order came from someone above the Manager.'

sentences.en: The delivery arrived at three in the morning — not the usual two trolleys, but a *massive* stack that filled the entire doorway and spilled onto the pavement outside.
The driver shrugged and handed me a slip.
sentences.cn: 司机耸了耸肩，递给我一张单据。

sentences.en: The order was three times the normal size.
sentences.cn: 订单是平时的三倍。

sentences.en: At the top, in red ink, someone had written 'new branch — trial stock.'
sentences.cn: 最上面用红墨水写着"新店试用库存"。

mix:2.en: Behind the store, I found a handwritten note taped to the back door. It listed a strange *mix* of items: three rice balls, one energy drink, and a folded map of the business district. Someone had planned something carefully — and left the note for whoever opened up that morning.
mix:2.cnHint: 我在后门发现一张字条，上面列着一份奇怪的____。
mix:2.hook: The handwriting matched no one I had ever met.
mix:2.line: 'It's a *mix* of things I need before the new branch opens,' Lin said quietly.

sentences.en: Behind the store, I found a handwritten note taped to the back door.
sentences.cn: 在店铺后面，我发现后门上贴着一张手写纸条。

sentences.en: It listed a strange *mix* of items: three rice balls, one energy drink, and a folded map of the business district.
Someone had planned something carefully — and left the note for whoever opened up that morning.
sentences.cn: 有人精心计划了什么——并给那天早上来开门的人留下了纸条。

necessity:2.en: The Manager spread blueprints across the counter at midnight. 'A second freezer is a *necessity*,' he said, tapping the paper. 'The new branch runs twice the volume.' I nodded, pretending I understood supply chains, while secretly hoping someone would bring me a warm drink soon.
necessity:2.cnHint: 店长说明了开分店时增加冷冻柜的____。
necessity:2.hook: Then he pointed to a name on the blueprint I did not recognise.
necessity:2.line: 'Trust me, a second freezer is a *necessity* for the new place,' the Manager said firmly.

sentences.en: The Manager spread blueprints across the counter at midnight.
sentences.cn: 店长在午夜时把建筑图纸铺在柜台上。

sentences.en: 'A second freezer is a *necessity*,' he said, tapping the paper.
'The new branch runs twice the volume.'
sentences.cn: "新店的营业额是这家的两倍。"

sentences.en: I nodded, pretending I understood supply chains, while secretly hoping someone would bring me a warm drink soon.
sentences.cn: 我点了点头，假装懂什么供应链，心里却暗暗希望有人能很快给我端来一杯热饮。

stuff:2.en: Tang arrived before sunrise dragging a heavy box. 'New branch *stuff*,' she said, dropping it with a loud thud. Inside were price-tag guns, spare shelf brackets, and a thick folder of forms. She looked at me, then at the box, and said nothing more for a very long time.
stuff:2.cnHint: 唐搬来了一箱开分店用的____。
stuff:2.hook: One folder at the bottom was sealed with red tape.
stuff:2.line: 'All this *stuff* has to reach the new branch by Friday,' Tang said, stretching her back.

sentences.en: Tang arrived before sunrise dragging a heavy box.
sentences.cn: 阿糖天没亮就拖着一个沉重的纸箱来了。

sentences.en: 'New branch *stuff*,' she said, dropping it with a loud thud.

sentences.cn: 里面装着打价签的枪、备用的架子夹子，还有一厚叠表格。

sentences.en: She looked at me, then at the box, and said nothing more for a very long time.
sentences.cn: 她看看我，又看看那个箱子，很久都没再说什么。

translate:2.en: Lin slid a printed page across the counter. 'Can this *translate* into a real advantage for us?' The page showed foot-traffic numbers for the new corner location. I studied the rows of figures, wondering if numbers this clean ever told the whole truth about a neighbourhood.
translate:2.cnHint: 林想知道这些数据能否____成真正的竞争优势。
translate:2.hook: The address on the page was only two streets from here.
translate:2.line: 'Can these numbers *translate* into something useful for the opening?' Lin asked.

sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林把打印好的一页纸推过柜台。

sentences.en: 'Can this *translate* into a real advantage for us?'
The page showed foot-traffic numbers for the new corner location.
sentences.cn: 纸上显示的是新店角落位置的客流量数字。

sentences.cn: 我盯着那一行行数字，琢磨这么整洁的数据有没有可能说出一个街区的全部真相。

wander:2.en: My break was fifteen minutes, so I let myself *wander* one block down to see the new branch site. A bare shopfront, a paper sign, dusty glass. It looked nothing like a store yet. I pressed my face to the window and thought: three weeks is not very long at all.
wander:2.cnHint: 我趁休息时间____到了分店的选址处。
wander:2.hook: A light was on inside, and somebody was already moving around.
wander:2.line: 'Don't *wander* too far — the Manager wants us back by two,' Tang called after me.

sentences.en: My break was fifteen minutes, so I let myself *wander* one block down to see the new branch site.
A bare shopfront, a paper sign, dusty glass.
sentences.cn: 一间空荡荡的店铺，一张纸质招牌，尘封的玻璃。

sentences.en: It looked nothing like a store yet.
sentences.cn: 看起来根本不像一家店。

sentences.en: I pressed my face to the window and thought: three weeks is not very long at all.
sentences.cn: 我把脸贴在窗户上想，三个礼拜其实真的不长啊。

warn:2.en: Tang pulled me aside near the drinks fridge. 'I have to *warn* you,' she whispered, 'the Manager plans to announce the branch manager tomorrow morning.' sentences.cn: 店长从后面的架子上拉出了一个落满灰尘的纸箱。

sentences.en: Inside was an old television *remote* with a sticky note attached: 'Works only on Channel 7.
Do not ask why.'
sentences.cn: 别问为什么。

sentences.en: Nobody could find the television it belonged to.
sentences.cn: 没人找到那台电视遥控器属于哪台电视。

sentences.en: The Manager placed it carefully back in the box and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 店长小心翼翼地把它放回纸箱里，什么都没说。

zoo:2.en: A woman came in at midnight carrying a canvas tote printed with giraffes. She bought a banana and handed me a loyalty card already stamped nine times. 'One more and I get a free drink,' she said. 'I work at the *zoo*. Nights are longer when the animals dream loud.'
zoo:2.cnHint: 一位动物园工作人员深夜来买香蕉，她的集点卡还差一格就满了。
zoo:2.hook: Her tenth stamp was dated the same night the store's fish tank went missing.
zoo:2.line: 'The *zoo* at 3 a.m. is quieter than you would think,' she said.

sentences.en: A woman came in at midnight carrying a canvas tote printed with giraffes.
sentences.cn: 一个女人在午夜时分走了进来，提着一个印着长颈鹿的帆布袋。

sentences.en: She bought a banana and handed me a loyalty card already stamped nine times.
sentences.cn: 她买了一根香蕉，递给我一张已经盖了九个章的会员卡。

sentences.en: 'One more and I get a free drink,' she said.
sentences.cn: "再来一个就能换免费饮料了，"她说。

sentences.en: 'I work at the *zoo*.
Nights are longer when the animals dream loud.'
sentences.cn: 夜晚很长，动物们梦得很响。

card:2.en: Tucked under the windscreen wiper of a bicycle outside was a small *card* with our store's address printed on it, but the store had not made any such cards. The Manager turned it over twice, said 'hm,' and pinned it to the board above the register without another word.
card:2.cnHint: 店外自行车上夹着一张印有本店地址的卡片，但我们从未印过这种卡。
card:2.hook: By morning, three more identical cards had appeared on three more bicycles.
card:2.line: 'Whoever printed this *card* knows our address better than we do,' said Lin.

sentences.en: Tucked under the windscreen wiper of a bicycle outside was a small *card* with our store's address printed on it, but the store had not made any such cards.
The Manager turned it over twice, said 'hm,' and pinned it to the board above the register without another word.
sentences.cn: 店长翻了两遍那张卡片，说了句"嗯"，然后就把它钉在收银机上方的公告栏上，一句话都没再说。

gene:2.en: A biology student spread her notes across the corner table for two hours. Her textbook lay open to a chapter on inheritance. 'This one *gene*,' she told me when I brought her a free coffee, 'decides whether you can smell rain before it falls.' Outside, it began to rain.
gene:2.cnHint: 一个生物系学生在角落里温书，告诉我某个基因能决定一个人是否能预感到下雨。
gene:2.hook: She had already packed her umbrella before the first drop hit the window.
gene:2.line: 'One *gene* is a tiny thing to carry so much weather in,' she said.

sentences.en: A biology student spread her notes across the corner table for two hours.
sentences.cn: 一个生物学学生在角落里的两人桌上摊开了她的笔记，呆了两个小时。

sentences.en: Her textbook lay open to a chapter on inheritance.
sentences.cn: 她的教科书翻到了遗传学的一章。

sentences.en: 'This one *gene*,' she told me when I brought her a free coffee, 'decides whether you can smell rain before it falls.'
Outside, it began to rain.
sentences.cn: 外面开始下雨了。

childhood:2.en: The Manager pulled a small photo from the back of the till. It showed two boys sharing a single ice cream outside a tiny shop. 'This corner,' he said softly, 'is where I spent my *childhood*.' He pinned the photo above the new store plan on the wall.
childhood:2.cnHint: 店长在收银台后面找到一张旧照片，指着它说这条街是他____度过的地方。
childhood:2.hook: The second boy in the photo looked a lot like Lin.
childhood:2.line: 'My *childhood* dream was always to run a shop on this exact corner.'

sentences.en: The Manager pulled a small photo from the back of the till.
sentences.cn: 店长从收银机后面拽出了一张小照片。

sentences.en: It showed two boys sharing a single ice cream outside a tiny shop.
sentences.cn: 照片上两个男孩在一家小店外面共享一个冰淇淋。

sentences.en: 'This corner,' he said softly, 'is where I spent my *childhood*.'
He pinned the photo above the new store plan on the wall.
sentences.cn: 他把照片钉在了墙上新的店铺平面图上方。

equal:2.en: Tang lined up two stacks of new product brochures on the counter, one for each proposed branch location. She measured them twice with a ruler. 'Both sites get *equal* attention,' she said firmly, sliding one stack to me. 'Fair is the only way to choose.'
equal:2.cnHint: 阿糖把两个候选分店地址的宣传册摆得整整齐齐，坚持两边要____对待。
equal:2.hook: But one stack had a handwritten note hidden inside.
equal:2.line: 'Every branch deserves *equal* resources, or the whole plan falls apart.'

sentences.en: Tang lined up two stacks of new product brochures on the counter, one for each proposed branch location.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在柜台上排列了两摞新产品手册，每个拟议分店位置一摞。

sentences.en: She measured them twice with a ruler.
sentences.cn: 她用尺子量了两遍。

sentences.en: 'Both sites get *equal* attention,' she said firmly, sliding one stack to me.
'Fair is the only way to choose.'
sentences.cn: 她说，公平是唯一的选择方式。

inspire:2.en: A retired teacher stopped in for warm milk at midnight. She noticed our hand-drawn map of the new branch on the wall and smiled. 'A neighbourhood shop *inspired* me to read as a child,' she said. 'Keep that warmth in the new place.' She left a small bookmarked card on the counter.
inspire:2.cnHint: 一位退休老师深夜来买热牛奶，看着分店地图说小小的街角商店曾____了她。
inspire:2.hook: The card had an address on the back — the same street as Branch Two.
inspire:2.line: 'Places like this *inspire* people more than you ever know.'

sentences.en: A retired teacher stopped in for warm milk at midnight.
sentences.cn: 一位退休教师在午夜时分进来要了杯温牛奶。

sentences.en: She noticed our hand-drawn map of the new branch on the wall and smiled.
sentences.cn: 她注意到我们挂在墙上的新分店手绘地图，露出了笑容。

sentences.en: 'A neighbourhood shop *inspired* me to read as a child,' she said.
'Keep that warmth in the new place.'
sentences.cn: 她说，要在新店保持那份温暖。

sentences.en: She left a small bookmarked card on the counter.
sentences.cn: 她在柜台上留下了一张贴着书签的卡片。

narrow:2.en: The Manager spread the floor plan of the second branch across the counter after closing. I leaned in. The entrance passage looked tight. 'That *narrow* corridor worries me,' I said. 'Deliveries will block it every morning.' He tapped the paper and said nothing, staring at it for a long time.
narrow:2.cnHint: 我和店长一起看分店平面图，我指出入口____的走廊可能造成麻烦。
narrow:2.hook: He finally circled the corridor in red and wrote one word: 'Lin.'
narrow:2.line: 'A *narrow* entrance might turn customers away before they even get inside.'

sentences.cn: 关店后，店长把第二家分店的平面图铺在柜台上。

sentences.cn: 入口通道看起来很狭窄。

sentences.en: 'That *narrow* corridor worries me,' I said.
'Deliveries will block it every morning.'
sentences.cn: 每天早上送货都会堵住它。

sentences.en: He tapped the paper and said nothing, staring at it for a long time.
sentences.cn: 他敲了敲纸，什么都没说，盯着它看了很久。

quantity:2.en: A delivery driver dropped off sample goods for the new branch and left a form on the counter. Tang read it and frowned. 'The *quantity* here is half what we ordered,' she said, underlining a number. 'We cannot open a second store with stock this thin.' She reached for her phone.
quantity:2.cnHint: 送货司机送来样品，阿糖发现单据上的____只有订单的一半，皱起了眉头。
quantity:2.hook: The number on the form matched a cancelled order from three weeks ago.
quantity:2.line: 'Check the *quantity* again — someone changed this after we signed.'

sentences.en: A delivery driver dropped off sample goods for the new branch and left a form on the counter.
sentences.cn: 一个送货司机给新分店送了样品，在柜台上留下了一份表格。

sentences.en: She reached for her phone.
sentences.cn: 她伸手去拿手机。

sustainable:2.en: Lin appeared just before dawn, coffee in hand, and dropped a thin report on the counter. 'Opening two branches at once is not *sustainable*,' she said, almost kindly. 'The numbers are all here.' She pushed the report toward me and left without buying anything. The pages smelled like fresh printer ink.
sustainable:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在黎明前来到店里，把一份报告放在柜台上，说同时开两家分店并不____。
sustainable:2.hook: The last page of the report had our store's private cost figures on it.
sustainable:2.line: 'A plan that drains everyone is never *sustainable*, no matter how bold it looks.'

sentences.en: Lin appeared just before dawn, coffee in hand, and dropped a thin report on the counter.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在天亮前出现了，手里拿着咖啡，把一份薄薄的报告扔在柜台上。

sentences.en: 'Opening two branches at once is not *sustainable*,' she said, almost kindly.
'The numbers are all here.'
sentences.cn: 她说，所有数据都在这儿。

delay:2.en: The sign for Branch One was supposed to go up that morning. By noon it still sat in its box near the door. Tang called the fitting crew three times. 'Another *delay* and we miss the weekend opening,' she told me, rubbing her temples. A knock at the door made us both jump.
delay:2.cnHint: 分店一的招牌本该上午装好，但一再____，阿糖急得直揉太阳穴。
delay:2.hook: The person at the door was not the fitting crew.
delay:2.line: 'One more *delay* and we lose the customers we already told about the opening.'

sentences.en: The sign for Branch One was supposed to go up that morning.
sentences.cn: 一号分店的招牌本该那天上午装好。

identity:2.en: I found an old staff badge in the lost-and-found box while sorting things for the new branch. The name on it was worn away, but the shop logo was still clear. 'Keeping that logo is important,' the Manager said. '*Identity* travels with the brand, even to a new address.' He pocketed the badge quietly.
identity:2.cnHint: 我在失物箱里发现一枚旧工牌，店长说无论搬到哪里都要保留店铺的____。
identity:2.hook: Later I noticed the badge was gone from his pocket — and so was he.
identity:2.line: 'A store's *identity* is the one thing you cannot pack in a moving box.'

sentences.en: I found an old staff badge in the lost-and-found box while sorting things for the new branch.

store:2.en: At two in the morning, I found a locked back room behind the freezers. The Manager had mentioned a *store* of emergency supplies kept there — candles, batteries, instant noodles — enough to last a small neighbourhood through a week-long blackout. I counted seven boxes. There were only six yesterday.
store:2.cnHint: 我发现后储藏室里的应急物资少了一箱，不知道是谁拿的。
store:2.hook: The seventh box was gone, and the door had been locked from inside.
store:2.line: 'We keep a *store* of candles back there — never touch them without asking me first.'

sentences.en: At two in the morning, I found a locked back room behind the freezers.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点，我在冷柜后面发现了一间上了锁的后室。

I counted seven boxes.

budget:2.en: Tang slid a handwritten note across the counter just before her shift ended. It was a rough *budget* for the new branch: rent, staffing, stock, a small sum for signage. Every column was neat except the last one, which had a large question mark circled three times in red ink.
budget:2.cnHint: 同事留下一份新分店的____草案，最后一栏画着大大的问号。
budget:2.hook: Under the question mark, someone had written a name — not Tang's.
budget:2.line: 'I worked out the *budget* myself, but one number just does not add up.'

sentences.en: Tang slid a handwritten note across the counter just before her shift ended.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在班要结束前，把一张手写的纸条滑过柜台。

grant:2.en: A folded letter sat under the register when I arrived. The Manager had applied for a small business *grant* from the city council to help open the second store. The letter said the application was successful. He had not told any of us he had even applied.
grant:2.cnHint: 店长偷偷申请了____，信封静静地压在收银机下面。
grant:2.hook: The amount on the letter was twice what the new branch actually needed.
grant:2.line: 'The council will *grant* us enough to open — if we submit one more form.'

sentences.cn: 我到达时，收银机下压着一封折叠好的信。

hospital:2.en: Around midnight, a tired man in a green uniform bought four sandwiches and two large coffees. He said he had come straight from the *hospital* across the avenue, where his whole ward had been awake since noon. He paid, smiled faintly, and jogged back into the dark.
hospital:2.cnHint: 一位穿绿色制服的人从街对面的____赶来买宵夜，匆匆离开。
hospital:2.hook: He left his phone on the counter, and it buzzed immediately with an urgent call.

He paid, smiled faintly, and jogged back into the dark.
sentences.cn: 他付了钱，淡淡地笑了一下，然后跑回了黑暗中。

island:2.en: Lin came in holding a travel magazine folded open to a bright photo. She pointed to a small *island* off the southern coast and said the Manager had once talked about opening a convenience store there, somewhere quiet with only fishing boats and one narrow road in.
island:2.cnHint: 竞争对手拿着杂志，指着一座____，说那是店长曾经提起的地方。
island:2.hook: On the magazine's margin, in the Manager's handwriting, was a date three weeks away.
island:2.line: 'He said he dreamed of a little *island* shop — just him, the sea, and the shelves.'

sentences.en: She pointed to a small *island* off the southern coast and said the Manager had once talked about opening a convenience store there, somewhere quiet with only fishing boats and one narrow road in.

native:2.en: A quiet older woman bought a jar of pickled vegetables and told me the recipe was a *native* tradition from the village where she grew up, three provinces away. She said no shop here ever stocked the right kind. Then she looked at our shelf and went very still.
native:2.cnHint: 一位老太太说这种泡菜是她家乡____的做法，随后在货架上发现了什么。
native:2.hook: She picked up the jar with shaking hands and whispered a name none of us knew.
native:2.line: 'This flavour is completely *native* to my home village — how did it get here?'

tradition:2.en: The Manager stayed late to rearrange the window display. He lined up the same seven items he arranges every time a new branch opens — a habit so old it had become a *tradition*, he said. He would not explain what the seven items meant, only that the order mattered.
tradition:2.cnHint: 店长按照老____布置橱窗，七件物品的顺序有特殊含义，他却不肯说明。
tradition:2.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he placed the seventh item facing outward.
tradition:2.line: 'It is a *tradition* I started with the very first store — I never break it.'

sentences.en: The Manager stayed late to rearrange the window display.
sentences.cn: 店长留到很晚来重新整理橱窗展示。

sentences.en: He lined up the same seven items he arranges every time a new branch opens — a habit so old it had become a *tradition*, he said.

africa:2.cnHint: 一个学生把地图铺在收银台上，追溯咖啡豆从____到我们这条街的旅程。

africa:2.line: 'These beans came all the way from *Africa* — that cup cost less than a bus fare.'
