sentences.cn: '汤能在冷夜里吸引人流，'她说着，翻开笔记本给他看，里面都是顾客的留言。

sentences.en: The Manager listened, nodded slowly, and then pointed at the shelf of instant noodles.
sentences.cn: 店长听着，慢慢地点了点头，然后指向架子上那排方便面。

sentences.en: I held my breath.
sentences.cn: 我屏住了呼吸。

directly:2.en: A letter arrived *directly* at the store, addressed not to the Manager but to 'the night clerk'. I was the only night clerk. Inside was a hand-drawn map with a circle around a building two streets away. There was no name, no phone number, just a small smiley face in the corner.
directly:2.cnHint: 一封信____寄给了夜班店员，里面装着一张神秘的手绘地图。
directly:2.hook: The building on the map was where our new branch was supposed to open.
directly:2.line: 'This came *directly* for you — no sender, no stamp, nothing.'

sentences.en: A letter arrived *directly* at the store, addressed not to the Manager but to 'the night clerk'.
I was the only night clerk.
sentences.cn: 我是唯一的夜班员工。

sentences.en: Inside was a hand-drawn map with a circle around a building two streets away.
sentences.cn: 信里装着一张手绘地图，在距离这儿两条街的一栋楼周围画了个圆圈。

sentences.en: There was no name, no phone number, just a small smiley face in the corner.
sentences.cn: 没有署名，没有电话号码，只有角落里一个小笑脸。

extend:2.en: The Manager called us together before dawn. 'We will *extend* the night shift by two hours at the new branch,' he announced, tapping the schedule on the wall. Tang crossed her arms. I did the maths quietly in my head. Outside, a cat on the kerb seemed to be doing the same.
extend:2.cnHint: 店长宣布新分店要____夜班时间，阿糖听完叉起了手臂。
extend:2.hook: The schedule on the wall had one name crossed out in red ink.
extend:2.line: 'We will *extend* the shift, and yes, that means you two as well.'

sentences.en: The Manager called us together before dawn.
sentences.cn: 店长在天亮前把我们召集到一起。

sentences.en: 'We will *extend* the night shift by two hours at the new branch,' he announced, tapping the schedule on the wall.
Tang crossed her arms.
sentences.cn: 阿糖抱起了胳膊。

sentences.en: I did the maths quietly in my head.
sentences.cn: 我在心里默默算了一笔账。

sentences.en: Outside, a cat on the kerb seemed to be doing the same.
sentences.cn: 外面，路边的一只猫好像也在琢磨着什么。

rat:2.en: I found a small toy *rat* sitting on top of the new branch's welcome box, which had been delivered that afternoon. It was plastic, painted grey, with tiny red eyes. Tang laughed. The Manager did not laugh. He picked it up carefully with two fingers and dropped it into a bag.
rat:2.cnHint: 新分店的欢迎礼盒上放着一只玩具____，店长的反应很耐人寻味。
rat:2.hook: Tang stopped laughing when she saw the Manager's face go pale.
rat:2.line: 'A toy *rat* on a welcome gift is not a joke — it is a message.'

sentences.en: I found a small toy *rat* sitting on top of the new branch's welcome box, which had been delivered that afternoon.
It was plastic, painted grey, with tiny red eyes.
sentences.cn: 它是塑料做的，涂成灰色，长着一双小红眼睛。

sentences.en: Tang laughed.
sentences.cn: 阿糖笑了。

sentences.en: The Manager did not laugh.
sentences.cn: 店长没有笑。

sentences.en: He picked it up carefully with two fingers and dropped it into a bag.
sentences.cn: 他用两根手指小心地捡起来，扔进了一个袋子。

saturday:2.en: The grand opening was set for *Saturday*, and by Thursday the Manager had already changed the date twice. A handwritten sign on the door still said 'Opening Soon'. Tang updated the sign every morning. On Friday evening, a stranger photographed the sign and walked away without buying anything.
saturday:2.cnHint: 新分店原定____开业，但日期已经改了两次，还来了个神秘拍照的人。
saturday:2.hook: The stranger came back an hour later and photographed it again.
saturday:2.line: 'If it opens on *Saturday*, I want to be the first one through that door.'

sentences.en: The grand opening was set for *Saturday*, and by Thursday the Manager had already changed the date twice.
A handwritten sign on the door still said 'Opening Soon'.
sentences.cn: 门上还贴着一张手写的纸条，写着"即将开业"。

sentences.en: Tang updated the sign every morning.
sentences.cn: 阿糖每个早上都更新这个纸条。

sentences.en: On Friday evening, a stranger photographed the sign and walked away without buying anything.
sentences.cn: 周五晚上，有个陌生人拍了张纸条的照片，什么都没买就走了。

april:2.en: Lin slid a printed article across the counter. It reported that three new convenience stores would open on our street before *April*. I read it twice. The Manager was in the back room, on the phone. His voice was low and steady, the way it gets when something is wrong.
april:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿来一篇报道，说在____之前这条街会多出三家便利店。
april:2.hook: One of the three stores on the list shared our Manager's family name.
april:2.line: 'Before *April*, there will be three new stores on this street alone.'

sentences.en: Lin slid a printed article across the counter.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林把一篇打印的文章推过柜台。

sentences.en: It reported that three new convenience stores would open on our street before *April*.
I read it twice.
sentences.cn: 我读了两遍。

sentences.en: The Manager was in the back room, on the phone.
sentences.cn: 店长在后间办公室里，在接电话。

sentences.en: His voice was low and steady, the way it gets when something is wrong.
sentences.cn: 他的声音低沉而平稳，就是那种有什么不对劲时才会出现的语调。

passion:2.en: A folded note fell out of the supply box the Manager sent over from the new branch. It read: 'Stack the noodle cups with *passion* — first impressions matter.' I laughed, then straightened every single cup. Tang leaned over and did the same without a word.
passion:2.cnHint: 店长在补给箱里留了一张纸条，叮嘱我们要用____摆放货品。
passion:2.hook: But the note had a second line none of us had noticed yet.
passion:2.line: 'Stack the noodle cups with *passion* — first impressions matter.'

sentences.en: A folded note fell out of the supply box the Manager sent over from the new branch.
sentences.cn: 一张折起来的纸条从店长从新店送来的供货箱里掉了出来。

sentences.en: It read: 'Stack the noodle cups with *passion* — first impressions matter.'
I laughed, then straightened every single cup.
sentences.cn: 我笑了，然后把每个杯子都整整齐齐地摆好。

sentences.en: Tang leaned over and did the same without a word.
sentences.cn: 阿糖探过身子，一句话没说就跟着做了一遍。

temperature:2.en: The Manager called from the new branch to say the drinks fridge there had stopped working. 'Check our *temperature* log,' he said. I found the little notebook under the counter and read out every number from the past week. Tang nodded slowly, as if the numbers told a story I could not yet hear.
temperature:2.cnHint: 店长打来电话，让我查看我们这边饮料柜的____记录。
temperature:2.hook: The last entry in the log was written in a hand neither Tang nor I recognised.
temperature:2.line: 'Please check the fridge *temperature* log and read it to me.'

sentences.en: The Manager called from the new branch to say the drinks fridge there had stopped working.
sentences.cn: 店长从新店打来电话，说那边的饮料冰箱坏了。

sentences.en: 'Check our *temperature* log,' he said.
I found the little notebook under the counter and read out every number from the past week.
sentences.cn: 我找到了柜台下的小本子，把过去一周的所有温度数字都读了一遍。

sentences.en: Tang nodded slowly, as if the numbers told a story I could not yet hear.
sentences.cn: 阿糖慢慢地点头，仿佛那些数字讲的是我还没听懂的故事。

board:2.en: Leaning against the door of the stock room was a wooden *board* covered in little notes — opening times, staff names, a hand-drawn map of the new branch layout. The Manager had left it for us to study. I traced the map with one finger and suddenly felt like a sailor reading a chart before a long voyage.
board:2.cnHint: 库房门边有一块____，上面密密麻麻写满了新分店的信息。
board:2.hook: One name on the staff list was circled in red, with no explanation.
board:2.line: 'Study this *board* carefully — the new branch opens in three days.'

sentences.en: Leaning against the door of the stock room was a wooden *board* covered in little notes — opening times, staff names, a hand-drawn map of the new branch layout.
The Manager had left it for us to study.
sentences.cn: 店长留下这块板子让我们学习。

sentences.en: I traced the map with one finger and suddenly felt like a sailor reading a chart before a long voyage.
sentences.cn: 我用一根手指沿着地图描了一遍，忽然觉得自己像个水手，正在读着一张航海图，准备出发去远航。

handle:2.en: A small package arrived addressed to the new branch but delivered here by mistake. The label said 'Fragile — *handle* with care.' Tang and I set it on the counter and stared at it. The Manager had not mentioned any package, and neither of us wanted to be the one to call and ask.
handle:2.cnHint: 一个写着"易碎品，请小心____"的包裹被误送到了我们店。
handle:2.hook: The package made a faint ticking sound every few minutes.
handle:2.line: '*Handle* it with care — it says fragile right there on the label.'

sentences.en: A small package arrived addressed to the new branch but delivered here by mistake.
sentences.cn: 一个小包裹本来是寄到新店的，结果被送错到了这儿。

sentences.en: The label said 'Fragile — *handle* with care.'
Tang and I set it on the counter and stared at it.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我把它放在柜台上，盯着看。

sentences.en: The Manager had not mentioned any package, and neither of us wanted to be the one to call and ask.
sentences.cn: 店长没提过什么包裹，我们俩都不想成为那个打电话去问的人。

ideal:2.en: Tang pointed at the corner spot on the new branch map and said it was the *ideal* place to put the hot-food counter — warm smell would pull people in from the street. I had never thought about a store that way before. I looked at our own corner and saw it, too, like seeing a picture inside a cloud.
ideal:2.cnHint: 阿糖指着地图上的一个角落，说那是摆放热食台的____位置。
ideal:2.hook: Lin walked in just then and had a very different idea about that corner.
ideal:2.line: 'That corner is the *ideal* spot for the hot-food counter, trust me.'

sentences.en: Tang pointed at the corner spot on the new branch map and said it was the *ideal* place to put the hot-food counter — warm smell would pull people in from the street.
I had never thought about a store that way before.
sentences.cn: 我从来没有这样想过一家店。

sentences.en: I looked at our own corner and saw it, too, like seeing a picture inside a cloud.
sentences.cn: 我看向了我们自己的角落，也看到了，就像在云里看到了一幅画。

ride:2.en: The Manager asked me to take a box of spare price tags to the new branch on my way home. The *ride* on the night bus was quiet — just me, the box on my lap, and the city sliding past the window in soft orange light. When I arrived, the new store smelled of fresh paint and possibility.
ride:2.cnHint: 店长让我骑车（乘车）把一箱价格标签带去新分店，这段____让我感触颇深。
ride:2.hook: Someone was already inside the new branch, moving around in the dark.
ride:2.line: 'The *ride* over was short — I can bring the next box tomorrow night.'

sentences.en: The Manager asked me to take a box of spare price tags to the new branch on my way home.
sentences.cn: 店长让我回家的路上，顺便把一盒多余的价签送到新店去。

sentences.en: The *ride* on the night bus was quiet — just me, the box on my lap, and the city sliding past the window in soft orange light.
When I arrived, the new store smelled of fresh paint and possibility.
sentences.cn: 当我到达时，新店里弥漫着新油漆的味道和无限可能。

adjust:2.en: The new branch had sent over its shelf plan, but the measurements were slightly off for our stockroom. Tang said we should *adjust* the plan rather than move the walls — a joke, but also good advice. We spent an hour with a pencil and a ruler, and by the end the numbers fit like a key in a lock.
adjust:2.cnHint: 新分店发来的货架方案尺寸有偏差，我们需要____一下再使用。
adjust:2.hook: The revised plan revealed a gap in the layout big enough to hide something.
adjust:2.line: 'We just need to *adjust* the numbers a little and it will fit perfectly.'

sentences.en: The new branch had sent over its shelf plan, but the measurements were slightly off for our stockroom.
sentences.cn: 隔壁新店铺送来了货架方案，但是我们储藏室的尺寸算得有点不对。

sentences.en: Tang said we should *adjust* the plan rather than move the walls — a joke, but also good advice.
We spent an hour with a pencil and a ruler, and by the end the numbers fit like a key in a lock.
sentences.cn: 我们拿着铅笔和尺子花了一个小时，最后数字吻合得就像钥匙插进锁里一样。

basis:2.en: The Manager pinned a one-page note to the board: the new branch would share stock with us on a weekly *basis* until it found its own suppliers. Tang read it twice, then looked at our shelves with fresh, slightly worried eyes. I counted the instant noodles quietly and said nothing.
basis:2.cnHint: 店长通知我们，新分店将以每周为____从我们这里共享库存。
basis:2.hook: Tang's worried look turned out to be about something other than the noodles.
basis:2.line: 'We will share stock on a weekly *basis* until the new branch is ready.'

sentences.en: The Manager pinned a one-page note to the board: the new branch would share stock with us on a weekly *basis* until it found its own suppliers.
Tang read it twice, then looked at our shelves with fresh, slightly worried eyes.
sentences.cn: 阿糖读了两遍，然后用一种新奇又有点担心的眼神看着我们的货架。

sentences.en: I counted the instant noodles quietly and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 我默默数了数方便面，什么都没说。

artificial:2.en: The Manager left a note on the counter before my shift: 'The flowers by the door are *artificial* — do not water them.' I had been watering them every night for a week. They did look suspiciously perfect. Tang saw my face and tried very hard not to laugh.
artificial:2.cnHint: 店长留了张便条，说门口的花是____的，而我已经浇了一周的水。
artificial:2.hook: Tang's laughter stopped the moment a regular walked in and headed straight for those flowers.
artificial:2.line: 'Don't worry — even I thought the *artificial* ones were real at first.'

sentences.en: The Manager left a note on the counter before my shift: 'The flowers by the door are *artificial* — do not water them.'
I had been watering them every night for a week.
sentences.cn: 我已经连续一个星期每晚都给它们浇水了。

sentences.en: They did look suspiciously perfect.
sentences.cn: 它们看起来确实没有一点瑕疵。

sentences.en: Tang saw my face and tried very hard not to laugh.
sentences.cn: 阿糖看到我的表情，竭力忍住不笑。

confirm:2.en: A delivery driver knocked at two in the morning, holding a clipboard. 'Can you *confirm* the order for this address?' He turned the board around. The address was our store. Nobody had ordered anything. I checked the system twice. Tang leaned over my shoulder, equally puzzled.
confirm:2.cnHint: 一个送货司机深夜来店，要我____一份没人下过的订单。
confirm:2.hook: Then the Manager's name appeared at the bottom of the receipt.
confirm:2.line: 'I just need you to *confirm* the name, and then I can leave it here.'

sentences.en: A delivery driver knocked at two in the morning, holding a clipboard.
sentences.cn: 一个送货司机在凌晨两点敲了门，手里拿着夹板。

sentences.en: 'Can you *confirm* the order for this address?'
He turned the board around.
sentences.cn: 他把夹板转过来。

sentences.en: The address was our store.
sentences.cn: 地址是我们的店。

sentences.en: Nobody had ordered anything.
sentences.cn: 没人下过单。

sentences.en: I checked the system twice.
sentences.cn: 我在系统里查了两遍。

sentences.en: Tang leaned over my shoulder, equally puzzled.
sentences.cn: 阿糖靠过我的肩膀，同样一脸困惑。

context:2.en: I found an old photo tucked behind the shelf of instant noodles — two young people smiling in front of what looked like this very store. Without any *context*, I could not tell who they were or when it was taken. Tang glanced at it and went quiet in a way that felt like a whole story.
context:2.cnHint: 我在货架后发现一张旧照片，没有任何____，无法判断照片里的人是谁。
context:2.hook: Tang slipped the photo into their pocket without a single word.
context:2.line: 'You need the *context* before you start asking questions about that photo.'

sentences.en: I found an old photo tucked behind the shelf of instant noodles — two young people smiling in front of what looked like this very store.
sentences.cn: 我在方便面架子后面找到了一张泛黄的照片——两个年轻人在什么看起来就像这家店的地方笑着。

sentences.en: Without any *context*, I could not tell who they were or when it was taken.
Tang glanced at it and went quiet in a way that felt like a whole story.
sentences.cn: 阿糖看了一眼，然后陷入了一种沉默，那沉默本身像是一整个故事。

date:2.en: A regular came in, bought a small cake, and asked me for a pen. She wrote a *date* on the box in careful numbers — not today's date. She smiled at my curious look. 'It's the day this store first opened,' she said softly, and walked out into the dark street.
date:2.cnHint: 一位常客买了蛋糕，在盒子上郑重写下一个____，那不是今天的日期。
date:2.hook: The date she wrote matched the photo I had found behind the noodle shelf.
date:2.line: 'I always write the *date* on the box so I never forget.'

sentences.en: A regular came in, bought a small cake, and asked me for a pen.
sentences.cn: 一位常客进来买了一个小蛋糕，然后问我要了支笔。

sentences.en: She wrote a *date* on the box in careful numbers — not today's date.
She smiled at my curious look.
sentences.cn: 她对我好奇的目光笑了笑。

sentences.en: 'It's the day this store first opened,' she said softly, and walked out into the dark street.
sentences.cn: 她轻声说，"这是这家店开张的日子，"然后走进了漆黑的街道。

flexible:2.en: Lin from the convenience store across the street came in to browse, which felt odd. 'Our hours are less *flexible* than yours,' Lin said simply, eyeing our night-shift shelf layout. I smiled and said nothing. Lin spent ten quiet minutes studying how we arranged the drinks.
flexible:2.cnHint: 对面店的隔壁咖啡店的林进来转了转，说他们的营业时间没我们____。
flexible:2.hook: Lin left without buying anything, but came back an hour later with a notebook.
flexible:2.line: 'You have to be *flexible* when you run a small store — I'm still learning that.'

sentences.en: Lin from the convenience store across the street came in to browse, which felt odd.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林进来逛逛，感觉有点奇怪。

sentences.en: 'Our hours are less *flexible* than yours,' Lin said simply, eyeing our night-shift shelf layout.
I smiled and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 我笑着什么都没说。

sentences.en: Lin spent ten quiet minutes studying how we arranged the drinks.
sentences.cn: 林安静地花了十分钟研究我们怎么摆放饮料的。

fly:2.en: Just before dawn, a single *fly* appeared from nowhere and circled the bright light above the rice-ball shelf. Tang grabbed a folded newspaper and missed three times. The fourth swing knocked a whole row of rice balls to the floor. We both stared at the mess in silence.
fly:2.cnHint: 快天亮时，一只____出现在货架上方，阿糖抄起报纸，结果把一排饭团打翻了。
fly:2.hook: The regular who always bought the first rice ball of the morning walked in exactly then.
fly:2.line: 'It is just one *fly*, Tang — please put the newspaper down.'

sentences.en: Just before dawn, a single *fly* appeared from nowhere and circled the bright light above the rice-ball shelf.
Tang grabbed a folded newspaper and missed three times.
sentences.cn: 阿糖拿起折叠的报纸打，连打了三次都没中。

sentences.en: The fourth swing knocked a whole row of rice balls to the floor.
sentences.cn: 第四次挥动就把一整排饭团打到了地上。

sentences.en: We both stared at the mess in silence.
sentences.cn: 我们两个人都盯着这一摊狼狈，谁都没吭声。

judge:2.en: The Manager stopped by at midnight to check the stock report. I had sorted the snacks by colour instead of by type. I waited for a reaction. The Manager studied the shelf for a long moment. 'I won't *judge* the system until I see the sales numbers,' the Manager said, and left.
judge:2.cnHint: 我把零食按颜色而不是种类摆放，店长说等看了销售数字再____我的方法。
judge:2.hook: The next morning, the colour-sorted snacks had sold out first.
judge:2.line: 'Don't *judge* a new system before you give it one full night.'

sentences.en: The Manager stopped by at midnight to check the stock report.
sentences.cn: 店长在午夜过来检查库存报表。

sentences.en: I had sorted the snacks by colour instead of by type.
sentences.cn: 我把零食按颜色分类了，而不是按种类。

sentences.en: I waited for a reaction.
sentences.cn: 我等着她的反应。

sentences.en: The Manager studied the shelf for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 店长盯着货架看了好久。

sentences.en: 'I won't *judge* the system until I see the sales numbers,' the Manager said, and left.

oil:2.en: At three in the morning, an older man came in asking for cooking *oil*. Just one small bottle. He told me he was making noodles for his son, who had just come home after two years away. He paid with exact coins he had clearly counted out in advance and thanked me twice.
oil:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点，一位老人来买____，说儿子阔别两年刚回家，他要亲手做碗面。
oil:2.hook: He came back the next night, bought the same bottle, and said nothing at all.
oil:2.line: 'Just the small *oil*, please — I only need enough for one bowl of noodles.'

sentences.en: At three in the morning, an older man came in asking for cooking *oil*.
Just one small bottle.
sentences.cn: 就要一小瓶。

sentences.en: He told me he was making noodles for his son, who had just come home after two years away.
sentences.cn: 他告诉我他在给儿子做面条，儿子两年后刚回家。

sentences.en: He paid with exact coins he had clearly counted out in advance and thanked me twice.
sentences.cn: 他用提前数好的硬币付了钱，还谢了我两次。

comfortable:2.en: The Manager spread a large *comfortable* on the back-room cot and smoothed out every wrinkle. 'Night shifts are long,' she said. 'You should sleep well between rushes.' I had not expected such care from someone who checked the receipt tape every single morning. Clearly there was more to her than spreadsheets.
comfortable:2.cnHint: 店长在后室的小床上铺好____，让夜班员工能好好休息。
comfortable:2.hook: But why did she lock the back-room door before leaving?
comfortable:2.line: 'A good *comfortable* makes the long night shift much easier to bear.'

sentences.en: The Manager spread a large *comfortable* on the back-room cot and smoothed out every wrinkle.
'Night shifts are long,' she said.
sentences.cn: "夜班很长，"她说。

sentences.en: 'You should sleep well between rushes.'
sentences.cn: "你应该在客流间隙好好睡。"

sentences.en: I had not expected such care from someone who checked the receipt tape every single morning.
sentences.cn: 我没想到一个每天早上都要检查收据纸带的人会这么细心。

sentences.en: Clearly there was more to her than spreadsheets.
sentences.cn: 看来她远不止是数字表格那么简单。

conclusion:2.en: A folded note sat under the milk shelf. I opened it slowly. It read: 'Check the second freezer.' Inside I found a hidden stock list with every item marked low. Someone had done a full count overnight. My *conclusion* was simple — whoever left that note knew this store far better than I did.
conclusion:2.cnHint: 我在货架下发现一张纸条，读完之后得出了一个____。
conclusion:2.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like Lin's.
conclusion:2.line: 'My *conclusion* is that someone has been watching this store very carefully.'

sentences.en: A folded note sat under the milk shelf.
sentences.cn: 牛奶架下面压着一张折好的纸条。

sentences.en: I opened it slowly.
sentences.cn: 我慢慢打开了它。

sentences.en: It read: 'Check the second freezer.'
sentences.cn: 上面写着："检查第二个冰柜。"

sentences.en: Inside I found a hidden stock list with every item marked low.
sentences.cn: 里面我找到了一份藏起来的库存清单，每一项都标注了短缺。

sentences.en: Someone had done a full count overnight.
sentences.cn: 有人连夜做了一次完整的盘点。

sentences.en: My *conclusion* was simple — whoever left that note knew this store far better than I did.

formal:2.en: A *formal* letter arrived at the store just before midnight, sealed with a red stamp. The Manager held it at arm's length as if it might bite. Tang leaned over my shoulder to read the return address. 'That's the city planning office,' Tang whispered. My stomach dropped — that could only mean one thing for our little corner store.
formal:2.cnHint: 一封____的信函在深夜送到了便利店，店长和同事都看起来很紧张。
formal:2.hook: The Manager slipped the letter into her bag without opening it.
formal:2.line: 'A *formal* letter from the city office is never just a greeting.'

sentences.en: A *formal* letter arrived at the store just before midnight, sealed with a red stamp.
The Manager held it at arm's length as if it might bite.
sentences.cn: 店长把信拿得远远的，好像它随时会咬人似的。

sentences.en: Tang leaned over my shoulder to read the return address.
sentences.cn: 阿糖探过我的肩膀去看回信地址。

sentences.en: 'That's the city planning office,' Tang whispered.
sentences.cn: "那是城市规划办公室，"阿糖小声说。

sentences.en: My stomach dropped — that could only mean one thing for our little corner store.
sentences.cn: 我的心一沉——对我们这间小角落店来说，这只能意味着一件事。

happiness:2.en: I found an old photo tucked behind the staff notice board — the Manager, much younger, cutting a ribbon in front of this very store. Her *happiness* in that moment lit up her whole face in a way I had never seen at the counter. Tang caught me staring and smiled quietly. 'That was opening day,' Tang said.
happiness:2.cnHint: 我在公告栏后发现一张旧照片，照片里满满的____让我对店长有了新的认识。
happiness:2.hook: Tang's smile faded the moment I asked when the second store had closed.
happiness:2.line: 'That kind of *happiness* on her face — you don't see it often anymore.'

sentences.en: I found an old photo tucked behind the staff notice board — the Manager, much younger, cutting a ribbon in front of this very store.
sentences.cn: 我在员工公告板后面找到了一张老照片——年轻得多的店长站在这家店前面剪彩。

sentences.en: Her *happiness* in that moment lit up her whole face in a way I had never seen at the counter.
Tang caught me staring and smiled quietly.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林看到我发呆，安静地笑了。

sentences.en: 'That was opening day,' Tang said.
sentences.cn: "那是开业那天，"林说。

intelligent:2.en: A small handwritten study guide was taped inside the supply closet door — vocabulary lists, grammar notes, and clever memory tricks. Tang said it belonged to the previous night clerk. 'She was very *intelligent*,' Tang added, 'finished her degree while working here alone every night.' The closet suddenly felt less like storage and more like a classroom.
intelligent:2.cnHint: 储物柜门上贴着一份手写学习笔记，唐说上一任夜班员工非常____。
intelligent:2.hook: No one knew why she had left so suddenly.
intelligent:2.line: 'She was so *intelligent* — she studied through every quiet hour of the night.'

sentences.en: A small handwritten study guide was taped inside the supply closet door — vocabulary lists, grammar notes, and clever memory tricks.
sentences.cn: 一份手写的学习指南贴在储物间门里面——词汇表、语法笔记，还有聪明的记忆技巧。

sentences.en: Tang said it belonged to the previous night clerk.
sentences.cn: 林说这是前一班夜间店员留下的。

sentences.en: 'She was very *intelligent*,' Tang added, 'finished her degree while working here alone every night.'
The closet suddenly felt less like storage and more like a classroom.
sentences.cn: 储物间突然感觉不像仓库了，更像是一间教室。

novel:2.en: An old hardback sat on the staff shelf with a bookmark near the final chapter. The title was handwritten on the spine in fading ink — someone had made their own *novel* and printed it at home. I opened the first page and read: 'This store, this street, these people.' My hands went a little cold. The clerk in chapter one had my exact shift hours.
novel:2.cnHint: 员工书架上放着一本自制的____，第一章的主人公竟然和我的班次完全一样。
novel:2.hook: Chapter three was torn out cleanly at the binding.
novel:2.line: 'Someone wrote a whole *novel* about working the night shift here.'

sentences.en: An old hardback sat on the staff shelf with a bookmark near the final chapter.
sentences.cn: 员工架子上放着一本旧精装书，书签夹在接近最后一章的地方。

sentences.en: The title was handwritten on the spine in fading ink — someone had made their own *novel* and printed it at home.
I opened the first page and read: 'This store, this street, these people.'
sentences.cn: 我翻开第一页读道："这家店，这条街，这些人。"

sentences.en: My hands went a little cold.
sentences.cn: 我的手有点冰冷。

sentences.en: The clerk in chapter one had my exact shift hours.
sentences.cn: 第一章里的店员工作时间跟我的完全一样。

political:2.en: Two customers arrived together just after two in the morning, mid-argument. One wanted the store to move its community board to the window; the other said that would block the light. Tang muttered that their *political* fight over one small board had been going on for three years. They both bought the same snack and left still arguing, almost in step.
political:2.cnHint: 两位常客为公告栏的位置争得不可开交，唐说这场____争论已经持续了三年。
political:2.hook: They always arrived together, which made no sense at all.
political:2.line: 'Their *political* battle over that board is older than my contract here.'

sentences.en: Two customers arrived together just after two in the morning, mid-argument.
sentences.cn: 两个顾客在凌晨两点多一起来了，正在吵架。

sentences.en: One wanted the store to move its community board to the window; the other said that would block the light.
sentences.cn: 一个想把店的社区公告板移到窗边；另一个说那样会挡住光线。

sentences.en: Tang muttered that their *political* fight over one small board had been going on for three years.
They both bought the same snack and left still arguing, almost in step.
sentences.cn: 他们都买了同样的零食，还在争论着离开了，步伐几乎一致。

property:2.en: The Manager arrived early with a rolled-up map and spread it across the counter. She pointed to a corner two blocks away. 'That *property* is empty,' she said, 'and the rent is low.' Tang and I looked at each other. She was not talking about storage. She was talking about a second store — and the map already had a floor plan sketched on the back.
property:2.cnHint: 店长带来一张地图，指着附近一处空置的____，背面已经画好了平面图。
property:2.hook: Lin's name was written in pencil in the map's top corner.
property:2.line: 'That *property* two blocks over — I have been watching it for months.'

sentences.en: The Manager arrived early with a rolled-up map and spread it across the counter.
sentences.cn: 店长早早到了，卷着一张地图，铺在柜台上。

sentences.en: She pointed to a corner two blocks away.
sentences.cn: 她指向两条街外的一个角落。

sentences.en: 'That *property* is empty,' she said, 'and the rent is low.'
Tang and I looked at each other.
sentences.cn: 林和我互相看了一眼。

sentences.en: She was not talking about storage.
sentences.cn: 她不是在谈论仓储。

sentences.en: She was talking about a second store — and the map already had a floor plan sketched on the back.
sentences.cn: 她在谈论第二家店——地图背面已经画好了楼层平面图。

attribute:2.en: A sealed envelope arrived at the store addressed to no one. Inside was a hand-drawn map of the block, with a red star marking our corner. The Manager studied it and said he could *attribute* the neat handwriting to only one person — the owner of the rival shop across the street.
attribute:2.cnHint: 一封神秘信封送到店里，店长说他能将工整的笔迹____给某个特定的人。
attribute:2.hook: The rival's name was not written anywhere, yet everyone knew.
attribute:2.line: 'I can *attribute* this map to exactly one person on this street.'

sentences.en: A sealed envelope arrived at the store addressed to no one.
sentences.cn: 一个密封信封寄到了店里，上面没有收件人名字。

sentences.en: Inside was a hand-drawn map of the block, with a red star marking our corner.
sentences.cn: 里面是一张手绘的街区地图，用红星标记了我们的角落。

sentences.en: The Manager studied it and said he could *attribute* the neat handwriting to only one person — the owner of the rival shop across the street.

badly:2.en: I found the stock room during my first night break. Boxes were stacked in every corner, some leaning *badly* to one side, ready to fall. A sticky note on the tallest pile read: 'Do not touch — Manager's system.' I decided that some systems were best left alone.
badly:2.cnHint: 我发现库房里箱子堆得____，一张便条警告我别乱动。
badly:2.hook: Behind the tallest stack, something quietly ticked.
badly:2.line: 'Those boxes are leaning *badly* — one bump and they all come down.'

sentences.en: I found the stock room during my first night break.
sentences.cn: 我在第一个夜班休息时发现了储物间。

sentences.en: Boxes were stacked in every corner, some leaning *badly* to one side, ready to fall.
A sticky note on the tallest pile read: 'Do not touch — Manager's system.'
sentences.cn: 最高的那堆箱子上贴着一张便签纸："不要动——店长的系统。"

sentences.en: I decided that some systems were best left alone.
sentences.cn: 我决定有些系统最好别去碰。

bridge:2.en: Tang slid a worn card across the counter during a slow hour. 'Do you play *bridge*?' she asked. Before I could answer, she dealt four hands on the empty counter top, explaining that the night shift regulars used to play until a certain customer stopped coming six months ago.
bridge:2.cnHint: 阿糖拿出一副旧扑克牌问我会不会打____，说某位常客六个月前突然消失了。
bridge:2.hook: She never said why that customer had stopped coming.
bridge:2.line: 'We used to play *bridge* here every Thursday night without fail.'

sentences.en: Tang slid a worn card across the counter during a slow hour.
sentences.cn: 林在淡季的时候拿过一张旧卡片放在柜台上。

sentences.en: 'Do you play *bridge*?' she asked.
Before I could answer, she dealt four hands on the empty counter top, explaining that the night shift regulars used to play until a certain customer stopped coming six months ago.
sentences.cn: 她没等我回答就在空荡荡的柜台上发起了牌，解释说夜班的常客过去常常一起玩，直到某个顾客六个月前停止来店。

casual:2.en: A man in a *casual* jacket drifted in just after two in the morning, bought a single mint, and left a folded note under the pen cup on the counter. He looked like any ordinary late-night walker. The note, however, contained a six-digit number and the words 'second location.'
casual:2.cnHint: 一个穿____服装的男人深夜买了一粒薄荷糖，悄悄留下一张写有神秘数字的纸条。
casual:2.hook: No one had mentioned a second location to me before tonight.
casual:2.line: 'He always looks *casual*, but he never comes in without a reason.'

sentences.en: A man in a *casual* jacket drifted in just after two in the morning, bought a single mint, and left a folded note under the pen cup on the counter.
He looked like any ordinary late-night walker.
sentences.cn: 他看起来像任何普通的深夜漫步者。

sentences.en: The note, however, contained a six-digit number and the words 'second location.'
sentences.cn: 但是那张纸条上却写着一个六位数和"第二地点"这几个字。

closely:2.en: The Manager pinned a printed floor plan to the back wall and asked me to study it *closely*. It showed a space twice the size of our store, with a counter, a cold section, and a small seating area. At the bottom, in red pen, someone had written: 'Opening — sooner than you think.'
closely:2.cnHint: 店长让我____观察一张新店面的平面图，图纸底部有人用红笔写了一句话。
closely:2.hook: The handwriting at the bottom matched the envelope from earlier.
closely:2.line: 'Look *closely* at where the second counter is placed — that detail matters.'

sentences.en: The Manager pinned a printed floor plan to the back wall and asked me to study it *closely*.
It showed a space twice the size of our store, with a counter, a cold section, and a small seating area.
sentences.cn: 它展示的空间是我们店的两倍大，有柜台、冷柜区和一个小的用餐区。

sentences.en: At the bottom, in red pen, someone had written: 'Opening — sooner than you think.'
sentences.cn: 下面用红笔写着："开业——比你想的要快。"

commit:2.en: Tang warned me during our handover that the Manager would not *commit* to an opening date for the new branch until every small detail was settled. She had seen three launch dates come and go. A corkboard in the back room held the evidence: three crossed-out calendar pages, all from different months.
commit:2.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我店长不肯____确定新分店的开业日期，后室的软木板上有三张被划掉的日历页为证。
commit:2.hook: The fourth calendar page was already pinned up, waiting.
commit:2.line: 'He will never *commit* to a date until every shelf is perfectly placed.'

sentences.en: Tang warned me during our handover that the Manager would not *commit* to an opening date for the new branch until every small detail was settled.
She had seen three launch dates come and go.
sentences.cn: 她见过三个开业日期来了又去。

sentences.en: A corkboard in the back room held the evidence: three crossed-out calendar pages, all from different months.
sentences.cn: 后间的软木板上保留着证据：三张被划掉的日历页，分别来自不同的月份。

concentrate:2.en: Around three in the morning the street outside went completely silent, and I found it easier to *concentrate* on the new branch paperwork the Manager had left me. One page listed every item to be moved from our store. A single line at the bottom had been circled twice: 'Night-shift clerk — TBD.'
concentrate:2.cnHint: 深夜街道安静下来，我终于能____看新分店的文件，发现最后一行提到"夜班店员——待定"。
concentrate:2.hook: 'TBD' meant the decision had not yet been made about me.
concentrate:2.line: 'It is easier to *concentrate* on the details when the street is this quiet.'

sentences.en: Around three in the morning the street outside went completely silent, and I found it easier to *concentrate* on the new branch paperwork the Manager had left me.
One page listed every item to be moved from our store.
sentences.cn: 一张纸上列着要从店里搬走的每一样东西。

sentences.en: A single line at the bottom had been circled twice: 'Night-shift clerk — TBD.'
sentences.cn: 底部只有一行被圈了两次：'夜班店员——待定'。

conscious:2.en: Lin appeared at the door at half past three, pressed her face against the glass, and waved. I was *conscious* of the fact that she was studying our new display stand, not greeting me. She pulled out a small notebook, wrote something, and walked away before I could open the door.
conscious:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜贴着玻璃门张望，我____意识到她其实是在打量我们的新展示架，并悄悄记了笔记。
conscious:2.hook: Whatever she wrote, she wrote it very quickly and very carefully.
conscious:2.line: 'Be *conscious* of what she looks at — it always tells you her next move.'

sentences.en: Lin appeared at the door at half past three, pressed her face against the glass, and waved.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林三点半出现在门口，贴着玻璃按了按脸，挥挥手。

sentences.en: I was *conscious* of the fact that she was studying our new display stand, not greeting me.
She pulled out a small notebook, wrote something, and walked away before I could open the door.
sentences.cn: 她掏出一个小笔记本，写了点什么，然后在我开门之前就走了。

relative:2.en: A handwritten note was taped to the back door when I arrived for my shift. It read: 'My shop next door pays only half the price for milk. Everything here is *relative*, I suppose.' The Manager peeled it off, sighed, and stuck it on the staff board without a word.
relative:2.cnHint: 后门贴着一张字条，让店长若有所思地把它贴到了员工告示板上。
relative:2.hook: Whose handwriting was it — Lin's, or someone closer?
relative:2.line: 'Everything is *relative*, so why does this note still bother me?'

sentences.en: A handwritten note was taped to the back door when I arrived for my shift.
sentences.cn: 我上班时发现后门贴着一张手写的纸条。

sentences.en: It read: 'My shop next door pays only half the price for milk.
sentences.cn: 上面写着：'我隔壁店的牛奶只卖半价。

sentences.en: Everything here is *relative*, I suppose.'
The Manager peeled it off, sighed, and stuck it on the staff board without a word.
sentences.cn: 店长撕下来，叹了口气，默默地贴到员工公告板上。

rent:2.en: I found a torn envelope under the counter while restocking the bottom shelf. Inside was a single line: 'The *rent* goes up again next month.' The Manager's name was on it. I slid it back quietly, but the number I had glimpsed stayed in my head all night.
rent:2.cnHint: 我在柜台下发现一封信，得知店里面临涨____的压力。
rent:2.hook: Could that number be the reason the Manager looked so tired lately?
rent:2.line: 'The *rent* went up again — I have not told the others yet.'

sentences.en: I found a torn envelope under the counter while restocking the bottom shelf.
sentences.cn: 我在整理下面货架时在收银台下找到一个破信封。

sentences.en: Inside was a single line: 'The *rent* goes up again next month.'
The Manager's name was on it.
sentences.cn: 店长的名字在上面。

sentences.en: I slid it back quietly, but the number I had glimpsed stayed in my head all night.
sentences.cn: 我悄悄地把它放回去，但我瞥到的那个数字在我脑子里整晚都挥不去。

round:2.en: Each hour I do a *round* of the store — cooler, snack aisle, counter — checking for anything out of place. Tonight, on my third loop, I noticed a small paper crane sitting on top of the instant-noodle shelf. It had not been there before, and no customer had passed that aisle.
round:2.cnHint: 我在例行巡查时，发现货架上多了一只无人认领的纸鹤。
round:2.hook: Someone left it there on purpose — but who, and why?
round:2.line: 'Every *round* I do, I find something new and strange in here.'

sentences.en: Each hour I do a *round* of the store — cooler, snack aisle, counter — checking for anything out of place.
Tonight, on my third loop, I noticed a small paper crane sitting on top of the instant-noodle shelf.
sentences.cn: 今晚第三遍巡店时，我注意到方便面架顶上坐着一只小纸鹤。

sentences.cn: 它之前没在那儿，也没有顾客经过那条走廊。

structure:2.en: Tucked behind the staff lockers I found a blueprint of the store. Someone had sketched a new *structure* in pencil — an extra room drawn onto the side wall, with a question mark beside it. The Manager's initials were in the corner. I rolled it up carefully and said nothing.
structure:2.cnHint: 我在储物柜后发现了一张图纸，上面画着店铺改建的____。
structure:2.hook: Was that extra room meant for a second branch, or something else?
structure:2.line: 'The *structure* I have in mind will change everything about this store.'

sentences.en: Tucked behind the staff lockers I found a blueprint of the store.
sentences.cn: 我在员工更衣柜后面找到了一份店铺的蓝图。

sentences.en: Someone had sketched a new *structure* in pencil — an extra room drawn onto the side wall, with a question mark beside it.
The Manager's initials were in the corner.
sentences.cn: 店长的首字母缩写在角落里。

sentences.en: I rolled it up carefully and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 我小心地卷起来，什么都没说。

typical:2.en: A regular customer left her umbrella again — third time this week. Tang shook his head. 'So *typical*,' he said, carrying it to the lost-and-found box under the counter. But this time there was a note tied to the handle, and it was addressed to the Manager by name.
typical:2.cnHint: 常客又忘了雨伞，但这次伞上绑着一张写有店长名字的纸条。
typical:2.hook: What message had she hidden inside that folded note?
typical:2.line: 'It is so *typical* of her — but this note is anything but usual.'

sentences.en: A regular customer left her umbrella again — third time this week.
sentences.cn: 一个常客又落下了她的伞——这周第三次。

sentences.en: Tang shook his head.
sentences.cn: 阿糖摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'So *typical*,' he said, carrying it to the lost-and-found box under the counter.
But this time there was a note tied to the handle, and it was addressed to the Manager by name.
sentences.cn: 但这次伞把上系着一张纸条，是写给店长的。

vacation:2.en: I was sorting the magazine rack near the window when I spotted a postcard on the floor. The front showed a sunny beach. The back said: 'Took a small *vacation* to think things over. Back soon. — T.' It was addressed to no one. I set it on the counter and waited.
vacation:2.cnHint: 我在杂志架旁捡到一张明信片，上面说某人趁____想清楚了一些事。
vacation:2.hook: 'T' could be Tang — but Tang was standing right beside me.
vacation:2.line: 'A short *vacation* was all I needed to make up my mind.'

sentences.en: I was sorting the magazine rack near the window when I spotted a postcard on the floor.

sentences.en: The front showed a sunny beach.
sentences.cn: 正面是个阳光沙滩。

sentences.en: The back said: 'Took a small *vacation* to think things over.
Back soon. — T.'
sentences.cn: 回来了。——阿糖。

sentences.en: It was addressed to no one.
sentences.cn: 上面没有收件人。

sentences.en: I set it on the counter and waited.

acquire:2.en: While wiping down the shelves I found a slim notebook wedged behind the soy sauce. The first page said: 'Skills to *acquire* before we open the new branch.' Below it was a neat list in Lin's handwriting — including one item I did not expect to see my own name beside.

acquire:2.hook: Why was my name written next to the last item on that list?
acquire:2.line: 'We need to *acquire* these skills fast if the new branch opens in spring.'

sentences.en: While wiping down the shelves I found a slim notebook wedged behind the soy sauce.

sentences.en: The first page said: 'Skills to *acquire* before we open the new branch.'
Below it was a neat list in Lin's handwriting — including one item I did not expect to see my own name beside.
sentences.cn: 下面是隔壁咖啡店的林的工整笔迹——其中一项后面写着我的名字，这是我没想到的。

adequate:2.en: The Manager left a checklist on the desk before going out. At the top, underlined twice, were the words: 'Is the space *adequate*?' Below that, an address I did not recognise — three streets away. I checked the clock. The Manager had been gone for exactly one hour.
adequate:2.cnHint: 店长留下了一份清单，询问某个地址的空间是否____，随后独自外出。
adequate:2.hook: Three streets away — could that be the site of the new branch?
adequate:2.line: 'Tell me honestly: is the back room *adequate* for a second counter?'

sentences.en: The Manager left a checklist on the desk before going out.
sentences.cn: 店长出门前在桌子上留了一份清单。

sentences.en: At the top, underlined twice, were the words: 'Is the space *adequate*?'
Below that, an address I did not recognise — three streets away.
sentences.cn: 下面是我没见过的一个地址——三条街外。

sentences.en: I checked the clock.
sentences.cn: 我看了看钟。

sentences.en: The Manager had been gone for exactly one hour.
sentences.cn: 店长已经出门整整一小时了。

conventional:2.en: The Manager spread a map across the counter and pointed to our store, then to a spot two blocks east. 'The new branch needs a fresh look,' he said. 'Nothing *conventional* — no plain white walls, no standard shelves. We want people to walk in and feel something different.' I stared at the map and tried to imagine it.
conventional:2.cnHint: 店长展开地图，说新分店不能走____的风格。
conventional:2.hook: But Lin had already sketched a very different design.
conventional:2.line: 'Nothing *conventional* — we want every customer to stop and stare.'

sentences.en: The Manager spread a map across the counter and pointed to our store, then to a spot two blocks east.
sentences.cn: 店长把地图铺在收银台上，指了指我们的店，然后指向东边两个街区。

sentences.en: 'The new branch needs a fresh look,' he said.
sentences.cn: '新分店需要焕然一新，'他说。

sentences.en: 'Nothing *conventional* — no plain white walls, no standard shelves.
We want people to walk in and feel something different.'
sentences.cn: 我们想让人走进来就感受到不一样的东西。

sentences.en: I stared at the map and tried to imagine it.
sentences.cn: 我盯着地图，试图想象那个样子。

disappear:2.en: Tang was restocking the back room when he noticed three boxes of the new store's sample cups were gone. 'They were here an hour ago,' he said, looking pale. Stock does not simply *disappear* from a locked room. I checked the log, found no record of anyone signing them out, and felt a cold knot form in my stomach.
disappear:2.cnHint: 唐发现新店的样品杯凭空____了，没有任何领用记录。
disappear:2.hook: The security camera, we soon found, had been unplugged.
disappear:2.line: 'Things don't just *disappear* — someone took them on purpose.'

sentences.en: Tang was restocking the back room when he noticed three boxes of the new store's sample cups were gone.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在后仓整货时发现新店样品杯的三盒不见了。

sentences.en: 'They were here an hour ago,' he said, looking pale.
sentences.cn: '一小时前还在这儿，'他说，脸色发白。

sentences.en: Stock does not simply *disappear* from a locked room.
I checked the log, found no record of anyone signing them out, and felt a cold knot form in my stomach.
sentences.cn: 我查了日志，没有任何人签出的记录，感到一股寒意攫住了我的胃。

district:2.en: The Manager handed me a printed report about foot traffic in the east *district* where the new branch would open. The numbers were strong: office workers at lunch, students in the evening, families on weekends. He tapped the page twice. 'This is why we chose that corner,' he said. I read every line twice.
district:2.cnHint: 店长拿出一份关于新店所在____的人流报告，数据相当亮眼。
district:2.hook: Lin's face stayed blank the whole time the Manager spoke.
district:2.line: 'That *district* has more young customers than anywhere else in town.'

sentences.en: The Manager handed me a printed report about foot traffic in the east *district* where the new branch would open.
The numbers were strong: office workers at lunch, students in the evening, families on weekends.
sentences.cn: 数字很漂亮——午餐时间上班族，傍晚学生，周末家庭。

sentences.en: He tapped the page twice.
sentences.cn: 他在页面上敲了两下。

sentences.en: 'This is why we chose that corner,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他说，这就是我们选那个角落的原因。

sentences.en: I read every line twice.
sentences.cn: 我把每一行都读了两遍。

greatly:2.en: After the Manager pinned the new branch's floor plan to the wall, Tang studied it for a long time. 'The storage space is *greatly* improved,' he said, almost to himself. He had complained about our cramped back room for months. I watched his shoulders relax for the first time all week, and thought: maybe he wants to transfer there.
greatly:2.cnHint: 唐看着新分店的平面图，发现储物空间____改善了，神情若有所思。
greatly:2.hook: He folded the plan carefully and slipped it into his pocket.
greatly:2.line: 'The storage here is *greatly* improved — I could actually breathe back there.'

sentences.en: After the Manager pinned the new branch's floor plan to the wall, Tang studied it for a long time.
sentences.cn: 店长把新店的平面图钉到墙上后，阿糖盯着看了好久。

sentences.en: 'The storage space is *greatly* improved,' he said, almost to himself.
He had complained about our cramped back room for months.
sentences.cn: 他为咱们那间狭窄的后房抱怨了好几个月。

sentences.en: I watched his shoulders relax for the first time all week, and thought: maybe he wants to transfer there.
sentences.cn: 我看着他的肩膀第一次在这一周放松下来，心想，也许他想调到那边去。

imitate:2.en: Lin arrived late and spent ten minutes studying the display at our store before saying anything. 'The new branch shouldn't just *imitate* us,' she said, setting a folder on the counter. 'Copy the layout and we copy the problems too.' No one answered right away. Outside, a bus rolled past and its headlights swept across the ceiling.
imitate:2.cnHint: 林认为新分店不应该只是____我们现有的布局，否则会复制同样的问题。
imitate:2.hook: Her folder, I noticed, was already full of her own plans.
imitate:2.line: 'Why *imitate* the old store when we can build something better?'

sentences.en: Lin arrived late and spent ten minutes studying the display at our store before saying anything.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林迟到了，走进来先花了十分钟研究咱们店的陈列，才开口说话。

sentences.en: 'The new branch shouldn't just *imitate* us,' she said, setting a folder on the counter.
'Copy the layout and we copy the problems too.'
sentences.cn: 照搬布局，问题也跟着来。

sentences.en: No one answered right away.
sentences.cn: 没人马上应声。

sentences.en: Outside, a bus rolled past and its headlights swept across the ceiling.
sentences.cn: 外面一辆公交车经过，它的车灯扫过天花板。

implement:2.en: The Manager placed a worn spatula, a pricing gun, and a box cutter on the counter. 'Every *implement* we use here has to be standard across both stores,' he said. 'Same tools, same steps, same result.' Tang nodded. I picked up the pricing gun and felt, oddly, that holding it made the second store suddenly real.
implement:2.cnHint: 店长把几件常用____摆在柜台上，说两家店的操作规范必须统一。
implement:2.hook: Tang quietly moved the box cutter to the far end of the counter.
implement:2.line: 'Each *implement* gets labeled so nothing wanders between the two stores.'

sentences.en: The Manager placed a worn spatula, a pricing gun, and a box cutter on the counter.
sentences.cn: 店长在柜台上摆了一把旧刮板、一把标价枪和一把美工刀。

sentences.en: 'Every *implement* we use here has to be standard across both stores,' he said.
'Same tools, same steps, same result.'
sentences.cn: 同样的工具，同样的步骤，同样的结果。

sentences.en: Tang nodded.
sentences.cn: 阿糖点了点头。

sentences.en: I picked up the pricing gun and felt, oddly, that holding it made the second store suddenly real.
sentences.cn: 我拿起标价枪，奇异地感到，握着它让第二家店突然变得真实了。

mood:2.en: I came in for my shift to find the Manager sitting alone at the small corner table, coffee untouched. Tang whispered that the landlord of the new building had called with a problem. The whole store felt the Manager's *mood* — even the hum of the drinks fridge seemed quieter. I made fresh coffee without being asked and slid it over.
mood:2.cnHint: 店长独自坐着不说话，整家店都感受到了他低落的____。
mood:2.hook: He wrapped both hands around the cup and finally looked up.
mood:2.line: 'My *mood* has nothing to do with you two — the landlord is the problem.'

sentences.en: I came in for my shift to find the Manager sitting alone at the small corner table, coffee untouched.
sentences.cn: 我来上班，发现店长独自坐在小角落的桌子旁，咖啡没动过。

sentences.en: Tang whispered that the landlord of the new building had called with a problem.
sentences.cn: 阿糖小声说新楼的房东打来电话说有问题。

sentences.en: The whole store felt the Manager's *mood* — even the hum of the drinks fridge seemed quieter.
I made fresh coffee without being asked and slid it over.
sentences.cn: 我没人让我就泡了新咖啡，推了过去。

motivation:2.en: Tang pulled me aside near the magazine rack and spoke quietly. 'The Manager is offering a bonus to whoever helps the new branch reach its first-month target,' he said. I felt something light up in my chest. A clear reward is powerful *motivation* — far better than a vague promise. I straightened my name badge and went back to the counter with new energy.
motivation:2.cnHint: 唐悄悄告诉我，店长设了奖金，这给了我强大的____去帮新店完成目标。
motivation:2.hook: Lin was already at the counter, smiling at the Manager.
motivation:2.line: 'A real bonus is the best *motivation* you can give a night-shift clerk.'

sentences.en: Tang pulled me aside near the magazine rack and spoke quietly.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在杂志架边拉到我，压低声音说。

sentences.en: 'The Manager is offering a bonus to whoever helps the new branch reach its first-month target,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他说，店长在给新店帮助达成第一个月目标的人发奖金。

sentences.en: I felt something light up in my chest.
sentences.cn: 我心里一下子亮了起来。

sentences.en: A clear reward is powerful *motivation* — far better than a vague promise.
I straightened my name badge and went back to the counter with new energy.
sentences.cn: 我理了理胸牌，带着新的能量回到柜台。

worldwide:2.en: Late at night, the Manager unrolled a large map on the counter. Red dots marked cities across every continent. 'Our parent company sells snacks *worldwide*,' he said proudly, tapping a dot near the sea. I stared at all those dots and wondered why our tiny store kept running out of milk.
worldwide:2.cnHint: 店长展开一张地图，自豪地介绍母公司的____业务。
worldwide:2.hook: But one red dot had a question mark drawn over it.
worldwide:2.line: 'Our snacks sell *worldwide*, yet this store can't keep milk stocked!'

sentences.en: Late at night, the Manager unrolled a large map on the counter.
sentences.cn: 深夜，店长在柜台上铺开一张大地图。

sentences.en: Red dots marked cities across every continent.
sentences.cn: 红点标记了世界各地的城市。

sentences.en: 'Our parent company sells snacks *worldwide*,' he said proudly, tapping a dot near the sea.
I stared at all those dots and wondered why our tiny store kept running out of milk.
sentences.cn: 我盯着所有这些点，纳闷为什么咱们这么小的店总是奶不够卖。

accomplish:2.en: Tang taped a handwritten list to the staff-room wall: restock shelves, fix the broken fan, sort expired goods, mop the back room. 'We must *accomplish* all of this before six,' she said calmly. I looked at the clock. It was already four forty-five.
accomplish:2.cnHint: 阿糖贴出任务清单，要求在天亮前____所有工作。
accomplish:2.hook: Then the lights in the back room went out completely.
accomplish:2.line: 'We need to *accomplish* every task before the morning rush arrives.'

sentences.en: Tang taped a handwritten list to the staff-room wall: restock shelves, fix the broken fan, sort expired goods, mop the back room.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在员工室墙上贴了一张手写清单：补货架、修坏风扇、整理过期商品、拖后房。

sentences.en: 'We must *accomplish* all of this before six,' she said calmly.
I looked at the clock.
sentences.cn: 我看了一眼时钟。

sentences.en: It was already four forty-five.
sentences.cn: 已经四点四十五分了。

address:2.en: A delivery driver handed me a small package and said the *address* on the label did not match any building on our street. I checked twice. The store name was right, but the street number was impossible — our block only went up to forty. Someone had sent this on purpose.
address:2.cnHint: 快递员送来一个包裹，但上面的____让人困惑。
address:2.hook: Inside, folded neatly, was a single key.
address:2.line: 'The *address* on this box makes no sense — your block ends at forty.'

sentences.en: A delivery driver handed me a small package and said the *address* on the label did not match any building on our street.
I checked twice.
sentences.cn: 我检查了两遍。

sentences.en: The store name was right, but the street number was impossible — our block only went up to forty.
sentences.cn: 店名对，但街号不对——咱们这条街只到四十号。

sentences.en: Someone had sent this on purpose.
sentences.cn: 这是有人故意寄来的。

barely:2.en: Lin walked in just as I finished arranging a neat pyramid of canned drinks. She glanced at it and then nudged the bottom can just slightly. The whole pyramid trembled. 'This store can *barely* hold itself together,' she said with a small smile, and walked to the back fridge.
barely:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林轻轻碰了一下饮料堆，笑着说这家店____能维持。
barely:2.hook: She stayed near the back fridge far longer than she needed to.
barely:2.line: 'This display can *barely* survive one customer — let alone a busy morning.'

sentences.en: Lin walked in just as I finished arranging a neat pyramid of canned drinks.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林走进来的时候，我刚好把一排罐头摆成了漂亮的金字塔。

sentences.en: She glanced at it and then nudged the bottom can just slightly.
sentences.cn: 她瞥了一眼，然后轻轻推了底下的一个罐头。

sentences.en: The whole pyramid trembled.
sentences.cn: 整个金字塔颤动了。

sentences.en: 'This store can *barely* hold itself together,' she said with a small smile, and walked to the back fridge.

blame:2.en: A jar of pickles fell from the top shelf and shattered at two in the morning. The Manager appeared from nowhere, looked at the mess, looked at me, then looked at Tang. No one spoke for a moment. 'Let's not *blame* anyone,' Tang said quietly. 'Let's just clean it up.'
blame:2.cnHint: 泡菜罐摔碎了，店长和阿糖都沉默片刻，阿糖说不必互相____。
blame:2.hook: The Manager's eyes, however, stayed on me a second too long.
blame:2.line: 'Let's not *blame* each other — just get the mop and move on.'

sentences.en: A jar of pickles fell from the top shelf and shattered at two in the morning.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点一罐泡菜从顶层架上掉了下来，碎了。

sentences.en: The Manager appeared from nowhere, looked at the mess, looked at me, then looked at Tang.
sentences.cn: 店长凭空出现，看了一眼狼藉，看了一眼我，又看了一眼阿糖。

sentences.en: No one spoke for a moment.
sentences.cn: 没人说话。

sentences.en: 'Let's not *blame* anyone,' Tang said quietly.
'Let's just clean it up.'
sentences.cn: 阿糖静静地说，咱们别追究谁的责任了，收拾干净就行。

chat:2.en: Around three in the morning a man in a raincoat came in, bought nothing, and stood by the magazine rack. After a while he looked up and asked if he could *chat* with someone for a bit. He said the night was very long. I put down my cloth and leaned on the counter.
chat:2.cnHint: 一个雨夜来客什么也不买，只想和人____一会儿。
chat:2.hook: An hour later, he mentioned he used to own this building.
chat:2.line: 'Can I *chat* with you for a while? The night feels very long tonight.'

sentences.en: Around three in the morning a man in a raincoat came in, bought nothing, and stood by the magazine rack.
sentences.cn: 凌晨三点左右，一个穿雨衣的男人走进来，什么都没买，靠在杂志架旁。

sentences.en: After a while he looked up and asked if he could *chat* with someone for a bit.
He said the night was very long.
sentences.cn: 他说夜太长了。

sentences.en: I put down my cloth and leaned on the counter.
sentences.cn: 我放下抹布，靠在柜台上。

combat:2.en: Tiny ants had found the honey shelf. Tang pulled on gloves, armed herself with spray and a cloth, and moved with great focus. 'Night-shift *combat*,' she said seriously, without looking up. I handed her a fresh cloth. We worked in silence until every last ant was gone and the shelf shone.
combat:2.cnHint: 蚂蚁入侵了蜂蜜货架，阿糖严肃地把这场清理称为____。
combat:2.hook: In the morning, a whole new line of ants appeared from behind the wall.
combat:2.line: 'Night-shift *combat* — hand me that cloth and don't let them reach the sugar.'

sentences.en: Tiny ants had found the honey shelf.
sentences.cn: 小蚂蚁们找到了放蜂蜜的架子。

sentences.en: Tang pulled on gloves, armed herself with spray and a cloth, and moved with great focus.
sentences.cn: 阿糖戴上手套，拿起喷雾和布，专注地动起来。

sentences.en: 'Night-shift *combat*,' she said seriously, without looking up.
I handed her a fresh cloth.
sentences.cn: 我递给她一块干净的布。

sentences.en: We worked in silence until every last ant was gone and the shelf shone.
sentences.cn: 我们沉默地工作，直到最后一只蚂蚁消失，架子闪闪发亮。

danger:2.en: The Manager called me to the storeroom and pointed at a shelf bending under the weight of too many heavy boxes. 'That is a real *danger*,' he said. 'Do not touch it until I bring a new shelf tomorrow.' He left. I stood there, watching the shelf slowly creak and lean a little more.
danger:2.cnHint: 仓库里有一排超重货架，店长警告那是真正的____。
danger:2.hook: Then one bolt near the bottom quietly pinged across the floor.
danger:2.line: 'That shelf is a real *danger* — stay away from it until tomorrow morning.'

sentences.en: The Manager called me to the storeroom and pointed at a shelf bending under the weight of too many heavy boxes.
sentences.cn: 店长把我叫进储藏室，指了指一个被太多重箱子压得弯曲的架子。

sentences.en: 'That is a real *danger*,' he said.
'Do not touch it until I bring a new shelf tomorrow.'
sentences.cn: 在我带来新架子之前，别碰它。

sentences.en: He left.
sentences.cn: 他离开了。

sentences.en: I stood there, watching the shelf slowly creak and lean a little more.
sentences.cn: 我站在那儿，看着架子慢慢地吱吱呀呀地响着，又往下倾斜了一点。

threaten:2.en: A note was taped to the back door when I arrived for my shift. It read: 'Open a second store on Oak Street and we will take all your customers.' I showed it to the Manager. He read it twice, folded it carefully, and smiled. 'Anyone who has to *threaten* us,' he said, 'is already afraid of us.'
threaten:2.cnHint: 我在后门发现一张字条，有人____要抢走我们所有顾客。
threaten:2.hook: But the Manager's smile faded the moment he thought I wasn't looking.
threaten:2.line: 'Anyone who has to *threaten* us is already afraid of us.'

sentences.en: A note was taped to the back door when I arrived for my shift.
sentences.cn: 我上班时发现后门上贴了张纸条。

sentences.en: It read: 'Open a second store on Oak Street and we will take all your customers.'
sentences.cn: 上面写着："在橡树街开第二家店，我们就会把你所有的顾客都抢走。"

sentences.en: I showed it to the Manager.
sentences.cn: 我把它给店长看了。

sentences.en: He read it twice, folded it carefully, and smiled.
sentences.cn: 他读了两遍，小心地折好，然后笑了。

sentences.en: 'Anyone who has to *threaten* us,' he said, 'is already afraid of us.'

throw:2.en: Opening a second store felt like a huge *throw* of the dice. The Manager spread maps and cost sheets across the counter at two in the morning, circling numbers and crossing them out. I swept the floor around his papers and said nothing. Some bets, I have learned, are best made in silence.
throw:2.cnHint: 开分店对店长来说是一次巨大的____，他深夜在柜台上研究地图和费用表。
throw:2.hook: Then Lin walked in, glanced at the maps, and her eyes went sharp.
throw:2.line: 'This whole plan is one big *throw* of the dice, Manager.'

sentences.en: Opening a second store felt like a huge *throw* of the dice.
The Manager spread maps and cost sheets across the counter at two in the morning, circling numbers and crossing them out.
sentences.cn: 店长在凌晨两点把地图和成本表铺在柜台上，圈圈画画。

sentences.en: I swept the floor around his papers and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 我在他的纸张周围扫地，什么也没说。

sentences.en: Some bets, I have learned, are best made in silence.
sentences.cn: 我发现，有些赌注最好是沉默地下的。

unlike:2.en: The new site was on the west side of town. I visited it on my lunch break. It was *unlike* our cosy corner store in every way: wide glass windows, bright overhead lights, a car park outside. I stood on the pavement and tried to imagine Tang stocking shelves in all that cold space.
unlike:2.cnHint: 新选址和我们温馨的角落小店____，我站在门口想象着那里的样子。
unlike:2.hook: A sign on the door said the lease had already been signed by someone else.
unlike:2.line: 'It is so *unlike* our store — I am not sure it feels right.'

sentences.en: The new site was on the west side of town.
sentences.cn: 新店址在镇的西边。

sentences.en: I visited it on my lunch break.
sentences.cn: 我在午休时去看了看。

sentences.en: It was *unlike* our cosy corner store in every way: wide glass windows, bright overhead lights, a car park outside.
I stood on the pavement and tried to imagine Tang stocking shelves in all that cold space.
sentences.cn: 我站在人行道上，想象着阿糖在那冷冰冰的大空间里整理架子。

vast:2.en: The storeroom in the new location was *vast*. Tang and I walked through it after the Manager got the keys. Our footsteps echoed. Back in our little store, every centimetre of shelf space is fought over. Here, whole walls stood empty, waiting. Tang spread her arms wide and slowly turned around.
vast:2.cnHint: 新店的库房____，唐和我在空荡荡的货架间走着，脚步声回响在空气中。
vast:2.hook: Tang stopped turning and stared at one dark corner without speaking.
vast:2.line: 'The storeroom is *vast* — we could stock enough for a whole neighbourhood.'

sentences.en: The storeroom in the new location was *vast*.
Tang and I walked through it after the Manager got the keys.
sentences.cn: 店长拿到钥匙后，阿糖和我走过了储藏室。

sentences.en: Our footsteps echoed.
sentences.cn: 我们的脚步声回荡着。

sentences.en: Back in our little store, every centimetre of shelf space is fought over.

absolutely:2.en: The Manager asked if I would take the night shift at the new store once it opened. I looked around our quiet corner: the humming fridge, the stack of warm buns, the regular who always bought one coffee at midnight. I took a slow breath. '*Absolutely*,' I said, and was surprised to mean it.

absolutely:2.hook: The midnight regular looked up from his coffee with wide eyes.
absolutely:2.line: '*Absolutely* — I will take the night shift at the new store.'

Regulars had heard about the new store and were offering quiet good wishes. 'Look at all this,' Tang said. 'You *accumulate* supporters without even trying.' I did not know what to say.

accumulate:2.line: 'You *accumulate* supporters without even trying — that is a real gift.'

'We *breakfast* together before the big decision,' he announced. The warm smell filled the store. Outside, the street was pale and quiet and full of possibility.

Three times the fridges, three times the shelf space.' I studied the numbers. Three times bigger also meant three times more things that could go wrong.

promise:2.line: 'I *promise* you, that location will beat yours by summer.'

rarely:2.hook: He pulled out a tape measure, and my heart jumped a little.
rarely:2.line: 'I *rarely* visit nights, but this shelf tells me everything I need.'

embrace:2.en: The Manager spread both arms wide the moment he stepped through the door of the new branch space, an empty room still smelling of paint. 'We *embrace* every challenge,' he told the bare walls, nodding slowly. Tang caught my eye behind his back and pressed both lips together very hard to keep from laughing.
embrace:2.cnHint: 店长张开双臂，说要____一切挑战，但新店只是一间空屋子。
embrace:2.hook: Then the Manager turned around and asked Tang to price the ceiling tiles.
embrace:2.line: 'We *embrace* every challenge, no matter how empty the room looks.'

sentences.en: The Manager spread both arms wide the moment he stepped through the door of the new branch space, an empty room still smelling of paint.
sentences.cn: 店长一踏进新分店的空房间，立刻张开双臂，房间里还飘着油漆的味道。

sentences.en: 'We *embrace* every challenge,' he told the bare walls, nodding slowly.
Tang caught my eye behind his back and pressed both lips together very hard to keep from laughing.
sentences.cn: 阿糖从他背后朝我使眼色，抿紧嘴唇才勉强忍住笑。

explanation:2.en: I found a second set of keys taped under the front counter with a small label: 'Branch B.' Nobody had mentioned a Branch B to me. I asked Tang, who shrugged. I asked the Manager, who gave a long *explanation* about permits and timing that somehow answered nothing. The keys stayed under the counter, waiting.
explanation:2.cnHint: 钥匙上写着"B分店"，店长给了一番____，但什么也没说清楚。
explanation:2.hook: That evening Lin came in and glanced straight at the spot where the keys were hidden.
explanation:2.line: 'The *explanation* is simple — the branch opens when the permit comes through.'

sentences.en: I found a second set of keys taped under the front counter with a small label: 'Branch B.'
sentences.cn: 我在前台下面发现了第二把钥匙，用胶带贴着，上面有个小标签："分店B。"

sentences.en: Nobody had mentioned a Branch B to me.
sentences.cn: 没人跟我提过分店B。

sentences.en: I asked Tang, who shrugged.
sentences.cn: 我问阿糖，他耸了耸肩。

sentences.en: I asked the Manager, who gave a long *explanation* about permits and timing that somehow answered nothing.
The keys stayed under the counter, waiting.
sentences.cn: 钥匙就这样留在台下，等待着。

intend:2.en: Lin walked in at two in the morning carrying a floor plan rolled under one arm. She spread it on the counter without asking, pointed to a red circle near the corner, and said she *intended* to put a coffee bar exactly there. I looked at the map. That corner was inside our store.
intend:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带着平面图来，说她____把咖啡台设在地图上圈出的地方。
intend:2.hook: The red circle sat twelve centimetres inside our property line.
intend:2.line: 'I *intend* to have that coffee bar running before your branch even opens.'

sentences.en: Lin walked in at two in the morning carrying a floor plan rolled under one arm.
sentences.cn: 林在凌晨两点走了进来，腋下夹着一份卷起来的平面图。

sentences.en: She spread it on the counter without asking, pointed to a red circle near the corner, and said she *intended* to put a coffee bar exactly there.
I looked at the map.
