sentences.en: That corner was inside our store.
sentences.cn: 那个角落在我们的店里面。

leadership:2.en: The Manager pinned a printed chart to the wall showing every task for the new branch opening. His own name sat at the top under the word *leadership*. Below it were two names: Tang and mine. Tang leaned close and whispered, 'Count the tasks under our names. Then count his.' I counted. It was not close.
leadership:2.cnHint: 店长贴出任务表，把____写在自己名字旁边，但任务全落在别人身上。
leadership:2.hook: Tang was already circling three items in red marker.
leadership:2.line: 'Good *leadership* means giving the hard work to the people you trust most.'

sentences.en: The Manager pinned a printed chart to the wall showing every task for the new branch opening.
sentences.cn: 店长在墙上钉了一张打印的表格，列出了新分店开业的每一项任务。

sentences.en: His own name sat at the top under the word *leadership*.
Below it were two names: Tang and mine.
sentences.cn: 下面是两个名字：阿糖和我。

sentences.en: Tang leaned close and whispered, 'Count the tasks under our names.
sentences.cn: 阿糖凑过来，小声说："数一下我们名字下面的任务数。

sentences.en: Then count his.'
sentences.cn: 再数他的。"

sentences.en: I counted.
sentences.cn: 我数了。

sentences.en: It was not close.
sentences.cn: 差得不是一点半点。

locate:2.en: The Manager asked me to *locate* the spare price-tag gun before the new branch opened. I checked every drawer, the back shelf, the box above the freezer, and the locked cabinet that Tang opened with a key from her lanyard. We found it inside a noodle cup on the top shelf. Nobody admitted putting it there.
locate:2.cnHint: 店长让我____备用价格标签枪，最后在一个面杯里找到了它。
locate:2.hook: The noodle cup had been opened and carefully resealed.
locate:2.line: '*Locate* it fast — we need to tag three hundred items by morning.'

sentences.en: The Manager asked me to *locate* the spare price-tag gun before the new branch opened.
I checked every drawer, the back shelf, the box above the freezer, and the locked cabinet that Tang opened with a key from her lanyard.
sentences.cn: 我查了每个抽屉、后面的架子、冰箱上方的盒子，还有阿糖用她钥匙扣上的钥匙打开的上锁柜子。

sentences.en: We found it inside a noodle cup on the top shelf.
sentences.cn: 我们在最上面的架子上一个面碗里找到了它。

sentences.en: Nobody admitted putting it there.
sentences.cn: 没人承认是谁放进去的。

original:2.en: Tang held up two logos printed on paper — one clean and modern, one hand-drawn with small stars around the store name. 'The Manager wants the clean one,' she said. 'But this star one is the *original* design, from when he first opened.' She looked at it for a long moment, then rolled it gently and slid it into her bag.
original:2.cnHint: 阿糖展示了两个标志，那个有星星的是店长最____的设计手稿。
original:2.hook: I noticed the roll of paper had a date on it — seven years ago.
original:2.line: 'The *original* design had stars — I think he forgot how much he loved them.'

sentences.en: Tang held up two logos printed on paper — one clean and modern, one hand-drawn with small stars around the store name.
sentences.cn: 阿糖举起两张打印的标志——一张干净现代，一张手绘的，店名周围还画着小星星。

sentences.en: 'The Manager wants the clean one,' she said.
sentences.cn: "店长要那个干净的，"她说。

sentences.en: 'But this star one is the *original* design, from when he first opened.'
She looked at it for a long moment, then rolled it gently and slid it into her bag.
sentences.cn: 她看了那张手绘的很久，然后轻轻地卷起来，塞进了她的包里。

overcome:2.en: The new branch sign arrived with the store name spelled wrong. The Manager sat on a crate outside and stared at it for three full minutes. Then he stood up, rolled his sleeves, and said we would *overcome* this small problem with a marker pen and a steady hand. Tang offered her hand. The Manager looked at it, then at her neat writing on the task chart.
overcome:2.cnHint: 新店招牌名字拼错了，店长说要____这个小问题，但需要一双稳当的手。
overcome:2.hook: Tang was already uncapping the marker before he finished the sentence.
overcome:2.line: 'We will *overcome* this — hand me the marker and stand back a little.'

sentences.en: The new branch sign arrived with the store name spelled wrong.
sentences.cn: 新分店的招牌送来了，店名被拼错了。

sentences.en: The Manager sat on a crate outside and stared at it for three full minutes.
sentences.cn: 店长坐在一个木箱上，盯着它看了整整三分钟。

sentences.en: Then he stood up, rolled his sleeves, and said we would *overcome* this small problem with a marker pen and a steady hand.
Tang offered her hand.
sentences.cn: 阿糖伸出了她的手。

sentences.en: The Manager looked at it, then at her neat writing on the task chart.
sentences.cn: 店长看了看她的手，又看了看她在任务表上整洁的笔迹。

consideration:2.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map across the counter just after midnight. 'We are opening a second store,' he said proudly. He had marked three possible street corners with small stars. '*Consideration* of foot traffic, nearby schools, and late-night bus stops all pointed to the same spot.' He tapped the middle star twice and smiled.
consideration:2.cnHint: 店长深夜拿出手绘地图，说明选址时综合了多项____。
consideration:2.hook: But the middle star was inside Lin's delivery zone.
consideration:2.line: '*Consideration* of the bus stop alone made this corner the clear winner.'

sentences.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map across the counter just after midnight.
sentences.cn: 店长在午夜刚过时，把一张手绘的地图铺在台子上。

sentences.en: 'We are opening a second store,' he said proudly.
sentences.cn: "我们要开第二家店，"他骄傲地说。

sentences.en: He had marked three possible street corners with small stars. '*Consideration* of foot traffic, nearby schools, and late-night bus stops all pointed to the same spot.'
He tapped the middle star twice and smiled.
sentences.cn: 他在中间的星星上点了两下，笑了。

disaster:2.en: Tang was restocking the instant noodle shelf when a full box slipped from his hands. Cups rolled everywhere, one knocked over a standing sign, and the sign hit a small bottle display. The bottles survived, but the sign did not. Tang stared at the mess. 'That,' he said quietly, 'was a *disaster*.' I handed him a broom without a word.
disaster:2.cnHint: 阿糖理货时一场小小的____让货架区乱成一片。
disaster:2.hook: The Manager's security camera had caught every second of it.
disaster:2.line: 'One dropped box and a total *disaster* — please don't tell the Manager.'

sentences.en: Tang was restocking the instant noodle shelf when a full box slipped from his hands.
sentences.cn: 阿糖正在补货方便面架子上的东西，一整盒突然从他手里滑下来。

sentences.en: Cups rolled everywhere, one knocked over a standing sign, and the sign hit a small bottle display.
sentences.cn: 杯子四处滚落，一个碰翻了一个立式招牌，招牌又打到了一个小瓶子的展示。

sentences.en: The bottles survived, but the sign did not.
sentences.cn: 瓶子完好无损，但招牌没有。

sentences.en: Tang stared at the mess.
sentences.cn: 阿糖盯着这一片狼狈。

sentences.en: 'That,' he said quietly, 'was a *disaster*.'
I handed him a broom without a word.
sentences.cn: 我递给他一把扫帚，什么都没说。

emergency:2.en: A folded note was taped to the staff-room door when I arrived for my shift. It read: 'Second-store opening moved to Friday. Stock transfer Thursday night. This is not an *emergency*, but please do not be late.' The Manager had underlined 'not' three times, which made it feel very much like one.
emergency:2.cnHint: 店长在门上贴了张字条，说分店开业提前了，虽然不是____，但请准时到岗。
emergency:2.hook: Friday was also the night Tang had already booked off.
emergency:2.line: 'It says not an *emergency*, but three underlines say otherwise.'

sentences.en: A folded note was taped to the staff-room door when I arrived for my shift.
sentences.cn: 我上班时，一张折叠的纸条被贴在员工休息室的门上。

sentences.en: It read: 'Second-store opening moved to Friday.
sentences.cn: 纸条上写着："二号店开业改到周五。

sentences.en: Stock transfer Thursday night.
sentences.cn: 周四晚上转移库存。

sentences.en: This is not an *emergency*, but please do not be late.'
The Manager had underlined 'not' three times, which made it feel very much like one.
sentences.cn: 店长把"不是"下面画了三条线，这让整件事看起来非常紧急。

familiar:2.en: A woman in a yellow coat walked in at two in the morning and went straight to the back shelf without looking at the signs. She picked up a specific brand of canned soup, checked nothing else, and brought it to me. Her face was *familiar* — I was certain I had seen her photo on the new-store planning board pinned in the staff room.
familiar:2.cnHint: 一位穿黄色外套的女士深夜径直走向货架，她的面孔对我来说____，在员工室的公告板上似乎见过。
familiar:2.hook: Her name tag, half hidden by her coat, read 'Site Manager.'
familiar:2.line: 'Your face is *familiar* — have you been in before, or am I imagining things?'

sentences.en: A woman in a yellow coat walked in at two in the morning and went straight to the back shelf without looking at the signs.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着黄色外套的女人凌晨两点走了进来，直奔后面的货架，都没看标牌。

sentences.en: She picked up a specific brand of canned soup, checked nothing else, and brought it to me.
sentences.cn: 她拿起一个特定品牌的罐装汤，什么都没再看，就拿来给我。

sentences.en: Her face was *familiar* — I was certain I had seen her photo on the new-store planning board pinned in the staff room.

furthermore:2.en: The Manager left a handwritten memo beside the register. It listed the new store's opening hours, its address, and which items would move there. '*Furthermore*,' the last line read, 'the night-shift clerk at the new store will be chosen from current staff.' I read that line four times before Tang leaned over and said, 'That means one of us.'
furthermore:2.cnHint: 店长的便条列出了分店信息，____还提到夜班员工将从现有员工中选出。
furthermore:2.hook: Tang had already circled the new address on his phone map.
furthermore:2.line: '*Furthermore*, the new store is only one bus stop from my apartment.'

sentences.en: The Manager left a handwritten memo beside the register.
sentences.cn: 店长在收银台旁边留了一张手写便签。

sentences.en: It listed the new store's opening hours, its address, and which items would move there. '*Furthermore*,' the last line read, 'the night-shift clerk at the new store will be chosen from current staff.'
I read that line four times before Tang leaned over and said, 'That means one of us.'
sentences.cn: 我读了那一行四遍，然后阿糖凑过来说，"意思就是我们中的一个。"

hardly:2.en: The supply delivery for the new store arrived at our back door by mistake. There were twelve large boxes stacked in the narrow corridor. I could *hardly* move between them to reach the shelf trolley. Tang squeezed past sideways, knocking a box of rice crackers off the top. We both froze. The box landed perfectly upright.
hardly:2.cnHint: 新分店的备货误送到本店后门，走廊被堆得____能通行。
hardly:2.hook: The delivery note listed one item that was not on our current stock list at all.
hardly:2.line: 'I can *hardly* get past — who ordered twelve boxes for a store that isn't open yet?'

sentences.en: The supply delivery for the new store arrived at our back door by mistake.
sentences.cn: 新店的供货在我们的后门误送到了。

sentences.en: There were twelve large boxes stacked in the narrow corridor.
sentences.cn: 走廊里堆着十二个大纸箱。

sentences.en: I could *hardly* move between them to reach the shelf trolley.
Tang squeezed past sideways, knocking a box of rice crackers off the top.
sentences.cn: 阿糖侧身挤过去，把顶上一盒米饼碰掉了。

sentences.en: We both froze.
sentences.cn: 我们都僵住了。

sentences.en: The box landed perfectly upright.
sentences.cn: 纸箱完美地竖着落地了。

hinder:2.en: Lin appeared at the door just as we were carrying the mislaid boxes back outside. He watched without offering to help. 'I hope the new store does not *hinder* my delivery times,' he said, arms folded. 'Your loading bay and mine share the same alley.' He left before I could answer, which I found both annoying and a little worrying.
hinder:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林出现在门口，担心新分店会____他的配送时间，因为两家共用同一条小巷。
hinder:2.hook: He already had a lawyer's business card in his shirt pocket.
hinder:2.line: 'A second store will *hinder* every driver in this alley, and you know it.'

sentences.en: Lin appeared at the door just as we were carrying the mislaid boxes back outside.
sentences.cn: 就在我们把那些送错的纸箱搬回外面时，林出现在门口。

sentences.en: He watched without offering to help.
sentences.cn: 他看着，什么忙都没帮。

sentences.en: 'I hope the new store does not *hinder* my delivery times,' he said, arms folded.
'Your loading bay and mine share the same alley.'
sentences.cn: "你的卸货区和我的在同一条巷子里。"

sentences.en: He left before I could answer, which I found both annoying and a little worrying.
sentences.cn: 他在我开口回答之前就走了，这让我既烦恼又有点担心。

injury:2.en: While I was moving the last box, I caught my wrist on the door frame. It was not serious, but I held it and winced. Tang looked alarmed. 'No *injury* report, no new-store transfer,' he warned, completely serious. I told him it was fine. He handed me a small bandage anyway, already peeled and ready, which meant he had been carrying one all night.
injury:2.cnHint: 我搬箱子时磕了手腕，阿糖一脸认真地警告说有____记录就别想调去新分店。
injury:2.hook: The bandage had tiny cartoon cats on it, which felt oddly comforting.
injury:2.line: 'Any *injury* on record and the Manager will pull you from the transfer list immediately.'

sentences.en: While I was moving the last box, I caught my wrist on the door frame.
sentences.cn: 我搬最后一个纸箱时，手腕在门框上擦伤了。

sentences.en: It was not serious, but I held it and winced.
sentences.cn: 伤不严重，但我按住了，龇牙咧嘴。

sentences.en: Tang looked alarmed.
sentences.cn: 阿糖看起来很惊慌。

sentences.en: 'No *injury* report, no new-store transfer,' he warned, completely serious.
I told him it was fine.
sentences.cn: 我跟他说没事。

sentences.en: He handed me a small bandage anyway, already peeled and ready, which meant he had been carrying one all night.
sentences.cn: 他还是递给我一个小创可贴，已经撕好了，这说明他整晚都带着一个。

lift:2.en: The Manager called me to the new branch store across town. There was no *lift* in the building, only a narrow staircase. I carried two heavy boxes of stock up four floors, stopping twice to catch my breath. By the top step, I found a handwritten note taped to the door.
lift:2.cnHint: 我帮店长把货物搬到新分店楼上，在门口发现了一张字条。
lift:2.hook: The note had no name, only three words: 'Don't open yet.'
lift:2.line: 'There is no *lift*, so watch your step on those stairs.'

sentences.en: The Manager called me to the new branch store across town.
sentences.cn: 店长叫我去城市另一边的新分店。

sentences.cn: 我搬着两个装货物的重纸箱上了四楼，中途停了两次喘气。

sentences.en: By the top step, I found a handwritten note taped to the door.
sentences.cn: 到了最上面一级台阶，我发现门上贴着一张手写便签。

mainly:2.en: The new branch store was *mainly* full of empty shelves when I arrived for the inspection. A few boxes sat in the corner, but most supplies had not come yet. I walked each aisle, making notes on my clipboard. Then I noticed one shelf already had items on it — things no one had ordered.
mainly:2.cnHint: 新分店的货架____是空的，但有一排货架上已经摆满了没人订购的商品。
mainly:2.hook: Every item on that shelf had the same strange label.
mainly:2.line: 'The store is *mainly* empty, but look at that one shelf over there.'

sentences.en: The new branch store was *mainly* full of empty shelves when I arrived for the inspection.
A few boxes sat in the corner, but most supplies had not come yet.
sentences.cn: 角落里放着几个纸箱，但大部分物资还没到。

sentences.en: I walked each aisle, making notes on my clipboard.
sentences.cn: 我走过每条过道，在剪贴板上记着笔记。

sentences.en: Then I noticed one shelf already had items on it — things no one had ordered.
sentences.cn: 然后我注意到一个货架上已经摆了东西——没人订过的东西。

moral:2.en: Tang found an old notebook in the back room of the new branch store. Inside were short stories, each ending with a *moral* written in careful handwriting. 'Honesty brings more customers than clever tricks,' read one. The last story had no ending — just a question mark on a blank page.
moral:2.cnHint: 唐在新分店的后室发现一本旧笔记本，每个故事都写有____，但最后一篇没有结局。
moral:2.hook: The handwriting in that last story matched the Manager's exactly.
moral:2.line: 'Every story here has a *moral*, except the very last one.'

sentences.en: Tang found an old notebook in the back room of the new branch store.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在新分店的后间发现了一本旧笔记本。

sentences.en: Inside were short stories, each ending with a *moral* written in careful handwriting.
'Honesty brings more customers than clever tricks,' read one.
sentences.cn: 其中一页写着："诚实比花招带来更多顾客。"

sentences.en: The last story had no ending — just a question mark on a blank page.

nor:2.en: I searched the new branch store from front to back. There was no sign of the delivery driver, *nor* any record of yesterday's shipment in the logbook. The loading bay door was unlocked. A single muddy boot print crossed the clean floor and stopped in the middle of the room.

nor:2.line: 'There is no driver here, *nor* is there any note about the delivery.'

sentences.en: I searched the new branch store from front to back.

sentences.en: There was no sign of the delivery driver, *nor* any record of yesterday's shipment in the logbook.
The loading bay door was unlocked.
sentences.cn: 卸货区的门没锁。

sentences.en: A single muddy boot print crossed the clean floor and stopped in the middle of the room.
sentences.cn: 一个泥泞的靴印穿过干净的地板，停在了房间中央。

pick:2.en: The Manager told me to *pick* one item from each box and check it before the new branch store opened. I worked through the first row easily enough. But the fifth box was sealed with three layers of tape and had no label on any side. I shook it gently — something shifted inside.
pick:2.cnHint: 店长让我从每箱货里____一件商品检查，但第五个箱子没有标签，里面有东西在晃动。
pick:2.hook: Whatever was inside moved again, all on its own.
pick:2.line: 'Please *pick* one item from each box and bring it to me.'

sentences.en: The Manager told me to *pick* one item from each box and check it before the new branch store opened.
I worked through the first row easily enough.
sentences.cn: 我轻易地完成了前几排。

sentences.cn: 但第五个纸箱用三层胶带封着，四面都没有标签。

sentences.en: I shook it gently — something shifted inside.

supermarket:2.en: Tucked under the new branch's counter I found a crumpled flyer from the big *supermarket* two streets away. Someone had circled its opening hours in red pen and scrawled 'competition?' across the top. The Manager smoothed it flat and pinned it to the wall without a word.
supermarket:2.cnHint: 我在柜台下发现了附近____的传单，上面有人用红笔写了一个问题。
supermarket:2.hook: The circled hours matched our quietest shift exactly.
supermarket:2.line: 'Why is a *supermarket* flyer hidden under our counter?' I asked.

sentences.en: Tucked under the new branch's counter I found a crumpled flyer from the big *supermarket* two streets away.
Someone had circled its opening hours in red pen and scrawled 'competition?' across the top.
sentences.cn: 有人用红笔圈出了它的营业时间，在上面潦草地写了"竞争对手？"

sentences.en: The Manager smoothed it flat and pinned it to the wall without a word.
sentences.cn: 店长把它摊平了，一句话没说就钉到墙上。

debate:2.en: Tang and I found two sets of store-layout sketches left on the back table, each by a different hand. One was neat, the other covered in crossing-out. There was clearly a long *debate* between two people about where the counter should go. We could not tell who had won.
debate:2.cnHint: 唐和我发现了两份关于新店布局的草图，显示出一场激烈的____痕迹。
debate:2.hook: The Manager went pale the moment he saw the sketches.
debate:2.line: Tang said, 'Looks like someone had a serious *debate* about this counter.'

sentences.en: Tang and I found two sets of store-layout sketches left on the back table, each by a different hand.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我在后面的桌子上发现了两份店铺布局草图，笔迹完全不同。

sentences.en: One was neat, the other covered in crossing-out.
sentences.cn: 一份画得很整洁，另一份密密麻麻都是涂改。

sentences.en: There was clearly a long *debate* between two people about where the counter should go.
We could not tell who had won.
sentences.cn: 我们根本看不出谁赢了这场争论。

egg:2.en: Behind the back shelf, I found a small basket with a single *egg* sitting inside it. A note was taped to the basket: 'Keep this safe. Do not sell.' The Manager's handwriting. I had no idea why one egg needed guarding, but I put it back carefully.
egg:2.cnHint: 我在货架后面发现了一个篮子，里面放着一颗被特别叮嘱保管的____。
egg:2.hook: Then I noticed the egg was ever so slightly warm.
egg:2.line: 'That *egg* is not for sale — not for any price,' the Manager said.

sentences.en: Behind the back shelf, I found a small basket with a single *egg* sitting inside it.
A note was taped to the basket: 'Keep this safe.
sentences.cn: 篮子上贴着一张纸条："保管好这个。

sentences.en: Do not sell.'
sentences.cn: 不许卖。"

sentences.en: The Manager's handwriting.
sentences.cn: 店长的笔迹。

sentences.en: I had no idea why one egg needed guarding, but I put it back carefully.
sentences.cn: 我想不出为什么一个鸡蛋需要被看守，但还是小心地把它放了回去。

hire:2.en: A folded letter sat on the back counter, addressed to the Manager. I should not have read it, but the words 'new *hire*' caught my eye. Someone was being brought on for the second branch. The name on the letter made me set it down very quickly.
hire:2.cnHint: 柜台上有一封信，提到新分店即将有新的____加入，那个名字让我大吃一惊。
hire:2.hook: The name on that letter was someone I already knew.
hire:2.line: 'The new *hire* starts next Monday,' Tang told me quietly.

sentences.en: A folded letter sat on the back counter, addressed to the Manager.
sentences.cn: 后面的柜台上放着一封折好的信，收件人是店长。

sentences.en: I should not have read it, but the words 'new *hire*' caught my eye.
Someone was being brought on for the second branch.
sentences.cn: 有人要被招进第二家分店。

sentences.en: The name on the letter made me set it down very quickly.
sentences.cn: 看到信上的名字，我立刻把信放了下来。

aid:2.en: I was struggling to carry four heavy boxes toward the stock room when Lin appeared in the doorway. Without a word, Lin took two boxes from my arms. That small act of *aid* surprised me, since Lin and I had not exactly been friendly all week.
aid:2.cnHint: 当我搬着沉重的箱子时，隔壁咖啡店的林给予了我意外的____，让我重新看待这个人。
aid:2.hook: Lin glanced back once, as if expecting me to ask a question.
aid:2.line: 'I don't need praise — I just offer *aid* when it matters,' Lin said.

sentences.en: I was struggling to carry four heavy boxes toward the stock room when Lin appeared in the doorway.
sentences.cn: 我正吃力地搬着四个沉重的纸箱往库房走，这时隔壁咖啡店的林出现在门口。

sentences.en: Without a word, Lin took two boxes from my arms.
sentences.cn: 林什么话都没说，直接从我怀里接过两个纸箱。

sentences.en: That small act of *aid* surprised me, since Lin and I had not exactly been friendly all week.

bill:2.en: I was tidying the noticeboard in the staff room when a folded *bill* fell out from behind a pinned note. It was a large one. On the back, someone had written a single address in pencil — the address of the new branch location.
bill:2.cnHint: 我在员工室的公告栏后面发现了一张夹着地址的____，那个地址正是新分店所在地。
bill:2.hook: The pencil writing was still fresh.
bill:2.line: 'Someone left this *bill* hidden here — and I want to know who,' said the Manager.

sentences.en: I was tidying the noticeboard in the staff room when a folded *bill* fell out from behind a pinned note.
It was a large one.
sentences.cn: 是一张大票。

sentences.en: On the back, someone had written a single address in pencil — the address of the new branch location.
sentences.cn: 背面有人用铅笔写了一个地址——新分店的位置。

paint:2.en: The back door of the store led to a narrow alley. I stepped out for air and found Tang crouching beside the wall, using a small brush to *paint* a tiny fish near the base of the bricks. Tang looked up, calm as anything, and simply said it was a good-luck sign for the new branch.
paint:2.cnHint: 阿糖在小巷的墙根处____了一条小鱼，说这是为新分店祈福的记号。
paint:2.hook: But the fish looked exactly like a mark I had seen at the rival shop.
paint:2.line: 'I always *paint* something small when a new place opens,' Tang said softly.

sentences.en: The back door of the store led to a narrow alley.
sentences.cn: 店铺的后门通向一条狭窄的小巷。

sentences.en: I stepped out for air and found Tang crouching beside the wall, using a small brush to *paint* a tiny fish near the base of the bricks.
Tang looked up, calm as anything, and simply said it was a good-luck sign for the new branch.
sentences.cn: 阿糖抬起头，镇定自若地说这是给新分店的幸运符号。

bean:2.en: Restocking the shelves at midnight, I found one tin had been opened and then resealed with tape. Inside, instead of the usual dried *bean* mix, there was a rolled-up note. I smoothed it out under the shelf light and read three words: 'Check the freezer.'
bean:2.cnHint: 我打开一个重新封好的罐子，里面藏着一张纸条，而不是该有的____。
bean:2.hook: Whatever was in the freezer, someone wanted only me to find it.
bean:2.line: 'There was a note inside the *bean* tin — this is not normal,' I whispered to Tang.

sentences.en: Restocking the shelves at midnight, I found one tin had been opened and then resealed with tape.
sentences.cn: 午夜补货时，我发现一罐东西被打开过，又用胶带重新封好了。

sentences.en: Inside, instead of the usual dried *bean* mix, there was a rolled-up note.
I smoothed it out under the shelf light and read three words: 'Check the freezer.'
sentences.cn: 我在架子灯下展开纸条，读到三个字："查一下冷柜。"

birthday:2.en: Tucked under the register I found a small card with 'Happy *Birthday*' printed on the front. Inside, the Manager had written a short message and a date — three days from now. There was no name on it. The card was still sealed, waiting for someone who had not yet arrived.
birthday:2.cnHint: 收银台下藏着一张未送出的____贺卡，收信人的名字一栏空着。
birthday:2.hook: Three days was not long, but the date matched something else entirely.
birthday:2.line: 'A *birthday* card with no name — who is it even for?' I asked the Manager.

sentences.en: Tucked under the register I found a small card with 'Happy *Birthday*' printed on the front.
Inside, the Manager had written a short message and a date — three days from now.
sentences.cn: 店长在里面写了一句短话和一个日期——三天后。

sentences.en: There was no name on it.
sentences.cn: 上面没有写名字。

sentences.en: The card was still sealed, waiting for someone who had not yet arrived.
sentences.cn: 贺卡还密封着，在等一个还没来的人。

flight:2.en: A customer left a printed *flight* confirmation on the counter and rushed out before I could call after them. The destination was a city two hours away — the same city where the Manager had mentioned opening the new branch. The departure time was tomorrow morning.
flight:2.cnHint: 一位顾客遗忘了一张____确认单，目的地正是新分店所在的城市。
flight:2.hook: The passenger name on the confirmation was the Manager's.
flight:2.line: 'This *flight* leaves at six — someone is in a real hurry,' Tang murmured.

sentences.en: A customer left a printed *flight* confirmation on the counter and rushed out before I could call after them.
The destination was a city two hours away — the same city where the Manager had mentioned opening the new branch.
sentences.cn: 目的地是两小时车程外的城市——店长提到新分店要开在那个城市。

sentences.en: The departure time was tomorrow morning.
sentences.cn: 出发时间是明天早上。

housing:2.en: The Manager slid a folded map across the counter. 'The new branch needs staff who can live nearby,' he said. He had circled three areas in red pen. 'Check the *housing* in each zone — cheap rent keeps good workers happy.' I studied the map, wondering which circle held my future.
housing:2.cnHint: 店长给我看地图，让我了解新分店附近的____情况。
housing:2.hook: One circled area had a question mark no one explained.
housing:2.line: The *housing* near the new branch is cheaper than you think.

sentences.en: The Manager slid a folded map across the counter.
sentences.cn: 店长把一张折好的地图推过柜台。

sentences.en: 'The new branch needs staff who can live nearby,' he said.
sentences.cn: "新分店需要能住在附近的员工，"他说。

sentences.en: He had circled three areas in red pen.
sentences.cn: 他用红笔圈了三个区域。

sentences.en: 'Check the *housing* in each zone — cheap rent keeps good workers happy.'
I studied the map, wondering which circle held my future.
sentences.cn: 我盯着地图，琢磨着哪个圆圈里装着我的未来。

behaviour:2.en: Tang noticed something odd on the security screen. A man in a yellow jacket had visited the drink fridge four times without buying anything. 'Watch his *behaviour*,' Tang whispered, nudging me. 'Last week someone like him turned out to be a location scout for a rival store.' The man finally bought one bottle of water.
behaviour:2.cnHint: 阿糖让我注意一个可疑顾客的____，怀疑他另有目的。
behaviour:2.hook: The yellow jacket man photographed the shelves before leaving.
behaviour:2.line: His *behaviour* near the fridges is making me nervous.

sentences.en: Tang noticed something odd on the security screen.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在监控屏幕上发现了什么奇怪的地方。

sentences.en: A man in a yellow jacket had visited the drink fridge four times without buying anything.
sentences.cn: 一个穿黄夹克的男人在饮料冷柜前转悠了四次，一次都没买。

sentences.en: 'Watch his *behaviour*,' Tang whispered, nudging me.
'Last week someone like him turned out to be a location scout for a rival store.'
sentences.cn: "上周也来过这样的人，后来才知道是竞争对手的选址员。"

sentences.en: The man finally bought one bottle of water.
sentences.cn: 那个男人最后买了一瓶水。

husband:2.en: A woman rushed in just before two in the morning, cheeks red from the cold. She bought a hot drink and two rice balls. 'My *husband* is outside measuring the empty shop next door,' she said with a tired smile. 'He wants to open something. I told him midnight is not office hours.' She shook her head fondly.
husband:2.cnHint: 一位女顾客的____深夜在外面勘察隔壁空铺，让她又好笑又无奈。
husband:2.hook: The empty shop next door had been on the market for years.
husband:2.line: My *husband* has been staring at that empty shop all night.

sentences.en: A woman rushed in just before two in the morning, cheeks red from the cold.
sentences.cn: 一个女人在凌晨两点刚过时冲了进来，脸颊因为寒冷泛着红。

sentences.en: She bought a hot drink and two rice balls.
sentences.cn: 她买了一杯热饮和两个饭团。

sentences.en: 'My *husband* is outside measuring the empty shop next door,' she said with a tired smile.
'He wants to open something.
sentences.cn: "他想开家店。

sentences.en: I told him midnight is not office hours.'
sentences.cn: 我跟他说半夜不是营业时间。"

sentences.en: She shook her head fondly.
sentences.cn: 她摇着头笑了。

tourist:2.en: A young man with a large backpack came in asking for a local bus map. He looked lost and happy at the same time. 'I am a *tourist*,' he explained, spreading his arms at the snack wall, 'but also I am hungry.' He bought six things I could not name and asked me to write down their flavours in English for his notes.
tourist:2.cnHint: 一位____走进来，买了很多零食，还请我帮他记下口味的英文名称。
tourist:2.hook: His notebook already held the names of forty other stores.
tourist:2.line: As a *tourist*, I try every local snack I can find.

sentences.en: A young man with a large backpack came in asking for a local bus map.
sentences.cn: 一个背着大背包的年轻人走了进来，问有没有本地公交地图。

sentences.en: He looked lost and happy at the same time.
sentences.cn: 他看起来既迷茫又开心。

sentences.en: 'I am a *tourist*,' he explained, spreading his arms at the snack wall, 'but also I am hungry.'
He bought six things I could not name and asked me to write down their flavours in English for his notes.
sentences.cn: 他买了六样东西，我根本叫不出名字，还让我把它们的口味用英文记下来。

agent:2.en: A neat woman in a grey coat came in twice in one hour, each time studying the view from our window. On her second visit she bought coffee and left a card on the counter. She was a property *agent*. The Manager picked up the card slowly and said nothing, but I saw him nod just once, very quietly.
agent:2.cnHint: 一位房产____两次进店，似乎在考察位置，还留下了名片。
agent:2.hook: The Manager locked the card in the drawer under the register.
agent:2.line: I am a property *agent* — I have news about the shop next door.

sentences.en: A neat woman in a grey coat came in twice in one hour, each time studying the view from our window.
sentences.cn: 一个穿灰外套的精致女人一小时内来了两次，每次都站在窗边研究外面的景色。

sentences.en: On her second visit she bought coffee and left a card on the counter.
sentences.cn: 第二次来的时候她买了咖啡，在柜台留下一张名片。

sentences.en: She was a property *agent*.
The Manager picked up the card slowly and said nothing, but I saw him nod just once, very quietly.
sentences.cn: 店长慢慢拿起名片，什么也没说，但我看到他非常轻地点了一下头。

cash:2.en: Lin came in from the street looking pale. 'The landlord of the new site wants three months up front,' she said, dropping into a chair by the hot-food shelf. 'All in *cash*.' She pressed her palms together. 'Who carries that much cash at a signing meeting?' The Manager set a warm can of tea in front of her and said, 'We do, now.'
cash:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林得知新店房东要求提前付____，感到十分为难。
cash:2.hook: The Manager had already counted the money that morning.
cash:2.line: The landlord wants everything in *cash* before we sign anything.

sentences.en: Lin came in from the street looking pale.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林从街上走了进来，脸色苍白。

sentences.en: 'The landlord of the new site wants three months up front,' she said, dropping into a chair by the hot-food shelf.
sentences.cn: "新店的房东要求三个月的租金一次性付清，"她一屁股坐在热食架旁的椅子上说。

sentences.en: 'All in *cash*.'
She pressed her palms together.
sentences.cn: 她两只手掌贴在一起。

sentences.en: 'Who carries that much cash at a signing meeting?'
sentences.cn: "谁会在签约会上带那么多现金？"

sentences.en: The Manager set a warm can of tea in front of her and said, 'We do, now.'
sentences.cn: 店长给她面前放了一罐温热的茶，说，"现在我们会了。"

competition:2.en: Lin spread a hand-drawn chart on the counter. Three other stores sat within five minutes of the planned new branch. 'This is real *competition*,' she said, tapping each dot. 'Two of them close at midnight. One sells hot food.' She looked at me. 'So what do we do that none of them do?' I looked at the chat and thought hard.
competition:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林分析新分店周边的____形势，想找出我们独特的优势。
competition:2.hook: One dot on the chart had a name that made the Manager go still.
competition:2.line: The *competition* around the new branch is stronger than we expected.

sentences.en: Lin spread a hand-drawn chart on the counter.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在柜台铺开了一张手绘的图表。

sentences.en: Three other stores sat within five minutes of the planned new branch.
sentences.cn: 三家其他的店就在计划中的新分店五分钟的范围内。

sentences.en: 'This is real *competition*,' she said, tapping each dot.
'Two of them close at midnight.
sentences.cn: "其中两家午夜就关门了。

sentences.en: One sells hot food.'
sentences.cn: 一家卖热食。"

sentences.en: She looked at me.
sentences.cn: 她看着我。

sentences.en: 'So what do we do that none of them do?'
sentences.cn: "那么我们做的是他们都做不了的什么呢？"

sentences.en: I looked at the chat and thought hard.
sentences.cn: 我看着图表，使劲儿想。

farmer:2.en: Just after dawn a quiet old man came in carrying a cloth bag of small sweet potatoes. He set it gently on the counter. 'I am a *farmer* from the village past the ring road,' he said. 'I heard the new shop will open near my land. I brought these as a greeting.' The Manager accepted the bag with both hands.
farmer:2.cnHint: 一位____清早送来自种的红薯，作为对新分店的欢迎礼物。
farmer:2.hook: The sweet potatoes were unlike any variety sold in the city.
farmer:2.line: I am a *farmer* — my land sits right behind your new branch.

sentences.en: Just after dawn a quiet old man came in carrying a cloth bag of small sweet potatoes.
sentences.cn: 天刚亮的时候，一个安静的老人拎着一布袋小红薯走了进来。

sentences.en: He set it gently on the counter.
sentences.cn: 他轻轻地把布袋放在柜台上。

sentences.en: 'I am a *farmer* from the village past the ring road,' he said.
'I heard the new shop will open near my land.
sentences.cn: "我听说新店要在我地边上开，"他说。

sentences.en: I brought these as a greeting.'
sentences.cn: "我带这些来打个招呼。"

sentences.en: The Manager accepted the bag with both hands.
sentences.cn: 店长用双手接过了布袋。

collection:2.en: A delivery driver left a heavy box at the back door with a note: 'For the manager.' Inside, wrapped in old newspaper, sat a *collection* of tiny ceramic cats — twenty at least, each one painted a different colour. I lined them up on the shelf above the tea kettles and waited.
collection:2.cnHint: 送货司机留下一箱东西，里面是店长的____，我把它们摆在了货架上。
collection:2.hook: By midnight, one ceramic cat had somehow moved to a different shelf.
collection:2.line: 'This *collection* has been growing for fifteen years,' the Manager said quietly.

sentences.en: A delivery driver left a heavy box at the back door with a note: 'For the manager.'
sentences.cn: 一个快递员在后门放了一个沉甸甸的纸箱，留了张纸条："给经理的。"

sentences.en: Inside, wrapped in old newspaper, sat a *collection* of tiny ceramic cats — twenty at least, each one painted a different colour.
I lined them up on the shelf above the tea kettles and waited.
sentences.cn: 我把它们排成一行放在茶壶架上面，然后等着。

depression:2.en: Tang found me sitting on an empty crate behind the store at three in the morning, staring at the dark street. 'First week?' he asked. I nodded. He handed me a warm meat bun without another word. That small act pulled me out of a *depression* I had not even named yet.
depression:2.cnHint: 唐发现我一个人坐在外面，用一个包子把我从____中拉了出来。
depression:2.hook: Tang never explained how he always knew when someone needed that bun.
depression:2.line: 'A little *depression* at three a.m. is basically the store uniform,' Tang said.

sentences.en: Tang found me sitting on an empty crate behind the store at three in the morning, staring at the dark street.
sentences.cn: 凌晨三点，阿糖在店后面找到了我，我坐在一个空木板箱上，盯着黑漆漆的街道。

sentences.en: 'First week?' he asked.
sentences.cn: "第一周？"他问。

sentences.en: I nodded.
sentences.cn: 我点了点头。

sentences.en: He handed me a warm meat bun without another word.
sentences.cn: 他没再说话，递给我一个热的肉馒头。

sentences.en: That small act pulled me out of a *depression* I had not even named yet.

foot:2.en: The new branch was one street over, and I walked there on my break to have a look. It was bigger, brighter, and had a coffee machine the size of a small car. Standing at the door, I measured the distance back to our store — exactly one *foot* of pavement for every year the Manager had worked.
foot:2.cnHint: 我步行去看新分店，用____来丈量两家店之间的距离。
foot:2.hook: A handwritten sign on the new door read: 'Opening soon — same family, new address.'
foot:2.line: 'Every *foot* of this street has a story,' the Manager said, looking down.

sentences.en: The new branch was one street over, and I walked there on my break to have a look.

sentences.en: Standing at the door, I measured the distance back to our store — exactly one *foot* of pavement for every year the Manager had worked.

graduate:2.en: A young woman came in just after midnight, still wearing a gown and a flat cap. She bought a single can of cold coffee, tapped it twice like a toast, and drank it at the counter alone. 'Fresh *graduate*,' Tang whispered to me. 'They all come here on the big night.'
graduate:2.cnHint: 一位刚刚完成学业的____深夜独自来店里买咖啡庆祝。
graduate:2.hook: She left her graduation cap on the counter and never came back for it.
graduate:2.line: 'Every *graduate* needs one quiet moment before the noise starts,' she said.

sentences.en: A young woman came in just after midnight, still wearing a gown and a flat cap.
sentences.cn: 一个年轻女人在午夜刚过时走了进来，还穿着礼服和平顶帽。

sentences.en: She bought a single can of cold coffee, tapped it twice like a toast, and drank it at the counter alone.
sentences.cn: 她买了一罐冰咖啡，在柜台上敲了两下像是敬酒，然后独自喝完了。

sentences.en: 'Fresh *graduate*,' Tang whispered to me.
'They all come here on the big night.'
sentences.cn: 他们都在这个大日子来这里。

intake:2.en: The Manager was reviewing a health report at the counter, frowning at a column of numbers. 'Salt,' he muttered, circling something with a red pen. He then looked up at the shelf of instant noodles and sighed. A customer's daily *intake* was apparently the talk of some clinic nearby, and that customer was a regular.
intake:2.cnHint: 店长看着一份健康报告皱眉，某位常客的____引起了附近诊所的关注。
intake:2.hook: The regular walked in right then, reaching for his usual extra-salty pack.
intake:2.line: 'Your daily *intake* is not a personal record to break,' the Manager said firmly.

sentences.en: The Manager was reviewing a health report at the counter, frowning at a column of numbers.
sentences.cn: 店长在柜台前看一份卫生报告，皱着眉头盯着一列数字。

sentences.en: 'Salt,' he muttered, circling something with a red pen.
sentences.cn: "盐，"他喃喃自语，用红笔圈了圈什么东西。

sentences.en: He then looked up at the shelf of instant noodles and sighed.
sentences.cn: 然后他抬起头看了看方便面的架子，叹了口气。

sentences.en: A customer's daily *intake* was apparently the talk of some clinic nearby, and that customer was a regular.

screen:2.en: A thin folding *screen* stood in the far corner of the store — old, painted with bamboo — and I had never noticed it before. Behind it was a small table, two chairs, and a plug socket. Tang said the Manager sometimes let people sit there to think. No purchase required.
screen:2.cnHint: 店里角落摆着一扇____，后面藏着一张桌子和两把椅子供人静思。
screen:2.hook: Tonight, someone had left a sealed letter on that little table.
screen:2.line: 'The *screen* is there so people can disappear for a while,' the Manager said.

sentences.en: A thin folding *screen* stood in the far corner of the store — old, painted with bamboo — and I had never noticed it before.
Behind it was a small table, two chairs, and a plug socket.
sentences.cn: 在它后面有一张小桌子、两把椅子和一个插座。

sentences.en: Tang said the Manager sometimes let people sit there to think.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说店长有时候会让人坐在那里想事情。

sentences.en: No purchase required.
sentences.cn: 不需要买东西。

chair:2.en: Lin arrived from the new branch carrying a flat box under one arm. Inside was a folding *chair* — a gift for the opening, she said, for whoever stood longest on the first shift. She set it against the wall with a card that read: 'Sit when you need to. No one is watching.' I liked her immediately.
chair:2.cnHint: 林从新分店带来一把____作为礼物，卡片上写着让人放松的话。
chair:2.hook: The Manager read the card twice, then quietly sat down for the first time all week.
chair:2.line: 'A good *chair* is a way of saying someone matters,' Lin told me, smiling.

sentences.en: Lin arrived from the new branch carrying a flat box under one arm.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林从新店回来，腋下夹着一个平纸箱。

sentences.en: Inside was a folding *chair* — a gift for the opening, she said, for whoever stood longest on the first shift.
She set it against the wall with a card that read: 'Sit when you need to.
sentences.cn: 她把它靠墙放好，旁边放了张卡片，上面写着："累了就坐下。

sentences.en: No one is watching.'
sentences.cn: 没人在看。"

sentences.en: I liked her immediately.
sentences.cn: 我立刻就喜欢上她了。

court:2.en: Behind the new branch there was a small basketball *court*, cracked and faded, with one bent hoop. Three kids played there every night, and they always came in for water at exactly ten. The Manager had quietly kept the water cold for them all summer, telling no one and charging nothing.
court:2.cnHint: 新分店后面有一块____，店长默默为每晚在那里打球的孩子们免费备水。
court:2.hook: Tonight the three kids came in at ten — and brought a fourth, carrying a mop.
court:2.line: 'That *court* has been here longer than the store,' the Manager said softly.

sentences.en: Behind the new branch there was a small basketball *court*, cracked and faded, with one bent hoop.
Three kids played there every night, and they always came in for water at exactly ten.
sentences.cn: 三个小孩每晚都在那儿打球，每次都在十点整来要水喝。

sentences.en: The Manager had quietly kept the water cold for them all summer, telling no one and charging nothing.
sentences.cn: 店长整个夏天都默默地给他们冰水，没跟任何人说起，也没收钱。

female:2.en: A delivery box arrived after midnight, addressed to the store. Inside, wrapped in soft cloth, sat a small cage. A tiny *female* rabbit blinked up at me, a note tied to the bars: 'Please keep her safe until I return.' I had no idea who sent her.
female:2.cnHint: 深夜送来一个箱子，里面是一只____兔子，还附有一张字条。
female:2.hook: The note was signed with only a small paw print.
female:2.line: 'She is a *female*, so she needs extra care tonight.'

sentences.en: A delivery box arrived after midnight, addressed to the store.
sentences.cn: 午夜后一个快递盒子送到了店里。

sentences.en: Inside, wrapped in soft cloth, sat a small cage.
sentences.cn: 打开来，用软布包着一个小笼子。

sentences.en: A tiny *female* rabbit blinked up at me, a note tied to the bars: 'Please keep her safe until I return.'
I had no idea who sent her.
sentences.cn: 我不知道是谁寄来的。

holiday:2.en: The Manager taped a new sign on the door before dawn: 'Open every *holiday*, no exceptions.' Tang groaned and rested his head on the counter. Outside, families were already walking past with balloons, laughing. I quietly refilled the hot-drink machine and said nothing.
holiday:2.cnHint: 店长贴出告示，说____也照常营业，同事唉声叹气。
holiday:2.hook: Then Tang found a second, hidden note behind the first sign.
holiday:2.line: 'Even on a *holiday*, this store never sleeps,' Tang muttered.

sentences.en: The Manager taped a new sign on the door before dawn: 'Open every *holiday*, no exceptions.'
Tang groaned and rested his head on the counter.
sentences.cn: 阿糖呻吟了一声，把脑袋靠在柜台上。

sentences.en: Outside, families were already walking past with balloons, laughing.
sentences.cn: 外面已经有一家家人拎着气球走过，笑声一片。

sentences.en: I quietly refilled the hot-drink machine and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 我默默地给热饮机加满了料，什么都没说。

pain:2.en: Lin walked in just before three in the morning, limping slightly. She set a folder on the counter and asked for a hot pack. 'Took *pain* to get these numbers right,' she said, sliding the folder toward me. It was a full sales report — for a second store location.
pain:2.cnHint: 林深夜进店，说整理好那份文件费了不少____，顺手把它放在柜台上。
pain:2.hook: The address on the report was only two streets away.
pain:2.line: 'It was real *pain* putting this together, but it had to be done.'

sentences.en: Lin walked in just before three in the morning, limping slightly.
sentences.cn: 林在凌晨三点不到走了进来，走得有点一瘸一拐的。

sentences.en: She set a folder on the counter and asked for a hot pack.
sentences.cn: 她在柜台上放下一个文件夹，要了个热贴。

sentences.en: 'Took *pain* to get these numbers right,' she said, sliding the folder toward me.
It was a full sales report — for a second store location.
sentences.cn: 那是一份完整的销售报告——针对第二家店的。

player:2.en: A teenage boy came in for a bottle of water, still in his sports kit. He was a basketball *player* from the school nearby — I recognised the team logo. He left a crumpled paper on the counter by mistake. Unfolding it, I found a hand-drawn map of the neighbourhood.
player:2.cnHint: 一名篮球____买水后，不小心把一张手绘地图落在了柜台上。
player:2.hook: One spot on the map was circled in red ink.
player:2.line: 'I'm just a *player*, but even I heard about the new place.'

sentences.en: A teenage boy came in for a bottle of water, still in his sports kit.
sentences.cn: 一个少年穿着运动服来买一瓶水。

sentences.en: He was a basketball *player* from the school nearby — I recognised the team logo.
He left a crumpled paper on the counter by mistake.
sentences.cn: 他不小心在柜台上落下了一张皱巴巴的纸。

sentences.en: Unfolding it, I found a hand-drawn map of the neighbourhood.
sentences.cn: 我打开来一看，是一张手绘的街区地图。

production:2.en: The Manager called me into the back room and pointed at stacked boxes. 'New *production* line from our supplier,' he said proudly. Each box carried a logo I had never seen before. He smiled and told me to stack them neatly. One box at the bottom felt much heavier than the rest.
production:2.cnHint: 店长展示了一批新____，但其中有一箱异常地重。
production:2.hook: The heaviest box had no label at all.
production:2.line: 'This *production* just arrived — handle every box with care.'

sentences.en: The Manager called me into the back room and pointed at stacked boxes.
sentences.cn: 店长把我叫到后间，指着一堆堆的盒子。

sentences.en: 'New *production* line from our supplier,' he said proudly.
Each box carried a logo I had never seen before.
sentences.cn: 每个盒子上都印着我从没见过的商标。

sentences.en: He smiled and told me to stack them neatly.
sentences.cn: 他笑了笑，让我把它们整齐地堆好。

sentences.en: One box at the bottom felt much heavier than the rest.
sentences.cn: 最底层的一个盒子重得不像样。

secure:2.en: Before his shift ended, Tang tested every window and checked the back lock twice. 'Got to keep the place *secure*,' he said, handing me a small key on a red cord. I did not know what it opened. He pointed at a drawer under the register and then walked out without another word.
secure:2.cnHint: 同事反复检查门窗，说要确保店铺____，然后递给我一把不知用途的小钥匙。
secure:2.hook: The drawer the key opened was already slightly ajar.
secure:2.line: 'Always make sure the store is *secure* before you sit down.'

sentences.en: Before his shift ended, Tang tested every window and checked the back lock twice.
sentences.cn: 班快结束时，阿糖把每扇窗都检查了一遍，还把后门的锁检查了两次。

sentences.en: 'Got to keep the place *secure*,' he said, handing me a small key on a red cord.
I did not know what it opened.
sentences.cn: 我不知道它开什么的。

sentences.en: He pointed at a drawer under the register and then walked out without another word.
sentences.cn: 他指向收银机下面的一个抽屉，然后一句话都没再说就走了。

audience:2.en: At two in the morning the Manager video-called someone and propped his phone on the counter. 'There is an *audience* waiting,' he told me, looking nervous. Faces on the screen leaned closer. He cleared his throat and began describing a new store plan in careful English. I stood very still and listened.
audience:2.cnHint: 店长深夜视频通话，说屏幕那头有一群____正等着听他的新开店计划。
audience:2.hook: One face in the call was Lin, sitting in a brightly lit office.
audience:2.line: 'We have an *audience* on the call — please speak clearly.'

sentences.en: At two in the morning the Manager video-called someone and propped his phone on the counter.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点，店长给谁打了个视频电话，把手机支在柜台上。

sentences.en: 'There is an *audience* waiting,' he told me, looking nervous.
Faces on the screen leaned closer.
sentences.cn: 屏幕上的脸都凑近了。

sentences.en: He cleared his throat and began describing a new store plan in careful English.
sentences.cn: 他清了清嗓子，开始用仔细的英文描述一个新店的计划。

sentences.en: I stood very still and listened.
sentences.cn: 我站得很直，听着。

borrow:2.en: Lin knocked on the glass door at half past one, holding nothing but her phone. 'Can I *borrow* your pen and a sheet of paper?' she asked, stepping inside. She wrote quickly, folded the paper, and slid it into an envelope she pulled from her coat. She left before I could ask any questions.
borrow:2.cnHint: 林深夜敲门，说想____一支笔和纸，写完就匆匆离开了。
borrow:2.hook: The envelope was addressed to the Manager, marked 'urgent'.
borrow:2.line: 'I only need to *borrow* it for one minute, I promise.'

sentences.en: Lin knocked on the glass door at half past one, holding nothing but her phone.
sentences.cn: 林在凌晨一点半敲了玻璃门，手里什么都没拿，只有手机。

sentences.en: 'Can I *borrow* your pen and a sheet of paper?' she asked, stepping inside.
She wrote quickly, folded the paper, and slid it into an envelope she pulled from her coat.
sentences.cn: 她飞快地写了起来，折好纸，从外套里掏出一个信封塞进去。

sentences.en: She left before I could ask any questions.
sentences.cn: 她没等我问什么就走了。

burn:2.en: The Manager left a note taped to the coffee machine: 'Handle with care.' I learned why at 2 a.m. when I grabbed the steam pipe without a cloth and felt a sharp *burn* across my palm. I ran cold water over it, then noticed a second note underneath the first: 'Sorry — I forgot to warn the last clerk too.'
burn:2.cnHint: 新店员不小心碰到蒸汽管，手掌留下了____，发现店长早知道这个危险。
burn:2.hook: The last clerk had quit after only one week.
burn:2.line: 'That *burn* on your hand — yeah, we've all been there.'

sentences.en: The Manager left a note taped to the coffee machine: 'Handle with care.'
sentences.cn: 店长在咖啡机上贴了张纸条："小心轻放。"

sentences.en: I learned why at 2 a.m. when I grabbed the steam pipe without a cloth and felt a sharp *burn* across my palm.
I ran cold water over it, then noticed a second note underneath the first: 'Sorry — I forgot to warn the last clerk too.'
sentences.cn: 我跑冷水冲着，然后注意到第一张纸条下面还压着第二张："抱歉——我也忘了跟上一个店员说。"

cook:2.en: A regular came in just before 3 a.m. carrying a small pot and a hopeful look. 'Can I use your back counter?' he asked. 'I like to *cook* ramen here — my kitchen fan broke and the smell drives my wife crazy.' The Manager had apparently said yes for two years. I had no idea what the rules even were in this store.
cook:2.cnHint: 一位常客在店里____方便面，这竟然是店长默许两年的惯例。
cook:2.hook: His wife showed up ten minutes later, looking less than crazy.
cook:2.line: 'I just need to *cook* one small thing — it won't take long, I promise.'

sentences.en: A regular came in just before 3 a.m. carrying a small pot and a hopeful look.
sentences.cn: 一个老顾客在凌晨三点不到走进来，拎着一个小锅，一脸期待。

sentences.en: 'Can I use your back counter?' he asked.
sentences.cn: "能用你们的后柜台吗？"他问。

sentences.en: 'I like to *cook* ramen here — my kitchen fan broke and the smell drives my wife crazy.'
The Manager had apparently said yes for two years.
sentences.cn: 店长显然已经同意两年了。

sentences.en: I had no idea what the rules even were in this store.
sentences.cn: 我根本不知道这家店有什么规则。

corporate:2.en: A suited woman slid a folder across the counter at midnight. 'We're scouting this block for a *corporate* expansion,' she said with a polished smile. 'How is business here?' I stared at her, then at the hand-drawn shelf labels and the Manager's lucky cat with the broken arm. I said business was fine.
corporate:2.cnHint: 一位女士深夜来店里做____扩张调查，店员望着歪歪扭扭的手写标签，平静回答生意很好。
corporate:2.hook: She wrote something in the folder and did not show me what it was.
corporate:2.line: 'Our *corporate* team has had an eye on this corner for months.'

sentences.en: A suited woman slid a folder across the counter at midnight.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着讲究的女人在午夜时分把一个文件夹推过柜台。

sentences.en: 'We're scouting this block for a *corporate* expansion,' she said with a polished smile.
'How is business here?'
sentences.cn: "生意还不错吧？"

sentences.en: I stared at her, then at the hand-drawn shelf labels and the Manager's lucky cat with the broken arm.
sentences.cn: 我盯着她，又看了看手写的架子标签和那只断了胳膊的店长招财猫。

sentences.en: I said business was fine.
sentences.cn: 我说生意还可以。

dangerous:2.en: Tang warned me on my first night: 'The mop bucket near the freezer is *dangerous* — the wheel is broken and it slides into people.' I nodded and forgot completely. By 4 a.m. I had knocked it into three customers and myself. Tang watched each time from behind the snack shelf with a cup of tea and a calm expression.
dangerous:2.cnHint: 同事提醒新店员拖把桶____，但店员完全忘记，一晚上撞倒了好几次。
dangerous:2.hook: Tang had been waiting for someone new to watch this happen.
dangerous:2.line: 'That broken wheel makes the whole thing *dangerous* — trust me on this one.'

sentences.en: Tang warned me on my first night: 'The mop bucket near the freezer is *dangerous* — the wheel is broken and it slides into people.'
I nodded and forgot completely.
sentences.cn: 我完全忘了。

sentences.en: By 4 a.m.
sentences.cn: 到了凌晨四点。

sentences.en: I had knocked it into three customers and myself.
sentences.cn: 我已经把它撞到了三个顾客和我自己身上。

sentences.en: Tang watched each time from behind the snack shelf with a cup of tea and a calm expression.
sentences.cn: 阿糖每次都在小食架后面看着，手里拿着茶杯，表情平静得很。

debt:2.en: A quiet student came in every night for a small coffee and always paid with exact coins. One night he was two coins short and turned red. 'I have a *debt* to you,' he said seriously, placing an IOU note on the counter. He came back the next night with the coins and a small bag of homemade cookies. The note had already meant more than the money.
debt:2.cnHint: 一位学生少带了零钱，郑重地说自己欠了店员一笔____，第二天还钱时还带来了饼干。
debt:2.hook: His handwriting on the IOU note was surprisingly beautiful.
debt:2.line: 'I don't like having any *debt*, even a small one — here are the coins.'

sentences.en: A quiet student came in every night for a small coffee and always paid with exact coins.
sentences.cn: 一个安静的学生每晚都来买一小杯咖啡，总是用硬币精确付款。

sentences.en: One night he was two coins short and turned red.
sentences.cn: 有一晚他少了两个硬币，脸红了。

sentences.en: 'I have a *debt* to you,' he said seriously, placing an IOU note on the counter.
He came back the next night with the coins and a small bag of homemade cookies.
sentences.cn: 他第二晚回来时带了那些硬币，还有一个小袋子装的自制饼干。

sentences.en: The note had already meant more than the money.
sentences.cn: 那张纸条已经比钱值钱得多了。

discipline:2.en: The Manager ran the stockroom with unusual *discipline*: every item faced front, every label aligned, every box dated in red pen. I spent my first hour trying to match it perfectly. When he arrived at dawn and saw my work, he nodded once — which Tang later told me was the highest praise he had ever given a new clerk.
discipline:2.cnHint: 店长用严格的____管理仓库，新店员努力做到完美，换来了店长最高级别的夸奖——点一下头。
discipline:2.hook: Tang had worked here three years and never received that nod.
discipline:2.line: 'Real *discipline* in the stockroom saves you an hour every single week.'

sentences.en: The Manager ran the stockroom with unusual *discipline*: every item faced front, every label aligned, every box dated in red pen.
I spent my first hour trying to match it perfectly.
sentences.cn: 我花了第一个小时试图完美匹配它。

sentences.en: When he arrived at dawn and saw my work, he nodded once — which Tang later told me was the highest praise he had ever given a new clerk.
sentences.cn: 天亮时他来了，看到我的工作，点了一下头——林之后告诉我那是他给新店员的最高表扬。

error:2.en: I scanned a bottle of juice twice by *error* and charged a customer double. She noticed before I did, pulled up the receipt on her phone, and showed me with a kind smile. I fixed it and apologized three times. She said it was fine and came back the next night — this time checking her receipt at the counter before she left.
error:2.cnHint: 店员误操作多收了顾客的钱，顾客温和地指出了这个____，第二天还是回来了。
error:2.hook: She always checked her receipt after that, without fail.
error:2.line: 'It was just a small *error* — these things happen on the night shift.'

sentences.en: I scanned a bottle of juice twice by *error* and charged a customer double.
She noticed before I did, pulled up the receipt on her phone, and showed me with a kind smile.
sentences.cn: 她在我之前发现了，用手机调出收据给我看，脸上带着温柔的微笑。

sentences.en: I fixed it and apologized three times.
sentences.cn: 我改正了，道歉了三次。

sentences.en: She said it was fine and came back the next night — this time checking her receipt at the counter before she left.
sentences.cn: 她说没关系，第二晚又回来了——这次在离开前在收银台检查了收据。

gym:2.en: A man came in at 5 a.m. soaked in sweat, heading home from the all-night *gym* two streets over. He bought three bananas, a bottle of water, and one small chocolate bar, then stared at the chocolate for a moment. 'Don't tell the gym,' he said. I promised. He came back the next morning with the same look on his face.
gym:2.cnHint: 一位顾客从深夜____回来，买了健康食品，又悄悄买了巧克力，请店员保密。
gym:2.hook: He had clearly been having this same argument with himself for weeks.
gym:2.line: 'I just came from the *gym*, so I think I've earned this chocolate bar.'

sentences.en: A man came in at 5 a.m. soaked in sweat, heading home from the all-night *gym* two streets over.
He bought three bananas, a bottle of water, and one small chocolate bar, then stared at the chocolate for a moment.
sentences.cn: 他买了三根香蕉、一瓶水，还有一块小巧克力，然后盯着那块巧克力看了一会。

sentences.en: 'Don't tell the gym,' he said.
sentences.cn: "别告诉健身房，"他说。

sentences.en: I promised.
sentences.cn: 我答应了。

sentences.en: He came back the next morning with the same look on his face.
sentences.cn: 第二天早上他又来了，脸上是同样的表情。

mile:2.en: A folded note appeared under the back-room door. I opened it and read: 'The new branch is almost a *mile* away — too far for me to walk at night.' The handwriting looked familiar, but no name was signed. I stared at the map on the wall and started counting blocks.
mile:2.cnHint: 一张没有署名的纸条出现在后室门缝里，说新分店离这儿太____了。
mile:2.hook: Only one person here knew my habit of checking that door.
mile:2.line: 'That new place is a full *mile* away — who decided that?'

sentences.en: A folded note appeared under the back-room door.
sentences.cn: 一张折叠的纸条从后房的门下面塞了进来。

sentences.en: I opened it and read: 'The new branch is almost a *mile* away — too far for me to walk at night.'
The handwriting looked familiar, but no name was signed.
sentences.cn: 笔迹看起来很熟悉，但没有署名。

sentences.en: I stared at the map on the wall and started counting blocks.

movement:2.en: Late at night I noticed a shadow through the front window. A slow, careful *movement* behind the magazine rack — someone was reading without paying. I walked over quietly and found a small boy hiding between the shelves, eyes wide, pretending to be a display stand.
movement:2.cnHint: 我在杂志架后面发现了一个可疑的____，没想到藏着个小孩。
movement:2.hook: The boy pressed a crumpled receipt into my hand and ran.
movement:2.line: 'I saw that *movement* behind the shelf — what are you doing back there?'

sentences.en: Late at night I noticed a shadow through the front window.

sentences.en: A slow, careful *movement* behind the magazine rack — someone was reading without paying.
I walked over quietly and found a small boy hiding between the shelves, eyes wide, pretending to be a display stand.
sentences.cn: 我悄悄走过去，发现一个小男孩躲在架子之间，眼睛睁得很大，假装自己是个展示架。

party:2.en: Tang waved a bright flyer at me: 'Branch opening *party* this Saturday.' Someone had drawn little balloons on the corners. The Manager had not mentioned a party to me. I checked the staff board — my name was not on the volunteer list, yet my face was on the poster.
party:2.cnHint: 同事拿来一张传单，说新分店要办开业____，但我的名字竟然没被列进去。
party:2.hook: My photo on that poster was taken six months before I was hired.
party:2.line: 'Why is your face on the *party* poster if nobody told you?'

sentences.cn: 我查了员工板——我的名字不在志愿者名单上，但我的脸在海报上。

rescue:2.en: The delivery elevator jammed between floors just before dawn. Inside it: three boxes of fresh bread for the new branch's opening day. I called Tang, who called the Manager, and we all stood staring up at the ceiling until the repairman arrived for the *rescue* forty minutes later.
rescue:2.cnHint: 送货电梯卡住了，装着新分店开业面包的箱子需要____。
rescue:2.hook: The repairman opened the doors and said the bread was already gone.
rescue:2.line: 'Good thing I called for the *rescue* — that bread is worth more than my shift pay.'

sentences.en: The delivery elevator jammed between floors just before dawn.
sentences.cn: 配送电梯在天亮前卡在了两层楼之间。

sentences.en: Inside it: three boxes of fresh bread for the new branch's opening day.
sentences.cn: 里面装着：新分店开业日用的三箱新鲜面包。

sentences.en: I called Tang, who called the Manager, and we all stood staring up at the ceiling until the repairman arrived for the *rescue* forty minutes later.

writing:2.en: I found a torn notebook page taped to the cold drinks fridge. The *writing* on it said: 'Do not stock the green tea on shelf B — that shelf belongs to the new branch's test display.' Nobody I asked knew who had put it there or when the test display had been agreed.
writing:2.cnHint: 冰柜上贴着一张字条，____内容让我对新分店的安排感到困惑。
writing:2.hook: The tape was still warm when I pulled the note free.
writing:2.line: 'Whose *writing* is this? It is not the Manager's hand at all.'

sentences.en: I found a torn notebook page taped to the cold drinks fridge.

sentences.cn: 我问的每个人都不知道是谁放的或什么时候商定的测试展示。

bite:2.en: Lin dropped a small paper bag on the counter. 'Try one,' she said. Inside were samples from the bakery supplier for the new branch — soft rolls the size of a coin. I took a *bite* and immediately understood why the Manager had been smiling all week. They were very, very good.
bite:2.cnHint: 竞争对手带来了新分店供应商的试吃品，我____了一口后明白了一切。
bite:2.hook: Lin watched my face and wrote something down without a word.
bite:2.line: 'Just one *bite* — tell me honestly what you think of it.'

sentences.en: 'Try one,' she said.

sentences.en: I took a *bite* and immediately understood why the Manager had been smiling all week.
They were very, very good.
sentences.cn: 它们非常、非常好吃。

capture:2.en: The Manager set up a small camera above the entrance of the new branch while I held the ladder. 'We need to *capture* every customer who comes in on opening day,' he said, meaning count them on video. I held the ladder steady and wondered if he also meant something more.
capture:2.cnHint: 店长在新分店门口架摄像头，说要____每一位进门的顾客。
capture:2.hook: That evening the camera showed a face neither of us recognised.
capture:2.line: 'We have to *capture* the crowd on opening day — every single face.'

sentences.en: The Manager set up a small camera above the entrance of the new branch while I held the ladder.
sentences.cn: 店长在新分店的入口上面装了一个小摄像头，我扶着梯子。

I held the ladder steady and wondered if he also meant something more.
sentences.cn: 我扶稳梯子，想知道他是不是还想表达什么别的意思。

cope:2.en: Opening day at the new branch was tomorrow, and the Manager asked me to cover both stores alone for one hour at noon. 'Can you *cope*?' he asked. I looked at the map — nearly a mile between them — and at the clock, and said yes before my brain could say no.
cope:2.cnHint: 店长问我能否独自____同时照看两家店铺一小时。
cope:2.hook: At noon a customer walked into one store, then the other, within minutes.
cope:2.line: 'I need to know — can you really *cope* with both stores alone?'

sentences.en: Opening day at the new branch was tomorrow, and the Manager asked me to cover both stores alone for one hour at noon.
sentences.cn: 新分店明天就要开业了，店长让我在中午单独看两家店，只有一个小时。

sentences.en: 'Can you *cope*?' he asked.
I looked at the map — nearly a mile between them — and at the clock, and said yes before my brain could say no.
sentences.cn: 我看了看地图——两家店之间差不多一英里——又看了看钟，还没等脑子反应过来就答应了。

salary:2.en: The Manager slid a small envelope across the back-room table. 'Your first *salary*,' he said, looking almost proud. I opened it — the amount was modest, barely enough for rent — but a handwritten note inside said the new branch would need a shift leader. My hands went still.
salary:2.cnHint: 店长把第一份____递给我，信封里还夹着一张意味深长的便条。
salary:2.hook: The note had no signature, only a question mark.
salary:2.line: 'Your *salary* goes up the day the new branch opens.'

sentences.en: The Manager slid a small envelope across the back-room table.
sentences.cn: 店长在后间的桌子上推过来一个小信封。

sentences.en: 'Your first *salary*,' he said, looking almost proud.
I opened it — the amount was modest, barely enough for rent — but a handwritten note inside said the new branch would need a shift leader.
sentences.cn: 我打开了——金额不多，勉强够付房租——但里面夹着一张手写的纸条，说新分店需要一个班次主管。

sentences.en: My hands went still.
sentences.cn: 我的手停住了。

shopping:2.en: I found a crumpled list near the door — someone had left it behind. It read: shelf liner, price-gun tape, spare keys, good-luck charm. At the bottom, in red ink: FOR THE NEW STORE. So the *shopping* for the second branch had already begun, quietly, without a single meeting.
shopping:2.cnHint: 我在门口发现一张皱巴巴的____清单，上面写的东西都是新店要用的。
shopping:2.hook: The handwriting matched no one I knew.
shopping:2.line: 'This *shopping* list tells me the new store is closer than we think.'

sentences.cn: 我在门边找到一张皱巴巴的清单——是谁丢下来的。

sentences.cn: 上面写着：铺板、价格枪胶带、备用钥匙、幸运符。

sentences.en: At the bottom, in red ink: FOR THE NEW STORE.
sentences.cn: 底部用红笔写着：给新店用。

tendency:2.en: Tang leaned on the mop and watched the late crowd drift in. 'There is a clear *tendency*,' she said, pointing to the corner table where three students had parked themselves with laptops three nights in a row. 'Give them an outlet, and they will come every night.' She smiled like she had already won something.
tendency:2.cnHint: 阿糖观察着顾客的____，觉得新店选址的答案已经很明显了。
tendency:2.hook: She pulled out a small notebook full of careful tallies.
tendency:2.line: 'The *tendency* is obvious — put the new branch near the campus.'

sentences.en: Tang leaned on the mop and watched the late crowd drift in.
sentences.cn: 阿糖靠着拖把，看着晚来的人群涌入。

'Give them an outlet, and they will come every night.'

sentences.en: She smiled like she had already won something.
sentences.cn: 她笑得像已经赢了什么似的。

tough:2.en: The delivery arrived at two in the morning, twelve heavy boxes of stock for a trial run at the new site. Lin and I carried them up a narrow stairwell. My arms ached. 'First night is always the *toughest*,' Lin said, not even breathing hard. I decided then that I seriously needed to exercise more.
tough:2.cnHint: 深夜搬货很____，但隔壁咖啡店的林一点都不喘，让我暗暗惭愧。
tough:2.hook: Lin glanced at the last box and said nothing at all.
tough:2.line: '*Tough* work now means smooth opening day later.'

sentences.en: The delivery arrived at two in the morning, twelve heavy boxes of stock for a trial run at the new site.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点，送货来了，十二个装得满满的箱子，是拿到新店试运营的。

sentences.en: Lin and I carried them up a narrow stairwell.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林和我一起抬着它们上窄窄的楼梯。

sentences.cn: 我的胳膊疼死了。

sentences.cn: 那时我就决定，我真的得好好健身了。

tour:2.en: The Manager led us on a quick *tour* of the empty unit two streets away. White walls, bare shelves, a window facing a bright bus stop. He walked slowly, tapping walls, checking corners. Neither Tang nor I spoke. The space felt full of something that had not happened yet.

tour:2.hook: He stopped at the back wall and measured it with his hand.
tour:2.line: 'After the *tour*, tell me honestly — can you manage this place?'

sentences.en: The space felt full of something that had not happened yet.
sentences.cn: 这个空间感觉充满了还没发生过的东西。

wake:2.en: I almost missed it. In the *wake* of the long midnight rush, after the last customer left and the floor was finally clean, I noticed a folded paper tucked under the register. It was a rough floor plan, drawn in pencil, with one room circled and labelled MANAGER OFFICE — my name written lightly beside it.
wake:2.cnHint: 繁忙的夜班____过后，我在收银台下发现了一张标有我名字的平面图。
wake:2.hook: The pencil line under my name was not quite erased.
wake:2.line: 'In the *wake* of every big change, someone has to step up.'

annual:2.en: The Manager pinned a single sheet to the staff board. It was the *annual* review, one line per person. My line was short: 'Reliable. Observant. Ready for more.' Tang read it over my shoulder and raised both eyebrows. 'More,' she repeated softly, as if the word held a door she had been knocking on for a long time.
annual:2.cnHint: 年度____张贴出来，我那一行简短的评语让阿糖意味深长地重复了一个词。
annual:2.hook: The Manager had already left before either of us could ask.
annual:2.line: 'The *annual* review this year has a few surprises in it.'

sentences.en: Observant.
sentences.cn: 眼力好。

sentences.en: Ready for more.'
sentences.cn: 准备好迎接更多挑战。"

sentences.cn: 阿糖从我肩膀后面读了一遍，然后扬起两条眉毛。

sentences.cn: "更多，"她轻声重复，仿佛这个词打开了她敲了很久的门。

charity:2.en: A regular — an older woman with a canvas bag — placed a small tin on the counter. 'For the new store opening,' she said. 'Put it toward something nice for the neighbourhood.' It was a *charity* collection tin, nearly full of coins. I had not known she even noticed us struggling to get the branch ready.

charity:2.hook: She left before I could read the label on the tin.
charity:2.line: 'A little *charity* from the street can open a store better than money.'

sentences.cn: "拿去给街坊买点儿好东西。"

strength:2.en: A folded note fell from a box of new stock the Manager had carried in from the delivery truck. I picked it up and read it aloud. It said the new branch would pull staff from our store. 'Do we have the *strength* to run two shops?' I asked myself, staring at the empty shelf.

strength:2.line: 'I'm not sure we have the *strength* for this.'

survive:2.en: I found an old schedule pinned behind the back-room door, yellow and curling at the edges. Someone had written across it: 'Night shift will *survive* — just bring snacks.' It made me smile. Outside, a light rain began, and the store felt like a small warm island in the dark street.

survive:2.hook: Below the writing was a name I did not recognise — yet.

touch:2.en: Inside a donated book box left near the counter, I found a handwritten card. It read: 'This store kept me company on hard nights. Thank you.' That small *touch* of kindness from a stranger stopped me mid-task. I set the card on the shelf beside the register where everyone could see it.

touch:2.hook: Tang leaned over, read the card, and said nothing for a long moment.
touch:2.line: 'That little *touch* of kindness really got to me.'

afraid:2.en: Near the end of my shift I found a small envelope wedged under the counter, addressed to 'whoever opens next.' I hesitated. Tang saw me holding it and laughed softly. 'Are you *afraid* of an envelope?' she said. I opened it — inside was a hand-drawn map with a single question mark over the corner plot next door.

couple:2.en: A *couple* came in just before midnight, both carrying large paper bags and whispering to each other. They bought two cups of hot tea, spread a city map on the counter, and circled a spot far to the north. The Manager watched them from the back room, his expression unreadable.

couple:2.hook: The circled spot was exactly where our new branch would open.
couple:2.line: 'That *couple* has been in here three nights running,' the Manager said quietly.

definition:2.en: Tang slid a printed form across the counter to me. 'Read clause four,' she said. I read it twice. The *definition* of a 'branch manager' in the company handbook listed twelve duties, but the one that caught my eye was the last: 'responsible for all outcomes, good or bad.' I looked up slowly.

definition:2.hook: Tang was already watching my face for a reaction.
definition:2.line: 'The *definition* of this role is not what I expected,' I told Tang.

imagination:2.en: The back storeroom was plain and dusty, just shelves and boxes. But Lin walked in, stood still for a moment, and said the new branch could look completely different. 'Use your *imagination*,' she said, pointing at the bare walls. She pulled out a notebook filled with little drawings of a brighter, warmer space.
imagination:2.cnHint: 竞争对手走进仓库，指着空墙说要靠____把新店变得不一样。
imagination:2.hook: The last drawing in Lin's notebook looked nothing like a convenience store.
imagination:2.line: 'A little *imagination* is all it takes to change a place,' Lin said.

sentences.en: The back storeroom was plain and dusty, just shelves and boxes.

journey:2.en: I found an old photo tucked behind the staff notice board: the Manager, much younger, standing outside a tiny shop in what looked like a mountain town. On the back, in faded ink, someone had written: 'First stop of a long *journey*.' I put it back carefully and said nothing.

journey:2.hook: I wondered if the new branch was supposed to be the last stop.
journey:2.line: 'Every *journey* starts with one small, unremarkable shop,' the Manager once said.

nearby:2.en: Lin came in holding a printout of a street map and dropped it on the counter. 'There is another convenience store *nearby* — two blocks from our planned branch,' she said. Her finger pressed hard on the red dot. No one spoke. The Manager poured himself a coffee and stared at the map for a long time.

nearby:2.hook: The red dot on the map had a name I recognised.
nearby:2.line: 'A rival store *nearby* changes everything about this plan,' Lin said firmly.

perspective:2.hook: She then showed me a second photo — of an empty room across town.
perspective:2.line: 'From this *perspective*, I think we have been doing things wrong,' Tang said.

requirement:2.en: The Manager pinned a short list to the staff board before dawn. requirement:2.line: 'The first *requirement* is simple, but it cuts out most of us,' Tang admitted.

classify:2.en: The Manager handed me a thick folder and asked me to *classify* all the new product samples by type before morning. I spread them across the counter — drinks, snacks, daily goods, frozen items. Lin walked past, glanced at my piles, and rearranged two stacks without saying a word.
