sentences.cn: 阿糖在柜台上贴了一张印刷的通知。

sentences.en: 'The Manager is offering a bonus to the clerk who brings in the most new loyalty-card members this month,' she said.
sentences.cn: "店长在给这个月带来最多新会员卡客户的店员发奖金，"她说。

sentences.en: 'Real *incentive*, right?'
She smiled in a way that was friendly but also slightly competitive.
sentences.cn: 她笑了，那种笑容既友好又暗含竞争。

sentences.en: My shift had three hours left.
sentences.cn: 我的班次还有三个小时。

lower:2.en: The Manager taped a new price list near the door of the second store. I noticed the numbers on the bottom half — the shelf drinks had a *lower* price than at our main branch. He winked at me. 'Opening week only,' he said. I wondered if Lin knew yet.
lower:2.cnHint: 店长在新店门口贴出价格表，下排商品的____比本店还便宜。
lower:2.hook: Lin's footsteps were already loud on the stairs.
lower:2.line: 'The *lower* price is just for opening week, so don't get used to it.'

sentences.en: The Manager taped a new price list near the door of the second store.
sentences.cn: 店长在第二家店的门边贴了一张新价格表。

sentences.en: I noticed the numbers on the bottom half — the shelf drinks had a *lower* price than at our main branch.
He winked at me.
sentences.cn: 他朝我眨了眨眼。

sentences.en: 'Opening week only,' he said.
sentences.cn: "只限开业周，"他说。

sentences.en: I wondered if Lin knew yet.
sentences.cn: 我想知道林是否已经知道了。

naturally:2.en: The new store had a small plant in the window. Nobody had put it there on purpose — Tang said a regular customer just left it one morning. Somehow it made the whole place feel warmer. Customers *naturally* drifted to that corner first, picked things up, and stayed a little longer.
naturally:2.cnHint: 新店角落里多了一盆植物，顾客们____地被吸引过去。
naturally:2.hook: But who was the customer who left it, and why?
naturally:2.line: 'People *naturally* stop here — something about this corner just feels right.'

sentences.en: The new store had a small plant in the window.
sentences.cn: 新店的窗边放着一株小植物。

sentences.en: Nobody had put it there on purpose — Tang said a regular customer just left it one morning.
sentences.cn: 没人故意放在那儿的——阿糖说一个常客某个早上就留在那了。

sentences.en: Somehow it made the whole place feel warmer.
sentences.cn: 不知怎的，整个地方感觉温暖了许多。

sentences.en: Customers *naturally* drifted to that corner first, picked things up, and stayed a little longer.

passionate:2.en: Lin arrived at the new store carrying a folder of handwritten notes. She had mapped every shelf, every fridge, every small display. The Manager looked surprised. 'You didn't have to do all this,' he said. Lin just shrugged. She was *passionate* about store layout, and everyone in the room knew it.
passionate:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了满满一本笔记，对新店的陈列布置____得让店长都惊讶了。
passionate:2.hook: Her last note had a question mark no one could explain.
passionate:2.line: 'I'm *passionate* about layout — a good shelf can double the sales.'

sentences.en: Lin arrived at the new store carrying a folder of handwritten notes.
sentences.cn: 林到新店时拿着一个装满手写笔记的文件夹。

sentences.en: She had mapped every shelf, every fridge, every small display.
sentences.cn: 她标注了每一个架子、每一个冰箱、每一个小展示区。

sentences.en: The Manager looked surprised.
sentences.cn: 店长看起来很惊讶。

sentences.en: 'You didn't have to do all this,' he said.
sentences.cn: "你不用做这么多，"他说。

sentences.en: Lin just shrugged.
sentences.cn: 林只是耸了耸肩。

sentences.en: She was *passionate* about store layout, and everyone in the room knew it.

pop:2.en: I was stocking the back fridge at the new store when a screen on the small wall display lit up by itself. A *pop* ad for a new energy drink started playing on a loop. Nobody had switched it on. Tang leaned around the corner, eyes wide. 'That thing wasn't plugged in this morning,' she said.
pop:2.cnHint: 新店仓库里一块广告屏突然自己亮起，播起了____广告。
pop:2.hook: The plug was still lying on the floor, disconnected.
pop:2.line: 'A good *pop* display there would double what we sell before midnight.'

sentences.en: I was stocking the back fridge at the new store when a screen on the small wall display lit up by itself.
sentences.cn: 我正在新店铺的后冰柜前整理货物，突然墙上的小屏幕自己亮了起来。

sentences.en: A *pop* ad for a new energy drink started playing on a loop.
Nobody had switched it on.
sentences.cn: 没有人把它打开。

sentences.en: Tang leaned around the corner, eyes wide.
sentences.cn: 阿糖从角落探出头来，眼睛睁得很大。

sentences.en: 'That thing wasn't plugged in this morning,' she said.
sentences.cn: "那东西今早根本没插电，"她说。

possibly:2.en: We found a locked drawer behind the counter of the new store. The Manager tried every key on his ring — none of them worked. He held one small key up to the light. 'This could *possibly* open it,' he said slowly, 'but I've never seen it before.' Tang and I exchanged a look.
possibly:2.cnHint: 新店柜台后有一个上锁的抽屉，店长拿出一把不知来历的钥匙，说____能打开它。
possibly:2.hook: The key was not on any list the Manager had ever made.
possibly:2.line: 'This could *possibly* open it — but I have no idea where this key came from.'

sentences.en: We found a locked drawer behind the counter of the new store.
sentences.cn: 我们在新店铺的柜台后面发现了一个上了锁的抽屉。

sentences.en: The Manager tried every key on his ring — none of them worked.
sentences.cn: 店长试了试钥匙串上的每一把钥匙——没有一把能打开。

sentences.en: He held one small key up to the light.
sentences.cn: 他拿起一把很小的钥匙对着光线。

sentences.en: 'This could *possibly* open it,' he said slowly, 'but I've never seen it before.'
Tang and I exchanged a look.
sentences.cn: 阿糖和我互相看了一眼。

previously:2.en: The new store stood where a small tea shop used to be. One regular customer walked in, looked around slowly, and touched the far wall with one hand. 'I *previously* came here every Sunday,' she said softly. She bought nothing, just stood there a moment, then walked back out into the night.
previously:2.cnHint: 新店原址____是一家茶馆，一位老顾客进来摸了摸墙，轻声说起旧事。
previously:2.hook: She left a folded paper on the counter without a word.
previously:2.line: 'I *previously* came here every Sunday — the smell was completely different.'

sentences.en: The new store stood where a small tea shop used to be.
sentences.cn: 新店铺开在一家老茶馆的原址。

sentences.en: One regular customer walked in, looked around slowly, and touched the far wall with one hand.
sentences.cn: 一个老顾客走进来，慢慢地环顾四周，然后用一只手摸了摸远处的墙。

sentences.en: 'I *previously* came here every Sunday,' she said softly.
She bought nothing, just stood there a moment, then walked back out into the night.
sentences.cn: 她什么都没买，只是站了一会儿，然后走回了夜色里。

profession:2.en: A man in a neat jacket came in late and asked for a specific brand of pen we didn't carry. He explained his *profession* required exact handwriting tools — he was a contract writer for local businesses. He seemed puzzled that we had run out. He left his card on the counter and promised to return.
profession:2.cnHint: 一位深夜来访的男士说他的____需要特定的钢笔，可惜我们刚好缺货。
profession:2.hook: His business card listed three different names.
profession:2.line: 'My *profession* sounds simple, but the right pen changes everything I write.'

sentences.en: A man in a neat jacket came in late and asked for a specific brand of pen we didn't carry.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着整洁夹克的男人很晚才来，问我们有没有一个特定品牌的笔，我们没有。

sentences.en: He explained his *profession* required exact handwriting tools — he was a contract writer for local businesses.
He seemed puzzled that we had run out.
sentences.cn: 他好像很奇怪我们怎么会缺货。

sentences.en: He left his card on the counter and promised to return.
sentences.cn: 他在柜台上留下了名片，承诺会再来。

readily:2.en: Tang had visited the new store site the week before and *readily* agreed to help set it up. She showed up early, moved shelves without being asked, and had the back room sorted before noon. The Manager watched her from the doorway and said quietly to me, 'She was made for this kind of work.'
readily:2.cnHint: 阿糖____地答应去新店帮忙布置，提前到场，把一切都安排妥当了。
readily:2.hook: But she had turned down a full-time offer there once before.
readily:2.line: 'I *readily* said yes — setting up a new space is my favourite part of this job.'

sentences.en: Tang had visited the new store site the week before and *readily* agreed to help set it up.
She showed up early, moved shelves without being asked, and had the back room sorted before noon.
sentences.cn: 她早早就来了，主动搬动货架，中午前就把后仓整理好了。

sentences.en: The Manager watched her from the doorway and said quietly to me, 'She was made for this kind of work.'
sentences.cn: 店长从门口看着她，轻声对我说，"她天生就适合做这种工作。"

preserve:2.en: The Manager found an old photo behind the register. 'We should *preserve* this,' she said, holding it up to the light. It showed the store on opening day, twenty years ago. Tang leaned over to look. 'Is that you in the corner?' The Manager smiled but did not answer.
preserve:2.cnHint: 店长在收银台后面发现了一张旧照片，她说应该____它。
preserve:2.hook: Why won't the Manager talk about that day?
preserve:2.line: 'We should *preserve* this,' she said, holding it up to the light.

sentences.en: The Manager found an old photo behind the register.
sentences.cn: 店长在收银机后面发现了一张老照片。

sentences.en: 'We should *preserve* this,' she said, holding it up to the light.
It showed the store on opening day, twenty years ago.
sentences.cn: 它拍的是店铺开业的那天，二十年前。

sentences.en: Tang leaned over to look.
sentences.cn: 阿糖探过身来看。

sentences.en: 'Is that you in the corner?'
sentences.cn: "角落里的那个是你吗？"

sentences.en: The Manager smiled but did not answer.
sentences.cn: 店长笑了，但没有回答。

procedure:2.en: A delivery truck arrived at dawn with twice the usual boxes. The driver handed me a thick folder. 'New *procedure*,' he explained. 'Every item needs a signature now.' I started signing, but Tang stopped me. 'Wait. Count first.' I opened the first box. Half the order was missing.
procedure:2.cnHint: 送货司机说有新的____，每件商品都需要签名。
procedure:2.hook: Who signed for the missing items last week?
procedure:2.line: 'New *procedure*,' he explained. 'Every item needs a signature now.'

sentences.en: A delivery truck arrived at dawn with twice the usual boxes.
sentences.cn: 一辆送货卡车在天亮时到了，箱子比平时多了一倍。

sentences.en: The driver handed me a thick folder.
sentences.cn: 司机递给我一个厚厚的文件夹。

sentences.en: 'New *procedure*,' he explained.
'Every item needs a signature now.'
sentences.cn: "每件物品现在都需要签名。"

sentences.en: I started signing, but Tang stopped me.
sentences.cn: 我开始签字，但阿糖阻止了我。

sentences.en: 'Wait.
sentences.cn: "等等。"

sentences.en: Count first.'
sentences.cn: "先点货。"

sentences.en: I opened the first box.
sentences.cn: 我打开了第一个箱子。

sentences.en: Half the order was missing.
sentences.cn: 一半的订单都不见了。

reasonable:2.en: Lin walked in at midnight, which was strange—her own store closed at ten. 'I need twenty batteries,' she said. I named the price. 'That is not *reasonable*!' she replied. Tang appeared from the back room. 'Then why come here?' Lin went quiet and bought them anyway.
reasonable:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林说价格不____。
reasonable:2.hook: What happened at Lin's store tonight?

sentences.en: Lin walked in at midnight, which was strange—her own store closed at ten.
sentences.cn: 林在午夜走了进来，这很奇怪——她自己的店铺十点就关门了。

sentences.en: 'I need twenty batteries,' she said.
sentences.cn: "我需要二十节电池，"她说。

sentences.en: I named the price.
sentences.cn: 我报了价格。

sentences.en: 'That is not *reasonable*!' she replied.
Tang appeared from the back room.
sentences.cn: 阿糖从后仓走了出来。

sentences.en: 'Then why come here?'
sentences.cn: "那你干吗还来？"

sentences.en: Lin went quiet and bought them anyway.
sentences.cn: 林沉默了，还是买了。

reduction:2.en: The Manager put red stickers on the old calendars. '*Reduction* sale,' she announced. 'Fifty percent off.' An old man bought seven of them. 'For my grandchildren,' he said. But when he left, I saw him drop six in the recycling bin outside. He kept only one.
reduction:2.hook: Why did he throw away the other six?

sentences.en: The Manager put red stickers on the old calendars. '*Reduction* sale,' she announced.
'Fifty percent off.'
sentences.cn: "五折。"

sentences.en: An old man bought seven of them.
sentences.cn: 一个老人买了七张。

sentences.en: 'For my grandchildren,' he said.
sentences.cn: "给我的孙子们，"他说。

sentences.en: But when he left, I saw him drop six in the recycling bin outside.
sentences.cn: 但他离开后，我看到他把其中六张扔进了外面的回收桶。

sentences.en: He kept only one.
sentences.cn: 他只留下了一张。

season:2.en: Tang pinned a paper moon on the window. 'Mid-autumn *season*,' he said. 'Customers like it.' By evening, someone had drawn a rabbit on it in pen. Tang laughed when he saw it. 'Now it is perfect.' I checked the security video later. The artist was the Manager.
season:2.cnHint: 阿糖在窗上贴了纸月亮，说是中秋____。
season:2.hook: Why did the Manager draw it in secret?

sentences.en: Tang pinned a paper moon on the window.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在窗户上钉了一张纸做的月亮。

sentences.en: 'Mid-autumn *season*,' he said.
'Customers like it.'
sentences.cn: "顾客喜欢。"

sentences.en: By evening, someone had drawn a rabbit on it in pen.
sentences.cn: 到了晚上，有人用笔在上面画了一只兔子。

sentences.en: Tang laughed when he saw it.
sentences.cn: 阿糖看到时笑了。

sentences.en: 'Now it is perfect.'
sentences.cn: "现在完美了。"

sentences.en: I checked the security video later.
sentences.cn: 我后来看了监控录像。

sentences.en: The artist was the Manager.
sentences.cn: 画画的人是店长。

sector:2.en: The Manager divided the store with tape on the floor. 'Your *sector* is drinks and snacks,' she told me. 'Tang handles the rest.' I nodded. But by noon, Tang was restocking my shelves and I was fixing his. The Manager watched us and smiled. 'Good,' was all she said.
sector:2.cnHint: 店长用胶带把店分成几个____，分配给我和阿糖。
sector:2.hook: Why did she smile when we switched jobs?
sector:2.line: 'Your *sector* is drinks and snacks,' she told me.

sentences.en: The Manager divided the store with tape on the floor.
sentences.cn: 店长用胶带在地上分出了店铺的区域。

sentences.en: 'Your *sector* is drinks and snacks,' she told me.
'Tang handles the rest.'
sentences.cn: "阿糖负责其他的。"

sentences.en: I nodded.
sentences.cn: 我点了点头。

sentences.en: But by noon, Tang was restocking my shelves and I was fixing his.
sentences.cn: 但到了中午，阿糖在补充我的货架，而我在整理他的。

sentences.en: The Manager watched us and smiled.
sentences.cn: 店长看着我们，笑了。

sentences.en: 'Good,' was all she said.
sentences.cn: "很好，"她只说了这一句。

setting:2.en: The store lights had three buttons: bright, soft, and night. Tang always chose soft. 'Best *setting* for tired eyes,' he said. One evening, a student fell asleep at the table near the window. Tang dimmed the lights further. The Manager saw but said nothing. The student woke at dawn.
setting:2.cnHint: 阿糖说柔和是疲劳眼睛的最佳____。
setting:2.hook: How many others has Tang let sleep here?

sentences.en: The store lights had three buttons: bright, soft, and night.
sentences.cn: 店铺的灯有三个按钮：亮、柔和和夜间模式。

sentences.en: Tang always chose soft.
sentences.cn: 阿糖总是选柔和。

sentences.en: 'Best *setting* for tired eyes,' he said.
One evening, a student fell asleep at the table near the window.
sentences.cn: 一个晚上，一个学生在窗边的桌子上睡着了。

sentences.en: Tang dimmed the lights further.
sentences.cn: 阿糖把灯调得更暗了。

sentences.en: The Manager saw but said nothing.
sentences.cn: 店长看到了，但什么也没说。

sentences.en: The student woke at dawn.
sentences.cn: 学生在黎明时醒来。

shrink:2.en: I washed my new uniform and hung it to dry. By morning, it had started to *shrink*. The sleeves barely reached my wrists. Tang saw me struggling and laughed. 'Same thing happened to me.' He opened a drawer. Inside were five uniforms, each smaller than the last.
shrink:2.hook: Why does Tang keep all the ruined uniforms?

sentences.en: I washed my new uniform and hung it to dry.
sentences.cn: 我洗了新制服，挂起来晾干。

sentences.en: By morning, it had started to *shrink*.
The sleeves barely reached my wrists.
sentences.cn: 袖子短到刚好露出手腕。

sentences.en: Tang saw me struggling and laughed.
sentences.cn: 阿糖看我在那儿折腾，笑了。

sentences.en: 'Same thing happened to me.'
sentences.cn: 他说，我也是这样。

sentences.en: He opened a drawer.
sentences.cn: 他打开了一个抽屉。

sentences.en: Inside were five uniforms, each smaller than the last.
sentences.cn: 里面放着五件制服，一件比一件小。

employment:2.en: I found a folded paper behind the cash register. It was the Manager's old notebook. One page listed everyone's *employment* dates—mine was still blank. Tang started three years ago; someone named 'Wei' left last spring. I wondered if Wei also worked nights, and why they never stayed.
employment:2.cnHint: 我发现了一张记录员工____日期的旧纸条。
employment:2.hook: Who was Wei, and why did they leave?
employment:2.line: The Manager glanced at the page and said, 'Your *employment* here begins when you finish your first month.'

sentences.en: I found a folded paper behind the cash register.
sentences.cn: 我在收银机后面找到了一张折叠的纸。

sentences.en: It was the Manager's old notebook.
sentences.cn: 那是店长的旧笔记本。

sentences.en: One page listed everyone's *employment* dates—mine was still blank.
Tang started three years ago; someone named 'Wei' left last spring.
sentences.cn: 阿糖三年前开始在这儿干活；有个叫"韦"的人在去年春天离职了。

sentences.en: I wondered if Wei also worked nights, and why they never stayed.
sentences.cn: 我想知道韦是不是也在夜班工作过，还有他为什么从来没有留下来过。

entire:2.en: A cardboard box arrived during my shift. The label said 'For Manager—Private.' Inside were photos of the store's *entire* history: the grand opening, old staff parties, faded faces I'd never met. One picture showed Lin standing inside our store, smiling, wearing our uniform. That made no sense.
entire:2.cnHint: 一个箱子里装着商店____历史的照片。
entire:2.hook: Why was Lin wearing our store uniform years ago?
entire:2.line: Tang saw the photo and whispered, 'That box contains the *entire* truth about Lin.'

sentences.en: A cardboard box arrived during my shift.
sentences.cn: 一个纸箱在我当班时送到了。

sentences.en: The label said 'For Manager—Private.'
sentences.cn: 标签上写着"给店长——私人物品"。

sentences.en: Inside were photos of the store's *entire* history: the grand opening, old staff parties, faded faces I'd never met.
One picture showed Lin standing inside our store, smiling, wearing our uniform.
sentences.cn: 有张照片里隔壁咖啡店的林穿着我们的制服，在我们店里面笑着。

sentences.en: That made no sense.
sentences.cn: 这一点都说不通。

gift:2.en: A small wrapped box sat on the counter when I arrived. No note, no name. I opened it carefully—a tiny silver bell, the kind that rings when a door opens. Tang said the old store cat used to wear one. Someone left this *gift* on purpose. But we haven't had a cat in years.
gift:2.cnHint: 有人留下了一个神秘的____在柜台上。
gift:2.hook: Who left the bell, and why now?
gift:2.line: The Manager held the bell and said, 'Every *gift* in this store carries a memory.'

sentences.en: A small wrapped box sat on the counter when I arrived.
sentences.cn: 我到班时，柜台上放着一个用纸包好的小盒子。

sentences.en: No note, no name.
sentences.cn: 没有纸条，没有名字。

sentences.en: I opened it carefully—a tiny silver bell, the kind that rings when a door opens.
sentences.cn: 我小心地打开了——一个小小的银铃铛，是那种门打开时会响的。

sentences.en: Tang said the old store cat used to wear one.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说店里以前的猫就戴着一个。

sentences.en: Someone left this *gift* on purpose.
But we haven't had a cat in years.
sentences.cn: 可我们已经好多年没有猫了。

kitchen:2.en: I noticed a door behind the storage room I'd never opened. Inside was a tiny *kitchen*—dusty but complete, with a rice cooker, two bowls, and a calendar from five years ago. Someone had lived here. Tang admitted she used to sleep in the store when she had nowhere else to go.
kitchen:2.cnHint: 我发现了一个隐藏的____，里面有人曾经住过。
kitchen:2.hook: Does someone still live here at night?
kitchen:2.line: Tang smiled sadly and said, 'That *kitchen* saved me when I had nothing.'

sentences.en: I noticed a door behind the storage room I'd never opened.
sentences.cn: 我发现了一扇在储藏室后面的门，从来没有打开过。

sentences.en: Inside was a tiny *kitchen*—dusty but complete, with a rice cooker, two bowls, and a calendar from five years ago.
Someone had lived here.
sentences.cn: 有人住过这里。

sentences.en: Tang admitted she used to sleep in the store when she had nowhere else to go.
sentences.cn: 阿糖承认过她曾经在店里睡觉，因为没地方去。

mystery:2.en: Every Thursday at 2 a.m., someone slips an envelope under the door. Inside is always exactly twenty yuan and a thank-you note with no signature. I asked the Manager about it. She said it's been happening for years. This small *mystery* has become part of the store's routine, and no one wants to solve it.
mystery:2.cnHint: 每周四有人留下信封，这是个小____。
mystery:2.hook: Who is grateful enough to pay every single week?
mystery:2.line: The Manager said softly, 'Some *mystery* is kindness we don't need to name.'

sentences.en: Every Thursday at 2 a.m., someone slips an envelope under the door.
sentences.cn: 每个星期四凌晨两点，有人会在门下塞进一个信封。

sentences.en: Inside is always exactly twenty yuan and a thank-you note with no signature.
sentences.cn: 里面总是正好二十块钱和一张没有签名的感谢信。

sentences.en: I asked the Manager about it.
sentences.cn: 我问了店长。

opposite:2.hook: What broke their friendship across the street?

permanent:2.hook: What else has this old store quietly remembered?
permanent:2.line: The Manager touched the print and said, 'Some marks become *permanent* witnesses to everything.'

comfort:2.en: A note was taped to the back of the stockroom door. The handwriting was Tang's. It read: 'Night shift is lonely at first. Hot water is in the green flask. Snacks are on the third shelf. You will be fine.' I stood there a moment, tired and a little lost, and felt the quiet *comfort* of those words settle around me like a warm coat.

comfort:2.hook: But why had Tang left that note and then never mentioned it once?
comfort:2.line: 'I left it there because a small *comfort* can make a long night shorter.'

plus:2.en: Lin slid a handwritten receipt across the counter and pointed at the bottom line. 'Two rice balls, one hot drink, *plus* the late-night charge — that is your total.' I looked at the neat column of numbers. Lin ran the noodle cart just outside and kept accounts sharper than any machine I had seen. Something about those careful figures made me uneasy.
